# octreg: OCT tissue block to whole-hemisphere MRI registration — project handoff

*Assembled 2026-08-24 from the project's code (`octreg` on the AutoDL container and its Mac mirror), the two servers and their run artefacts, the meeting and Slack archive, and the published literature; it supersedes the scattered notes, corrections files and internal documents it was built from.*

## Addendum, 2026-09-13: v1.1 and the I58 verdict

This document describes the state on 2026-08-24. Since then v1.1 was built, run and regression-tested; the full technical record is [docs/v11/REPORT_I58_v11.md](docs/v11/REPORT_I58_v11.md) (probe records P1 to P10, the spec, the implementation review and the evidence figures are in `docs/v11/`). What changed, in seven lines:

1. The tree is now a git repository (`7ef90e5` = the v1 baseline described below, `4170ef0` = v1.1, later commits = records); the 21 server-only scripts were pulled into `scripts/`; the server keeps a v1 snapshot at `/root/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration_v1/`.
2. v1.1 adds, all behind flags whose defaults reproduce v1 bit for bit (verified by `regress.py` on I46 and I55, 0 of 26 rows failing on each): a texture-based specimen mask for agarose-embedded blocks, an axis-detected destripe, a `--init-transform` prior path (the PI confirmed a position prior exists), a vascular-stage acceptance gate, and a sign-corrected intensity fine stage that refuses to ship a pose its own restarts cannot reproduce. The fine stage is NOT validated on cortex and stays off by default: on I46 and I55 it passes all of its own gates (8/8 restarts, U 0.4 to 1.1 mm) yet moves the pose 0.7 to 1.0 mm off the annotation optimum (I46 vessel median 123 to 165 um and depth stretch 1.219 to 1.31, I55 GM Dice 0.930 to 0.916), so its self-consistency U must never be quoted as accuracy, and the labelled cortical pairs are the calibration set for any future fine objective (`regress.py --tol fine`). v1.1b adds only options with v1.1 defaults (fixed-point-set polish, small restarts, FOV-rind exclusion, `--fine-dof rigid`, switchable mask pocket/hole rules, a 2 mm core mask); on I58 no polish configuration converges at P_R5 (report Appendix C.2), and the I46/I55 calibration of the conservative polish (`scripts/run_v11_polish.sh`) had not run when the compute instance froze.
3. Two facts about serial-sectioning OCT that this document did not know: the OCT to MRI intensity relation on the brainstem pair is inverted (raw NCC is negative and V-shaped at the correct pose), and on I58 the physical sectioning axis is array axis 2, not axis 0 as v1 assumed.
4. On I58 the brainstem body registers at body level (structural pose reproducible to 0.3 mm / 1 deg across seeds, boundary agreement about 2 mm) and nothing finer is achievable label-free, because the MRI crop and the OCT block do not depict the same rigid assembly: the MRI cerebellar lobe has no rigid counterpart in the OCT (exhaustive reverse search), while torn cerebellar folia sit at the bottom of the OCT block on the opposite side of the body (0.04 mm close-ups). Surface distance, mutual information, piecewise registration and symmetric-partner starts were all tried and all fail for that reason.
5. Chapter 11's roadmap item "our own data down to sub-millimetre" is therefore withdrawn until Xiangrui supplies the un-cropped MRI, the dissection and embedding sequence, the OCT depth-axis metadata, and about 20 landmark pairs on the body.
7. Update 2026-09-14: Xiangrui's pair runs end to end from the two original NIfTI files with one command (`scripts/run_xiangrui_i58.sh`: prep, register without fine stage, QC, export in the original NIfTI frames, 27.5 min) and reproduces the reported pose exactly. OCT intensity re-normalisation and cerebellum exclusion were tested and do not help. The OCT-to-MRI handedness is not decided by the data: the other handedness fits the outline better (rim forward 1.57 vs 2.02 mm) but the internal class correlation worse (NCC 0.113 vs 0.124), and the OCT header orientation agrees with the other handedness; both candidates are exported for a visual decision (report Appendix C.4).
6. The label-mapping bug of chapter 7 (`map_labels_to_grid`) is confirmed empirically (I38 keeps 65.7 % of labels under the affine-derived permutation, 100 % under the shape-consistent one) and is still unfixed; the corrupted DANDI `sub-I58` flip-1 file was re-downloaded and verified.

## How to use this document

**Who it is for.** A competent researcher or agent who has never seen this project and is expected to either take it over or judge it. After reading it you should be able to explain the project to a third party, defend every design decision in a lab meeting, read the results without over-claiming them, understand why the lab's constraints make the method look the way it does, and decide what to do next. It is not a code manual — the code appears only where a specific line, flag or file carries an argument.

**What it assumes.** Working familiarity with 3D medical image registration (affine transforms, cross-correlation, coarse-to-fine optimisation) and with neuroimaging file conventions (NIfTI, voxel-to-world affines, BIDS sidecars). It does not assume any knowledge of OCT, of serial-sectioning microscopy, of this dataset, or of this lab; chapter 2 supplies all of that. Provenance markers are used throughout and must never be silently dropped when this text is reused. There are exactly three. `[UNVERIFIED]` means the claim is stated in a source but no artefact on disk was checked to confirm it. `[NOT RE-MEASURED]` means it was measured once and recorded, and was not re-derived while this document was written. `[OPEN]` means nobody has answered the question yet. Older copies of the project's notes use other bracketed forms; those were folded into these three, and chapter 2 records the mapping.

Where sources disagreed, precedence went to facts verified first-hand against the running servers and the files on disk, then to the project's own correction records, then to its narrative documents. Those corrections have been applied *here* but **not** to the project's own files, several of which still carry superseded numbers. Chapter 12 is the ledger of what was corrected, what remains unverified, and which files still need editing.

**Reading order.** If you are **taking over the work**: chapter 1, then chapter 10 (where everything physically is, and how to look at a real result in five minutes), then chapter 5 (the method as a chain of reasoning), chapter 6 (what the numbers do and do not license), chapter 7 (the failures and dead ends, so you do not re-run them), and chapter 11 (the ordered roadmap, ending in six things to do if you do nothing else) — keeping chapter 2 open as a glossary and chapter 12 as the list of what is still unresolved; chapters 3, 4, 8 and 9 on demand. If you only need to **understand and evaluate** it: chapter 1, chapter 3 (the scientific question and why the problem is hard), chapter 5 §5.0–§5.4 (the four stages and the one finding), chapter 6 (especially §6.1, §6.5, §6.11, §6.15 and §6.16), chapter 8 (how it differs from the published baseline, and what in it is not novel), and chapter 12 Part B and Part C (every claim without an artefact behind it). Do not read chapter 6 without chapter 6 §6.2, which says what each metric physically measures.

## 1. The project in fifteen lines

**The question.** Cellular measurements — neuron counts, laminar thickness, fibre orientation — are made inside centimetre-scale blocks of human brain imaged at micrometre resolution, and they are *unplaced*. A count becomes a census only if you can say where in the brain it was taken, and only the whole-hemisphere ex-vivo MRI, acquired before the tissue was cut up, still holds that geometry. `octreg v1` produces the one 4×4 matrix per block that puts it back, plus the evidence that the matrix is right.

**The approach.** Reduce both modalities to the only representation they share — a soft two-class white-matter/grey-matter map, obtained on the MRI side by dividing out a local tissue mean at σ = 10 mm and then applying Otsu, with no annotation anywhere — and score every translation by FFT against 8 000 quasi-uniform SO(3) rotations × {proper, mirrored} = 16 000 orientations at 0.6 mm, then refine top candidates through a clamped rigid → similarity → affine ladder at 0.6 → 0.3 → 0.15 mm. Because a two-class cortical block is geometrically degenerate along its serial-sectioning axis, a third channel — MRI local darkness against automatically segmented OCT vessel density — is added last to recover the one scale the structural objective provably cannot see.

**Demonstrated.** Two of nine public subjects (I46, I55 of Costantini 2023 / DANDI:000026) have quantitative agreement: Dice 0.803/0.825 and 0.921/0.930 against the dataset's manual labels, and on I46 a nearest-vessel median of 166.7 µm with 47.3 % within 150 µm against an oracle ceiling of 0.466 and a chance level of 0.117. The strongest single result is not a Dice value: the depth-axis scale, which moves the structural NCC by only 0.021 over a ±22.5 % sweep against 0.169 along an in-plane axis, is recovered automatically at **1.219** where three independent human-derived sources say 1.174 / 1.177 / 1.167 — with a correct null on I55, whose sidecar is right. On the lab's own I58 brainstem pair a coarse pose is recovered in 362.3 s with no prior, no labels and no initialisation.

**Not demonstrated.** No numeric residual exists for the lab's own data at all — the brainstem "a few millimetres" is a visual estimate. No target registration error exists anywhere. The published baseline has never been run, and the authors' own pose for I46 disagrees with ours by 23 mm, unresolved. Evaluation is computed against a corrupted label volume on six of the nine subjects, so "5 of 9 correct" is really **2 confirmed, 3 unresolved, 1 undecidable, 3 failed**. Five of the nine headline runs were produced by a code revision that no longer exists.

**The two constraints the PI set (2026-08-23).** *"We do have a lot of scans and volumes, but we do not have many labels"* — so label-freeness is a match to the real operating constraint, not an aesthetic, and visual QC drives development while quantitative results are still owed for the paper. And *"we do have prior knowledge of where it might be… we can crop a small part there"* — so the whole-hemisphere prior-free search is robustness insurance and a paper capability, not the value proposition. Lead with the annotations, not with the prior.

**The single most important risk.** The authoritative tree is not a git repository at all, and 21 files — every orchestration and figure script — exist only on a rented GPU container that reassigns its `host:port` on every restart. The absence of version control has already cost one result outright: the revision that produced the project's most-cited run is unrecoverable.

**The single most important next step.** Rescue and version the code (`rsync` the 21 server-only scripts down, `git init` behind a vetted `.gitignore`), then fix `map_labels_to_grid` in `prep_subject.py` and re-run evaluation only on the six 0.12 mm subjects — one hour, no re-registration, and it is the difference between a claim of 5 of 9 and a defensible 2 of 9.

## 2. Orientation and glossary

The whole project fits in one sentence: **you are moving a small block of human brain tissue that was imaged with a microscope (OCT, voxels 12–35 µm) into the coordinate frame of a whole half-brain that was imaged in an MRI scanner (voxels 0.12–0.15 mm), nobody tells you where in the hemisphere the block came from, both images are grayscale and their intensities mean completely different physical things, and the output is one 4×4 matrix.** Every piece of vocabulary in this document decorates one clause of that sentence:

| The clause | The jargon for it |
|---|---|
| small block of brain | *tissue block*, *slab*, *BA44/45 block*, *brainstem block* |
| imaged with a microscope, slice by slice, destroying the block as it goes | *serial-sectioning OCT*, *block-face imaging*, *vibratome* |
| a whole half-brain in a scanner, donor already deceased | *whole-hemisphere ex vivo 7T MRI*, *FLASH*, *VFA*, *EPIC* |
| the two images look nothing alike | *cross-modality registration*, *multimodal similarity* |
| nobody tells you where the block came from | *label-free*, *prior-free*, *blind localization*, *partial-to-whole* |
| one 4×4 matrix | *affine transform*, `T_oct2mri.npy` / `T_oct2mri.lta` |

The first half of this chapter is the reference for names, machines, datasets and documents — come back to it whenever a path or a person confuses you. The second half is the vocabulary, with the project-specific reason each term is load-bearing here rather than only its textbook meaning.

**Provenance markers, defined here once for the whole document.** Exactly three are used anywhere in these twelve chapters, and they mean:

| Marker | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[UNVERIFIED]` | Stated in a source, but not independently checked for this document |
| `[NOT RE-MEASURED]` | Measured once and recorded, not re-run for this document |
| `[OPEN]` | An unresolved question — nobody has answered it |

Nothing else is a marker. If you meet `[NOT RE-VERIFIED]`, `[REPORTED, NOT VERIFIED]`, `[NOT RUN]` or `[interpretation]` in an older copy of this material, they were folded into the three above (the first two become `[UNVERIFIED]`, `[NOT RUN]` becomes `[OPEN]` or plain prose, and an interpretation is now simply *said* to be an interpretation). The three markers must not be silently dropped when this text is reused.

#### A.2 The two parallel projects

The lab runs two lines at once. Confusing them is the single easiest way to misread a number in this document — most of the metrics people quote in meetings (PSNR, SSIM, HD95, DSC ≈ 0.99) belong to the *other* project.

This is a **name-and-metric decoder only** — enough to tell, from a term or a number, which project a sentence is about. It is deliberately the shortest of the three cuts at this comparison: the *scientific* relationship between the two projects (why one specimen produces both problems, and what one hands the other) is chapter 3, The scientific problem and why it matters, §3.6, and the *organisational* side-by-side — advisor, members, inputs, core problems, method state, numbers on record, venue, and the status verdict to use for each — is chapter 9, The lab: people, history, and the constraints that shape this work, §9.3.1. Do not copy rows out of either of those into here.

| | **(a) LSFM / SVR reconstruction** — older | **(b) Cross-modality registration** — newer, **this project** |
|---|---|---|
| Internal names | "the old project", `proj-lsfm`, SVR = slice-to-volume registration | `octreg`, "OCT→MRI" |
| Lead | Lavanya Kotha (since 2026-06-02) | **Yuntian Yang** (since 2026-07-24) |
| Methods | GumNet2D, VoxelMorph (vanilla + diffeomorphic), TransMorph, LapIRN, TPS, NIIV, NeSVoR | `octreg v1`: Otsu two-class maps → mirror-aware FFT global search on SO(3) → coarse-to-fine affine → vessel-density channel |
| Metrics | DSC, PSNR, SSIM, NCC, HD95 | Dice (WM/GM), nearest-vessel distance / `f150`, restart convergence, oracle gap |

**How they relate, in one line.** The full chain is **LSFM → OCT → MRI**, and Yuntian owns the **OCT→MRI** segment (08-07, per `WORKSPACE_STATE.md` §2.2); project (a) is **not** an upstream dependency of `octreg`, because OCT is already a volume. Why the same specimen produces both problems at once, and what (a) genuinely supplies to (b) — its failure modes and its validation philosophy — are chapter 3, §3.6. The dated organisational history of the split (the PI's idea on 2026-06-02, seven weeks before (b) had a lead; 2026-08-23 the first meeting where both lines presented in one session) is chapter 9, §9.3.2.

Six of nine are mirrored — **I38, I46, I48, I56, I58, I62**; not mirrored: I55, I57, I61 and both brainstem runs. Any document saying "5 of 9" and listing "I46, I38, I56, I58, I62" is wrong; **I48 is the one that was dropped from the list**. Three of nine fail (I57, I61, I58).

Two verdict subtleties that are routinely conflated:

- **I62's Dice of 0.0 is a label-coverage artefact, not a registration failure.** It has no whole-hemisphere label on DANDI at all, so it is scored against the tiny BA-only patch — 0.23 % of the volume — and Dice's full-class denominator drives the number to zero. The same coverage argument applies to the other large slabs.
- **I48 is a different case and must not be lumped in with it.** Its Dice is untrustworthy in **both** directions (its labels are one of the 0.12 mm volumes whose label→MRI axis pairing is broken, and only 62.7 % of its whole-hemisphere labels land on MRI tissue), so the number can be neither believed nor dismissed as an artefact. Its "uncertain" verdict does not rest on Dice at all: it rests on the **0.0013 search-score margin** between the top two candidate poses.

Annotations on the MRI side, per subject: `label-infrasupra_dseg` (BA 44/45 only, values 1/2/3), `label-infrasupra_seg-wholehemi_dseg` (same scheme, whole hemisphere — **missing entirely for I62**), `label-vessels_dseg` (manual MRI vessels). On the OCT side, `derivatives/sub-XX/ses-OCT/vessel/ves_seg.tif` exists for only **5 subjects in the dandiset** (I38, I45, I46, I48, I60), of which we hold I38, I46, I48. Traps that have already cost time: the vessel-label non-zero value is **not standardised** (1 for I38/I58/I61/I62, 255 for I46/I48/I56/I57, 30 for I55, plus 17 voxels of −32,768 in I57) so always threshold `> 0`; five label files are bounding-box crops rather than full-FOV volumes; `seg-wholehemi` is always stored in `R,A,S` order and is therefore always axis-permuted relative to the EPIC MRI.
