#### A.7 Two standing constraints from the PI that colour every definition below

Both were stated on 2026-08-23 and both change how you should read the vocabulary.

1. **"We do have a lot of scans and volumes, but we do not have many labels."** The label-free design is therefore a match to the real constraint, not over-engineering. Annotations enter only at evaluation time. The PI also explicitly discounts Dice as a development signal because manual labels have their own error — *"during development I usually prefer to just check visually whether things look right"* — while still requiring quantitative results for a paper. Evaluation is therefore two-track: QC overlays and restart consistency during development, a defensible quantitative protocol for the paper.
2. **"We do have prior knowledge of where it might be. … We know where it is, so we can crop a small part there."** The prior-free whole-hemisphere search is therefore **robustness insurance and a paper capability, not the operational value proposition**. The cropped path already exists in the code (`--crop-centre x,y,z --crop-half-mm 30`). What the prior actually *is* — a region label, a cutting record, a coordinate range, a manual ROI — has never been specified `[OPEN]`, and its default half-width of 30 mm is smaller than five of the nine blocks.

---

### Glossary of working vocabulary

Textbook definitions carry no marker. The project-specific half of each entry is what matters; where it comes from code it names the file, flag or constant.

#### B.1 Imaging modalities, specimen preparation and acquisition

| Term | Plain definition | Why it matters HERE |
|---|---|---|
| **OCT** (Optical Coherence Tomography) | An optical method that measures **backscattered light** from tissue by low-coherence interferometry, giving a 3D volume at micrometre resolution. Contrast comes from how strongly tissue scatters light; in brain, **myelin scatters strongly**, so white matter is bright at native resolution | The *moving* image of this whole project. Every OCT volume here is a block of a few cm³ at 12–35 µm. Its intensity has **no calibrated meaning** and the file carries **no world coordinate system** — it is just an array, so `prep_subject.py --oct-spacing-um z,y,x` and `--oct-layout SPR` (default) are how a world frame gets attached at all |
| **PSOCT** (Polarization-Sensitive OCT) | OCT that also measures how tissue changes the **polarization** of the light, yielding a birefringence / optic-axis channel on top of scattering. Myelinated fibre bundles are birefringent, so PSOCT reveals fibre orientation | The Costantini OCT is acquired on a serial-sectioning **PSOCT** rig (`ses-OCT`, 51 assets, 133.4 GB). **We only ever use the scattering/intensity channel.** The birefringence channel is not in the files we downloaded and `octreg` has no code path for it — it is the single most obvious unused signal, and a fibre-orientation channel would be a natural fourth NCC channel |
| **Serial-sectioning imaging** | Image the exposed top surface of a tissue block, physically cut that layer off, image the new surface, repeat. The volume is assembled from hundreds of these slabs. Because the block never moves between cuts, the stack has **no slice-to-slice deformation** — that is its entire advantage over classical histology | This is why OCT is the intermediate modality in the LSFM → OCT → MRI chain: it is the only step that is geometrically undistorted. It also creates the two artefacts that dominate OCT preprocessing here: **periodic depth attenuation** (light penetrates less deeply toward the bottom of each slab, producing a sawtooth in brightness) and **section seams** at the cut planes. The seams are what kills the vascular channel on the brainstem pair |
| **Section period** | The number of z-slices between two cut planes — one slab's worth of depth | **A documented factual error you will meet everywhere.** `octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py:125` says `window = max(10, int(round(1200.0 / sp[0])))  # ~1.2 mm of depth = one section period at 12 um`, and `common.oct_slab_normalize` defaults to `window=100`. The **measured** period is **33 slices for I46 (0.396 mm)** and **12 slices for I56 (0.420 mm)** — about **3× smaller** `[NOT RE-MEASURED]`, inherited from an FFT + autocorrelation analysis of the raw OME-TIFFs (I46: FFT peak 33.0, autocorrelation r = 0.857 at lag 33 with clean harmonics at 66/99/132/165/198; I56: FFT peak 12.17, r = 0.882 at lag 12). The "≈100" figure originates in `costantini_b0/reports/costantini_i46_data_audit.md:43`, where a mean-intensity profile was inspected at **25-slice granularity**, which aliases a true 33-slice period to ≈100. The code is not broken — 100 ≈ 3 × 33 for I46 — but the printed justification is false, and for I56 `window = 34` is 2.83 periods, not an integer multiple. **Do not extend this into an argument about I46's voxel size.** It was once presented that way — 500 µm vibratome cut ÷ 33 slices = 15.15 µm/slice, therefore the 12 µm sidecar is wrong — and that line of evidence is **withdrawn**: the identical arithmetic on I56 gives 500/12.17 = 41.7 µm against a 35 µm sidecar that is corroborated twice inside the file *and* by registration, so the premise cannot hold for both. Read consistently, the two measured periods say the real cut is ≈0.40–0.42 mm, which would imply a correction of only **1.06** for I46, not 1.167. The 500 µm figure is itself `[UNVERIFIED]`. The I46 sidecar bug stands on other evidence entirely (chapter 4, The data, §4.5) |
| **Block-face imaging** | Any technique where the *cut face* of the block is imaged before each cut; in histology, usually an optical photograph used as an undistorted reference to un-warp the cut sections | Named in the literature review as the mechanism behind **TIRL**, a competing staged route to MRI that requires blockface and slab photographs. **We have no blockface photographs**, which is precisely why blind localization was necessary in the first place |
| **Vibratome** | A microtome that cuts tissue with a **vibrating blade**, letting you slice unfrozen, unembedded or agarose-embedded soft tissue at tens to hundreds of µm | The cutting half of serial sectioning. `[UNVERIFIED]` in this repo — no primary source read here names the instrument explicitly. The section thickness evidence is indirect and is the measured period above, not the code comment |
| **LSFM / SPIM** (Light-Sheet Fluorescence Microscopy / Selective Plane Illumination Microscopy) | Two names for the same idea: illuminate the sample with a thin **sheet** of light and image the lit plane side-on. Fast, low photobleaching, cellular-resolution volumes of large cleared specimens. DANDI uses `ses-SPIM` as the key | The **third** modality of the chain. It carries the cell-level information (stains Calretinin, NeuN, Calbindin) the whole enterprise ultimately wants placed in MRI coordinates. In DANDI:000026 `ses-SPIM` is 38,735 assets / 34.25 TB, deliberately **never downloaded**. LSFM is also the input of the *other* lab project (A.2a) |
| **Tissue clearing** | Chemically making tissue optically transparent — matching refractive indices, removing lipids — so a light sheet can penetrate a whole block instead of ~100 µm. CLARITY, iDISCO, SHIELD are named protocols | Required for LSFM, not for OCT. It matters here only through **shrinkage**: clearing and fixation change specimen dimensions, which is one justification for allowing **scale** in the OCT→MRI transform rather than solving rigid-only. The project plan wants a measured shrinkage prior and records that it has not been measured `[OPEN]` |
| **Agarose embedding** | Setting the specimen in a block of agarose gel so it holds still and cuts cleanly | **A named failure mode of our own data.** In Xiangrui's I58 brainstem OCT the agarose scatters light about as much as the tissue does, so an intensity threshold cannot separate specimen from embedding medium and the tissue mask swallows the agarose. The fix that made the run work at all was making the search's overlap gate **adaptive to the tissue volumes of both sides** rather than a fixed fraction. A texture-based specimen mask is the top v1.1 item |
| **Ex vivo** | Imaging tissue **outside** the living body — here a fixed post-mortem brain in a scanner: no motion, no breathing, unlimited scan time, and altered contrast because fixation changes T1/T2 | Everything here is ex vivo, with two consequences you must internalize. (a) Scan times of many hours give 0.12–0.15 mm whole-hemisphere resolution that in-vivo MRI cannot reach. (b) **Contrast is inverted relative to in-vivo intuition** — in these ex-vivo FLASH volumes at ~20° flip, **GM is bright and WM is dark**, which is why `register.py --mri-wm-bright` is an opt-in flag whose default is off ("default: GM bright, as ex-vivo FLASH ~20 deg"). Blood vessels appear as **dark blobs** for the same reason, and that is the entire basis of the vascular channel |
| **Whole hemisphere** | One half of a brain, imaged in one volume | The *fixed* image, and the reason this problem is hard. A whole-hemisphere EPIC volume is 1280×1040×576 @ 0.15 mm or 1600×1400×640 @ 0.12 mm — up to **1.4 G voxels**. The OCT block is a few percent of it, so this is a **partial-to-whole** search, not an image-to-image alignment. The memory strategy follows directly: MRI features live on the CPU as `float16`, and only pooled levels and block-sized crops move to the GPU |

#### B.2 MRI physics, contrast and correction

| Term | Plain definition | Why it matters HERE |
|---|---|---|
| **7T** | Static field strength of 7 tesla, about 4.7× a standard clinical 3T. More signal, finer voxels, and worse field inhomogeneity | All Costantini MRI is 7T on a Siemens **MAGNETOM Terra** at MGH/HST (`MagneticFieldStrength 7`, `InstitutionName "MGH, HST"` in every sidecar) |
| **FLASH** (Fast Low Angle SHot) / **GRE** | A fast gradient-echo sequence: small flip angle, short repetition time. Contrast between tissues depends strongly on the chosen flip angle | The only MRI contrast this project uses. Sidecars report `PulseSequenceType "GRE"`, `RepetitionTime` 0.034 s or 0.045 s. One sidecar (I55) records TR as the string `"34"` — a units bug, s vs ms |
| **Flip angle** | How far the RF pulse tips the magnetization away from the main field, in degrees. The main knob controlling GM/WM contrast in FLASH | **The single most important acquisition parameter for us.** At ~20° an ex-vivo FLASH has good GM/WM contrast; at 10° it has almost none. **The I58 run failed for exactly this reason** — the pipeline was pointed at the 10° volume. Seven of nine subjects are confirmed 20° |
| **`flip-N`** (the BIDS index) | In DANDI filenames, `flip-1`, `flip-2`, … is an **index into the acquisition list, not the angle in degrees** | Verified trap, and an inverted claim that survived into several project documents: for I58, **`flip-1` has `FlipAngle "30"` and `flip-3` has `"10"`** — both TR 0.045, Siemens MAGNETOM Terra, GRE. I58 was registered on **flip-3 = 10°**. Any text saying "flip-1 = 10°, flip-3 = 30°" is exactly backwards. The 30° volume `sub-I58_ses-MRI_flip-1_VFA.nii.gz` (**2,890,933,645 B**) is already on disk and was never tried — re-running I58 on it is a free experiment. `flip-2` is 20° for I38/I46/I55/I56, `flip-4` is 20° for I57/I61, and `flip-3` is 20° for I62. **Never infer the angle from the index — read the `.json` sidecar.** I48's sidecar was never downloaded, so its angle is unknown `[OPEN]` |
| **VFA** (Variable Flip Angle) | Acquiring the same anatomy at several flip angles so quantitative maps (PD, T1) can be fitted from the intensity differences | The DANDI protocol is a VFA multi-echo FLASH; that is what the `_VFA` filename suffix means. We use exactly **one flip per subject** (two downloaded for I58) and ignore the rest, saving 2.4–4.9 GB per file |
| **MEF / multi-echo** | Multiple echoes read out after each excitation (`echo-1..4` in filenames); combining them improves SNR and enables T2* fitting | The **raw** DANDI MRI is per-echo, per-flip (`sub-I46_ses-MRI_echo-{1..4}_flip-{1..3}_VFA.nii.gz`), ~1.58 TB for all `ses-MRI` raw. **We never touch raw echoes** — `derivatives/EPIC/` is already echo-combined and corrected |
| **B0 inhomogeneity** | The main field is never perfectly uniform across the sample; where it deviates, spins precess at the wrong frequency, so voxels are **geometrically displaced** and intensities distorted. Worse at 7T | A **geometric** error and therefore fatal for registration: if the MRI is spatially warped, no rigid or affine OCT→MRI transform can be correct. Corrected upstream by EPIC — this is the main reason we use the derivative rather than the raw data |
| **EPIC correction** | The B0-distortion-correction method named in `derivatives/EPIC/dataset_description.json`. The derivative pipeline is EPIC B0 correction → FreeSurfer `mri_ms_fitparms` with the B1+ transmit fieldmap → **synthesised** per-flip contrasts corrected for both B0 and B1+ inhomogeneity | `derivatives/EPIC/sub-XX/ses-MRI/anat/sub-XX_ses-MRI_flip-N_VFA.nii.gz` **is the only MRI this project ever reads.** EPIC is also the name of the label space — annotations are `space-EPIC`. Redoing the correction ourselves would mean re-implementing EPIC plus `mri_ms_fitparms`, explicitly rejected |
| **B1+ / transmit field / `TB1DAM`** | Spatial variation in the *transmit* RF field, so the nominal flip angle is not the actual flip angle everywhere. `*_TB1DAM.nii.gz` (16 per subject, ~0.4 MB each) are the measured transmit maps | Input to the EPIC derivative pipeline. Not downloaded; needed only if the correction is ever redone |
| **Bias field** | A smooth, low-spatial-frequency multiplicative brightness gradient across an MRI, caused mostly by **receive**-coil sensitivity. Physically identical tissue looks brighter near the coil | **The single highest-value preprocessing step in `octreg`.** A global two-class threshold over a whole hemisphere fails because the bias field shifts the histogram from one end of the brain to the other — the measured local-mean tissue field on I46 runs p5 29.3 / p50 36.6 / p95 55.4, a **1.9× intensity drift**. Dividing by a local tissue mean (Gaussian **σ = 10 mm**, `flatten_sigma_mm=10.0`) before Otsu lifts WM/GM Dice against the manual labels from **0.66 / 0.62 to 0.90 / 0.93**. **This result is confirmed** — it was once flagged as having no artefact behind it, and that doubt has been withdrawn: it was re-derived first-hand on I46 against `work/I46/labels4.npy`, and all four `octreg/README.md` figures agree with the re-derivation to ≤ 0.02. Quote the rounded pair; the precise pair and the reproduction recipe are in chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning (§5.1) |
| **Quantitative maps (PD / T1 / T2\*)** | Per-voxel estimates of physical tissue parameters fitted from the VFA/multi-echo data, rather than an arbitrary-units image. Files `*_{PD,T1,T2star}_VFA.nii.gz` or `*_{PDmap,T1map,T2starmap}.nii.gz` — naming is inconsistent between subjects | Not downloaded (~45 GB for our 9 subjects). Rationale on record: v1 is contrast-agnostic and mask-based, so quantitative maps buy nothing; they are a candidate input only if a learned parser is revisited |

#### B.3 Anatomy and the specimens

| Term | Plain definition | Why it matters HERE |
|---|---|---|
| **GM** (grey matter) | The outer few millimetres of cerebral cortex plus deep nuclei: mostly **cell bodies**, little myelin | One of the two structural feature channels on both sides. In ex-vivo FLASH at 20° GM is **bright**; in serial-sectioning OCT pooled to 0.15 mm GM is also brighter than WM — hence `--oct-wm-bright` default `no` |
| **WM** (white matter) | The interior: **myelinated axon bundles** connecting regions | The other channel. Strongly light-scattering (bright) in raw OCT at native resolution but *darker* than GM in the pooled two-class split used here; dark in ex-vivo FLASH at 20°. The `[P(WM), P(GM)]` pair is the entire structural representation the global search works on |
| **Class polarity** | This project's name for "which of the two intensity classes is WM". Not a biology term — a **protocol** property of the imaging setup | Controlled by `--oct-wm-bright {auto,yes,no}`, whose **default is `no`**, not `auto`. Critical finding: the 0.6 mm global search score **cannot tell the two polarities apart** (I46: 0.741 vs 0.726 — swapping the classes just finds a different, equally good-scoring wrong place, because cortex is a GM sheet wrapping WM), but the **refined** NCC can (0.756 vs 0.730). `auto` runs stages ①② for both polarities and keeps the higher refined NCC. **Trap:** every DANDI run passed `--oct-wm-bright auto` explicitly because `run_subject.sh` line 21 hard-codes it; a successor calling `register.py` directly will silently get single-polarity behaviour, and will also see half the search cost |
| **Cortex / gyrus / sulcus** | The folded sheet of GM on the brain's surface; a *gyrus* is an outward fold, a *sulcus* an inward one | The QC criterion for the large slabs: I38/I56/I62 have no usable quantitative score, and their "correct" verdict rests entirely on **gyrus-by-gyrus** correspondence visible in the overlay figures. Cortical geometry is also why polarity is ambiguous, and why a shift **along** a sulcus is nearly invisible to structural NCC |
| **BA44 / BA45** (Brodmann areas 44 and 45) = **Broca's area** | Two cytoarchitecturally defined patches of left inferior frontal cortex, together the classical speech-production region. Brodmann numbered cortical areas by microscopic cell-layer structure in 1909 | The anatomical target of the entire public dataset — DANDI:000026 is titled "Human brain cell census for BA 44/45", and every Costantini OCT block we register is a BA44/45 block (`sample-BrocaAreaS01`). The manual `label-infrasupra` annotation is drawn inside BA44/45; its non-zero bounding box for I46 is ≈ 15 × 36 × 32 mm, which is why Dice computed with the full OCT class count in the denominator collapses toward zero when the block extends beyond the labelled patch |
| **Infragranular / supragranular ("infrasupra")** | Cortical GM is layered I–VI. Layer IV is the *granular* layer; layers above it are **supragranular** (II/III), below it **infragranular** (V/VI) | The DANDI manual label scheme. `label-infrasupra_dseg.nii.gz` has values `{0,1,2,3}` and `octreg` maps them **0 = background, 1 = WM, 2 = infragranular GM, 3 = supragranular GM**, collapsing 2 ∪ 3 → GM for scoring. `label-infrasupra_seg-wholehemi_dseg.nii.gz` extends the same scheme to the whole hemisphere (14.5 % non-zero for I46) |
| **Brainstem** | The stalk connecting cerebrum to spinal cord — midbrain, pons, medulla. Dense with fibre tracts and nuclei, and with **no cortical folding at all** | Xiangrui's own data is a **brainstem** block, so every intuition built on the Costantini cortical blocks (a GM sheet wrapping WM, the gyral pattern as the matching cue) is inapplicable there. The signal that actually works is **shared fibre texture** between the two modalities. Files: `I58_Brainstem_mus_Slice_full_20um_corr.nii.gz` (13.0 GB OCT) and `I58_brainstem_MRI_cropped_to_OCT.nii.gz` (92 MB MRI) |
| **Blood vessels / vasculature** | The branching tube network perfusing the tissue. Visible in both modalities: **dark blobs/tubes** in ex-vivo FLASH MRI, **dark tubes** in OCT because the lumen does not scatter | The **third feature channel** and the thing that makes sub-millimetre accuracy possible. Structural WM/GM geometry is nearly invariant to a stretch along the block's depth axis; vessels are not. On I46 the vascular stage moved nearest-vessel agreement from 265 µm / 28 % within 150 µm to **167 µm / 47 %**. On the brainstem pair the same channel is **actively harmful** — the OCT "vessels" there are section-seam artefacts — which is why the reported brainstem run is `xiangrui_I58bs_novasc` |

#### B.4 Image processing: features and segmentation

| Term | Plain definition | Why it matters HERE |
|---|---|---|
| **Tissue mask** | A binary volume marking "this voxel is specimen" versus air, fluid or embedding medium | Computed on both sides. MRI: the **histogram peak-walk threshold** (next entry) separating tissue from air and MR bath fluid. OCT: `common.oct_tissue_mask` = Otsu threshold on positive voxels → binary closing (2 iterations) → hole filling → **largest connected component**. The mask is what makes masked NCC meaningful, and it is the documented cause of the agarose problem on the brainstem. **On the MRI side, be precise about which subjects it explains.** The mask-failure signature — a threshold far *below* the volume's own median, a runaway `tissue_fraction`, and `valley_ratio: null` — is present in exactly **I56 (0.9886), I58 (0.5867) and I61 (0.7423)**, and it is the standing explanation for **I61's** wrong result. It is **not** the explanation for **I57**, whose threshold 15.77 sits *above* its median 13.8, whose `tissue_fraction` is 0.209 — the second-lowest in the corpus — and which did find a valley (0.0631): **I57's failure currently has no explanation** `[OPEN]`. The old shorthand "I57 and I61 — bath-heavy MRI, tissue-mask failure" is half wrong. A related trap: because I56's mask calls almost everything tissue, any "label ∩ tissue = 100 %" sanity check is meaningless for I56 — and I56 is currently marked *correct* |
| **Histogram peak-walk tissue threshold** | The shipped MRI foreground rule, `common.histogram_tissue_threshold` (`common.py:214–238`). An ex-vivo whole-hemisphere FLASH histogram is **not** bimodal — air near zero, a large low-but-nonzero bath/fixative mode, then tissue — so a two-class cut puts the bath on whichever side wins. The peak-walk anchors on tissue instead: clip above the **99.5th percentile**; 256-bin histogram smoothed with `uniform_filter1d(size=5)`; `find_peaks(prominence = 0.05·max, distance = 5)`; take the **rightmost** peak as the tissue mode; walk **left** across prominent peaks and cut at the first valley deep enough to count | The single most consequential preprocessing decision after bias flattening, because everything downstream is masked by it: the Otsu statistics, the search's overlap gate, and the block's own template. **Its fallback fails open** — when no deep-enough valley exists it writes `valley_ratio: null` and falls back to `thr = min(p1, 0.5 · multiotsu3[0])` (or `percentile(sub, 10)` if multi-Otsu throws), i.e. it keeps essentially everything and proceeds silently. That is the wrong default for a method whose robustness story is "nothing fails silently", and it is the direct mechanism behind I61, I58 and I56. Full reasoning, the three generations that preceded it, and the two-part v1.1 fix are in chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning (§5.1.6) |
| **`valley_ratio`** | The peak-walk's own diagnostic, written into `work/<SUB>/prep.json` as `mri.valley_ratio`: the depth of the accepted valley relative to the shallower of the two peaks it sits between, `h[valley] / min(h[left_peak], h[tissue_peak])`. It must fall below **0.5** for the cut to be accepted; when no valley qualifies the field is `null` | **The cleanest automatic red flag the pipeline already computes, and it is surfaced nowhere** — not in `result.json`, not in `results_inspection/INDEX.md`, not in any figure. Printing it is one line. Measured values, all nine: I57 **0.0631**, I62 0.0869, **I46 0.1161**, **I38 0.1984**, I48 0.4737 (the worst separation in the set — 0.4737 barely clears the 0.5 gate), and `null` for I55, I56, I58, I61. **I46 and I38 have a valley; do not print them as missing.** `null` is a *warning*, not a verdict: I55 is `null` and correct, because its fallback threshold happened to land in the right place. Values read from `mri.valley_ratio` in each `work/<SUB>/prep.json` on the compute server; the per-subject diagnostic table is chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us |
| **Otsu's method** | An automatic threshold: pick the intensity that splits the histogram into two classes with maximum **between-class variance**. Assumes a bimodal histogram | `octreg`'s entire *training-free* structural representation. `features.otsu_two_class(vol, tissue, wm_bright, smooth_sigma_vox=1.0)` blurs, takes `skimage.filters.threshold_otsu` **over tissue voxels only**, and converts to a **soft** two-class map by `sigmoid((x − thr)/scale)` with `scale = 0.25 · std(tissue values)`. `otsu_two_class_lowmem` is the whole-hemisphere version: local-mean flattening (σ = 10 mm) first, then `zchunk=64` slabs with a `3σ+1` halo. The chosen threshold is recorded in `result.json` as `mri_otsu_thresh` |
| **Slab / depth-attenuation normalization** | Removing the periodic brightness decay of serial-sectioning OCT so the same tissue has the same brightness at every depth | `common.oct_slab_normalize(oct_zyx, tissue_thresh=30.0, window=100, out_dtype)`: per-z-slice tissue median → divide by it → multiply by a running mean of those medians over `window` slices, nominally one section period. Slow trends survive, the sawtooth does not. The `float16` output is gain-scaled so the tissue median lands near 16 000, safely under the `float16` maximum of 65 504. **See B.1 "section period" — the `window=100` justification is wrong by ~3×, though the code still works for I46** |
| **Frangi filter / vesselness** | A multi-scale filter (Frangi 1998) scoring each voxel on how **tube-like** it is, from the eigenvalues of the local **Hessian**. A tube has one small and two large same-sign eigenvalues; the response is the max over scales σ | Our label-free vessel detector, in the **dark-tube** sign convention (λ2, λ3 > 0). `features.frangi_dark_vesselness(vol, sigmas_vox=(1.0,1.5,2.2), alpha=0.5, beta=0.5, gamma=None)`, scale-normalized by σ², closed-form symmetric 3×3 eigenvalues (`sym3x3_eigvals`, deliberately avoiding cuSOLVER). On OCT it runs at **σ = 24, 36, 53, 72, 106 µm** and is thresholded at the **top 1 %** (99th percentile) inside tissue. `frangi_gamma` computes the structureness constant **once for the whole volume** from a strided subsample, so responses are comparable between processing chunks |
| **`frangi_chunked`** | Slab-wise Frangi with a discarded halo | `zchunk=24, overlap=10` in `vascular.py`; the 10-voxel halo is thrown away on write so the response has no seams |
| **Local-darkness / dark-blob map** | "How much darker is this voxel than its local neighbourhood?", computed as `clip(local_median − value, 0, ∞)` and normalized by a high percentile | The **MRI** side of the vascular channel, since vessels are dark in ex-vivo FLASH and a median-based local background is robust to them. `vascular.mri_dark_channel(..., q=99.5, vox_mm=0.15, window_mm=1.35)` — the window is a **physical** 1.35 mm = 9 voxels at 0.15 mm, and above 4·10⁷ voxels the median is computed on a half-resolution grid and upsampled. Preferred over running Frangi on the MRI (`mri_frangi_channel` exists but is not the default). **Critical distinction:** this map is computed in RAM inside `register.py` and **never written to disk**. It is *not* `mri_vessels.npy` — see B.8. Confusing the two would make the vessel evaluation circular |
| **Vessel density** | Binary vessel voxels max/mean-pooled onto the coarse 0.15 mm grid, giving a continuous "how many vessels here" field | Nearest-vessel matching between two *automatic* vessel sets is ambiguous (dense against dense); correlating MRI **darkness** against OCT vessel **density** is a proper similarity. That reasoning is written out in the `vascular.py` module docstring |
| **MIND-SSC** | A hand-crafted modality-invariant descriptor (self-similarity context) encoding local patch structure instead of intensity; standard in multimodal registration | Implemented faithfully in `features.mind_ssc(img, radius=2, dilation=2)` (from the ConvexAdam repo) but **not used by the v1 pipeline** — dead-but-working code, and a ready alternative feature channel |
| **Parser (3D U-Net)** | A trained convolutional segmentation network producing `[bg, WM, infragranular, supragranular]` probability maps | The **ablation** arm: `register.py --features parser --parser-dir …` reads `mri_prob_{wm,gm,tissue}.npy`. Trained on I46 manual labels with synthetic augmentation (`octreg/synth.py`: sawtooth attenuation, bias field, Gamma speckle, anisotropic resolution loss). Conclusion on record: it gives the **same** registration (I46 parser block centre −5.55, 25.91, 8.53 mm vs otsu −5.53, 25.90, 8.51 mm), so v1 ships training-free. Keep it as the "we checked" answer to a reviewer |
| **Pyramid / coarse-to-fine** | Solve at low resolution first, then refine at higher resolution | Search at **0.6 mm**, refine at **0.6 → 0.3 → 0.15 mm**. Crucially, every window, kernel and σ in `octreg` is specified in **physical units (mm/µm)** and converted to voxels per level, which is why one parameter set runs unchanged on 0.12–0.15 mm MRI and 12–35 µm OCT |
| **EDT** (Euclidean distance transform) | For every voxel, the distance to the nearest voxel of a target set | Precomputed once per subject so evaluation is a lookup rather than a nearest-neighbour search: `oct_ves_dist48_own.npy` and `oct_ves_dist48_vesseg.npy` hold distances **in µm** on a ~48 µm grid (35–56 µm voxels depending on subject), written by `prep_subject.py::edt48` |

#### B.5 Geometry: transforms, degrees of freedom, handedness

| Term | Plain definition | Why it matters HERE |
|---|---|---|
| **Affine transform** | `x → A·x + b` with `A` any invertible 3×3: translation, rotation, anisotropic scale and shear. 12 degrees of freedom. Straight lines stay straight, parallel lines stay parallel | **The output of this project.** `T_oct2mri.npy` is a 4×4 homogeneous matrix taking **OCT world coordinates (mm) → MRI world coordinates (mm)**, also written as `T_oct2mri.lta`. An intermediate `T_oct2mri_structural.npy`, before the vascular stage, is saved for QC |
| **Rigid** | Rotation + translation only, 6 DOF. Preserves all distances | Stage ③'s first pass, `Refiner.refine(dof="rigid")` — the correct model for a solid object that only moved |
| **Similarity** | Rigid + one **isotropic** scale, 7 DOF | Stage ③'s second pass. Absorbs global shrinkage and voxel-size error without letting the block distort |
| **Shear** | The off-diagonal part of `A` that turns a rectangle into a parallelogram: angles change, parallelism survives | Parameterized as a **unit-diagonal upper-triangular** 3×3 with exactly three free numbers `Sh[0,1], Sh[0,2], Sh[1,2]`, obtained by QR as `A = R · Shear · diag(exp(ls)) · diag(1,1,±1)`. Constrained by `--sh-clamp` (default **0.15**), with log-scales constrained by `--ls-clamp` (default **0.15**) and an L2 penalty `--reg` (default **2.0**) — this is what "scale prior" means in the README |
| **Degrees of freedom (DOF)** | How many independent numbers the transform has: rigid 6 < similarity 7 < affine 12 < non-rigid (thousands) | `Refiner.refine(dof=…)` accepts `"rigid"`, `"similarity"` or `"affine"`; the pipeline climbs that ladder rather than optimizing 12 parameters from a cold start |
| **SO(3)** | The group of 3D rotations: 3×3 matrices with `RᵀR = I` **and `det R = +1`** (proper rotations, no reflection). A 3-dimensional curved space, so "sample all rotations" means sampling a manifold, not a box | The global search enumerates **`--n-rot 8000` rotations sampled uniformly on SO(3)** via random unit quaternions (`common.random_rotations`). Distances between candidate poses use the **geodesic** angle on SO(3) (`common.rotation_geodesic_deg`), and candidate de-duplication uses `min_sep_mm=3.0, min_sep_deg=10.0` |
| **Rotation vector (rotvec) / axis-angle** | A rotation encoded as a 3-vector whose direction is the axis and whose length is the angle. Three numbers, no constraints — ideal for gradient descent | `common.rotvec_to_matrix` / `matrix_to_rotvec` (Rodrigues). Refinement optimizes `(r, t, ls, sh)` with Adam, `lr_rot=0.02`, `lr_t=0.3`, `iters=200` per level |
| **Polar decomposition** | Splitting `A` into the **closest rotation** times a symmetric stretch | `common.polar_rotation(A)` — the fallback when QR yields an improper (det < 0) factor in `params_from_matrix` |
| **Handedness / chirality** | Whether a coordinate frame is right- or left-handed. Numerically, the **sign of `det(A)`**; a negative determinant means the transform includes a **reflection**, which no physical motion can produce | **A first-class unknown in this project, not a bug.** A microscopy stack's array axes may correspond to the physical specimen in either handedness depending on how the sample was mounted and how the file was written. If you forbid mirroring, roughly half the subjects can never be solved |
| **Mirroring** | Composing with `diag(1,1,−1)` to flip handedness | The search scores **both** the proper rotations and their reflections `R·diag(1,1,−1)`, so `mirror=True` doubles the orientation set to **16 000**; `register.py --no-mirror` disables it. Empirically **the answer differs per subject** and every correct run auto-detected it: mirrored = I38, I46, I48, I56, I58, I62 (**6 of 9**); not mirrored = I55, I57, I61, and both brainstem runs. Note that `common.rotation_geodesic_deg` refuses to compare rotations of different handedness — they are "not comparable" |
| **Non-rigid / deformable registration** | A transform with a per-voxel or per-control-point displacement, able to bend and stretch locally | Implemented as an **ablation only**. `octreg/nonrigid.py::nonrigid_refine` optimizes a free-form displacement on a **(5,8,8) control grid**, trilinearly interpolated, with the same multi-channel masked NCC plus first-difference smoothness (`lam_smooth=5.0`) and magnitude (`lam_mag=0.5`) penalties, 300 iterations, Adam lr 0.05, factors (2,1). Measured gain on I46: **Dice +0.015, vessels +0.01** — judged not worth the complexity, so **v1 ships affine-only** |
| **SVF** (Stationary Velocity Field) | Represent a deformation as a constant-in-time **velocity** field and take its flow (exponential map, usually scaling-and-squaring). Guarantees invertibility | The representation **Costantini et al. used** for their MRI→OCT deformation ("affine + invertible SVF"), and a recurring proposal in the sibling LSFM project. `octreg` uses a plain displacement grid, **not** an SVF — if a reviewer asks about topology guarantees, that is the honest gap |
| **Diffeomorphism** | A deformation that is smooth, invertible, with a smooth inverse: it cannot fold tissue onto itself or tear it. The Jacobian determinant stays positive everywhere | The field's default expectation for deformable registration ("TransMorph, LapIRN, all recent SOTA report on it. Reviewers will ask" — Slack, 2026-05-17). The sibling project adopted it; `octreg` does not claim it. If any future version does, it must report **Jacobian determinant / folding rate** |
| **LDDMM** | Large Deformation Diffeomorphic Metric Mapping — the classical, computationally heavy framework for diffeomorphic registration via time-varying velocity fields | Referenced in the literature review as the method class of Tward et al. 2020 (damaged/multi-stain histology → MRI). Not implemented here |
| **TPS** (Thin-Plate Spline) | An interpolating deformation driven by a sparse set of control points, minimizing bending energy | Sibling-project method only (VoxelMorph-TPS experiments). Not in `octreg`. Note the open cross-project question about TPS control-point order (YX) versus spatial-transformer order (XY) `[OPEN]` |
| **World / voxel coordinates, affine header** | A voxel index `(i,j,k)` times the 4×4 header matrix gives a physical position in mm. Two volumes are "in the same space" when their headers map to the same physical frame | The MRI side has a trustworthy world frame from NIfTI. **The OCT side does not** — it gets one synthetically from `common.layout_affine(shape, spacing, layout)` with `--oct-layout` (default `SPR`, array axes mapped to RAS letters). That is safe *because* the global search covers all orientations anyway. `world_bbox_to_voxel` converts an mm bounding box to indices for `--crop-centre` |
| **Axis codes (RAS / ASL / ILP …)** | Three letters saying which anatomical direction each array axis increases toward: R = right, A = anterior, S = superior, and their opposites L/P/I | **The most common silent bug in this dataset.** Label volumes do not share the MRI's axis order — `seg-wholehemi` is always stored `R,A,S` while the EPIC MRIs are `I,L,P` or `A,S,L`. `prep_subject.py::map_labels_to_grid` resolves this from the affines; **never index a label array directly.** The resolution is currently **wrong for the 0.12 mm subjects**: the affine pairs the label's 640-voxel axis to a 1400-voxel MRI axis, only 36–40 % of the MRI grid ever receives a label lookup, and the whole-hemisphere labels lose 31.7–41.6 % of their voxels. I46 and I55 (both 0.15 mm) are exactly lossless `[UNVERIFIED]` — recorded by an earlier pass and not re-checked here |

#### B.6 Similarity measures — what actually drives the alignment

| Term | Plain definition | Why it matters HERE |
|---|---|---|
| **Cross-correlation** | Sum of the products of two overlapping images as a function of shift; large where they look alike | The raw quantity the FFT search computes |
| **NCC** (Normalized Cross-Correlation) | Cross-correlation after subtracting means and dividing by standard deviations: `cov(a,b)/√(var a · var b)`, in `[−1, 1]`. **Invariant to any linear rescaling of either image's intensities** | The one similarity used everywhere in `octreg` — global search, structural refinement, vascular refinement and the non-rigid ablation. Intensity-scale invariance is what makes it usable when the two images have arbitrary units. **Never turn `refine.final_ncc` into an acceptance threshold.** Its absolute value does not separate right from wrong across subjects: **I61 scores 0.5020 and I57 0.5121 and both are wrong, while I62 scores 0.2842 and is correct.** A high NCC on a homogeneous region of bath fluid is exactly what a failed run looks like. If a document quotes a "good result means final NCC above *x*" rule, it is wrong and this counterexample is why |
| **Masked NCC** | NCC computed only over a weighted subset of voxels (here the OCT tissue mask), with the means and variances computed **inside** the mask | `refine.masked_ncc(a, b, w, eps=1e-6, chan_w)`: `a, b` are `[C,N]`, `w` are per-point weights, and it returns a channel-weighted mean of per-channel NCCs. Without masking, a pose that parks the block over empty background scores well by matching nothing to nothing |
| **Overlap-normalized / Padfield-style masked NCC** | Padfield's formulation lets you compute masked NCC for **all** translations at once with FFTs, normalizing each shift by the actual overlapping mask area | Named explicitly in `search.py`'s docstring. Two guards come with it: `--min-overlap` (default **0.85**) rejects poses where too little OCT tissue lands on MRI tissue, and a **variance floor** of 0.02 × the MRI in-tissue variance per channel prevents near-constant windows from producing huge scores through FFT round-off |
| **Adaptive overlap gate** | The effective minimum-overlap threshold, lowered automatically when the MRI region is smaller than the OCT block | Requested 0.85 by default, but reduced toward a hard **floor of 0.15** when the MRI tissue volume is small relative to the OCT block. Two things to carry: the floor exists (several documents drop it), and the gate **never binds on DANDI** — it binds only on the brainstem pair, where the agarose-inflated OCT mask pushes it to 0.369. `work/runs/I46_otsu/result.json` has `overlap_gate: null` because the gate did not exist when I46 was run. The exact formula, its derivation and the per-run values are stated once in chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning (§5.2) |
| **FFT cross-correlation** | Correlation is a convolution, so by the convolution theorem it is a pointwise multiply in the Fourier domain: **all translations** cost one forward FFT, one multiply and one inverse FFT instead of one pass per shift | The only reason a prior-free whole-hemisphere search is affordable at all. Implementation detail: the MRI grid is **zero-padded by half a template on every side** (`pad = n//2 + 1`, features and tissue both zero) so a block hanging over the edge of a crop is still scored, and the overlap test — not the padding — decides acceptability. **On timing, do not repeat the "150 s" figure carelessly.** The honest sentence, every part verified: an exhaustive 16 000-orientation search over all translations costs **45 s** on a 0.08 mm brainstem crop and **299 s** on a 0.15 mm whole hemisphere with the label-free Otsu features (**154 s** with parser-probability features); the shipped wrapper runs it **once per class polarity**, so budget **598 s** of search for a whole hemisphere. Whole-corpus single-branch range **44.8 s – 1 010.3 s**; the per-branch timing table is in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means. The widely quoted 153.4 / 153.7 s is a real full-search measurement but comes from `run_demo_i46.py --features mixed`, whose MRI channels are the trained U-Net parser's probabilities — quoting it in a passage about the label-free path attributes a parser-assisted runtime to the training-free pipeline. The 150 s in the prose docs is a rounding of that same 153.7 s |
| **Multi-channel / weighted NCC** | Compute NCC per feature channel and take a weighted mean | Structural stage: channels `[P(WM), P(GM)]` with equal weight. Vascular stage: `[P(WM), P(GM), vessel]` with weights **(1, 1, 2)** — `--vascular-w` default `2.0` |
| **LCC** (Local Cross-Correlation) | NCC computed in a sliding local window and averaged rather than once globally. Robust to slowly varying intensity differences; effectively the standard loss for cross-modal deformable registration | **Not implemented in `octreg`** — we use global masked NCC plus explicit bias-field flattening, which addresses the same problem differently. It matters because it is part of **Costantini's own loss** (LCC + grey-matter soft Dice + vessel mean Euclidean distance) and is named in `WORKSPACE_STATE.md` as the metric a planned reproduction would lean on. If asked "why not LCC", that is the context |
| **Soft Dice (as a loss)** | Dice overlap made differentiable by using probabilities instead of hard labels | Part of Costantini's loss; **not** used by `octreg`, which is label-free by construction. Dice appears here only as an evaluation number |
| **Restarts / perturbed restarts** | Re-run the optimizer from randomly jittered starting poses and check they converge to the same answer — a cheap, honest convergence-basin test | `--n-restarts` default **12**, `--seed` default `0`; perturbations measured from the JSONs are 6.0–26.5° and 3.2–6.6 mm, with the code comment "5-30 deg, <=5 mm". The vascular stage runs a separate 8 restarts counted within 0.3 mm corner-mean. Reported as e.g. "10/12". This is the **only** stability evidence available for subjects with no usable labels. The verified counts, all out of 12: **I38 12, I46 9, I48 11, I55 9, I56 10, I57 10, I58 12, I61 12, I62 11, xiangrui_I58bs 10, xiangrui_I58bs_novasc 10**. Several documents claim I57 was 12/12 — it was **10/12**, with corner-mean min/median/max 0.381 / 0.388 / 0.536 mm, two restarts over the 0.5 mm gate. The uncomfortable observation that "the tightest-converging runs are the wrong ones" survives on **I58 and I61 (both 12/12)** only |
| **Corner-mean displacement** | The mean displacement of the block's 8 corners between two candidate transforms, in mm — a single interpretable number for "how different are these two poses" | `evaluate.transform_diff(..., extent_mm: float = 7.0)` uses a standardised **7 mm** lever arm so restart scatter is comparable across subjects with very different block sizes |

#### B.7 Evaluation metrics

Two things to know before reading any number in this project:

1. **In `octreg`, annotations are used only to score, never to register.** That is the central methodological claim.
2. **`octreg` does not report TRE, HD95, PSNR or SSIM.** Those belong to the sibling LSFM project or to the literature. They are defined here because they appear all over the project's documents and you will be asked about them.

| Metric | Plain definition | Why it matters HERE |
|---|---|---|
| **Dice / DSC** (Dice similarity coefficient) | Overlap of two binary sets, `2·card(A∩B) / (card A + card B)`, from 0 (disjoint) to 1 (identical) | `evaluate.gm_wm_overlap` transforms every OCT tissue voxel into MRI voxel space, looks up the manual label, collapses `{2,3}→GM`, and computes `dice_WM`, `dice_GM`, `frac_on_mri_labels` and a 3×3 confusion matrix. **Dice is computed with the full OCT class count in the denominator**, so it collapses toward 0 when label coverage is low — which is why I62 reports 0.0 (its `labels4` is the tiny BA-only label, 0.23 % of the volume, because I62 has no whole-hemisphere label on DANDI at all). Verified headline values: **I46 0.803 / 0.825**, **I55 0.921 / 0.930**. **Caveat you must carry:** the label→MRI axis pairing is wrong for every 0.12 mm subject, so **every Dice for I38 / I48 / I56 / I57 / I58 / I61 is computed against a corrupted label volume** `[UNVERIFIED]` — recorded by an earlier pass and not re-checked here. Independent of that, only 6.56 % of I57's BA labels, 37.3 % of I62's, 62.7 % of I48's whole-hemi labels land on MRI tissue at all. **Keep two failure modes apart:** the *label-coverage* explanation — score collapses because the labelled patch is far smaller than the block — belongs to I62 and the other large slabs. **I48 does not have it.** Its Dice is simply untrustworthy in both directions, and its "uncertain" verdict comes from the 0.0013 search-score margin, not from any artefact of the labels |
| **`f150`** (project-internal) | The fraction of manually annotated MRI vessel points that, after transformation into OCT space, land within **150 µm** of the nearest automatically detected OCT vessel | The project's headline accuracy number, because 150 µm is roughly the annotation's own precision. I46 `vessels_vesseg`: 0.28 → **0.473** (median 265 → 167 µm) against a random-shift control of ~350 µm median; `vessels_own`: 0.44 → 0.56 (173 → 123 µm, control 215 → 212) |
| **Nearest-vessel distance** | Median and percentile distance from transformed manual MRI vessel points to the nearest OCT vessel, in µm, with a **random-shift control** computed from the same points | `evaluate.vessel_distance_stats`. The control — the same points translated by a single uniform random offset of ±3.0 mm per axis, 30 draws, `seed=0` — is what turns "167 µm" from a number into evidence |
| **Oracle** | An upper bound obtained by fitting the transform **directly to the manual annotations**, something the method is forbidden to do. Tells you how much of the remaining error is method error versus annotation noise | The I46 oracle affine showed ~1.4 mm corner residual remaining after the structural stage, mostly a **1.14–1.18 stretch along the OCT depth axis**, which the vascular channel recovers (to 0.29 mm corner error). **The metric is now saturated:** `vessels_vesseg` f150 = **0.473** against a held-out cross-validated oracle ceiling of **0.416 ± 0.041** (197.1 ± 13.5 µm) — it can no longer rank an improvement. Chance level is 0.117 |
| **TRE** (Target Registration Error) | The distance in mm between corresponding **landmark points** after registration. The field's standard accuracy metric because it is interpretable and independent of the similarity being optimized | **`octreg` cannot compute it** — there are no landmark correspondences in either dataset. The vessel-distance / `f150` pair is the stand-in. Quoted from the literature for calibration: ReMIND2Reg mean TRE ≈ 2.385 ± 0.397 mm for keypoint methods versus 1.903 mm for the best dense method. The literature review's conclusion — that **no public human-brain OCT-block → whole-hemisphere benchmark with independent TRE annotation exists** — is the project's novelty claim. The proposed fix for our own unlabelled data is ~20 matched anatomical points per pair, roughly 30 min of annotation, reported as TRE; this has **not yet been requested of the PI** `[OPEN]` |
| **HD95** (95th-percentile Hausdorff distance) | Hausdorff distance is the worst-case distance between two surfaces; the 95th percentile instead of the max makes it robust to a few outlier voxels. Reported in mm, lower is better. Complements Dice, which is blind to thin-structure boundary errors | **Sibling-project metric.** In the 2026-08-23 meeting it was the only failing item: **0.1227 → 12.3535**, ~89× worse, suspected on the spot to be a decimal-point error (possibly 0.1235), still unresolved `[OPEN]` |
| **PSNR** (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio) | `10·log10(peak² / MSE)` in dB — a log-scaled reconstruction-error measure, higher is better | **Sibling-project metric** for LSFM super-resolution on held-out xy slice pairs, reported 20.5 → 43.7 dB. Two self-flagged caveats on record: PSNR depends on the intensity-normalization convention, and MAE/RMSE were deliberately dropped as redundant since PSNR already encodes MSE |
| **SSIM** (Structural Similarity Index) | A perceptual similarity in `[0,1]` combining local luminance, contrast and structure agreement; catches structural degradation PSNR misses | **Sibling-project metric**, same held-out pairs, motivated explicitly by cortical layer boundaries. Reported "> 0.807" |
| **Evaluation leakage** | Reporting a metric on the same data the model was fitted to, so the number reflects fitting rather than generalization | Raised unprompted by Lavanya on 08-23 about her NCC ≈ 0.99, and the 08-23 minutes generalize it explicitly to this project: **our own metrics must state which data participated in fitting and which only in scoring.** In `octreg` the natural exposure is the oracle and the vessel channel — the oracle affine is fitted to the very vessels being scored, which is why the cross-validated held-out ceiling (0.416 ± 0.041) is the number that matters |
| **Jacobian determinant / folding rate** | The local volume-change factor of a deformation field; if it goes ≤ 0 the transform has folded tissue onto itself. The standard evidence that a claimed diffeomorphism really is one | Not currently reported anywhere. Flagged as required-if-claimed in the sibling project's risk register |
| **Ceiling / annotation ceiling** | The best score any method could get, given that the reference annotation is itself imprecise | Used constantly in this project's write-ups. **Do not read a stalled metric as a stalled method without checking the ceiling first** — on I46, f150 has already passed the held-out oracle ceiling |

#### B.8 File formats, containers, infrastructure and software

| Term | Plain definition | Why it matters HERE |
|---|---|---|
| **NIfTI** (`.nii`, `.nii.gz`) | The standard neuroimaging volume format: a fixed header (dimensions, dtype, and the `sform`/`qform` 4×4 voxel→world matrices in mm) followed by raw voxels, optionally gzipped | The MRI format throughout, and the format of Xiangrui's OCT. Written by `common.save_nifti(arr, affine, path)`, which sets `xyzt_units("mm")` and both `qform` and `sform` with `code=1`. Read with `nibabel` (5.3.2 on both the Mac and AutoDL). The outputs `mri_region.nii.gz` and `oct_in_mri_region.nii.gz` are deliberately written **on the same grid** so a viewer can cross-fade them |
| **MGZ / MGH** (`.mgz`) | FreeSurfer's own volume format, same role as NIfTI | Appears only in the Costantini authors' code (`flash20.mgz`, `mri.crop.mgz`). Relevant because the authors' published `affine.lta` is defined in the FreeSurfer `flash20.mgz` frame, not the DANDI NIfTI frame |
| **OME-TIFF** (`.ome.tiff`) | A TIFF carrying an **OME-XML** metadata block describing dimensions, physical pixel sizes and channels. A single flat file whose pages can be memory-mapped if uncompressed | The Costantini OCT format (92 assets, 76.0 GB across the dandiset). Read via `tifffile.memmap()` with a fallback to `tifffile.imread()`. **Its embedded physical size is often unusable**: for I46 the OME-XML says `PhysicalSize = 1.0 "pixel"` and `XResolution = 0`, so spacing must come from the BIDS sidecar or `--oct-spacing-um`. Six of our nine volumes present axes `TYX` (slices as *timepoints*, `SizeZ=1`) and three `ZYX` — `tifffile.series[0]` returns the right 3D array either way, but anything keying off `SizeZ` will read 1. Three of the nine (I48, I56, I57) are plain **ImageJ** TIFFs, not OME at all |
| **OME-ZARR** (`.ome.zarr`) | Not a file but a **directory tree of compressed chunks** plus JSON metadata, designed for cloud and partial access and multi-resolution pyramids of terabyte-scale data | The format of everything in DANDI:000026 we deliberately did **not** download: 1,003 assets / 28.07 TB, including the LSFM data, the Hip-CT volumes, and the single raw un-stitched OCT tile set `sub-I48_..._sample-BrocaAreaS23_acq-Raw_OCT.ome.zarr` (50.40 GiB — note it is block S23, not the S01 we hold, so it is not the raw form of any volume we have). Practical consequence: **neither the Mac nor AutoDL has `zarr` or `dask` installed**, so any future OME-ZARR work needs an install first |
| **BIDS** (Brain Imaging Data Structure) | A filesystem-and-naming convention: `sub-<id>/ses-<session>/<modality>/sub-…_key-value_suffix.ext`, with a JSON **sidecar** of metadata next to each data file | The organizing scheme of DANDI:000026. Every acquisition parameter you need (`FlipAngle`, `RepetitionTime`, OCT `PixelSize`) lives in a sidecar, not in the image header. `dataset_description.json` claims BIDSVersion `1.0` at top level and `1.5.0` inside the derivatives |
| **Sidecar** | The `.json` file paired with a data file, holding its metadata | Both the source of truth and a source of bugs. **I46's OCT sidecar says `PixelSize [12,12,12]` µm isotropic**, while every other subject's says `30×30×35` or `12×12×14` µm — depth = in-plane × 7/6 = 1.1667 — and I46's OME-XML carries no in-file spacing at all to check it against. Our own vascular stage independently recovered a depth stretch of **1.219** for I46. Those are two of the four independent lines that say **I46's sidecar omits the larger depth spacing**; the other two come from the authors' own published affine and from an oracle affine fitted to manual labels and vessels, and all four are laid out in chapter 4, The data (§4.5). A fifth line once circulated — the measured 33-slice section period against a nominal 500 µm vibratome cut — and it has been **withdrawn**; see B.1 above. Note the key order is `PixelSize = [x, y, z]` and `prep_subject.py` reverses it to `(z,y,x)` at line 118 — do not copy the sidecar list into a z-first slot. Also: I48's sidecar was never downloaded at all, and the label sidecars' `Source` field names the MRI the labels were drawn on, which **does not always match the flip we registered against** (mismatches for I48, I57, I58) |
| **`dseg`** | BIDS suffix for a **discrete segmentation**, i.e. an integer label volume | `sub-XX_ses-MRI_space-EPIC_label-{infrasupra,vessels,infrasupra_seg-wholehemi}_dseg.nii.gz`. Because they are integers, **never interpolate them linearly** — always nearest-neighbour (the sibling project logged exactly this bug) |
| **`.lta`** | FreeSurfer's **Linear Transform Array**: a small human-readable text file holding a 4×4 matrix plus a type code saying which spaces it maps between | `common.lta_text(M, src_desc, dst_desc)` writes `type = 1  # LINEAR_RAS_TO_RAS`, `nxforms = 1`, `mean`, `sigma`, `1 4 4`, the four rows, and `# src:` / `# dst:` comments. Emitted as `T_oct2mri.lta` alongside the `.npy` so FreeSurfer tools (`mri_vol2vol`, `freeview`) can consume the result directly |
| **`.npy`** | NumPy's raw array format: a small header plus contiguous bytes, memory-mappable | The internal cache format for everything under `--work`: `mri.npy`, `mri_tissue.npy`, `oct150.npy`, `octv.npy`, `labels4.npy`, `T_oct2mri.npy` |
| **`mri_vessels.npy`** | One specific cache file, worth its own entry because it has been described wrongly | It is the **manual MRI vessel label** — loaded from `--mri-vessels …label-vessels_dseg.nii.gz`, thresholded `> 0`, mapped to the MRI grid, and used for **evaluation only**. It is *not* a local-median dark-blob map; that map is `vascular.mri_dark_channel`, computed in RAM inside `register.py` and never written to disk. The distinction matters because the wrong version would make the vessel evaluation circular — scoring the registration against the very channel that drove it |
| **mmap / memory-mapping** | Point the process's address space at a file on disk and let the OS page in only the parts you actually read: you "open" a 13 GB volume instantly and use ~0 RAM until you index into it | Load-bearing for whole-hemisphere volumes. `np.load(path, mmap_mode="r")` is used for `mri.npy`, `mri_tissue.npy`, `labels4.npy` and the parser probability maps in `register.py`; `tifffile.memmap()` gives zero-copy access to uncompressed OME-TIFF. The pattern is always **mmap → slice the region → `np.asarray(...)` to materialize just that block** |
| **`float16` (half precision)** | 16-bit floats: half the memory of `float32`, ~3 decimal digits of precision, and a **maximum representable value of 65 504** | The storage dtype for the big OCT arrays (`octv.npy`, the Frangi response buffer) and for the MRI feature maps, which stay on the **CPU** in float16 while only pooled levels and block-sized crops move to the GPU. The overflow limit is handled explicitly — `oct_slab_normalize` gain-scales so the tissue median sits near 16 000 and caps bright outliers |
| **Presigned URL** | A time-limited signed download link, here from DANDI's S3 backend, expiring after **6 hours** | Why the download tooling looks the way it does: `data/restart_dl.sh` (aria2) plus `data/dl_watchdog.sh`, which periodically restarts the transfer as links expire. The full 8-subject pull finished 2026-08-20 14:11:58 CST with zero `.aria2`/`.part` remnants |
| **Checksum (SHA-256 / MD5)** | A hash used to prove a file arrived intact | The transfer of Xiangrui's 13 GB pair streams `tar` xulab → Mac → AutoDL with no local copy and verifies with `sha256sum -c` on the destination. Code-copy authority between machines was established with MD5. `download_costantini.sh` pins a sha256 for each of its 16 assets; `manifest_multisub.txt` has none |
| **`aria2`** | A multi-connection command-line downloader | Used for the DANDI pull (`prefetch_dandi_aria2.sh`, `data/restart_dl.sh`) because presigned URLs expire and single-stream HTTP was too slow |
| **conda env `octmri`** | The Python environment on AutoDL where everything runs | `conda activate octmri`, interpreter `/root/miniconda3/envs/octmri/bin/python`. Present: `torch` (CUDA), `numpy`, `scipy`, `skimage`, `nibabel`, `tifffile`. **Absent by design:** `sklearn`, `pandas`, `zarr`, `dask`, `h5py`, `numcodecs`, `ants`/`antspyx`, `cupy`, `numba`, `joblib`, `cv2`, `dandi` |
| **RTX 4090 / 24 GB** | The single consumer GPU the project runs on: 24 564 MiB, driver 595.71.05 | The binding constraint behind every chunking constant in the code (`zchunk=64` for Otsu, `zchunk=24, overlap=10` for Frangi, a ~30 M-voxel GPU slab budget in `prep_subject.py`). **Hard operational rule: one heavy job at a time.** End-to-end cost per DANDI subject is **1 124.7 – 7 864.1 s = 18.7 – 131.1 min**, not the "15–40 min" several documents claim — only 4 of 9 runs fall inside that range. And the expensive stage is **not** the search: on I38 the vascular stage is 5 696.8 s of 7 864.1 s (72 %), on the brainstem pair 4 778.4 s of 5 244.0 s (91 %) and it made the result worse; search is 8–38 % of wall clock |
| **Freeview** | FreeSurfer's volume viewer: loads NIfTI/MGZ, overlays volumes with adjustable opacity, shows three orthogonal planes | **The PI's preferred verification tool** — he repeatedly asks for the *file path on the server* so he can open it himself, not for screenshots or videos. That is why `octreg` writes `mri_region.nii.gz` + `oct_in_mri_region.nii.gz` on a common grid, and why deliverables must be server-resident openable NIfTI pairs. **There is no NIfTI viewer installed on this Mac**, so the QC PNGs are the only fast local path |
| **ITK-SNAP / 3D Slicer / FSLeyes** | Other free volume viewers; ITK-SNAP is the usual alternative to Freeview and better for drawing labels | Named as alternatives in the meeting document. All absent from this Mac |
| **QC figure** | "Quality Control" overlay image — the thing a human actually looks at to decide whether a registration is right | `scripts/viz_result.py` writes `qc_vessels.png`: 3 rows = OCT depth slices at **20 % / 50 % / 80 %** of block depth; columns = (left) raw OCT + **green** own-Frangi vessel-density contour at `> 0.35` + **cyan** OCT WM/GM class boundary; (middle) MRI resampled into OCT space via the **structural** transform with the same overlays plus **yellow** manual MRI vessels and a **white** block outline; (right) the same via the **final** transform. **Read the suptitle first** — it carries `search top1/top2`, `mirror`, `stretch ijk` |
| **Checkerboard** | A QC display tiling alternating squares from the two registered images; if the alignment is right, anatomical boundaries continue straight across every tile edge | The primary visual evidence for the large slabs and for the brainstem, where the verdict is "boundaries continuing across tiles with a visible but bounded offset" |
| **Canny edges** | A classic edge detector, used to draw one image's outlines on top of the other | The panel-E convention in the figure system |
| **nitorch** | The PyTorch-based imaging library the Costantini authors' code depends on (a submodule of `biccn-broca-I46`) | Installed on xulab under `/shared/scratch/0/home/v_yuntian_yang/registration/code/costantini/`; needed only to run or read the authors' original pipeline |
| **SmartInterpol** | <https://github.com/aleatzeni/SmartInterpol> — the tool the DANDI authors used to interpolate manual labels drawn on every 10th slice into a full volume, followed by manual touch-up | Explains the labels' precision: they are **not** slice-exact everywhere, which sets the annotation ceiling our saturated `f150` is bumping against |
| **DANDI Archive** | `dandiarchive.org`, an NIH-funded public repository for neurophysiology and neuroimaging data — BIDS-organized, S3-backed, with a REST API and presigned download URLs. Datasets are called **dandisets** and cited as `DANDI:NNNNNN` | Our only public data source. Note our dandiset is version **`draft`**, which is mutable — there is no published version tag to pin, so reproducibility rests on our own `asset_uuid` + sha256 manifest |

#### B.9 Project-internal tokens you will meet in filenames, flags and logs

| Token | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `octreg` | The Python package and the name of the method/codebase. `octreg/octreg/` is the library, `octreg/scripts/` the entry points |
| `--work <dir>` | The per-subject cache directory produced by `prep_subject.py` (`mri.npy`, `oct150.npy`, `prep.json`, …), consumed by `register.py` |
| `--out <dir>` | The per-run output directory (`T_oct2mri.npy/.lta`, `result.json`, `qc_*.png`, the overlay NIfTIs) |
| `oct150` | The OCT block pooled to the registration resolution, **0.15 mm** (`--target-mm` default) |
| `octv` | The OCT at the "**vessel level**": native if ≥ 24 µm, else pooled to ~24 µm (`--vessel-level-um` default `24.0`). Stored `float16` |
| `*_otsu` / `*_parser` | Run-name suffix for `--features otsu` (the shipped default) versus the U-Net ablation |
| `mixed` | A third feature mode that exists **only** in `run_demo_i46.py` (MRI parser probabilities + OCT intensity-derived WM/GM). `register.py` accepts only `{otsu, parser}` and `features.build_features` raises `ValueError` on `mixed`. This is the configuration behind the widely quoted 153.7 s search time |
| `_novasc` | A run with `--vascular off`. The brainstem result **to report** is `work/runs/xiangrui_I58bs_novasc`, because on that pair the vascular channel latches onto section seams instead of vessels |
| `stretch ijk` | The per-axis scale factors of the recovered affine, printed in the QC suptitle and stored in `result.json` as `final_transform.stretch_ijk`, defined as `‖T[:3,:3] · R_axes[:,q]‖`. **Index 0 is the OCT depth / serial-sectioning axis.** `final_transform.column_scales` is a *different* ordering — do not confuse them. I46's depth value ≈ **1.219** is the headline finding; I55's depth value is **0.913** (its 1.097 is the in-plane j axis, and any document quoting "I55 needs only a 1.10 depth stretch" has read the wrong index). **Two cautions before you use these as evidence.** (a) I55 is *not* a clean reverse control: its recovered depth-to-in-plane anisotropy is **0.8570**, which is `6/7 = 0.857143` to four decimal places — exactly the inverse of the 7/6 that I46 is supposed to be missing, on the one subject whose sidecar is corroborated twice inside its own file. Say so every time I55 is offered as a null result. (b) I38's **structural** depth stretch of **0.861** is not a measurement at all: it is the refiner's clamp bound `exp(−0.15) = 0.860708`, i.e. clamp-saturated, so every structural metric for I38 describes the constraint rather than the optimiser's answer. The wider-clamped vascular stage promptly moved it to 0.808. Both points are developed in chapter 4, The data (§4.5.3) |
| `search top1 / top2` | The best and second-best global-search scores. Their **gap** is the de-facto confidence measure: I48's 0.2571 vs 0.2558 (margin 0.0013) is why it is marked "uncertain", and a reject gate built on this gap is a roadmap item |
| `polarity_trials.{False,True}` | The two `result.json` sub-objects holding the losing and winning polarity branches when `--oct-wm-bright auto` was used |
| `overlap_gate` | `{requested, effective}` in `result.json`. `null` on `I46_otsu` because the adaptive gate did not exist when that run was made |
| `INDEX.md` | `results_inspection/<run>/…/INDEX.md` on AutoDL — the per-run verdict table (5 correct / 1 uncertain / 3 wrong). **One known error in it:** it gives I56's block size as "33×49×44 mm"; the block is **9.8 × 45.2 × 43.0 mm** — the first axis is wrong by about 3×. Attach that correction whenever you quote the file |
| `run_subject.sh` / `run_xiangrui.sh` / `run_all.sh` | Server-only orchestration wrappers; `run_subject.sh` line 21 is where `--oct-wm-bright auto` is hard-coded and `run_all.sh` line 5 is the per-subject flip-file driver list. Remember: **21 scripts exist only on AutoDL** |
| `T0` | The **v0 label-free structural baseline transform**, `work/runs/crop_mixed_real/T_oct2mri.npy` on I46, `stretch_ijk = [1.032, 1.004, 0.971]`. It is the common starting pose and the reference row of **every** ablation table in this document — the vessel-channel sweep, the scale probe, the oracle comparison, the scrambling controls and the distillation rounds all report "moved *x* mm vs T0". Its own scores are vessel median **276.5 µm / f150 0.254**, Dice 0.805 / 0.837. When a table has a T0 row, that row is "structure only, before the vascular stage" |
| `zoff0` / `zoff66` | The two candidate z-alignments between DANDI's OCT vessel segmentation and the OCT stack itself. For I46, `ves_seg.tif` has **561** z-slices against the volume's **627**, so the segmentation could be aligned at the start of the stack (`zoff0`) or offset by the 66-slice difference (`zoff66`) — a 0.79 mm ambiguity the data cannot settle by itself. `prep_subject.py` assumes `zoff0`. **After** the vascular stage `zoff0` wins clearly (166.8 µm / f150 0.469 against 301.9 µm / 0.187); **before** it the structural rows invert the answer (276 vs 245 µm), so the offset is currently decided by the very metric the vascular stage optimises. Verified on I46 only |
| `v1.1` | The **next version of the method**, and in this document a defined milestone rather than a vague future: v1.1 is the release that fixes **foreground separation** — the bath-fluid MRI mask (I56, I58, I61), the agarose specimen mask on the brainstem OCT, and an artefact-resistant fine channel — treated as one problem because they have one root cause. Its scope is fixed, its files to change are named, and none of it has been started beyond a prototype (`scripts/test_texture_mask.py`). See chapter 11, What to do next (§11.6) |
| "label-free / training-free / prior-free" | The three v1 constraints: no annotations as input, no learned weights, no knowledge of where the block came from. **The PI removed the third on 2026-08-23** — a position prior exists and the MRI can be cropped. `--crop-centre x,y,z --crop-half-mm 30` is the corresponding, largely untested path, and its default half-width of 30 mm is smaller than five of the nine blocks |
