**† These three MRI tissue volumes are not anatomy, they are a broken mask**, and the "OCT / MRI %" beside
them is understated by the same factor. See §4.9 trap 19 and chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and things that
bit us, for the mechanism.

**The one hemisphere-volume figure this document uses, established here.** Read from the same nine
`prep.json` files — `mri.shape × mri.voxel_mm³ × mri.tissue_fraction`, also written into
`result.json → overlap_gate.V_mri_tissue_cm3` — the MRI tissue volume handed to the search is
**386–806 cm³** on the six subjects whose tissue mask works — I48 386.3, I57 518.0, I62 531.5, I55 620.5,
I46 802.9, I38 805.8 cm³, median 576 — and 1 453.4 / 1 838.8 / 2 519.0 cm³ on the three where it does not
(I58, I61, I56). **Use 386–806 cm³ as the expected volume of a fixed ex-vivo human hemisphere in this
dataset, and anchor any derived threshold on the 806 cm³ top of that band.** It is a measurement from this
data, re-read from the compute server on 2026-08-24 — not a textbook figure and not a remembered one. Note
that even the sensible values include residual bath fluid and dura, so they are upper bounds on brain tissue
proper. **This section is the single place the band is established and derived**; every other chapter states
the number and points here.

**The one threshold that follows from it.** A "tissue" mask above **1.5 × 806 ≈ 1 210 cm³** is broken. That
is the document's only volume-based reject gate, and it is clean: it catches all three flagged rows — I58
1 453.4, I61 1 838.8, I56 2 519.0 cm³ — with a factor of 1.2–2.1 to spare, and clears all six sane masks, the
largest of them, I38's 805.8 cm³, sitting a third below the gate. Any "≈600 cm³" or "≈900 cm³" hemisphere
figure met in the project's older prose is a from-memory number with no artefact behind it, superseded by
this band.

While you are in those files: `mri.valley_ratio` is present for six of the nine subjects and is **not**
missing for I46 or I38, whatever older summaries say — I48 0.4737, **I38 0.1984**, **I46 0.1161**, I62
0.0869, I57 0.0631, and `null` only for I55, I56, I58, I61. Four nulls, not three; §4.9 trap 19 explains
which of them matter.

Three consequences, and none of them is in the older project notes:

1. **The difficulty of the problem varies by 80×.** I46's specimen is **0.09 %** of its hemisphere; I48's is
   **7.19 %**. "Find a small block in a whole hemisphere with no position prior" is demonstrated **once**, on
   I46. Everything else is a 0.5–7 % chunk, which is a materially easier retrieval.
2. **Only I46 matches the paper's described block.** The lab's literature review records the paper's block as
   `约 1.5 × 1.3 × 0.8 cm`; I46 measures 1.53 × 1.48 × 0.75 cm. No other subject is remotely that shape — I56
   is 4.5 × 4.3 cm across and 1 cm deep, I38 is 5.2 × 4.7 × 2.9 cm. Reading those numbers, they are almost
   certainly **coronal slabs** rather than excised blocks, and the protocol changed after the pilot — but
   that is an inference from the extents, not something anyone has looked at. Confirmable in one minute by
   opening any of them in Freeview, which nobody has done. `[OPEN]`

   **Correction to carry with you.** `results_inspection/INDEX.md:14` on the compute box describes I56 as a
   "**33x49x44 mm** slab". The true extent, computed from `prep.json` and confirmed against the ImageJ TIFF
   header, is **9.8 × 45.2 × 43.0 mm** — the first axis is wrong by about **3×**, which turns a 1 cm-thick
   slab into a 3.3 cm block. The other two axes are approximately right. Wherever that INDEX.md row is
   quoted, quote the correction with it.
3. **Search NCC is therefore not comparable across subjects.** The template volume differs by 40×, and a
   small homogeneous specimen scores higher masked NCC than a large heterogeneous slab almost regardless of
   correctness. Any cross-subject claim built on `search top1` needs a size-normalised statistic first.
   Reading it as a candidate explanation — the interpretation, not the measurement — this is why the two
   highest-scoring subjects (I46 0.726, I55 0.611) are also the two smallest, and why score magnitude has
   been such a poor guide to correctness.

   **The refined score behaves the same way, and this is the fact that kills any numeric acceptance
   threshold.** `refine.final_ncc` is **0.5020** for I61 and **0.5121** for I57 — both of which are wrong,
   I61's block landing ~95 mm outside the labelled hemisphere — while **I62 scores 0.2842 and is correct**.
   Absolute NCC does not separate right from wrong across subjects, in either direction. Never state a
   "good result if `final_ncc` > *x*" criterion anywhere in this project without that counterexample
   attached. The per-run numbers are in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means; the failure analysis is
   in chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us.

Related, and never designed for: **neighbouring pieces of one hemisphere mutually constrain each other.** v1
registers one specimen at a time, independently. That is the right choice for v1 — it is the only thing the
public data supports, one volume per subject — but it is a *choice*, and it is nowhere defended. Two
neighbouring blocks registered independently should abut; the residual gap/overlap is a scalar error in
millimetres that needs no annotation at all. That is the cheapest unexplored label-free evaluation idea in
the project, and it is a concrete reason to ask Xiangrui for **adjacent** blocks specifically.

### 4.4 Per-subject inventory (all nine DANDI subjects we touched)

Shapes read from the files themselves — OME-TIFF/ImageJ headers via `tifffile`, NIfTI headers via `nibabel` —
and cross-checked against `work/<SUB>/prep.json` written by `octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py`.

#### 4.4.1 The MRI actually registered against

Reading of that table:

* **Seven of nine are 20°.** Only I58 was registered on a non-20° contrast, and it was the 10°, the worst
  possible choice for GM/WM separation. `sub-I58_ses-MRI_flip-1_VFA.nii.gz` (**2,890,933,645 B**,
  `FlipAngle 30`, mtime 2026-08-20 11:49) **is already on disk and was never tried.** Re-running I58 on it is
  a free experiment and the obvious first fix.
* **I48's flip angle is unknown** because its `.json` sidecar was never fetched. It was run as if it were the
  20° like its `flip-2` siblings. **What its "uncertain" verdict does and does not rest on:** it rests on the
  **search-score margin of 0.0013** — top1 0.2571 against top2 0.2558, the second-worst separation in the
  project — and on nothing else. It does **not** rest on a label-coverage artefact, and I48 must not be filed
  alongside I62 and the other large slabs, whose zero Dice *is* a coverage artefact (§4.4.3). Separately and
  independently, **I48's Dice is untrustworthy in both directions**: only 62.7 % of its whole-hemisphere
  labels and 64.2 % of its BA labels land on MRI tissue at all, so its Dice can be read neither as evidence
  that the registration worked nor as evidence that it failed. Two distinct problems; do not merge them. The
  margin analysis is in chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us.
* **The paper says 150 µm isotropic MRI; seven of nine subjects are 0.12 mm.** Only I46 and I55 — the two
  subjects whose OCT is 12 µm in-plane, and the only two whose label mapping is lossless (§4.4.3) — match the
  published protocol. That looks like the same protocol change that turned excised blocks into slabs (§4.3)
  showing up on the MRI side, but that is an interpretation of the pattern, not a documented change.
* I56 is the only 1600×1600×576 volume; every other 0.12 mm subject is 1600×1400×640.
* The label `Source` sidecar disagrees with the registered flip for I48, I57 and I58. The labels were drawn on
  a different synthesised contrast than the one we searched in. They are in the same `space-EPIC` frame, so
  this is not by itself an error — but it is one more reason not to treat the labels as a rigid ground truth.

| I57 | 768×1251×2021 | uint16 | ImageJ TIFF | `[30,30,35]` | 35 / 30 / 30 | ImageJ `spacing=0.035`, `XResolution 33.3333` ✓ | 26.88 × 37.53 × 60.63 | 1.942e9 |
| I58 | 672×1067×1407 | uint16 | OME-TIFF, axes `TYX` | `[30,30,35]` | 35 / 30 / 30 | OME-XML placeholder `1.0 pixel`, `XResolution 0` ✗ (sidecar only) | 23.52 × 32.01 × 42.21 | 1.009e9 |
| I61 | 608×1067×1407 | uint16 | OME-TIFF, axes `TYX` | `[30,30,35]` | 35 / 30 / 30 | placeholder ✗ (sidecar only) | 21.28 × 32.01 × 42.21 | 0.913e9 |
| I62 | 600×1231×1500 | uint16 | OME-TIFF, axes `TYX` | `[30,30,35]` | 35 / 30 / 30 | placeholder ✗ (sidecar only) | 21.00 × 36.93 × 45.00 | 1.108e9 |

The distinction between the last two spacing columns is the point of the table. "Spacing used" is what
`prep_subject.py` fed the pipeline; "independent evidence inside the file" is whether anything other than the
sidecar corroborates it. **Four of nine blocks (I46, I58, I61, I62) have no in-file spacing at all** — the
OME-XML `PhysicalSize*` fields are the literal placeholder `1.0 "pixel"` and the TIFF resolution tags are
zero. That is exactly how the I46 error survived (§4.5).

Things in this table that will bite:

* **Sidecar key order is `PixelSize = [x, y, z]`.** `prep_subject.py:118` reverses it to `(z,y,x)`:
  `sp = [px[2], px[1], px[0]]`. Never copy a sidecar list into a z-first slot.
* **Six volumes are stored with OME axes `TYX`** — slices as *timepoints*, with `SizeZ = 1`. Three are `ZYX`.
  `tifffile.series[0]` returns the correct 3-D array either way; anything that keys off `SizeZ` reads 1.
* **I56's OCT is float32 with negative values** (min −209.8). Every other block is unsigned integer. Any
  `log`/`sqrt` preprocessing must clamp.
* **I46 is the only 8-bit block**, and with I55 one of only two at 12 µm in-plane.

All 25 downloaded label volumes were opened and counted (script `/tmp/lc5.py` on the AutoDL box). Counts are
exact voxel counts **on the label file's own grid**.

**Which are EMPTY: none of them.** Every one of the 25 label volumes we hold contains labelled voxels. That
statement has to be made explicitly because several of these files *look* empty and are routinely assumed to
be: **five are bounding-box crops, not full-FOV volumes** — I48 `vessels` (305×284×276), I56 `infrasupra`
(301×294×351), I57 `infrasupra` + `vessels` (101×338×248), I61 `infrasupra` + `vessels` (102×315×260) — and
their `.nii.gz` sizes of 61 KB … 590 KB are a consequence of the crop, not of emptiness.

What **is** absent, and must not be confused with a zero:

| absence | detail | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **I62 has no `infrasupra_seg-wholehemi` at all** on DANDI | not a download choice — the asset does not exist | `prep_subject.py` prefers `--labels-wholehemi` and falls back to `--labels-ba`, so I62's `labels4_counts` (1: 1,403,085 · 2: 1,071,480 · 3: 876,215) is the tiny BA-only label, **0.23 % of the volume**. `I62_otsu` reports **Dice 0.0**, which is an evaluator artefact, not a registration failure |
| `derivatives/Labels/ses-I61/` | mis-named duplicate directory containing `…_label-infrasupra_dseg.json` (50 B) with **no matching `.nii.gz`** | a genuine dandiset bug; ignore the directory |
| I48's EPIC `flip-2` `.json` sidecar | never fetched | flip angle unknown |
| `Dice 0.000` for I57, I58, I61 | the placed block has essentially no overlap with the label cloud, so **both Dice sets are empty** | a *coverage* zero, not a measured disagreement |
| Vessel dashes (`—`) for I38, I48, I56, I57, I58, I61, I62 | `vessel_distance_stats` requires **≥ 20** annotation points inside the OCT vessel-EDT box; below that it returns `{"n_inside": n}` and every downstream field is `null` | **missing data, not zeros.** For all seven, `n_inside == 0`; no median, no `f150`, and **no control** was ever computed |

Six hard-won caveats about the annotations that a successor will otherwise rediscover the slow way:

1. **The MRI vessel-label value convention is not standardised**: `1` (I38, I58, I61, I62), `255` (I46, I48,
   I56, I57), `30` (I55). The authors' own script uses `--label 255`. **Always threshold `> 0`, never test
   `== 255`.**
2. `sub-I57_…_label-vessels_dseg.nii.gz` contains **17 voxels of value −32,768** — an int16 sentinel that
   leaked into an int32 file. Thresholding `> 0` also handles this.
3. **Label volumes do not share the MRI's axis order.** `infrasupra` / `vessels` follow the MRI orientation
   for some subjects and not others (I38's `infrasupra` is 1400×640×1600 against a 1600×1400×640 MRI);
   `seg-wholehemi` is **always** stored `R,A,S` and is therefore always axis-permuted relative to the EPIC
   MRI. `prep_subject.py::map_labels_to_grid` resolves this from the affines — never index a label array
   directly.
4. **Two MRI vessel labels lose voxels when mapped onto the MRI grid**, a genuine geometry defect verified by
   comparing affines. **I56**: 21,240 → **6,513** (69 % lost); `inv(A_vessels) @ A_mri` is
   `[[0,0,1,512],[1,0,0,0],[0,−1,0,1088]]`, i.e. the label grid is translated by 512 and 1088 voxels and about
   a third of its vessels sit outside the MRI box in world coordinates — **treat I56's MRI vessel label as
   unreliable.** **I48**: 86,116 → **79,331** (8 % lost); here the composed affine carries **half-voxel
   offsets** (`+24.5`, `−642.5`) and nearest-neighbour resampling of 1-voxel-thick vessels drops ~8 %.
   Lossless: I38 (10,236 → 10,236), I46 (34,069 → 34,069), I55 (13,899 → 13,899, and its label affine is
   *bit-identical* to its MRI affine), I58 (33,745 → 33,745), I61 (33,670 → 33,670). I57 loses only its 17
   sentinel voxels; I62 loses 88.
5. **`prep.json`'s `labels4_counts` is the whole-hemisphere label**, not the BA label — except for I62, where
   no whole-hemi label exists.
6. **Whole-hemi vs BA-label agreement** (fraction of BA-labelled voxels where the two label sets agree, from
   `prep.json`): I38 0.900, I46 0.932, I48 0.937, I55 0.909, I56 0.882, **I57 0.671**, I58 0.939, I61 0.940.
   I57's 0.671 means its two annotation sets genuinely disagree with each other.

**And the defect that matters most: the whole-hemisphere label mapping has a wrong axis pairing on all six
0.12 mm subjects.** `map_labels_to_grid` computes `M = inv(A_label) @ A_ref` and takes
`perm[r] = argmax|M[r,:3]|`. The two 0.15 mm subjects get `perm = [2,0,1]`, which pairs equal-length axes
(576↔576, 1280↔1280, 1040↔1040) and is lossless. The six 0.12 mm subjects get `perm = [1,2,0]`, which pairs
the label's **640-voxel** axis against a **1400-voxel** MRI axis — only 36–40 % of the MRI grid ever receives
a label lookup.

| subject | MRI voxel | source nonzero | after mapping | loss | MRI grid receiving a lookup | labels on MRI tissue | BA labels on MRI tissue |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **I46** | 0.15 | 111,293,541 | 111,293,541 | **0.0 %** | **100.0 %** | 99.94 % | 99.77 % |
| **I55** | 0.15 | 127,943,011 | 127,943,011 | **0.0 %** | **100.0 %** | 99.67 % | 99.25 % |
| I48 | 0.12 | 200,449,445 | 136,880,167 | −31.7 % | 40.0 % | **62.68 %** | **64.19 %** |
| I58 | 0.12 | 234,433,984 | 155,401,827 | −33.7 % | 40.0 % | 91.18 % | 100.00 % |
| I38 | 0.12 | 245,782,385 | 161,556,093 | −34.3 % | 40.0 % | 87.80 % | 99.94 % |
| I57 | 0.12 | 233,264,392 | 149,540,041 | −35.9 % | 40.0 % | **57.89 %** | **6.56 %** |
| I61 | 0.12 | 275,918,996 | 167,062,778 | −39.5 % | 40.0 % | 92.71 % | 99.99 % |
| I56 | 0.12 | 231,427,122 | 135,133,392 | −41.6 % | 36.0 % | 100 % (meaningless — its MRI tissue fraction is 0.989) | 100 % (meaningless) |
| I62 | 0.12 | *no wholehemi label exists* | 3,350,780 (BA only) | — | — | **37.27 %** | **37.27 %** |

The root cause is in the **headers, not the code**. For I46 the label and MRI world boxes coincide to 0.2 mm.
For I38 they do not: the same three extents {76.8, 192, 168} mm are assigned to *different world axes*, so the
boxes overlap in only 76.8 × 76.8 × 168 mm. The label header's assignment (76.8 mm L–R, 192 mm A–P, 168 mm
I–S) is anatomically sensible for a hemisphere; the EPIC MRI header's (168 mm L–R, 76.8 mm A–P) is not.
**The EPIC MRI affine is the broken one for the 0.12 mm subjects.** Using the shape-consistent permutation
instead keeps **52.5 % more labels** *and* places them better (0.990 vs 0.878 on tissue).

What that invalidates: every `dice_WM` / `dice_GM` / `frac_on_mri_labels` for **I38, I48, I56, I57, I58, I61**
in `work/runs/*/result.json` and `results_inspection/`, and every verdict built on them. What it does **not**
invalidate: the registrations themselves — search and refinement never touch the labels, they run on the
MRI's own voxel grid with an isotropic voxel size and the orientation search is exhaustive, so a wrong
world-axis labelling in a header cannot bias the result. I46's (0.803 / 0.825) and I55's (0.921 / 0.930) Dice
are unaffected.

**One row of that table is routinely misread. I48's** 62.68 % / 64.19 % coverage means its Dice cannot be
believed **in either direction** — not as evidence the registration worked, not as evidence it failed. It is
*not* the reason I48's verdict is "uncertain"; that verdict comes from the 0.0013 search-score margin and
from nothing else (§4.4.1). I62's zero Dice, by contrast, genuinely *is* a label-coverage artefact — it has
no whole-hemisphere label at all and only 37.3 % of its BA labels land on MRI tissue. Two different problems
with two different causes: do not file I48 with I62 and the other large slabs.

The **OCT-side** `ves_seg.tif` has its own version of the same problem — **it is not on the OCT grid** for two
of the three subjects that have it:

| sub | `ves_seg.tif` shape | OCT shape | relationship |
|---|---|---|---|
| I46 | 561×1271×1230 | 627×1271×1230 | in-plane identical, **66 slices short** |
| I38 | 520×1386×1294 | 832×1724×1573 | differs in **all three** axes |
| I48 | 441×893×780 | 735×1408×1244 | differs in all three; ratios 1.577 / 1.595 are **not integers**, so it is a crop, not a downsample |

`prep_subject.py` (~line 181) does `full[:nz] = seg[:nz]` — it **assumes alignment at z = 0 and identical
in-plane grids**, which is defensible only for I46. **The I38 and I48 `ves_seg`-based evaluation numbers
(`evaluation/*/vessels_vesseg/*` in `result.json`) are therefore suspect.** Even for I46 the 66-slice offset
is unresolved: the 2026-08-18 audit found 0 and 66 statistically indistinguishable.

---

### 4.5 The I46 metadata bug

**The claim.** `sub-I46_ses-OCT_sample-BrocaAreaS01_OCT.json` records `"PixelSize": [12, 12, 12]` µm —
isotropic. The real depth step is **≈14 µm**; the sidecar omits the depth-to-in-plane factor of
**7/6 = 1.1667**.

This matters because I46 is the subject every headline number in the project is quoted from, and because a
wrong depth spacing is exactly the kind of error that a registration absorbs silently — it comes out as a
scale in the recovered affine rather than as a failure.

#### 4.5.1 The evidence: four lines, plus one that does not discriminate

Count them carefully, because the count has been wrong in circulation. There are **four** lines of evidence
**that I46's declared 12 µm depth spacing is wrong**, (a) to (d) below, and one further item (e) that is
recorded for honesty and settles nothing either way. A **fifth** line — "the measured 33-slice section period
reconciles with the vibratome's 500 µm cut only at 15.15 µm/slice" — used to be counted here and has been
**withdrawn**; it fails on I56 and, read consistently, argues *against* a large correction. See §4.8.3, which
explains exactly why. If you find a source claiming a fourth or a fifth independent confirmation via the
section period, that is the withdrawn one.

**Say which count you mean.** Three counts circulate in this document and they are not in conflict — they
cover different sets, all three are correct within their own scope, and the withdrawn section period is in
none of them.

- **Four** — lines that the declared 12 µm is wrong: (a)–(d) here.
- **Three** — independent routes to the *value* ≈1.17, **none of them ours**: the sibling sidecars **1.1667**,
  the authors' published affine **1.17419**, and an oracle affine fitted to their manual annotations in our
  frame **1.177**. See chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.11.2. (b) is not among them because it
  carries no number, and (d) is not because it is our own measurement rather than an outside corroboration;
  the oracle affine is not a separate line here because it is fitted to the same manual annotations that
  carry (c).
- **Two** — *annotation-free anchors*, the specific numbers quotable without a manual annotation behind them:
  our pipeline's **1.219** and the sidecar ratio **14/12 = 1.167**. See chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and
  things that bit us, §7.3.8.

**(a) Every other subject has depth = in-plane × 7/6, exactly.**

| sub | in-plane µm | depth µm | ratio | source of the depth number |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| I38 | 30 | 35 | 1.16667 | OME-XML `PhysicalSizeZ = 0.035 mm` **and** sidecar |
| I48 | 30 | 35 | 1.16667 | ImageJ `spacing = 0.035` **and** sidecar |
| I55 | 12 | **14** | 1.16667 | OME-XML `PhysicalSizeZ = 0.014 mm` **and** sidecar |
| I56 | 30 | 35 | 1.16667 | ImageJ `spacing = 0.035` **and** sidecar |
| I57 | 30 | 35 | 1.16667 | ImageJ `spacing = 0.035` **and** sidecar |
| I58 / I61 / I62 | 30 | 35 | 1.16667 | sidecar only (TIFF metadata is placeholder) |
| **I46** | 12 | **12** | **1.000** | sidecar only — **the outlier** |

I55 is the comparison that carries the argument: it is the *other* 12 µm in-plane block, and its sidecar says
`[12, 12, 14]`. Read §4.5.3 point 1 before leaning on it — I55's own recovered anisotropy is 0.8570 = 6/7,
the exact inverse of the factor at issue, which is not what a clean control looks like.

**(b) I46 is one of only four blocks with no spacing recorded inside the file at all.** Its OME-XML `Pixels`
element reads `PhysicalSizeX="1.0" PhysicalSizeXUnit="pixel" … PhysicalSizeZ="1.0" PhysicalSizeZUnit="pixel"`,
and its TIFF `XResolution` / `YResolution` tags are `(0, 1000)` — zero. There is **no independent record to
contradict the sidecar**, which is precisely how the error survived.

**(c) The authors' own published affine carries a ≈17 % stretch on one axis.**
`code/costantini/biccn-broca-I46/results/mri2oct/affine.lta` (type 1, `LINEAR_RAS_TO_RAS`):

```
 1.1741251    0.109609105  -0.105837345  -7.432568
-0.003448261  1.0491916    -0.11666678   -6.1766615
 0.011982521  0.058345348   0.99289995   -2.8748932
```

Column norms **1.17419 / 1.05651 / 1.00532**; singular values **1.21149 / 1.03593 / 0.98222**; det 1.2327.
`1.17419 / (7/6) = 1.0064` — within **0.6 %** of the missing factor.
`[UNVERIFIED]` — *which OCT array axis* that 1.174 column corresponds to cannot be pinned down, because the
2026-08-18 audit (`costantini_b0/reports/costantini_i46_data_audit.md`) established that the authors'
`oct.nii` origin/orientation cannot be recovered from DANDI (best-fit layouts `SRP` 95.8 % / `SPR` 94.8 % /
`IRP` 93.8 % of OCT tissue inside BA 44/45, but sub-millimetre vessel agreement never better than 260 µm
median, against ~150–200 µm expected). Treat the 1.174 as **magnitude** evidence, not axis-resolved evidence.

**(d) Our own pipeline, run with the buggy 12 µm, has to stretch I46's depth axis by 1.219.**
`stretch_ijk[0]` is by construction the scale on OCT array axis 0 = the slice/depth axis (`register.py:186`;
`R_axes = A_oct[:3,:3] / ‖·‖`, `stretch_ijk(T)[q] = ‖T[:3,:3] @ R_axes[:,q]‖`).

| sub | depth stretch after structural stage | after vascular stage | vascular corner-mean motion |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| I38 | **0.861 ‡ — clamp bound, not a measurement** | 0.808 | 0.398 mm |
| **I46** | 1.026 | **1.219** | **1.524 mm** |
| I48 | 0.975 | 0.949 | 0.857 mm |
| **I55** | 0.920 | **0.913** | **0.334 mm** |
| I56 | 0.981 | 0.998 | 0.669 mm |
| I57 | 0.980 | 0.994 | 1.350 mm |
| I58 | 0.996 | 0.986 | 1.331 mm |
| I61 | 1.003 | 1.009 | 0.596 mm |
| I62 | 0.942 | 0.919 | 0.261 mm |

**‡ I38's 0.861 is the refiner's clamp bound `exp(−0.15) = 0.860708`, not a measured scale.** The optimiser
was pinned against the edge of its own search box, so that cell reports the constraint and not an answer.
Do not read it, average it, or compare it with the other rows. The derivation is in §4.5.3 point 2 and it
applies to every table in this document that carries I38's structural depth scale.

I46 is the **only** subject the vascular stage has to *stretch* along depth (every other subject stays within
0.81–1.01), and its is the largest correction in the table. I55 — same tissue type, same in-plane resolution,
correct sidecar — needs the **smallest** motion of any subject, 0.334 mm. Caveats: the vascular stage's scale
clamp is `--vascular-clamp 0.3`, so 1.219 is not free of a ceiling effect; and 1.219 exceeds the expected
1.1667 by 4.5 %, so the sidecar is not the only thing that is off.

(Note for anyone quoting I55: several older project notes say I55 "needs only a 1.10 depth stretch". **It is
0.913.** `work/runs/I55_otsu/result.json → final_transform.stretch_ijk = [0.913, 1.097, 1.084]`, and index 0
is depth — the 1.097 is the in-plane **j** axis. The same reversal is visible in the `mirror`/`stretch`
columns of `work/runs/summary_all/summary.md`. The *argument* survives the correction — I55's sidecar is
right, so it needs no depth correction, and the vascular stage moves it only 0.334 mm — but the number does
not.)

**And I55 is not a clean null control.** Its recovered depth-to-in-plane anisotropy is **0.8570**, which is
`6/7 = 0.857143` to four decimal places — *exactly the inverse* of the 7/6 factor I46 is supposed to be
missing, on the one other subject at 12 µm in-plane and the one subject whose sidecar is corroborated twice
inside its own file. Every use of I55 as a null result in this chapter, including the smallest-motion row in
the table above, has to carry that coincidence with it. It is worked through in §4.5.3 point 1, and it is the
single strongest reason not to treat "I46 sidecar bug, everyone else fine" as settled.

**(e) Weak counter-evidence, recorded for honesty.** The paper describes the block as "~1.5 × 1.3 × 0.8 cm".
At 12 µm the depth is 627 × 12 µm = 7.52 mm; at 14 µm it is 8.78 mm; at 12.7 µm it is 7.96 mm. All round to
"~0.8 cm", so this does not discriminate. In-plane is no better: declared 15.25 × 14.76 mm against a stated
15 × 13 mm, and the array carries ~1.8 mm of background padding on one axis.

#### 4.5.2 The physical alternatives, ruled out quantitatively

A reviewer will immediately propose two non-metadata explanations. Both can be dismissed with arithmetic, and
this is the strongest part of the argument.

The chronology decides what can shrink what: the hemisphere is fixed → **MRI is acquired on the intact
hemisphere** → the block is excised → 1 month PBS wash, agarose embedding → **optical clearing in 20/40/60 %
TDE, 24 h each, ≈1 week** → serial-sectioning OCT. So the MRI images the tissue *before* clearing and the OCT
*after*. Any dimensional change from clearing sits between the two images and must appear in the OCT→MRI
affine.

**Hypothesis 1 — clearing-induced dimensional change.** To first order such a change is **isotropic**: TDE
equilibration is diffusive and the block has no imposed anisotropy. A metadata error in one spacing field is
by construction **confined to one axis**. The two hypotheses therefore predict opposite *spectra*, and the
spectrum is measurable.

| source | per-axis values | det | shape |
|---|---|---:|---|
| isotropic change at det = 1.2327 would give | **1.0723 on all three** | 1.2327 | — |
| authors' `affine.lta`, singular values | **1.2115, 1.0359, 0.9822** | 1.2327 | one axis high, two ≈ 1 → **single-axis** |
| authors' `affine.lta`, column norms | 1.1742, 1.0565, 1.0053 | 1.2327 | **single-axis** |
| our oracle affine (fitted to manual labels + vessels), `stretch_ijk` | **1.177, 0.999, 1.046** | — | **single-axis** |
| our label-free v1, I46, `stretch_ijk` | **1.219, 0.977, 1.031** | −1.2277 | **single-axis** |

Isotropic swelling of the observed magnitude would put **1.072 on every axis**; it puts 1.005–1.046 on two of
them, on four independent routes. The residual is small but real — two axes at 1.03–1.05 rather than 1.00 —
so the honest statement is: *predominantly a one-axis metadata error, with a possible few-percent isotropic
component that the data cannot separate from registration error.*

**Hypothesis 2 — refractive index.** OCT measures **optical** path length and the reconstruction divides by an
assumed refractive index; the paper states **n = 1.4**. A wrong index misestimates depth *and only depth*,
which is the right shape. But the magnitude fails: producing a 1.17 under-measurement needs
`n_true = 1.4 / 1.17 = 1.197`, below water (1.33) and impossible for TDE-equilibrated brain (TDE at 60 % is
used precisely *because* its index is ~1.42–1.46). And the sign is wrong — a *higher* true index makes the
reconstruction *over*-estimate depth, requiring compression, not a stretch. The 1.42–1.46 figure for
TDE-equilibrated tissue is general optics knowledge rather than anything measured on this project's data, so
treat that step of the argument as an interpretation; the sign argument stands on its own regardless.

(The oracle-affine row in that table is derived in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means — it is a
ceiling measurement, never part of the method.)

#### 4.5.3 What the story does not yet explain — and it must be said

The "I46 sidecar bug, everyone else fine" account is the current project story. It is **not sufficient**, and
three facts say so. The first of them is the one to remember.

> **I55'S RECOVERED ANISOTROPY IS 6/7, TO FOUR DECIMAL PLACES.**
>
> Depth ÷ mean-in-plane for I55's structural transform is **0.8570**. `6/7 = 0.857143`.
>
> I55 is the *control*. It is the other 12 µm in-plane block, the one subject whose depth spacing is
> corroborated **twice inside its own file** (OME-XML `PhysicalSizeZ = 0.014 mm` and `XResolution`), and it is
> quoted throughout this project — and throughout this chapter — as the null result that makes I46 look like
> the outlier. Yet its registration behaves **exactly as if its own 14 µm were wrong and the truth were
> 12 µm**: 0.8570 is the precise multiplicative inverse of the 7/6 = 1.1667 that I46 is supposed to be
> missing.
>
> Whatever this is — a real dataset-wide convention error, an artefact of the scale prior, or coincidence at
> four decimal places — **I55 cannot be quoted as a clean reverse control without this stated alongside it**,
> and it is not currently explained. `[OPEN]`

1. **I55's anisotropy is 6/7 to four decimal places**, as above. Restated here so the numbered list is
   complete: the control subject's own recovered depth-to-in-plane ratio is the exact inverse of the factor
   the whole §4.5 argument turns on.
2. **I38's structural stage is saturated at the scale clamp.** Its structural depth stretch of **0.861** is
   the clamp bound `exp(−0.15) = 0.860708`. Since `compose()` is `M = R · Shear · diag(exp(ls))` with a unit
   upper-triangular shear, `‖M[:,2]‖ = exp(ls[2]) · √(1 + sh₁² + sh₂²) ≥ exp(ls[2])`, so
   `ls[2] ∈ [−0.15, −0.14966]` — saturated, with `|sh₁|, |sh₂| ≤ 0.026`. **I38's reported structural
   transform is the box's corner, not the optimiser's answer**, and every structural metric derived from it
   describes the constraint. The vascular stage, whose clamp is wider (`exp(±0.3)`), promptly took it to
   0.808. No other run is at either clamp on any axis.
3. **The anisotropy is large only in the runs judged correct.** `d/ip final` for the five correct runs (I46,
   I55, I38, I56, I62) is 1.214 / 0.837 / 0.852 / 0.937 / 0.961 — a 45 % spread; for the three judged wrong
   (I57, I58, I61) it is 1.095 / 1.004 / 1.026, all within 10 % of isotropic. The reading of that — an
   interpretation, not a measurement — is that it is the
   right way round for the anisotropy to be *signal*: a wrong pose has nothing to explain, so the scale prior
   (`reg = 2.0`, quadratic in `ln s`) pulls it to 1.0; a correct pose has real residual geometry to absorb and
   pays the prior's price. If it were optimiser noise you would see it in the wrong runs too. n = 9, so this
   is a hypothesis — but it is also the only **label-free correctness indicator** anyone has proposed, and it
   costs nothing to report.

Also worth knowing: `|det final|` has a geometric mean of **0.983** over the five correct runs (range
0.73–1.23) versus 0.910 over the three wrong ones. **There is no dataset-wide clearing-shrinkage signature in
these transforms** — a consistent shrinkage would put every determinant on the same side of 1. And `|det|`
deviation is *not* a usable sanity gate: the two most extreme determinants (0.726 I38, 1.228 I46) belong to
runs marked correct, and the three wrong runs cluster nearest 1.

**And the authors themselves believed 12 µm.** `scripts/registration/lsfm_slide_center_and_scale.py:30` reads
`vx_new[2] = 0.396 / 50` — they resize every LSFM slice to 50 z-samples and declare its physical thickness
0.396 mm, which is exactly 33 slices × 12 µm. They kept the 12 µm and let the OCT→MRI affine absorb the whole
1.174 as a *registration* parameter. So the authors' 1.174 and our 1.219 measure **the same thing in the same
units**. If the 12 µm is wrong, their LSFM slice z-geometry (7.92 µm/sample) is wrong by the same factor, and
that factor enters their published cell-density numbers twice — through the declared slab thickness and
through the Jacobian.

#### 4.5.4 What to do about it

`octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py` accepts **`--oct-spacing-um Z,Y,X`** (default `None` → read the sidecar). It
was **not** used for I46: `run_all.sh` prepped every subject from the sidecar. So every stored `work/I46/*`
array and every `work/runs/I46_*` transform is built on 12 µm depth. Re-prep:

```bash
ssh -p 49018 root@connect.westb.seetacloud.com
cd ~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration
source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate octmri
D=data/costantini/dandi-000026
L=$D/derivatives/Labels/sub-I46/ses-MRI/anat/sub-I46_ses-MRI_space-EPIC_label
python octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py --work work/I46_14um \
  --mri $D/derivatives/EPIC/sub-I46/ses-MRI/anat/sub-I46_ses-MRI_flip-2_VFA.nii.gz \
  --oct $D/sub-I46/ses-OCT/micr/sub-I46_ses-OCT_sample-BrocaAreaS01_OCT.ome.tiff \
  --oct-spacing-um 14,12,12 \
  --labels-wholehemi ${L}-infrasupra_seg-wholehemi_dseg.nii.gz \
  --labels-ba ${L}-infrasupra_dseg.nii.gz \
  --mri-vessels ${L}-vessels_dseg.nii.gz \
  --oct-vesseg $D/derivatives/sub-I46/ses-OCT/vessel/ves_seg.tif
```

Prediction if the sidecar diagnosis is right: `stretch_ijk[0]` drops from 1.219 to ≈1.04 and the vascular
corner motion drops from 1.52 mm toward I55's 0.33 mm. **Run I55 at `12,12,12` in the same session** — that is
the experiment that actually discriminates, and the I55 6/7 coincidence in §4.5.3 is precisely why it has to
be run rather than assumed. If the sidecar story is right, I46 improves and I55 gets worse; if the whole 7/6
convention is backwards dataset-wide, both go to ≈1.0. `[OPEN]`
**Only one heavy job at a time on this box** — the instance froze once with two running.

Which sidecars are correct, for the record:

| status | subjects |
|---|---|
| Correct **and** independently corroborated inside the file | I38, I48, I55, I56, I57 |
| Correct but uncorroborated (TIFF metadata is placeholder; sidecar already carries the 7/6 ratio) | I58, I61, I62 |
| **Wrong** | **I46 only** |

### 4.8 Why the OCT volumes are geometrically self-consistent

This is the fact that licenses the entire method. Without it, `octreg` would be solving a different and much
harder problem.

#### 4.8.1 How a serial-sectioning block-face OCT volume is built

Read from Costantini et al. 2023, p.9 right column and p.10 left column.

| parameter | value |
|---|---|
| System | custom-built **polarisation-sensitive OCT (PSOCT)**; only the **intensity** signal is used in this paper, so it is called OCT throughout |
| Light source | swept source, AxsunTech; A-line rate 100 kHz; centre wavelength 1310 nm; bandwidth 135 nm |
| Axial resolution | **5.6 µm in tissue**, assumed refractive index **1.4** |
| Sample arm | pair of XY scanning mirrors, 4× telescope, 4× air objective (Olympus UPLFLN4x, NA 0.13) → **6 µm lateral resolution** |
| Detection | balanced detector; post-objective power 3.7 mW; 95 dB SNR |
| Tile FOV | **3 mm × 3 mm**, 3 µm lateral step, **10 % overlap** between tiles, 16 s per tile |
| **Stages** | motorized xyz: x and y = Thorlabs **LTS150**, z = Thorlabs **MLJ150**; travel 150 / 150 / 50 mm; **unidirectional moving accuracy 2 / 2 / 10 µm** |
| **Vibratome** | 6.35 cm custom sapphire blade (DDK CO.), 50 Hz, 1.2 mm peak-to-peak amplitude, 0.1 mm/s feed; **cuts a 500 µm superficial slice** after each surface is fully scanned |
| Control | custom LabVIEW software drives **both** the OCT imaging and the vibratome slicing |
| Clearing, before sectioning | 1 month wash in 0.01 M PBS at RT with gentle shaking; embed in agarose; serial incubations in 100 ml of **20 / 40 / 60 % (v/v) TDE in 0.01 M PBS**, 24 h each; ≈1 week per large block; equilibrium declared when the floating embedded block sinks |
| Acquisition computer | 4-core CPU, 64 GB RAM, ATS9350 Alazar digitizer, NVIDIA RTX 4000; k-clock from the light source so the signal is digitized in even-k space; GPU does dispersion compensation + FFT depth profile + rough trimming on the fly |
| Storage | 28 TB local server over 10 Gb/s Ethernet, then uploaded to Boston University SCC at MGHPCC |

**The reconstruction convention, p.10 left column, is the single most important sentence about this dataset:**
tiles are stitched in 2D using the average intensity projection; once each tile's coordinate is known they are
linearly blended in x and y; **and then stacked in z**.

There is **no z-direction image-based registration between slabs.** The z stacking is done from the motorized
stage coordinates. Post-processing on the cluster additionally corrects OCT-specific distortions (shading,
grid distortion) with ImageJ plug-ins plus custom code, and the authors then extract vessels, axonal bundles
and cortical laminar structure with feature-enhancement algorithms.

#### 4.8.2 Why that makes the stack one rigid object

**The block never leaves the stage.** The tissue is fixed on the motorized xyz stages; the top surface is
imaged; the vibratome shaves 500 µm off **in place**; the newly exposed surface is imaged with the stage
coordinates still valid. Stacking in z is therefore a **bookkeeping operation**, not a registration problem —
its accuracy is the stage's, **2 µm in x and y and 10 µm in z**.

Compare that to the voxel sizes in §4.4.2. For the 30/30/35 µm subjects, 10 µm of stage error is under a third
of one depth voxel. For I46 at 12 µm it is under one voxel. For the brainstem pair at 20 µm isotropic it is
half a voxel. **The inter-section geometric error is at or below the voxel scale of the reconstructed volume
in every case.** So the reconstructed OCT volume is one rigid, undistorted 3-D object, and it can be related
to the MRI by a single global affine.

Everything downstream depends on this:

* **The search can be a single 12-DoF global optimisation over one object**, rather than a per-slice
  registration with an inter-slice regulariser. There is no slice-order recovery, no per-slice pose, no
  bending-energy term, no L1 consensus over neighbours.
* **The exhaustive orientation search is meaningful.** Enumerating 16,000 rigid orientations is only sensible
  if there is one true orientation for the whole stack. If sections had independent poses, the top-1 pose of
  the stack would be a fiction.
* **Affine is defensible as the final model.** Non-rigid deformation was implemented and rejected: on I46 the
  best label-free non-rigid variant moved points by 0.048 mm mean / 0.134 mm max and changed the vessel
  median from 179 µm to 177 µm — gain ≈ noise, cost = a whole stage. That verdict is only reasonable because
  there is no accumulated inter-section drift for a deformation field to have to undo. The full ablation,
  including the oracle non-rigid that bounds the available headroom, is in chapter 6, What we found, and what
  it means.

**LSFM is the counterexample that proves the point.** Each 500 µm slice the vibratome removes is *manually
captured to preserve the sequence*, stored between two TDE-rinsed gauze pads in a plastic shell, labelled,
stacked, sealed in a bag and **shipped to another site**. It is then cleared (SDS, 55 °C, 4 days),
antigen-retrieved at 95 °C, stained for 7 days, TDE-graded, and sandwiched between a quartz coverslip and a
500 µm steel spacer. Between the block face and the light sheet the slice has been detached, transported,
swollen, shrunk, folded and squashed. **Whatever coordinate system it had is gone.**

Which is exactly why the modality chain runs **LSFM → OCT → MRI** and not LSFM → MRI. For every slice `i`, the
OCT block still contains the exact 500 µm slab that slice came from, in its correct place. The authors exploit
this literally: `scripts/registration/oct2lsfm_affine.sh` loops `for i in {08..23}` and registers each LSFM
slice to `oct/slices/unstack/oct.${i}.masked.nii.gz` — the *unstacked* corresponding OCT slab, with
`@affine affine -2d` and `@nonlin svf 1 -2d`, i.e. **2D per slice, with no inter-slice 3-D pose estimation at
all**. `lsfm_slide_center_and_scale.py` *assigns* each LSFM slice its z position by copying the corresponding
OCT slab's centre. The LSFM slice's z geometry is **imported from OCT, not measured**.

```
LSFM slice i  --(2D affine + 2D SVF, per slice, vessel-guided)-->  OCT slab i
OCT block     --(3D affine, optionally SVF)                    -->  whole-hemisphere MRI
```

Reconstructing LSFM *across* slices — recovering slice order, orientation and inter-slice deformation without
a block-face reference — is a different and unsolved problem, and it is what the lab's *older* reconstruction
project works on. `octreg v1` deliberately does not touch it. It solves the other end of the same chain, and
the reason that end is tractable is the paragraph above.

#### 4.8.3 The one geometric artefact block-face acquisition does leave

Self-consistent geometry does **not** mean uniform intensity. Each 500 µm cut is imaged from its own new
surface, so every slab carries its own depth-attenuation profile, and the stacked volume shows a **periodic
intensity sawtooth along z**. This is the direct justification for `octreg`'s per-slab depth normalisation
(`oct_slab_normalize`), and it is why any raw-intensity similarity measure — LCC included — is corrupted on
these volumes.

The period, measured directly on the raw OME-TIFFs: per-slice median of in-tissue voxels (16× in-plane
subsample, using the same `raw_tissue_thresh` the pipeline used), detrended by a 301-slice running mean, then
FFT and autocorrelation. Two subjects were measured; the other seven and the brainstem pair were not.
**This is the canonical presentation of the section period, and of the line of evidence that was built on it
and withdrawn** — the section period is a property of the data, so it is tabulated in full only here; chapter
5, The method, as a chain of reasoning, uses it for the `slab_window` sizing and points back here.

| sub | sidecar z spacing | `slab_window` used | **measured period** | period × spacing | window ÷ period |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| I46 | 12 µm | 100 | **33 slices** (FFT 33.0; autocorr r = 0.857, harmonics 66/99/132/165/198) | **0.396 mm** | 3.03 ✓ |
| I56 | 35 µm | 34 | **12 slices** (FFT 12.17; autocorr r = 0.882, harmonics 24/36/48/60) | **0.420 mm** | 2.83 ✗ |

I46's raw medians visibly reset at slice 33 (`… 113, 108, 108, [33] 159, 159, 159 …`); I56's at 0, 12, 24, 36
(`… 1952.7, [12] 3251.0 …`).

Three things follow.

1. **The code comment is wrong by ~3×.** `prep_subject.py:125` reads
   `window = max(10, int(round(1200.0 / sp[0])))   # ~1.2 mm of depth = one section period at 12 um`. The
   formula still works for I46 **by luck** (100 ≈ 3 × 33 periods), but for I56 the window is **2.83 periods,
   not an integer multiple**, and the running mean leaves a residual sawtooth. The robust fix is to measure
   the period per subject — the autocorrelation is ten lines — and set `window` to the nearest integer
   multiple of it. The same risk applies to the brainstem pair, which runs `slab_window = 60` at 20 µm with
   its period never measured at all. `[OPEN]`
2. **The "≈100 slices" figure has a traceable origin and it is an aliasing artefact.** It comes from
   `/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/costantini_b0/reports/costantini_i46_data_audit.md:43` — a mean
   profile inspected at **25-slice granularity**, which aliases a true 33-slice period to ≈100.
3. **The section period is NOT evidence for the I46 sidecar bug. That line of evidence is withdrawn.** It is
   spelled out immediately below, because four other parts of this project were leaning on it.

> **⚠ WITHDRAWN LINE OF EVIDENCE — THE 33-SLICE SECTION PERIOD**
>
> **The claim, as it circulated:** the vibratome cuts a nominal **500 µm** slice; the measured period for I46
> is **33 slices**; therefore I46's true depth spacing is `500 / 33 = 15.15 µm`, not the sidecar's 12 µm —
> "a fourth independent line of evidence" for the sidecar bug, alongside the siblings' implied 14.0 µm and
> the vascular stage's recovered `1.219 × 12 = 14.6 µm`.
>
> **Why it fails: the identical computation on I56 gives the wrong answer.** I56's measured period is 12.17
> slices, so the same premise gives `500 / 12.17 = 41.7 µm` — against a sidecar of **35 µm that is
> corroborated twice inside the file** (ImageJ `spacing = 0.035`, `XResolution 33.3333`) **and** by a
> recovered depth stretch of **0.998**, i.e. a registration that finds no error at all. Both cannot hold.
>
> **Read consistently, it argues the other way.** The reading that reconciles the two subjects is that the
> **actual cut is ≈0.40–0.42 mm, not the nominal 500 µm** — both `period × spacing` products land there
> (I46 0.396 mm, I56 0.420 mm). Apply I56's actual cut to I46 and you get `420 / 33 = 12.7 µm`, a correction
> of only **1.06**, not 1.167. So the section period is not neutral evidence that happens to fail; it is
> weak evidence **against** a large depth correction.
>
> **What to do with it.** Do not cite the section period as confirming evidence anywhere. Do not count it
> when counting lines of evidence — §4.5.1 has **four**, (a) through (d), and this is not among them. **The
> I46 sidecar bug does not depend on it**: §4.5.1 (a), the sibling-sidecar argument, and (b), the absence of
> any in-file spacing for I46, are untouched.
>
> **What is still true and still useful.** The periodic sawtooth is real and measured, the `slab_window`
> mis-sizing in point 1 above is real, and the ≈0.40–0.42 mm figure for the real cut is the best current
> estimate of the vibratome's behaviour. `[OPEN]` — settle it either by asking the authors for the true cut
> thickness, or by measuring the period on the remaining seven DANDI subjects and the brainstem pair
> (≈10 min CPU each, read-only, method as described above). If `period × declared_spacing` lands at
> 0.40–0.42 mm for all of them, the cut is ~0.4 mm and the question is closed.

Everything below has already cost someone time on this project. They are ordered roughly by how quickly they
will bite a newcomer.

| # | Trap | What actually happens | Defence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **`flip-N` is an index, not an angle** | I58 was registered on `flip-3` = **10°**, a contrast with almost no GM/WM separation, and the run failed. The 30° `flip-1` volume (2,890,933,645 B) was on disk the whole time | Read `FlipAngle` from the `.json` sidecar for every subject, every time. Never infer from the index |
| 2 | **Plain `.ome.tiff` vs `acq-Raw .ome.zarr`** | The zarr is un-stitched tiles of a *different block* (S23) with no reconstructed counterpart and no labels. | 3 | **Sidecar `PixelSize` is `[x, y, z]`** | Copying it straight into a z-first slot silently transposes the anisotropy — for the 30/30/35 subjects it puts 35 µm in-plane and 30 µm along depth | `prep_subject.py:118` reverses it. `stretch_ijk[0]` is depth and **nothing else in the codebase is** |
