### 5.4 Vascular refinement: the one decision that is a finding rather than an engineering choice

#### 5.4.1 The geometric argument

Take a cortical block: 7.5 mm along the depth (serial-sectioning) axis by ~15 × 15 mm in plane (I46:
627 × 1271 × 1230 at 12 µm nominal). Reduce it to two classes. What is inside it?

**One sheet.** A patch of grey matter wrapped over white matter, with a single GM/WM interface running through
the block, and sulcal walls that run *roughly parallel to the depth axis*. That is all the geometry a two-class
map of such a block contains.

Now stretch the block along the depth axis. Because the interface and the sulcal walls are approximately
parallel to that axis, the stretch slides tissue **along** the interface rather than **across** it. The
interface stays in almost the same place. Every voxel of WM is still WM, every voxel of GM is still GM, and the
boundary the NCC measures has barely moved.

**The depth-axis scale is a null direction of the structural objective.** Not a shallow direction — a geometric
degeneracy of the representation. A one-sheet block does not encode its own thickness scale, and no amount of
optimiser cleverness recovers information the representation does not contain.

#### 5.4.2 The measurement

`scale_probe.py` → `work/runs/summary/scale_profiles.json` (byte-identical to
`work/runs/validate_real/scale_profiles.json`): apply a single-axis scale `s` about the block centre on top of
T0, `s ∈ [0.85, 1.30]` in steps of 0.025, and record NCC, label Dice and the manual vessel metric on each of
the three OCT array axes. Columns are `[s, NCC-mixed, Dice WM, Dice GM, vessel median µm, f150]`.

**The result in one line: sweeping the full `s ∈ [0.85, 1.30]` range — a 45 % span — along the depth axis moves
the structural objective by 0.021 of NCC, while the same sweep along the in-plane k axis moves it by 0.169.**
The objective is roughly **8× less sensitive along depth than across it**, and the manual GM/WM labels are just as blind — Dice varies by
only 0.007 along depth, with its own maximum at s = 1.100, a maximum the NCC essentially cannot see (its own
argmax sits at 1.075, on a 0.021-wide plateau). The full three-axis table — argmax, value at s = 1.0, span and
Δ for NCC, Dice and vessel f150 on each axis — is canonical in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means,
§6.10.3, and is not repeated here.

(One correction to carry when you read it: do not repeat the older claim that the i-axis span is
"0.713–0.727". 0.713 is the value at s = 0.85; the writer read only the ascending half. The corrected span,
0.7062 at s = 1.300 to 0.7274 at s = 1.075, makes the negative result **stronger**, not weaker.)

Independently confirmed by `oracle_cv.json`: an oracle affine fitted to the **labels only** moves the block
0.19 mm and gains nothing (269.3 µm vs T0's 273.3 µm held-out), while an oracle fitted to **labels + vessels**
reaches 197.1 µm. So the degeneracy is real, it is not an artefact of our particular similarity metric, and
**it is not fixable by better labels.** That is a publishable negative result: anyone doing OCT→MRI with a
structure-only similarity will silently absorb this error.

And it is the *whole* residual, as the following arithmetic on the recorded numbers shows. `transform_diff`
measures corner displacement at `c_o ± 7 mm` on
each axis. A pure depth-scale change from T0's 1.032 to the oracle's 1.177 displaces every corner by
`(1.177/1.032 − 1) × 7 = 0.98 mm`. The measured structural-to-oracle residual is **1.362 mm**. So **~72 % of
everything the structural stage gets wrong on I46 is the one parameter it cannot see.**

One point of hygiene: the prose docs sometimes say the "true" depth scale is ~1.18. **[UNVERIFIED]** — no
artefact on disk carries 1.18. The two defensible anchors are the pipeline's own **1.219** and the
sidecar-vs-siblings ratio **14/12 = 1.1667**, with the authors' affine at 1.17419 and the oracle at 1.177 as
external corroboration. Name which one you mean.

#### 5.4.3 Why vessels are the right thing to add

Vessels satisfy exactly the two properties §5.1 demanded of the class map — both modalities can produce them
independently, without annotation — and they are **transverse to the degenerate direction**. Vessels penetrate
the cortex, so their positions along depth are informative in precisely the way a parallel interface is not.

- MRI: in ex-vivo FLASH there is no flow, so vessels appear as **dark blobs**.
- OCT: vessel lumens are **dark tubes**.

Both are extractable with no annotation on either side, which is what keeps the stage compatible with
C-nolabels.

#### 5.4.4 Sub-decision (a): a correlation, not a distance

This is the one non-obvious modelling choice, and `vascular.py`'s docstring states it:

> Nearest-vessel distances between *automatic* candidates are ambiguous (dense-vs-dense), but the correlation
> of an MRI dark-blob map with the OCT vessel *density* is a proper similarity: where the OCT has many vessels
> the MRI is darker.

Measured: `refine_validate.json` row **A2** drove the refinement with automatic symmetric vessel distance only
— Dice collapses to **0.462 / 0.563**, NCC to **0.172**, and the pose moves **2.77 mm** off. The reason is in
`check_vesselness.py` → `work/vesselness_check/vesselness_check.json`: MRI-side vessel *detection* reaches at
best **7.9 % precision** against dilated manual labels. Of 64 192 automatic MRI vessel candidates only **3 %**
fall within 0.3 mm of a manual vessel, and only **10 %** of manual vessels are within 0.3 mm of a candidate.
Nearest-neighbour distance between two such point sets is noise.

A **soft density-vs-darkness correlation** never has to commit to "this blob is a vessel"; it only has to be
right about where vessels are *denser*, which is a much weaker and much more reliable claim. That is the whole
modelling idea, and it generalises: when your detector's precision is under 10 %, correlate a density, do not
match a point set.

#### 5.4.5 Sub-decision (b): which maps, and at what weight

`vessel_channel_refine.json` swept MRI channel {dark, frangi} × OCT channel {density, frangi map} × weight
{0.5, 1, 2, 4}, plus vessel-only and no-vessel controls — 22 variants. The variant-by-variant table is
canonical in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.10.4. Four anchors from it are enough to follow
the argument here: the shipped setting (MRI **dark** / OCT **density**, w = 2.0) reaches **166.7 µm /
f150 0.477** and lands 0.430 mm from the oracle; the **oracle affine** — the reference ceiling, fitted with
manual annotations — is 171.5 µm / 0.466; **T0**, with no vascular stage at all, is 276.5 µm / 0.254; and the
**control that runs the identical schedule with no vessel channel** manages only 265.8 µm / 0.277.

What the sweep actually licenses:

- **The OCT side must be a density of a segmentation, not a raw Frangi map** (188–241 µm vs 167 µm). This is
  the one strong conclusion in the table.
- **The MRI side can be either dark-blob or Frangi** (165.1 vs 166.7 µm — a statistical tie; the Frangi variant
  is in fact *closer* to the oracle at 0.316 vs 0.430 mm corner). `register.py` hard-codes `mri_dark_channel`.
  That is defensible **on cost** — a local median is far cheaper than a multi-scale Hessian on a hemisphere —
  **not on accuracy.** Say it that way if challenged.
- **The weight is insensitive between 1 and 4** (166.7–167.3 µm). The shipped `--vascular-w 2.0` is defensible
  but not optimal; w = 1.0 is marginally closer to the oracle.
- **The control proves the gain is the channel, not the looser prior** (§5.3.4).

Implementation specifics of the two maps:

- `mri_dark_channel(mri_reg, tissue_reg, q=99.5, vox_mm, window_mm=1.35)`: `size = max(3, round(1.35/vox) | 1)`
  — forced **odd**, a *physical* 1.35 mm window, so 9 voxels at 0.15 mm, 11 at 0.12 mm, **17 at 0.08 mm**.
  `dark = clip(local_median − x, 0, None) · tissue`, normalised by its 99.5th percentile inside tissue.
  Speed guard: when `x.size > 4e7` and `size >= 7`, the median is computed at half resolution with
  `size//2 | 1` and zoomed back (order 1) — a `scipy.ndimage.median_filter` with a 9³ footprint on 100 M+
  voxels is hours, and a local median is a low-frequency field, so half resolution is exact enough.
  **This map is computed in RAM inside `register.py` and never written to disk.** Do not confuse it with
  `work/<SUBJ>/mri_vessels.npy`, which is the **manual** MRI vessel label loaded from
  `--mri-vessels …label-vessels_dseg.nii.gz`, thresholded `> 0`, and used for **evaluation only**. Conflating
  the two would make the vessel evaluation circular.
- `oct_vessel_mask(oct_lvl, tissue_lvl, q=99.0, …)`: Frangi dark-tube vesselness, then **the top 1 % inside
  tissue** via `kthvalue(int(q/100 · tissue.sum()))`. Then `density_on_grid` pools the binary mask by
  `pool = max(1, round(VOX_O·1000 / sp_v.mean()))` (6 for a 24 µm vessel level onto a 0.15 mm target, 4 for a
  40 µm level), samples it onto the target grid, divides by the 99.5th percentile inside the target mask, and
  clamps to `[0,1]`. **The density is the operative object; the binary segmentation is only an intermediate.**
- `vascular_refine` then builds `FM = cat([FM2, mri_v])`, `FO = cat([FO2, oct_v])` and runs an **affine**
  `Refiner.refine` with `chan_w = [1, 1, w]`, coarse-to-fine over `factors = (2, 1)`, 300 iterations each,
  `reg = 0.5`, `clamp = 0.3`, on a box `bc ± BOX` where `BOX = BLOCK_R + 8.0` mm clipped to the feature region.
  Eight restarts around `T_struct` — rotation `U(3°, 8°)`, translation `U(−2.5, 2.5)` mm, log-scale
  `U(−0.1, 0.1)` on all three axes, refined with `factors = (4, 2, 1)` — count as converged at
  `corner_mean_mm < 0.3`.

#### 5.4.6 Sub-decision (c): at what physical scale, and the calibration that must not be skipped

`crop_final_v12 / v24 / v48 / final2` — the same run with different OCT vessel maps:

| OCT vessel source | vessel-channel NCC | depth stretch | vessel median / f150 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| own Frangi @ **12 µm** | **0.007** | 1.089 | 227.5 / 0.349 |
| own Frangi @ 24 µm | 0.092 | 1.110 | 206.7 / 0.392 |
| own Frangi @ **48 µm** (shipped) | 0.142 | 1.146 | 179.0 / 0.440 |
| DANDI manual `ves_seg` @ 12 µm → density | 0.159 | 1.184 | 166.8 / 0.469 |

At 12 µm, **Frangi finds speckle, not vessels** (`EXPLAINER_zh.md` §5). The scales are therefore set as
*physical* lumen diameters — `sig_um = (24, 36, 53, 72, 106) µm` in `prep_subject.py`, converted to voxels per
dataset (I46 at 24 µm: `[1.0, 1.5, 2.21, 3.0, 4.42]`) — the vessel level is pooled to
`kv = max(1, ceil(vessel_level_um/sp − 1e-6))`, i.e. **never finer than requested** (24 µm from 12 µm data,
40 µm from 20 µm data), and the density is pooled to ~48 µm before being sampled onto the 0.15 mm grid.

**An implementation detail that is really a correctness requirement.** `features.frangi_gamma` calibrates
Frangi's structureness constant `c` **once for the whole volume**, from 6 strided full-resolution slabs
(`nsl = clip(20e6 // (H·W), 4, 8)` slices per slab at `linspace(0, D−nsl, 6)`). For I46 the result is
`[21.96, 26.19, 27.30, 28.04, 26.10]` for the five sigmas. With `gamma=None` each processing chunk computes its
own `c` from its own `max(S)`, so a z-slab containing a bright artefact is normalised differently from a quiet
one, and the "vessel density" acquires **striping at the chunk boundaries** — a false periodic structure along
exactly the axis whose scale we are trying to measure. **This is the single most dangerous latent bug in the
pipeline**, and the calibration pass exists to prevent it. Anyone refactoring the vessel path must keep it.

#### 5.4.7 Does it work? Four confirmations — the fourth carrying a caveat — then the failures

1. **It reaches the annotation ceiling.** I46, scored against the **DANDI manual OCT `ves_seg`** — the honest
   channel, because `vessels_own` is the channel the stage optimises and is therefore optimistic: median
   **264.7 → 166.7 µm**, f150 **0.283 → 0.473**, against a ±3 mm random-shift control of ~352 µm / f300 0.43.
   The full-fit oracle ceiling is f150 **0.466** and the cross-validated held-out ceiling is **0.42**. We reach
   **0.473** — at or slightly above the ceiling of a single-voxel line annotation.
2. **Scrambling controls kill it.** `test_own_vessels.json`: flipping the OCT vessel density along depth gives
   269.5 µm / f150 0.269; permuting its k-slices gives 266.2 µm / 0.275. Both collapse to T0's 276.5 / 0.254.
   **The gain is geometric correspondence, not extra degrees of freedom.**
3. **Three independent sources agree on the number.** The authors' hand-drawn-vessel affine has largest-axis
   scale **1.17419** (`results/mri2oct/affine.lta`); an oracle affine fitted to those same manual annotations
   in *our* frame gives **1.177** on the depth axis; the sibling sidecars' depth/in-plane ratio is **1.1667**.
   Our fully automatic channel lands at **1.14–1.24** depending on weight, **1.219** shipped. That is agreement
   at the ±0.05 level on a quantity the structural objective cannot measure. **Do not overclaim it as
   three-decimal agreement**, and do not present it as a registration error — the authors' affine is not a
   sub-millimetre ground truth (different world conventions, no OCT world coordinates in the OME-XML, and the
   561-vs-627 `ves_seg` slice ambiguity).
4. **The reverse test, with a qualification that must never be dropped.** I55's sidecar records the *correct*
   anisotropic spacing (14/12/12 µm). Its depth `stretch_ijk[0]` is **0.913** — essentially no correction —
   and the vascular stage moves the block only **0.334 mm** (corner mean, rotation 1.15°, 8/8 restarts within
   0.3 mm). **The channel fires when there is something to correct and stays quiet when there is not.**
   (Several docs say I55 "needs only a 1.10 depth stretch". Wrong: 1.097 is `stretch_ijk[1]`, the in-plane j
   axis. Index 0 is depth, and it is 0.913.)

   **I55 is not a clean null, and it must not be presented as one.** Compute the quantity the experiment is
   actually about — depth scale divided by in-plane scale — from I55's *structural* column scales in
   `work/runs/I55_otsu/result.json`, `0.919927 / mean(1.062646, 1.084156)`, and it comes out at **0.8570**.
   `6/7 = 0.8571`. To better than 0.02 % I55's recovered anisotropy is the exact **inverse** of the
   `7/6 = 1.1667` factor that I46's sidecar is supposed to be missing. Either the same metadata convention is
   off on I55 in the opposite direction, or it is a coincidence; nothing on disk decides which `[OPEN]`. Use
   I55 as the null control — the argument above survives — but state this number when you do. A reviewer who
   divides the two columns will find it, and it is far easier to raise than to answer.

Bonus, and a neat second-order demonstration: the `ves_seg` depth-offset ambiguity (561 vs 627 slices, i.e.
offset 0 or 66) is *only decidable after* the vascular stage — `zoff0` 166.8 µm / f150 0.469 vs `zoff66`
301.9 / 0.187. Before it, the structural rows invert the answer (276 vs 245 µm). A wrong depth scale makes a
depth-offset test undecidable.

**The honest caveats, all of which must travel with the story:**

- **[UNVERIFIED]** In `scale_profiles.json` the *vessel* metric responds strongly on the **k** axis (f150
  0.254 → 0.317 at s = 1.10) and **not** on the i/depth axis (f150 stays 0.23–0.26). The pipeline's vascular
  stage stretches **i**, and that is what moves the vessel score end to end. Single-axis probes about the block
  centre and a full 12-DOF affine are not the same experiment, so this is plausibly axis coupling — but the raw
  i-axis column does not, on its own, show the vessel metric preferring a depth stretch. **To settle it:**
  re-run `scale_probe.py` starting from the *final* transform and report the i-axis profile of the
  **vessel-channel NCC**, not the mixed NCC.
- **The channel fails on our own data, and the failure is instructive.** On the I58 brainstem pair,
  `vascular.ncc_channels = [0.0013, 0.1844, 0.0055]` — the vessel channel scores **0.0055**. The stage moved
  the block 2.652 mm, **0/8** restarts returned within 0.3 mm, and it consumed **4 778.4 s of the 5 244.0 s**
  run. Cause: the serial-section seam artefacts are dark and tube-like, so the Frangi dark-tube detector fires
  on them — **4 534 410 "vessel" voxels** from the top 1 %. The "vessel density" is a map of the sectioning
  grid, not of the vasculature. `--vascular off` for that pair; `xiangrui_I58bs_novasc` (362.3 s total) is the
  reported run. **The general lesson: the vessel channel assumes the OCT's high-frequency content is anatomy.
  Where it is instrumentation, the channel inverts from the method's best idea into its most expensive
  liability.**
- I38 (7/8 restarts, vessel NCC 0.053), I56 (0/8, 0.020) and I62 (1/8, 0.003) show the same weakness at 35 µm
  sampling on large slabs. **The vascular restart count is the honest health indicator for this stage**: 8/8 on
  I46 and I55, near zero on everything doubtful.
- Cost: the vascular stage, not the search, dominates wall clock. I38 spends 5 696.8 s of 7 864.1 s (72 %) in
  it; the brainstem pair spent 4 778.4 s of 5 244.0 s (91 %) making the result worse.

---

### 5.5 Why affine, and not a non-rigid model

**The obvious objection to 12 DOF:** tissue deforms. Blocks are cut, they relax, they are mounted. Surely a
free-form deformation would fit better? It would. The question is whether it should be allowed to.

**Both alternatives are implemented.** `nonrigid.py` works: a `[1,3,gz,gy,gx]` displacement grid in **mm along
MRI world axes**, evaluated by trilinear `grid_sample` in the block's normalised voxel coordinates, optimised
with Adam on the grid alone while `T` stays frozen, with a first-difference smoothness penalty and a magnitude
penalty. `run_demo_i46.py --nonrigid on` wires it in, wrapped in a `try/except` so it can never lose the affine
result. It was swept: `work/runs/nonrigid/nonrigid_stage.json`. The variant-by-variant table is canonical in
chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.10.7. Five numbers from it carry the whole argument: the
shipped **vascular affine** reaches 179.0 µm / f150 0.440; the best **label-free non-rigid** variant (5×8×8,
smoothness 1) reaches 172.7 µm / 0.458 with displacements of 0.116 mm mean / 0.355 mm max; the
best-regularised variant (5×8×8, smoothness 5) reaches 176.6 µm / 0.450 at 0.048 mm mean / 0.134 mm max;
removing the vessel channel from the non-rigid stage costs 191.1 µm / 0.413; and the **oracle** non-rigid,
fitted with manual annotations the method may never see, tops out at 159.8 µm / 0.480.

Four readings, in order of importance:

1. **The ceiling is 0.04 f150 away.** The *oracle* non-rigid — fitted with manual annotations the method may
   never see — reaches f150 0.480 against the shipped affine's 0.440. **There is at most 0.04 f150 of headroom
   left in any deformation model whatsoever on this data.** You are not choosing between affine and "much
   better"; you are choosing between affine and "at most 9 % better on one metric".
2. **The best label-free gain is +0.018 f150 and +0.015/+0.019 Dice** — real, reproducible, and small.
3. **The displacements are sub-voxel.** 0.048 mm mean / 0.134 mm max at the well-regularised setting, against
   an MRI voxel of 0.15 mm; the oracle non-rigid in `refine_validate.json` (row B2) is 0.100 mm mean /
   0.119 p95 / 0.124 max. **The residual deformation is smaller than the grid it would be estimated on.**
   Physically that makes sense: both volumes are the *same fixed specimen*, the OCT is block-face imaging of a
   still-embedded block rather than of freely relaxing sections, and the dominant geometric error was never
   tissue deformation — it was a linear stack-spacing error (§5.4).
4. **The vessel channel carries the non-rigid stage too.** Removing it: 176.6 → 191.1 µm, f150 0.450 → 0.413.
   The non-rigid stage is not an alternative to the vascular stage; it is a small extra on top of it.

Cost/benefit is the stated reason for shipping affine only, and the authors independently concluded the same
for MRI↔OCT (their SVF stage exists in `mri2oct_nonlin.sh` but the paper says it is unnecessary for this pair)
— an agreement worth stating in a lab meeting.

**The unstated reason is more important, and it is the argument to make if pressed. A free-form deformation
would hide the failures this project has not yet fixed.** Of the nine DANDI subjects, **I61** fails because the
MRI foreground mask admits the bath (§5.1.6); **DANDI-I58** has that same bath-heavy mask *and* no GM/WM
contrast to correlate, because the only acquisition for it is a 10° flip angle; **I48** is uncertain on a flat
search landscape, with a top1 − top2 margin of 0.0013; and **I57's failure has no explanation at all**
`[OPEN]` — its mask, its threshold and its valley ratio are all healthy. On any of those runs a deformation
field would happily improve the loss by warping the block into whatever is nearby, and the QC figure would
look *better*, not worse. An affine cannot do that: it has 12 parameters, and the block either
lands on the right anatomy or it does not. **v1's job was to establish whether the method finds the right place
at all, and a model that can absorb being in the wrong place is the wrong instrument for that question.** Once
the foreground problem is fixed, re-enabling the non-rigid stage is a fifteen-minute change — the code is
written, swept, and its ceiling measured.

---

### 5.6 Why no training, given that a U-Net was built and worked

This is the decision most likely to be challenged, so it carries the most evidence.

**What was built.** The learned branch is not a toy:

- `parser.py` — a 3-D U-Net (`chans=(16,32,64,128)`), 4 classes (`0 bg, 1 WM, 2 infragranular GM, 3
  supragranular GM`), CE(ignore_index = −1) + soft Dice on foreground classes, Adam + OneCycleLR, AMP fp16,
  sliding-window inference with **per-window z-scoring** (identical to training) and a tent blending kernel
  that never reaches zero.
- `synth.py` — a SynthSeg-style generator with domain randomisation tailored to *this* problem: multiplicative
  Gamma speckle (`k ~ U(2,25)`, OCT-like), a **sawtooth attenuation** with period `U(4,14)` voxels to mimic
  serial sectioning, random bias fields, anisotropic resolution loss, and random block cuts to simulate a
  field of view.
- `train_parser.py`, `parse_mri.py`, and a full `--features parser` branch in `register.py`.
- `distill_oct_parser.py` — cross-modal self-distillation of an *OCT* parser from the MRI parser through the
  current transform.

It works. `EXPLAINER_zh.md` §3.2 claims the parser reaches Dice 0.98 where labels exist. **[UNVERIFIED]** — no
artefact supports 0.98; the only whole-hemisphere parser Dice on disk is `logs/parse_I46.log`: **WM 0.485 /
GM 0.586**, and `work/runs/crop_parser_v1/result.json` records parser-class Dice 0.687/0.912 on a crop. The
0.98 is most likely a patch-level or in-label-box figure. **Do not quote it without re-deriving it.**

**The four reasons it is not shipped, in ascending order of finality.**

**1. It does not improve the registration.** Same subject, same everything else, `otsu` vs `parser`:

| | `I46_otsu` | `I46_parser` |
|---|---:|---:|
| search top1 / top2 | 0.7259 / 0.7039 | 0.7273 / 0.7215 |
| refined NCC | **0.7564** | 0.7218 |
| block centre (mm) | −5.53, 25.90, 8.51 | −5.55, 25.91, 8.53 |
| depth stretch struct → final | 1.026 → **1.219** | 1.032 → 1.217 |
| structural restarts | 9/12 | 8/12 |
| vascular restarts | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| wall clock | 1 124.7 s | 1 082.2 s |

**The two poses differ by 0.03 mm.** On the I46 crop ablation the untrained representation is also *better* at
the search: otsu top1 0.727 / refined 0.753 against parser 0.650 / 0.710, restarts 7/8 vs 5/8. A better
segmentation did not produce a better registration, which is itself informative: **the registration is limited
by the geometry the representation encodes (§5.4), not by the fidelity with which it encodes it.**

**2. Distillation makes the score look better without making the answer better.** Two rounds of it, in
`distill_log.json`; the round-by-round table is in **chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.10.8**.
The search becomes dramatically more decisive (0.708 → 0.874) and the final NCC hits 0.96 — but the
**registration barely moves** (0.51 mm, then 0.68 mm) and the vessel score **never gets past the structural
stage** (258–265 µm / f150 0.27–0.28, against T0's 276 / 0.254 and the vascular stage's 167 / 0.47). The high
scores are self-consistency: the metric is being distilled along with the parser. This is the single most
important cautionary result in the project — **an objective that a model was trained to make agree with itself
is not evidence of accuracy.** The trained OCT parser is preserved at `work/oct_parser_v1`.

**3. There is a sign the learned model does not know when it is wrong.** `parse_mri.py --auto-polarity` had to
decide GM-bright vs WM-bright with a **geometric** cue — "cortex borders the background/CSF, WM does not",
scored as `gm_near − wm_near` after a 7³ max-pool dilation of the predicted background — *because parser
confidence turned out not to be discriminative*. A network whose softmax cannot distinguish its own class
assignment from its inversion is not a component you want carrying a registration on an unseen specimen.

**4. It cannot run at all on the data the project exists for.** This is the decisive one, and it is C-nolabels.
`train_parser.py` requires `labels4.npy`, which comes from `--labels-wholehemi`, which is a **manual
whole-hemisphere segmentation**. Xiangrui's I58 brainstem pair has none. The next twenty specimens will have
none. **A method that needs a manual segmentation of the target modality in order to be trained has not removed
the annotation requirement — it has moved it upstream and made it more expensive.** The parser would also not
transfer without retraining: it is a cortical WM / infra-GM / supra-GM model and the target specimen is a
brainstem.

**The line to use**, from `TALK_2026-08-21.md`, and it is exactly right:

> I trained a 3D U-Net as a check and it gives the same registration, so v1 ships with no training.

The negative result is the contribution. Keeping the branch alive as `--features parser` is what makes the
claim checkable rather than a preference — a reviewer can run both.

**What would change the decision.** If the *foreground* problem (§5.1.6) were solved by a learned model rather
than by texture heuristics, that would be a different question — I61's failure, and half of DANDI-I58's, is a
failure of the *foreground* mask rather than of the WM/GM split, and I56's mask fails the same way without
costing it the search. (It would not help I57, whose failure is unexplained `[OPEN]`, nor I48, whose problem
is a flat search landscape.) A lightweight learned foreground/bath discriminator is a much narrower ask than a
learned parser, needs only coarse masks rather than layer labels, and is the one place where training is
plausibly worth its cost in v1.1.

---

### 5.7 Why physical units (mm / µm) everywhere instead of voxel units

**The problem.** The corpus spans **0.08, 0.12 and 0.15 mm** MRI and **12, 14, 20, 30×30×35 µm** OCT. A
parameter expressed in voxels means a different physical thing on each. Worse, it means a different thing
*silently* — the code runs, produces a number, and the number is wrong in a way no assertion catches. This is
not hypothetical; it is C-meta.

**The choice, made everywhere:**

| Constant | Physical value | Voxel value it becomes |
|---|---|---|
| Bias-field kernel (`otsu_two_class_lowmem`) | **σ = 10 mm** | 16.67 pooled voxels at 0.15 mm; 20.8 at 0.12 mm |
| MRI darkness window (`mri_dark_channel`) | **1.35 mm**, forced odd | 9 voxels @0.15, 11 @0.12, **17 @0.08** |
| Frangi lumen scales (`prep_subject.py`) | **24, 36, 53, 72, 106 µm** | I46 @24 µm: `[1.0, 1.5, 2.21, 3.0, 4.42]`; different on every dataset |
| Registration pyramid (`register.py LEVELS`) | **0.6 / 0.3 / 0.15 mm** | factors 4/2/1 on a 0.15 mm MRI, 5/2/1 on 0.12 mm |
| Structural registration level (`--target-mm`) | **0.15 mm** | per-axis integer pooling, then resample to an exactly isotropic grid |
| Vessel level (`--vessel-level-um`) | **24 µm**, never finer | `kv = ceil(24/sp)`: 24 µm from 12 µm data, 40 µm from 20 µm data |
| Search template | `n = ceil(2·radius/spacing) + 3` | 39 (I46) … 128 (I57) — derived from the block's bounding-sphere radius |
| NMS separation | **3.0 mm** and 10.0° | — |
| Refinement translation LR | **0.3 mm** | — |
| Restart perturbation | **±5 mm**, 5–30° (structural); **±2.5 mm**, 3–8° (vascular) | — |
| Convergence tolerance | **0.5 mm** (structural), **0.3 mm** (vascular) corner-mean on a **7 mm** lever | — |
| Evaluation vessel bands | **150 µm / 300 µm**; control shift **±3 mm** | — |
| EDT grid (`edt48`) | **48 µm** target, `k = round(48/spacing)` | k = 2 at 24 µm; **k = 1** at 40 µm |

Even the OCT world frame is physical: `layout_affine` builds a millimetre affine from three RAS letters and a
voxel size, and every inter-volume transform in the codebase is a **4×4 world→world matrix in mm**.
`sample_at_world` is the single sampling primitive — search, refinement, evaluation, output resampling and QC
all go through it — so there is exactly one place where a voxel↔world convention can be wrong, and
`selftest_search.py` exists to test that one place synthetically.

**What it buys.** *The same flags run on every dataset.* The DANDI subjects (0.12–0.15 mm MRI, 12–35 µm OCT)
and the brainstem pair (0.08 mm MRI, 20 µm OCT) were registered with identical parameters. That is the actual
claim of transferability. It also makes every constant **arguable**: "σ = 10 mm" invites the question "is the
coil bias field really smooth at 10 mm?", which is a physical question with a physical answer. "σ = 16.67
voxels" invites nothing.

**Two traps this creates, both real.**

**(a) The naming trap.** `oct_ves_dist48_own.npy` is *not* always a 48 µm grid: `k = max(1, round(48/sp))`, so
a 40 µm vessel level gives `k = 1` and the EDT sits on the 40 µm grid (the brainstem case). **Always trust the
companion `_affine.npy`, never the filename.** Physical units in the code, voxel-flavoured names in the
filesystem — pick one.

**(b) The physical constant can itself be wrong, and then the discipline gives you nothing.** The
slab-normalisation window (§5.1.7) is the case in point: `window = max(10, round(1200.0/sp_z))` justified in a
comment as "one section period at 12 µm", when the measured period is **33 slices / 0.396 mm** on I46 and
**12 slices / 0.420 mm** on I56 — wrong by ~3×. I46 survives by luck; I56 does not. **Physical units are
necessary but not sufficient: the physical quantity has to be measured from the data, not asserted from a
protocol description.**

**One place where a deliberately non-physical unit is right.** `transform_diff` uses a **fixed 7 mm** corner
half-extent regardless of the real block size. That is not an oversight — it makes `corner_mean_mm` a
*standardised lever-arm* metric, comparable between a 7.5 mm block and a 50 mm slab. The consequence must be
carried: the 0.5 mm and 0.3 mm convergence thresholds are on that standardised arm, **not** on the true block
corners, so on a 50 mm slab the true corner error at "0.5 mm converged" is larger.

---

### 5.8 The engineering that makes it run at all

Every item here exists because of C-scale: one RTX 4090 with 24 GB, whole-hemisphere MRIs of 0.77–1.43 G
voxels, and OCT stacks of 1–5 G voxels. None of it changes the method; all of it decides whether the method
runs.

#### 5.8.1 CPU-resident float16 MRI features

`features.otsu_two_class_lowmem` returns `np.float16` of shape `[2, D, H, W]` **on the CPU**, filled one z-slab
at a time (`zchunk = 64`, halo `pad = int(3·smooth_sigma_vox) + 1` so the blur is seamless across slab
boundaries; each slab goes to the GPU, is flattened/blurred/sigmoided, and comes back as `.half()`).

| Subject class | fp16 CPU features | fp32 GPU features (the naive alternative) |
|---|---:|---:|
| I46, 1280×1040×576 = 767 M voxels | 2 × 767 M × 2 B = **3.07 GB host RAM** | 6.1 GB device |
| 0.12 mm subjects, 1600×1400×640 = 1.43 G voxels | **5.7 GB host RAM** | 11.5 GB device |

`register.py`'s `MRIFeatures` never moves the full-resolution features to the GPU. Only two things reach the
device: `pooled(0.6)`, built by streaming `step = max(f, (64//f)·f)` input z-planes at a time (for I46 the
result is 320×260×144 × 2 channels × 4 B = **96 MB**), and `region(centre, half, level)`, a block-sized crop
for the 0.3 / 0.15 mm refinement sized `BLOCK_R + 6` mm (or `+ 12` mm for the restart refiners). The MRI and
its tissue mask are always opened `mmap_mode="r"` and never fully read.

**Without it:** an immediate CUDA OOM at feature construction on any whole-hemisphere subject — the 11.5 GB
float32 copy simply does not fit alongside the padded FFT buffers, the OCT pyramid and the Refiner point
lists. The float16 precision is harmless here: these are probabilities in `[0,1]`, and the NCC is computed
after an `astype(np.float32)` on the pooled or cropped slab.

#### 5.8.2 The gain trick in slab normalisation

When `oct_slab_normalize` is asked for `out_dtype = np.float16`:

```python
gain = 16384.0 / max(float(np.nanmedian(ref)), 1e-3)
cap  = 60000.0
```

and every slice is clipped to `[0, cap]` after scaling. This **pins the tissue median at 16384 whatever the
input's native units**, which gives (a) 3.66× headroom to fp16's maximum of 65504, so no slice can produce
`inf`, and (b) no denormal underflow for inputs whose native units are tiny.

Both cases occur in this project, which is why the trick is not paranoia:

| Input | Native tissue level | Gain | What breaks without it |
|---|---|---:|---|
| DANDI OME-TIFFs, uint16 | tissue median ~170 | ~96× (scaled **up**) | a dark slice with a large `scale[i]` can push the product past 65504 → `inf` → `NaN` propagating through the pooling and the Frangi Hessian |
| `I58_Brainstem_mus_Slice_full_20um_corr.nii.gz`, float µs | raw tissue threshold **9.6e-4** | ~1e7 | the volume lands in fp16 denormals and quantises to a handful of levels, destroying both the Otsu split and the Frangi vesselness downstream |

The in-code comment names only the overflow half; the denormal half is the one that matters for our own data.
The float16 output is also what makes the intermediate `octn` array affordable at all: I46's 627×1271×1230
stack is 1.96 GB in fp16 against 3.9 GB in fp32.

**Latent defect to know about:** `cap` is bound only inside the `out_dtype == np.float16` branch but read under
`if gain != 1.0`. Unreachable today (gain is exactly 1.0 when the branch is not taken), but a one-line change
to the gain formula turns it into a `NameError`.

#### 5.8.3 GPU slab budgeting

Every heavy loop has an explicit, *computed* slab size rather than a guessed constant:

| Where | Rule | Why, and what breaks without it |
|---|---|---|
| `features.frangi_dark_vesselness` / `frangi_gamma` | `chunk = 4_000_000` Hessian rows | the `[N,3,3]` Hessian is 9 floats/voxel = 36 B; 4 M rows = 144 MB plus eigen intermediates. At I46's 122 M-voxel 24 µm level an unchunked `H` alone is **4.4 GB**, on top of six 488 MB convolution outputs. |
| `vascular.frangi_chunked` | `zchunk = 24`, `overlap = 10` | six separable-convolution buffers per slab; the 10-voxel halo is discarded on write so the response is seamless. Without the halo the vesselness has visible slab seams — the same failure mode the `frangi_gamma` calibration prevents in amplitude. |
| `prep_subject.py` Frangi pass | `zc = clip(30e6 // (H·W) − 2·ov, 8, 64)`, halo `ov = ceil(3·max σ) + 1` | targets a **~30 M-voxel** GPU budget per slab, adjusted for the halo, hard-bounded to 8–64 z-planes so neither a very wide nor a very narrow stack breaks it. |
| `prep_subject.py` gamma calibration | `nsl = clip(20e6 // (H·W), 4, 8)` slices, 6 slabs at `linspace(0, D−nsl, 6)` | a ~20 M-voxel sample spanning the whole depth range — enough for a stable 99.9th percentile without loading the block. |
| `features.otsu_two_class_lowmem` | `zchunk = 64` + halo `3σ + 1` | the blur must be seamless across slabs, or the class map acquires horizontal seams. |
| `common.pool_mean_np` | `step = max(1, 64//kz)·kz` input z-planes | lets a memmapped 1 G-voxel OME-TIFF be pooled in a few hundred MB of host RAM. Without it, prep cannot open the raw stack at all. |
| `common.resample_to_grid` | `chunk = 8_000_000` points | bounds the temporary `[N,3]` world-point buffer at 96 MB. |
| `register.py` output resampling | z-slabs of 64 planes | a whole-block box at 0.08–0.12 mm is hundreds of millions of voxels; the brainstem `oct_in_mri_region.nii.gz` is 150 MB compressed. |
| `MRIFeatures.pooled` | `step = max(f, (64//f)·f)` | §5.8.1. |
| `vascular.mri_dark_channel` | half-resolution median when `size > 4e7` and `size >= 7` | a 9³ `scipy` median filter on 100 M+ voxels is hours of CPU; a local median is a low-frequency field, so half resolution plus order-1 zoom is exact enough. |

Explicit lifetime management does the rest inside `register.py`: `del mri_reg` immediately after the features
are built; `del s; torch.cuda.empty_cache()` after each search; the losing polarity's tensors deleted after the
choice; a large `del ref03, ref015, lvl015, PO, PMask, FO, trials, tr, PM06, PT06` before the vascular stage;
`del vmask` after the density; `del FM2v, FO2v, mri_v, oct_v` after the vascular refinement.

#### 5.8.4 Five numerical and structural safeguards that are not about memory

- **`var_floor` in the FFT search.** FFT-based sums are round-off-prone: computing `varI = SII − SI²/N` as a
  difference of two large FFT sums can go slightly negative or near zero in a nearly-constant window, and then
  `cov/√(varT·varI)` explodes and a flat region wins by numerical accident. `search.py.__init__` precomputes
  `var_floor[c] = I[c][tissue].var() · 0.02` and clamps `varI` at `var_floor[c]·N`. **2 % of the in-tissue
  global variance** is the statement "no window may claim to be 50× more uniform than the specimen as a
  whole". **Without it** the search returns a maximum in the flattest available region — which is, note, the
  same failure mode a bath-filled tissue mask produces (§5.1.6), reached by a different route.
- **Zero-padding by `pad = n//2 + 1` on all six sides**, with the affine origin shifted back accordingly, so a
  block sitting partly over the edge of a cropped MRI is still scored — the *overlap gate*, not the array
  bounds, decides admissibility. Essential for an already-cropped MRI like the brainstem pair. A hard
  `assert self.n <= every MRI grid dimension` catches the genuinely impossible case.
- **`self.tgrid` is built in world mm through the MRI grid's linear part `A_M[:3,:3]`**, not in the OCT's own
  axes. That is what makes the correlation index `u` directly convertible to a world translation
  (`pose_from`) on a possibly permuted or flipped MRI array, with no per-dataset bookkeeping — and therefore
  what keeps `--oct-layout` a purely arbitrary labelling.
- **`sym3x3_eigvals`** solves the 3×3 symmetric eigenproblem in closed form (trace/deviator/`acos`) rather
  than calling `torch.linalg.eigvalsh`, specifically to avoid cuSOLVER on 100 M+ matrices; `p1 < 1e-20`
  (already diagonal) falls back to sorting the diagonal.
- **`result.json` is written before the heavy outputs and again after them**, with identical content — an
  explicit guard so that a QC-figure or NIfTI-writing failure cannot lose a two-hour result. Small, and the
  kind of thing that only looks important the first time a run dies at step 5 of 6.

## 6. What we found, and what it means

Every number below was read from the JSON and log artefacts on the AutoDL box
(`ssh -o BatchMode=yes -p 49018 root@connect.westb.seetacloud.com`, tree
`~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration`, interpreter `/root/miniconda3/envs/octmri/bin/python`), not from any
prose summary. Where a prose document disagrees with a JSON, the JSON wins; the surviving disagreements are
listed in §6.14. Where a shipped document — `octreg/README.md`, `octreg/EXPLAINER_zh.md`, or a meeting note
under `meeting_recordings/` — disagrees with an artefact on disk, the artefact wins, and the correction is
stated inline so a successor can see what was wrong and why.

The rule this chapter follows, without exception: **no number appears without the claim it licenses and the
claim it does not.** A metric is a physical measurement of something specific. Most of the misreadings this
project is exposed to come from taking a metric that measures one thing and reading it as if it measured
accuracy.

---

### 6.1 The one-paragraph verdict

On **two** subjects of one public dataset (I46 and I55 of Costantini 2023, DANDI:000026), octreg v1 places an
OCT block into a whole hemisphere with no position prior and no labels, and two independent manual
annotations agree the placement is right at the **millimetre** scale. On **one** of those two (I46) a third,
finer annotation — the authors' hand-drawn OCT vessel segmentation — agrees at the **167 µm median** scale,
which is that annotation pair's own ceiling. On **our own data** (Xiangrui's I58 brainstem pair) the only
evidence that exists is a human looking at a checkerboard overlay plus a restart-stability count; **no numeric
residual has ever been computed for it**. Everything else in the corpus — the other seven DANDI subjects, most
of the Dice table, every restart count — either rests on a broken label mapping, on unverified visual QC, or
measures something other than accuracy. The strongest single result in the project is not a Dice value: it is
that a scale factor along the block's serial-sectioning axis, which the structural objective **provably cannot
see**, was recovered automatically at ≈1.22 and lands on the value three independent human-annotated sources
put at 1.167–1.177.

Honest scorecard on the nine DANDI subjects: **2 confirmed, 3 unresolved, 1 undecidable, 3 failed.**
Not "5 of 9 correct".

---

### 6.2 What each headline number is physically made of

Read this table before reading any other table in this chapter. Definitions come from
`octreg/octreg/evaluate.py` and `octreg/scripts/register.py`.

| Metric | Exact definition | Can detect | **Cannot** detect | Field |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dice_WM` / `dice_GM` | the OCT's **own Otsu two-class map** vs the authors' manual labels resampled through `T`, restricted to voxels the OCT calls tissue. `lab==1 → WM`, `lab∈{2,3} → GM`. Denominator is the full OCT class count, so it collapses toward 0 when label coverage is low | gross class inversion inside the block; catastrophic non-overlap (via `frac_on_mri_labels`) | *where* the block is. Proven: **0.857 WM Dice at a pose 71.1 mm from the truth** (§6.5.3) | `evaluation.{structural,final}.gmwm` |
| `frac_on_mri_labels` | fraction of registered OCT-tissue voxels landing on **any** nonzero label | whether the block left the labelled hemisphere | anything finer. I48 scores 0.575 while sitting 50.7 mm from its own annotations | same |
| `vessels_vesseg.median_um` / `frac_within_150um` | manual **MRI** vessel voxels → `inv(T)` → trilinear lookup in a precomputed EDT (µm) of the DANDI manual **OCT** `ves_seg.tif`, on a 48 µm grid. Only points inside the EDT box are scored | sub-millimetre residual, including the depth-axis scale | anything about points outside the block; anything at all if `n_inside < 20`, where it returns `{"n_inside": n}` and every downstream field is `null` | `evaluation.*.vessels_vesseg` |
| `vessels_own.*` | identical, but against **our own Frangi** OCT segmentation | — | **this is the channel the vascular stage optimises.** It is a *training* metric and must never be quoted as accuracy | `evaluation.*.vessels_own` |
| `random_shift_control` | the **same** points, translated by **one** `uniform(−3,+3) mm` 3-vector per draw, 30 draws, `seed=0`. Rotation, scale, shear and mirror of the accepted solution are **kept** | that the metric is not flat over a ±3 mm neighbourhood of the accepted pose | that a different pose elsewhere would score worse. **It is a local control, not a random-placement control** (§6.7) | same block |
| `evaluation.restarts.n_converged` (`x/12`) | 12 perturbations of the **already-accepted** pose (`rot U(5°,30°)`, `trans U(−5,+5) mm` per component), each re-refined `0.3 mm rigid(150 it) → 0.3 mm affine(150) → 0.15 mm affine(150)`; "converged" iff `corner_mean_mm < 0.5` on a fixed **7 mm** half-extent lever arm. **The 0.6 mm exhaustive search is never re-run** | the width and uniqueness of the refinement basin around the pose the search already chose | whether that basin is the right one. On this dataset it is **anti-correlated** with correctness (§6.9) | `register.py:170–179` |
| `vascular.restarts.n_within_0.3mm` (`x/8`) | 8 perturbations (`rot U(3°,8°)`, `trans U(−2.5,2.5) mm`, `log-scale U(−0.1,0.1)`), threshold 0.3 mm | whether the vessel objective has a basin at all at this pose | same limitation | `register.py:~200` |
| `search.top1 / top2` | best vs best **distinct** masked-NCC over 16 000 orientations × all translations at 0.6 mm | *decisiveness*. A ratio near 1.000 means the landscape is flat and the answer is arbitrary | correctness. I61 has a 1.2 % margin and is 95.7 mm wrong | `search` |
| `refine.final_ncc` | masked NCC of the two-class maps at 0.15 mm, after the affine cascade, at the accepted pose. It is also the field that decides class polarity | how well a 12-DOF affine fits *at the pose the search already chose*; **within** one subject it separates the two polarity branches cleanly | **correctness, across subjects.** I61 scores 0.5020 and I57 0.5121 and both are wrong; I62 scores 0.2842 and is the strongest of the three unresolved subjects. No absolute threshold separates them — see the box at the end of §6.3.1 | `refine` |
| `vascular.ncc_channels[2]` | NCC of the vessel channel at the final pose | **the only quantity in the pipeline that separates a correct pose from a 71 mm-wrong one** (0.301 vs −0.035) | anything on a specimen where the OCT "vessels" are section seams — brainstem: 0.0055 | `vascular` |
| `stretch_ijk[0]` | `‖T[:3,:3] · R_axes[:,0]‖`, the linear scale along the **OCT depth / serial-sectioning axis**. **Not** the same ordering as `final_transform.column_scales`, where the same number sits at index 2 | a systematic depth-spacing error | — | `evaluation.*.stretch_ijk` |
| `transform_diff(...).rotation_deg` | geodesic angle between polar rotation factors | **nothing, when either transform is mirrored** — the field is broken (§6.14.1) | | everywhere |

Two structural facts that bound every label-based claim in this chapter:

1. The evaluator collapses the authors' three-class `infrasupra` scheme (`1` WM, `2` infragranular GM,
   `3` supragranular GM) to WM/GM, and the OCT side is a two-class Otsu map. **Nothing in this project
   demonstrates laminar alignment.** The labels carry the layer boundary; the evaluation throws it away.
2. `vessel_distance_stats` needs **≥ 20** annotation points inside the OCT vessel-EDT box. Below that every
   downstream field is `null`, printed as `nan` in logs and `—` in `summary.md`. **A dash in a vessel column
   is missing data, not a zero** (§6.8).

### 6.3 Master table — every completed run and its verdict

`work/runs/` holds **33** `result.json` files. Two directories exist with **no** `result.json` because the run
failed: `work/runs/I56_parser/` and `work/runs/crop_final_inv/`.

#### 6.3.1 v1 subject runs (`register.py`, whole-hemisphere search, no position prior)

All nine DANDI subjects ran with identical flags:
`--features otsu --n-rot 8000 --topk 24 --min-overlap 0.85 --n-restarts 12 --vascular on --vascular-w 2.0
--vascular-reg 0.5 --vascular-clamp 0.3 --ls-clamp 0.15 --sh-clamp 0.15 --reg 2.0 --seed 0 --oct-wm-bright auto`
(`I46_parser` differs only in `--features parser`). 16 000 orientations = 8 000 rotations × {normal, mirrored}.

Note on `--oct-wm-bright auto`: it is **not** `register.py`'s default (`default="no"`); the shipped wrapper
`run_subject.sh` hard-codes it, which is why every DANDI run executes the whole search **twice**, once per
class polarity. A successor calling `register.py` directly gets single-polarity behaviour silently, so read
`octreg/scripts/run_subject.sh` before comparing any timing or any result against a DANDI run.

**‡ I38's structural depth scale of 0.861 is not a measurement — it is the clamp bound.** `--ls-clamp 0.15`
confines every per-axis log-scale to `[exp(−0.15), exp(+0.15)] = [0.8607, 1.1618]`, and 0.861 is that lower
bound to three decimals. The structural stage pushed the depth axis as far down as it was permitted to go and
stopped there, so the label-free optimum is *at most* 0.861 and may lie well below it. Read the cell as
"saturated, true value unknown", never as "the block is 14 % thinner than declared", and carry the same flag
wherever this number is tabulated. (I38's **final** 0.808 sits inside the looser `--vascular-clamp 0.3` band
`[0.741, 1.350]` and is not clamp-saturated.)

Every cell above was read back from `work/runs/<run>/result.json` on the compute server, and three columns
disagree with figures that circulate in the shipped prose. The restart counts are the
`evaluation.restarts.n_converged` fields — in particular **I57 is 10/12, not 12/12**; two of its restarts miss
the 0.5 mm gate at 0.536 mm. The mirror column is `final_transform.mirror`: **6 of 9 are mirrored — I38, I46,
I48, I56, I58, I62** — and I55, I57, I61 and both brainstem runs are not, against the five-name list in
`octreg/README.md`. The wall times are `total_seconds`: **18.7 – 131.1 min** across the nine otsu runs, not the
"15–40 min" that `octreg/README.md` and `octreg/EXPLAINER_zh.md` quote.

The **margin ratio** column is `top1/top2` computed here from the two verified scores. It is the single most
useful early-warning field in `result.json` and §6.9.4 discusses what a gate built on it would and would not
catch.

> **The refined-NCC column must never be turned into a pass mark.** Read it down the rows: **I61 scores 0.5020
> and I57 scores 0.5121, and both are wrong — I61 by 95.7 mm — while I62 scores 0.2842 and is the strongest of
> the three subjects nobody has been able to fault. Any acceptance rule of the form "`refine.final_ncc` ≥ 0.35
> means the result is good" accepts both of the worst failures in the corpus and rejects a plausibly correct
> subject.** The absolute level of the refined NCC is set by how much structure the MRI side happens to
> contain: a bath-heavy 0.12 mm hemisphere whose tissue mask failed scores *high*, because a large smooth
> field correlates smoothly with almost anything (§6.9.2). What is comparable across subjects is the **margin**
> `top1/top2`, not the level. Attach this paragraph to any proposed numeric NCC criterion — it is the reason no
> such criterion appears among the reject gates in §6.9.4.

| I56_otsu | GM-bright (False) | True: 0.2835 / 0.2476 | 9.64, 8.43, 65.03 | 106³ | 802.8 |
| I62_otsu | WM-bright (True) | False: 0.2583 / 0.2339 | −8.81, 1.42, 53.17 | 105³ | 764.7 |
| I48_otsu | WM-bright (True) | False: 0.2422 / 0.2503 | −5.02, 19.81, −49.33 | 104³ | 762.7 |
| I57_otsu | WM-bright (True) | False: 0.3625 / 0.3335 | 30.70, 33.51, 18.51 | 128³ | 1 010.3 |

| xiangrui_I58bs | WM-bright (True) | False: 0.1170 / 0.0851 | 4.22, −6.50, 21.31 | 93³ | 44.8 |

Two things to read off this table. First, **the polarity decision is made by the refined NCC, not the search
score** — for I48 the losing branch actually *refines higher* (0.2503 vs the winner's 0.2584 is a 0.008 gap,
and its search score is only 0.015 below), which is one of the reasons I48 is "uncertain". Second, search cost
scales with the **MRI template grid**, not with the block: the brainstem crop (0.08 mm MRI, 0.6 mm grid
42×61×61) is 6.7× faster than I46's whole hemisphere, and I57's 0.12 mm hemisphere is 3.4× slower than I46's
0.15 mm one.

On timing, the figure that circulates in the prose docs — "a whole hemisphere search takes 150 s" — is a
rounding of a **real** 153.4 s / 153.7 s measurement, but one made by a *different entry point with different
features*: `run_demo_i46.py --features mixed`, whose MRI channels are the trained 3D-U-Net parser's
probabilities. The label-free shipped path costs **298.9 s** per polarity on the identical subject and grid, and
**597.8 s** with the `--oct-wm-bright auto` that every DANDI run used. Quoting 154 s
under a "label-free" heading attributes a parser-assisted runtime to the training-free pipeline. The honest
sentence is: *an exhaustive 16 000-orientation search over all translations costs 45 s on a 0.08 mm brainstem
crop and 299 s on a 0.15 mm whole hemisphere with label-free Otsu features (154 s with parser-probability
features); the shipped wrapper runs it once per class polarity, so budget 598 s of search for a whole
hemisphere. Whole-corpus single-branch range 44.8 s – 1 010.3 s.*

**Per-branch cost, whole corpus.** This is the canonical timing table for the project; every other statement
about runtime in this document is a summary of it. All figures are `search.seconds`,
`polarity_trials.{False,True}.seconds`, `vascular.seconds` and `total_seconds` from
`work/runs/<run>/result.json`, on an otherwise idle RTX 4090.

| subject | s per 4 000 orientations | full 16 000 search, one polarity | polarity trial ① / ② | vascular stage | total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| I46 | 75 | **298.9** | 388.4 / 388.4 | 158.3 | 1 124.7 |
| I55 | 107 | 430.9 | 518.9 / 528.0 | 18.8 | 1 278.8 |
| I58 (DANDI) | 152 | 604.8 | 712.4 / 711.2 | 54.0 | 1 789.8 |
| I61 | 177 | 707.5 | 825.4 / 826.5 | 52.8 | 2 019.7 |
| I38 | 182 | 727.6 | 863.1 / 866.9 | **5 696.8** | **7 864.1** |
| I48 | 191 | 762.7 | 892.5 / 889.8 | 87.2 | 2 222.9 |
| I62 | 191 | 764.7 | 905.3 / 901.3 | 84.7 | 2 242.6 |
| I56 | 201 | 802.8 | 928.9 / 926.1 | 81.8 | 2 263.2 |
| I57 | 254 | **1 010.3** | 1 167.1 / 1 166.7 | 130.0 | 2 831.3 |
| I58 brainstem, vascular **on** | 11 | 44.8 | 156.0 / 131.2 | **4 778.4** | 5 244.0 |
| I58 brainstem, vascular **off** (the reported run) | 11 | 45.1 | 137.7 / 139.9 | — | **362.3** |

Three things to read off it. **The stage that dominates wall clock is not the search — it is the vascular
stage.** I38 spent 5 696.8 s of 7 864.1 s (72 %) there, and the brainstem run spent 4 778.4 s of 5 244.0 s
(91 %) there **and made the result worse**; search is only 8–38 % of wall clock. **Search cost scales with the
MRI template grid, not with the block**, which is why I57's 0.12 mm hemisphere costs 3.4× I46's 0.15 mm one.
And there are exactly **two levers**: pin `--oct-wm-bright yes|no` once the protocol polarity is known, which
removes a whole polarity branch, and switch the vascular stage off when its channel NCC is near zero, which on
the brainstem pair took 5 244 s down to 362 s.

#### 6.3.4 A caveat that applies to the whole table

**Five of the nine headline runs predate the current source tree.** Compare mtimes on the compute server:
`register.py` has
mtime 2026-08-20 23:30, `prep_subject.py` 15:11, `vascular.py` 19:31; the `result.json` mtimes are I46 10:23,
I38 19:48, I55 20:18, I56 21:07, I62 22:01 — all *before* the current `register.py` — versus I61 00:03,
I48 01:01, I57 01:50, I58 04:24 after it. **I46 is the only subject whose prep (`work/I46/prep.json`, 10:04)
and registration both predate the current code.** Concretely: `work/runs/I46_otsu/result.json` has
`overlap_gate: null`, because the adaptive overlap gate did not exist when it ran. The tree is unversioned —
`/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project` is not a git repository at all — so the revision that produced
`I46_otsu` is **unrecoverable**. A successor re-running I46 with today's code should **expect the numbers to
differ**, and should not treat a mismatch as a regression until the two configurations have been compared.
`[OPEN]`

### 6.4 Per-subject detail — the five subjects marked "correct"

#### 6.4.1 I46 — the only subject with both vessel and label evidence

Data: MRI `sub-I46_ses-MRI_flip-2_VFA` (FlipAngle 20°), 1280×1040×576 @ 0.15 mm. OCT 627×1271×1230, sidecar
spacing **12/12/12 µm** (`work/I46/prep.json`), pooled to 49×100×97 @ 0.15 mm. Our own Frangi vessel
segmentation: 491 472 voxels = 1.24 % of the 48 µm grid. DANDI `ves_seg.tif`: 561 z-slices, 0.904 % of the same
grid. Actual block size recomputed from `prep.json` is **7.5 × 15.3 × 14.8 mm** (≈8.8 mm deep at the recovered
≈14 µm spacing) — the "15×15×7 mm" quoted in several docs is wrong; always recompute from
`oct.shape_native × oct.spacing_um_zyx`.

Vessel distance, manual MRI vessels → nearest OCT vessel (µm; `n` = points landing inside the OCT EDT box):

| channel | stage | n_inside | median | p75 | p95 | f≤150 µm | f≤300 µm | ±3 mm control (30×): mean median / best-of-30 / mean f300 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `vessels_own` (our Frangi) | structural | 4 040 | 173.0 | 596.6 | 2 228.7 | 0.4384 | 0.6606 | 214.6 / 173.1 / 0.6164 |
| `vessels_own` | final | 4 999 | 122.8 | 594.6 | 3 036.4 | 0.5585 | 0.6727 | 212.4 / 177.2 / 0.6189 |
| `vessels_vesseg` (DANDI manual OCT seg) | structural | 4 040 | **264.7** | 679.3 | 2 288.9 | **0.2829** | 0.5502 | 354.4 / 286.2 / 0.4278 |
| **`vessels_vesseg`** | **final** | **4 999** | **166.7** | 728.5 | 3 165.8 | **0.4733** | 0.6145 | 352.4 / 284.8 / 0.4328 |

**`vessels_vesseg` is the honest channel for I46.** `vessels_own` is the very map the vascular stage maximises
against; the tell that it is a training metric is that its own ±3 mm control (212–215 µm) sits almost on top of
its structural-stage registered value (173.0 µm). Never quote 122.8 µm as accuracy.

Dice vs manual labels (`labels4` whole-hemisphere plus BA):

| stage | frac_on_mri_labels | Dice WM | Dice GM | confusion (rows = OCT class 0/1/2, cols = MRI none/WM/GM) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| structural | 0.9850 | 0.8010 | 0.8318 | `[[0,0,0],[2456,75484,12418],[573,22642,88095]]` |
| final | 0.9987 | **0.8026** | **0.8251** | `[[0,0,0],[266,76277,13815],[0,23444,87866]]` |

Of the OCT-WM voxels that land on a label, **84.7 %** land on MRI WM. That is the number that makes the class
correspondence unambiguous — far more informative than the Dice value itself.

Restarts: structural 9/12, with three outliers at 6.5–15.5 mm corner mean; vascular 8/8 within 0.3 mm (corner
means 0.004–0.026 mm). The vascular stage moved the block **0.733 mm centre, 1.524 mm corner mean, 2.480 mm
corner max** relative to the structural solution; its per-channel NCC is `[0.729, 0.730, 0.296]`, the third
entry being the vessel channel.

Depth scale `stretch_ijk[0]`: **1.026 → 1.219** (a factor of 1.188 applied by the vascular stage). §6.11 is
entirely about why this number, not the Dice, is the strongest result in the project.

**Independent corroboration from a second feature path.** `I46_parser` uses the trained 3D-U-Net MRI parser
probabilities instead of the training-free Otsu features and lands at block centre
−5.55, 25.91, 8.53 mm against `I46_otsu`'s −5.53, 25.90, 8.51 mm — the two centres agree to **0.03 mm** — and
recovers depth scale 1.217 against 1.219. Two quite different MRI representations converge on the same pose
and the same anomalous depth scale. That is a real, if weak, internal consistency check: it rules out the
possibility that the pose or the depth stretch is an artefact of one particular feature construction.

**What I46 licenses.** That on this subject the block is placed correctly at the millimetre scale (BA labels,
§6.4.3), that its two-class map agrees with manual labels at a level comparable to the authors' own two
annotations of the same tissue disagreeing with each other, and that the sub-millimetre residual against an
independent manual OCT vessel annotation is at that annotation pair's ceiling. It does **not** license a target
registration error, a laminar claim, or any statement about the other eight subjects.

#### 6.4.2 I55 — the independent confirmation, and the depth-scale control

Data: MRI `flip-2` (20°), 1280×1040×576 @ 0.15 mm. OCT 1573×1768×1772 @ **14/12/12 µm** — the correct
anisotropy, declared in the sidecar. Block 22.0 × 21.2 × 21.3 mm. Own Frangi vessels 3 479 888 voxels (2.06 %).
**No DANDI `ves_seg` exists for this subject**, so `vessels_vesseg` is absent and the only vessel channel is
the training metric.

| channel | stage | n_inside | median µm | p75 | p95 | f≤150 | f≤300 | control: mean median / best / mean f300 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `vessels_own` | structural | 7 722 | 173.2 | 449.6 | 2 918.8 | 0.4490 | 0.6755 | 232.2 / 154.3 / 0.5889 |
| `vessels_own` | final | 7 817 | 140.9 | 395.2 | 2 869.5 | 0.5239 | 0.7041 | 227.8 / 153.1 / 0.5961 |

| stage | frac_on_mri_labels | Dice WM | Dice GM | confusion |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| structural | 0.9796 | 0.9217 | 0.9283 | `[[0,0,0],[0,601866,39458],[32916,62762,875376]]` |
| final | 0.9809 | 0.9208 | **0.9298** | `[[0,0,0],[24,596041,45259],[30736,57319,882999]]` |

**93.8 %** of on-label OCT-WM voxels land on MRI WM.

The strongest single piece of evidence in the whole project is not in either table above: **59.0 % of the
Broca's-area label voxels fall inside the registered block, and the BA label centroid is 7.8 mm from the block
centre** — from an annotation the method never sees, on a subject whose label mapping is provably lossless
(§6.5.2). Compare I46: 12.8 % of BA inside, centroid 9.6 mm away.

**Depth scale 0.920 → 0.913** — essentially 1.0 — and the vascular stage moves the block only **0.334 mm**
corner mean, with 8/8 vascular restarts within 0.3 mm and vascular NCC channels `[0.766, 0.717, 0.083]`. This
is the negative control that turns I46's 1.219 into evidence rather than a coincidence (§6.11.3).

**The caveat travels with that sentence, every time it is used.** I55 is **not a clean null**. Its
*structural* `stretch_ijk` is `[0.920, 1.084, 1.063]`, i.e. a recovered depth-to-in-plane anisotropy of
**0.8570** — and **6/7 = 0.857143**. That is the exact inverse, to four decimal places, of the 7/6 = 1.1667
factor I46's sidecar is supposed to be missing: the subject whose job is to demonstrate "no correction
needed" recovers, on the same axis, the reciprocal of the correction. Two readings are open and the data
does not choose between them (§6.11.3). What survives that unexplained is the **vascular displacement** —
0.334 mm here against 1.524 mm on I46 — because it measures how far the vessel channel had to move the
block, not the scale itself. Never quote I55 as the negative control without stating the 0.8570. `[OPEN]`

Correction to carry: several shipped documents state "I55 needs only a 1.10 depth stretch". `stretch_ijk` in
`work/runs/I55_otsu/result.json` is `[0.913, 1.097, 1.084]` and **index 0 is depth**; the 1.097 is the in-plane
**j** axis. The argument survives, the sentence does not.

Where labels *do* exist under these slabs (61 % and 45 % of the OCT tissue), the OCT WM class lands on MRI
**GM about twice as often** as on MRI WM. That is *below* chance, not a coverage artefact.

**So the "correct" verdict for I38, I56 and I62 rests entirely on visual inspection** of
`octreg/figures/fig_I38.png`, `fig_I56.png`, `fig_I62.png` and `work/runs/*/qc_vessels.png` — figures that were
generated by an AI agent and, per the 2026-08-23 meeting, **have not been human-verified**. Two independent
quantitative checks (manual MRI vessels, BA labels) point the other way, and for I38 and I56 a third (label
confusion) does too. **This is the single most important open question in the results and none of these three
may be reported as a success until it is resolved.** `[OPEN]` §6.8 gives the geometry, the competing
explanations, and the test that settles it.

### 6.5 Dice 0.80 / 0.92 — what it licenses

#### 6.5.1 What the labels actually are

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| File | `derivatives/Labels/sub-XX/ses-MRI/anat/sub-XX_ses-MRI_space-EPIC_label-infrasupra_seg-wholehemi_dseg.nii.gz` |
| Classes | `1` WM, `2` infragranular GM, `3` supragranular GM |
| **How they were made** | **manual drawing on every 10th slice**, then **SmartInterpol** (`github.com/aleatzeni/SmartInterpol`) interpolation between the drawn contours, then manual touch-up (`derivatives/Labels/dataset_description.json`) |
| ⇒ implication | at 0.15 mm a human drew a contour every **1.5 mm**; roughly **90 % of the label volume is algorithmically interpolated** |
| Drawn on | the flip named in the sidecar `{"Source": ...}`. For I46 and I55 that **matches** the volume we registered against (`flip-2`, 20°). For I48, I57, I58 it does **not** |
| Annotation self-consistency `labels_agreement_wholehemi_vs_ba` — the authors' *two* label products of the *same* tissue | I46 **0.932**, I55 0.909, I38 0.900, I48 0.937, I56 0.882, I58 0.939, I61 0.940, **I57 0.671** |

That last row is the one to internalise. **The authors' own two annotations of I46 disagree with each other on
6.8 % of the BA voxels.** Our WM Dice against one of them is 0.803. The gap between 0.803 and 1.0 is not all
registration error; a meaningful part of it is the same kind of disagreement two human-plus-interpolated
annotations of the same brain show with each other.

#### 6.5.2 Coverage — which Dice values are computable at all

`prep_subject.py::map_labels_to_grid` derives the label→MRI axis permutation from the two affines. For the six
0.12 mm subjects that permutation is **wrong**: it pairs the label's 640-voxel axis against a 1400-voxel MRI
axis, so only 36–40 % of the MRI grid ever receives a label lookup. The bug is in
`octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py::map_labels_to_grid` and is carried as an open, unfixed bug in chapter 7,
Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us.

| subject | MRI voxel | label loss on mapping | MRI grid reachable | labels landing on MRI tissue | **Dice usable?** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **I46** | 0.15 mm | **0.0 %** | **100 %** | 99.94 % | **yes** |
| **I55** | 0.15 mm | **0.0 %** | **100 %** | 99.67 % | **yes** |
| I38 | 0.12 | −34.3 % | 40 % | 87.80 % | no |
| I48 | 0.12 | −31.7 % | 40 % | 62.68 % | no |
| I56 | 0.12 | −41.6 % | 36 % | 100 % (meaningless — `tissue_fraction` 0.9886) | no |
| I57 | 0.12 | −35.9 % | 40 % | 57.89 % (BA: **6.56 %**) | no |
| I58 | 0.12 | −33.7 % | 40 % | 91.18 % | no |
| I61 | 0.12 | −39.5 % | 40 % | 92.71 % | no |
| I62 | 0.12 | no whole-hemisphere label exists on DANDI | — | 37.27 % | no |

Root cause, from the raw headers: for I38 the label volume and the MRI volume describe **different physical
boxes** — the same three extents {76.8, 192, 168} mm are assigned to different world axes, so the boxes overlap
in only 76.8 × 76.8 × 168 mm. The label header's assignment (76.8 mm L–R, 192 mm A–P, 168 mm I–S) is
anatomically sensible for a hemisphere; the MRI header's (168 mm L–R, 76.8 mm A–P) is not. **The EPIC MRI
affine is the broken one for the 0.12 mm subjects.** For I46 the two boxes coincide to 0.2 mm.

**Only I46 (0.803 / 0.825) and I55 (0.921 / 0.930) are Dice values you may quote.** Every other `dice_WM` /
`dice_GM` / `frac_on_mri_labels` in `work/runs/*/result.json` is computed against a corrupted label volume and
must be recomputed after the mapping fix.

This does **not** invalidate the registrations. Search and refinement never touch labels: they run on the MRI's
own voxel grid with isotropic spacing and an exhaustive orientation search, so a wrong world-axis labelling in
a *label* header cannot reach the transform. The fix is re-prep plus re-evaluation only — **no
re-registration**, because `result.json` stores `final_transform`.

#### 6.5.3 The counterexample that caps what Dice can ever mean

`work/runs/I46_parser_wrongpol_v0/` is the wrong-OCT-class-polarity branch of I46, run to completion and kept
deliberately: same subject, same data, a pose **71.1 mm** from the accepted one (block centre 4.54, −41.89,
27.50 mm against −5.55, 25.91, 8.53 mm). At that wrong pose **WM Dice is 0.8565 against the correct pose's
0.8030** — higher — the coarse search score is also higher (0.7275 vs 0.7273), the structural NCC is also
higher, and 99 % of the block still lands on labels. The only quantities that separate the two poses are the
**vessel-channel NCC (0.301 vs −0.035)** and the vascular restart count (**8/8 vs 0/8**).

The full comparison table, the symmetry argument for why a class-swapped cortical sheet fits somewhere else in
the hemisphere, and the polarity machinery this drove are in **chapter 5, The method, as a chain of
reasoning**. The consequence for reading results is what belongs here: **a label-Dice endpoint on this problem
will confidently accept a 71 mm error**, and this is the strongest single argument for keeping the vascular
stage even on subjects where its geometric effect is small.


#### 6.5.4 The licence

- Dice 0.80 / 0.92 **licenses**: *"the OCT's automatic tissue classes agree with the manual MRI labels under the
  block, at a level comparable to the disagreement between the authors' own two label products of the same
  tissue."*
- Dice 0.80 / 0.92 does **not license**: *"the registration is accurate"*, *"accurate to X mm"*, or *"method A
  beats method B"* on any Dice difference below ~0.05.
- **Never** present a Dice improvement of 0.005–0.02 as evidence of anything. Measured sensitivity: over a
  ±22.5 % single-axis stretch of the depth axis, WM Dice moves by **0.007 in total** while the far face of the
  block sweeps ~1.7 mm. Dice is flat on the axis that matters.
- On the polarity question specifically, Dice is not merely uninformative but actively misleading (§6.5.3).

### 6.6 Vessel median 167 µm and 47 % within 150 µm — the ceiling argument

#### 6.6.1 The claim

`vessels_vesseg` for `I46_otsu`: the vascular stage moves the median from **264.7 → 166.7 µm** and f150 from
**0.2829 → 0.4733**, against a ±3 mm control at 352.4 µm / f300 0.4328. `ves_seg.tif` is the authors'
manual/semi-automatic OCT vessel segmentation and the pipeline never sees it; the MRI vessel labels are also
the authors'. Both sides of this metric are external to the method.

#### 6.6.2 Why 47 % is an annotation-imposed ceiling and not a failure

Four independent arguments, three of them empirical.

**(a) The oracle argument — strongest.** `work/runs/validate_real/refine_validate.json` row B1 fits a 12-DOF
affine *directly to the manual MRI vessels and the manual labels* — the answer key — and scores it against the
same manual vessels:

| | vessel median µm | f150 | Dice WM/GM |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| T0, structural only (label-free) | 276.5 | 0.254 | 0.805 / 0.837 |
| **ORACLE affine, fitted to the annotations** | **171.5** | **0.4657** | 0.802 / 0.831 |
| shipped `I46_otsu`, fully automatic | **166.7** | **0.4733** | 0.803 / 0.825 |

Letting an optimiser use the answer key reaches f150 = 0.466. That is what "as good as it is possible to be
against this annotation pair" looks like, and the automatic run is at that value.

**Caveat that must be stated whenever this is quoted:** the three rows are scored on *different point sets*
(3 935 / 4 945 / 4 999 points inside their respective block boxes). "We beat the oracle by 0.007" is inside
that noise. The defensible sentence is **"at the annotation ceiling, ±0.05"** — never "better than the oracle".

**(b) The annotation is physically incapable of doing better.** Four separate floors:

| Floor | Magnitude | Source |
|---|---|---|
| MRI vessel labels are 1-voxel traces on a **0.15 mm** grid; a voxel centre is up to 130 µm (half-diagonal) from the true vessel axis before any registration error | ~100–130 µm | `work/I46/mri_affine.npy` |
| The two annotations mark **different populations**: MRI labels mark only vessels big enough to darken a 0.15 mm ex-vivo FLASH voxel; `ves_seg` is a 12 µm Frangi segmentation. Many MRI-labelled voxels have **no** `ves_seg` counterpart | unbounded tail — hence p95 = 3.2 mm | `derivatives/…/sub-I46_ses-MRI_space-EPIC_label-vessels_dseg.nii.gz` vs `derivatives/sub-I46/ses-OCT/vessel/ves_seg.tif`; the two annotation products are compared in chapter 4, The data |
| `ves_seg.tif` for I46 has **561** z-slices against the OCT's **627** — a 0.79 mm depth-alignment ambiguity the data cannot settle. `zoff0` wins (167 vs 302 µm) but only *relatively* | up to 0.79 mm systematic | §6.10.6 |
| The EDT is stored on a **48 µm** grid, shape (156, 317, 307), and trilinearly interpolated | ~48 µm quantisation | `work/I46/oct_ves_dist48_*.npy` |
| Whether the MRI vessel labels are *systematically offset* from the dark blobs they mark was never measured — `octreg/scripts/label_offset.py` exists, was run, and **its output was not persisted** | **unknown** | `[UNVERIFIED]` — script present, results not persisted |

That last row matters more than its length suggests: it is the one measurement that would decide whether
167 µm is a **registration** floor or an **annotation** floor. The script is ~30 lines and re-running it is a
half-hour job.

**(c) The true no-information floor.** Measured on 2026-08-23 by taking the distribution of the vessel EDT
itself, i.e. what a point thrown uniformly into the I46 OCT block scores:

| baseline | median distance | f≤150 µm | f≤300 µm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **uniform random point inside the block, `ves_seg` EDT** | **530.2 µm** | **0.1165** | 0.3138 |
| ±3 mm rigid shift of the correct pose (`random_shift_control`) | 352.4 µm (best of 30: 284.8) | — | 0.4328 |
| **registered, final** | **166.7 µm** | **0.4733** | 0.6145 |
| oracle affine | 171.5 µm | 0.4657 | 0.6120 |
| uniform random point, `own` Frangi EDT | 344.5 µm | 0.2403 | 0.4724 |

Two consequences. First, **chance for f150 is 0.117, not 0** — so 0.473 is 4× chance, and reading "only 47 %"
as if the target were 100 % is precisely the misreading this section exists to prevent. Second, **the `own`
channel looks better than the `vesseg` channel mainly because our Frangi segmentation is denser** (491 472
voxels = 1.24 % of the 48 µm grid vs `ves_seg`'s 0.904 %): its *chance* f150 is 0.240 against 0.117. The
apparent superiority of 122.8 µm over 166.7 µm is largely a density effect, not an accuracy effect.

**(d) There is nothing left for a better transform model to win.** The best label-free free-form deformation on
top of the vascular affine reaches f150 **0.458** (from 0.440), and the **oracle** non-rigid — a deformation
fitted to the answer key — reaches only **0.480**. At most 0.014–0.04 of f150 exists in *any* deformation model
on this data (§6.10.7). The residual is the annotation, not the transform.

#### 6.6.3 The point-set objection, checked, and it works against us

A reviewer's first objection to "265 → 167 µm" is that the two rows have different `n_inside` (4 040 → 4 999):
the depth stretch 1.026 → 1.219 enlarges the block box, so the final transform admits 959 extra annotation
points. Both transforms were recomputed on the **3 950-point intersection** (points inside the box under
*both*):

| channel | stage | point set | n | median µm | p75 | p95 | f150 | f300 |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `vesseg` | structural | as reported | 4 040 | 264.7 | 679.3 | 2 288.9 | 0.2829 | 0.5502 |
| `vesseg` | structural | **common** | 3 950 | 259.8 | 635.0 | 2 053.8 | 0.2868 | 0.5595 |
| `vesseg` | final | as reported | 4 999 | 166.7 | 728.5 | 3 165.8 | 0.4733 | 0.6145 |
| **`vesseg`** | **final** | **common** | **3 950** | **119.3** | **348.2** | **1 843.7** | **0.5676** | **0.7261** |
| `own` | structural | common | 3 950 | 168.3 | 532.5 | 1 951.4 | 0.4478 | 0.6727 |
| `own` | final | common | 3 950 | **98.9** | 237.7 | 1 746.3 | 0.6595 | 0.7727 |

The improvement is **larger** on the matched set (260 → 119 µm, f150 0.287 → 0.568) and the p95 tail
**improves** (2 054 → 1 844 µm) instead of worsening. The apparent p95 degradation in the shipped JSON
(2 289 → 3 166 µm) is entirely the 1 049 newly-admitted peripheral points, which sit at the edge of the enlarged
box and are worse than average.

**Do not "fix" the reported number to 119 µm.** 166.7 µm is computed the same way for every run and is the
figure that is comparable across runs. But you may say the point-set confound was checked and works against us,
i.e. the shipped number is conservative.

### 6.7 The random-placement control — what it rules out and what it does not

`vessel_distance_stats(..., rng_shift_mm=3.0, n_ctrl=30, seed=0)` does exactly this:

```python
ctrl = [stats(pts_o + rng.uniform(-rng_shift_mm, rng_shift_mm, 3)) for _ in range(n_ctrl)]
```

**One** random 3-vector per draw, applied as a pure translation to all points, in OCT space. Rotation, scale,
shear and mirror of the accepted solution are **preserved**. Maximum displacement √3 × 3 = 5.2 mm; typical
≈ 2.6 mm.

| The control **does** rule out | The control does **not** rule out |
|---|---|
| that 167 µm is an artefact of a dense vessel map — a ±3 mm-displaced version of the *same* block scores 352 µm | that a *different* pose elsewhere in the hemisphere would score comparably |
| that the metric is flat at the millimetre scale, i.e. that we would have got 167 µm anywhere nearby | that the *rotation* or the *mirror* is right — both are held fixed in the control |
| that the vascular gain is degrees-of-freedom overfitting: depth-flip and k-slice-permutation scrambles of the vessel density collapse it back to T0 (269.5 / f150 0.269 and 266.2 / 0.275, vs T0 276.5 / 0.254 and shipped 166.7 / 0.477) | that the vessel channel would find the right answer from a *bad* starting pose — it is a refinement, always initialised from the structural solution |
| that the gain comes from the looser regularisation schedule rather than the vessel channel: the identical schedule with **no** vessel channel reaches only 265.8 µm / 0.277 | |

**The honest summary sentence:** *"a ±3 mm rigid perturbation of the same solution scores 352 µm against
167 µm; a point thrown at random inside the block scores 530 µm; scrambling the OCT vessel map along depth or
by slice permutation destroys the entire gain."*

**Do not write "random-placement control" without qualification.** A true random-pose-in-hemisphere control was
never run. `[OPEN]` It is cheap — reuse the existing 16 000-orientation search grid, score
`vessel_distance_stats` at N random poses that pass the overlap gate — and it is the single most valuable
missing experiment in the project.
