### 6.8 Why the three large slabs have no vessel numbers

#### 6.8.1 The mechanical reason the cell is a dash

`vessel_distance_stats` maps each manual MRI vessel voxel through `inv(T)` into the OCT vessel-EDT grid and
keeps those inside the grid box. If fewer than **20** survive it returns `{"n_inside": n}` and every downstream
field is `null`. For I38, I56, I62 — and also I48, I57, I58, I61 — `n_inside == 0`, so **no median, no f150 and
no control was ever computed.** The dashes in every summary table are missing data, not zeros.

The same trap applies to two other cells that look like measurements:

- **`Dice 0.000` for I57, I58, I61** — the block has essentially no overlap with the label cloud, so both Dice
  sets are empty. A coverage zero, not a measured disagreement.
- **`Dice 0.000` for I62** — I62 has **no whole-hemisphere label on DANDI at all**, so `labels4` is the BA-only
  label (3 350 780 voxels ≈ 0.23 % of the volume). Any Dice against it is meaningless.

That much is unambiguously an artefact of the **evaluator**.

#### 6.8.2 But the reason coverage is zero is itself a measurement, and it is not benign

Recomputed directly on the server from `work/<SUB>/mri_vessels.npy`, `work/runs/<SUB>_otsu/T_oct2mri.npy` and
the EDT grid affine:

| subject | manual MRI vessel voxels | **n_inside** | block centre → annotation centroid | **nearest annotation point to the block box** | median annotation point to the box | block bbox (mm) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **I46** | 34 069 | **4 999** | **7.8 mm** | **0.0 mm** (inside) | 4.9 mm | 14.1 × 20.8 × 21.3 |
| **I55** | 13 899 | **7 817** | **4.6 mm** | **0.0 mm** (inside) | **0.0 mm** | 28.5 × 31.6 × 34.2 |
| **I38** | 10 236 | **0** | **55.2 mm** | **25.7 mm** | 33.8 mm | 55.7 × 45.3 × 49.5 |
| **I56** | 6 513 | **0** | **65.9 mm** | **23.2 mm** | 39.1 mm | 62.8 × 21.4 × 62.5 |
| **I62** | 16 287 | **0** | **58.6 mm** | **26.4 mm** | 37.2 mm | 55.7 × 19.8 × 55.2 |
| I48 | 79 331 | 0 | 50.7 mm | 11.1 mm | 35.4 mm | — |
| I57 | 15 650 | 0 | 51.3 mm | 23.3 mm | 35.9 mm | — |
| I58 | 33 745 | 0 | 66.9 mm | 26.8 mm | 41.8 mm | — |
| I61 | 33 670 | 0 | **95.7 mm** | 57.5 mm | 79.0 mm | — |

(Two independent recomputations used slightly different box conventions and give min gaps of 21.2 / 24.0 /
24.4 mm versus 25.7 / 23.2 / 26.4 mm for I38 / I56 / I62. They agree to a few mm and the conclusion is
identical. Cross-check on the control case: an older diagnostic
`work/diag/mixed/diag_candidates.json` records `vessel_centroid = [-6.833, 23.890, 15.985]` for I46 — identical
to the recomputation — and `dist_to_vessel_centroid_mm = 8.01` for its top candidate.)

**The nearest annotation voxel is 23–26 mm outside the block, and the median annotation voxel is 34–39 mm
outside — roughly half a block-width.** This is not a near-miss that a coverage threshold happened to exclude.

A **second, completely independent** annotation says the same thing. Every DANDI OCT block is a
`sample-BrocaAreaS01` block, and `ba_labels` marks Broca's area in the same EPIC MRI space:

| subject | whole-hemi `labels4` voxels | dist. block centre → label centroid | frac of labels inside block | BA voxels | dist. → BA centroid | **frac of BA inside block** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **I46** | 111 293 541 | 22.4 mm | 0.003 | 2 934 215 | **9.6 mm** | **0.128** |
| **I55** | 127 943 011 | 36.5 mm | 0.015 | 2 061 821 | **7.8 mm** | **0.590** |
| **I38** | 161 556 093 | 39.5 mm | 0.120 | 4 683 068 | **57.4 mm** | **0.000** |
| **I56** | 135 133 392 | 41.8 mm | 0.054 | 2 957 062 | **65.2 mm** | **0.000** |
| **I62** | 3 350 780 (BA only) | 60.5 mm | **0.000** | 3 350 780 | **60.5 mm** | **0.000** |
| I48 | 136 880 167 | 42.8 mm | 0.130 | 3 302 389 | 51.1 mm | 0.000 |
| I57 | 149 540 041 | 44.5 mm | 0.000 | 202 756 | 57.3 mm | 0.000 |
| I61 | 167 062 778 | 94.5 mm | 0.000 | 3 750 625 | 96.0 mm | 0.000 |
| I58 | 155 401 827 | 63.0 mm | 0.000 | 2 874 973 | 74.8 mm | 0.000 |

And for I38 and I56 a **third** check disagrees: where labels *do* exist under the slab (`frac_on_mri_labels`
0.607 and 0.450), the OCT WM class lands on MRI GM about twice as often as on MRI WM — 35.0 % and 36.8 % of
on-label OCT-WM voxels land on MRI WM, which is *below* chance.

#### 6.8.3 Is this an annotation-coverage artefact or a registration failure? The measured evidence

The strongest available evidence says **annotation-coverage artefact**, and it is a correlation, not an
argument:

> The annotation cloud sits **55–66 mm away for exactly the six 0.12 mm subjects whose label mapping is known
> to be broken**, and **4–8 mm away for exactly the two 0.15 mm subjects whose mapping is known to be
> lossless.** That correlation is perfect across all nine subjects.

The `vessels` and `ba_labels` volumes are mapped to the MRI grid by the **same code path**
(`map_labels_to_grid`) that mis-pairs the label axes for the 0.12 mm subjects, and the header analysis in
§6.5.2 shows the EPIC MRI affine — not the label affine — is the broken one for exactly that group. So the
"annotation is 60 mm away" measurement is made in a coordinate frame that is independently known to be wrong
for those subjects, which is precisely the situation in which a 60 mm displacement of an annotation cloud is
expected.

That is a strong prior, not a proof. Three mutually exclusive explanations remain, with the test that
discriminates them:

| Hypothesis | Prediction | Test |
|---|---|---|
| **H1: the pose is wrong** | the overlay looks wrong when a human opens it | open `results_inspection/I38_otsu/{mri_region.nii.gz, oct_in_mri_region.nii.gz, mri_labels_region.nii.gz}` in Freeview and look for the BA label patch near the slab |
| **H2: the label / vessel / BA volumes are in a different space than assumed for the 0.12 mm subjects** (the `perm = [1,2,0]` mis-pairing) | re-mapping with the shape-consistent permutation moves the annotation cloud onto the slab | fix the axis permutation in `octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py::map_labels_to_grid` and recompute §6.8.2. **Cheapest test, run it first** — one re-prep, **no re-registration**, because `result.json` stores `final_transform`. ~1 h |
| **H3: the OCT slab for these subjects is not from Broca's area despite the `sample-BrocaAreaS01` filename** | the BA label stays 60 mm away no matter what | read Costantini 2023 methods, or ask the authors |

H2 is not a formality. Until it is run, the honest position is: *the absence of a vessel number for
I38/I56/I62 is a property of the evaluator; the cause of the absence is a 23–26 mm gap to two independent
annotations; the gap correlates perfectly with a known, fixable header bug; and the "correct" verdict rests on
unverified visual QC.* Nothing stronger. `[OPEN]`

A note on which annotation to trust in the meantime: after mapping, I38, I58 and I61 keep essentially all of
their BA labels and place them on MRI tissue at 99.9–100 %, so for those three **the BA label is the only
trustworthy annotation on disk** and is the right thing to score against until the whole-hemisphere mapping is
fixed. I57's BA labels place on tissue at only 6.56 % and I62's at 37.27 % — neither is usable at all.

### 6.9 Restart consistency — what it actually measures

#### 6.9.1 Mechanically

Twelve perturbations of the **already-accepted** structural pose (`rot U(5°, 30°)` about a random axis,
`trans U(−5, +5) mm` per component, up to 8.7 mm; the perturbations actually realised in the JSONs span
6.0–26.5° and 3.2–6.6 mm), each re-refined `0.3 mm rigid (150 it) → 0.3 mm affine (150) → 0.15 mm affine (150)`.
A restart "converged" iff `corner_mean_mm < 0.5`, measured on a **fixed 7 mm half-extent** lever arm
(`evaluate.py:72`, `extent_mm: float = 7.0`) regardless of the real block size — so the same 0.5 mm threshold
is a much tighter angular tolerance for I46's 7.5 mm-deep block than for I57's 61 mm slab.

**The 0.6 mm exhaustive search is never re-run.** The restarts therefore measure exactly one thing: *how wide
and how unique the refinement basin is around the pose the search already chose.* They are a **stability**
measurement and contain **no** information about whether the search picked the right basin.

#### 6.9.2 Empirically, on this dataset, they are anti-correlated with correctness

Mean converged over the five human-"correct" subjects: **10.2 / 12**. Over the three human-"wrong" subjects:
**11.3 / 12**. I61 returns 12/12 within 0.18 mm to a pose that is **95.7 mm** from the labelled hemisphere.
I57's scatter (max 0.536 mm) is far tighter than I46's (max 15.5 mm), and I57 is wrong while I46 is the
best-validated subject in the corpus.

For **I61 and DANDI I58** the mechanism is understood, and it is the MRI foreground mask.
`common.py::histogram_tissue_threshold` walks left from the tissue peak and cuts at the first histogram valley
whose depth ratio `valley_ratio = h[valley] / min(h[left_peak], h[tissue_peak])` falls below 0.5; when no such
valley exists it records `valley_ratio: null` and falls back to `thr = min(p1, 0.5 × multiotsu_first)`, a floor
that keeps essentially everything. I61 hits exactly that fallback (`valley_ratio: null`, `tissue_thresh 6.80`
against an intensity **median of 10.42** — the cut lands *below* the median — 74.2 % of the volume called
tissue = 1 838.8 cm³, three hemispheres' worth), as does I58 (`null`, 2.12 against median 16.93, 58.7 %,
1 453.4 cm³). I56 fails the same way (`null`, 3.62 against median 15.15, **98.9 %**, 2 519.0 cm³) without being
one of the "wrong" runs. A flat homogeneous field gives a **wide, smooth, extremely reproducible** correlation
maximum. **Stability is exactly what you get when the objective has no structure.**

**The mask story covers I61, DANDI I58 and I56. It does not cover I57, and it must not be extended to it**
(§6.13.3); nor does it cover I48 or I62, whose masks are also normal. Read the whole column before repeating
the story. All values from `work/<SUB>/prep.json → mri`; volumes are `tissue_fraction × grid volume`.

| subject | `tissue_thresh` | intensity median (p50) | `tissue_fraction` | `valley_ratio` | MRI tissue cm³ | mask verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| I46 | 18.88 | 14.88 | 0.310 | **0.1161** | 803 | normal |
| I55 | 13.82 | 26.58 | 0.240 | `null` | 621 | fallback taken, but it landed correctly |
| I38 | 22.28 | 19.92 | 0.325 | **0.1984** | 806 | normal |
| I48 | 14.71 | 11.50 | 0.156 | 0.4737 | 386 | normal mask, **worst valley separation in the corpus** |
| I62 | 15.80 | 13.60 | 0.215 | 0.0869 | 532 | normal |
| **I57** | **15.77** | **13.80** | **0.209** | **0.0631** | 518 | **normal** — cut above the median, clean valley, ordinary fraction |
| I56 | 3.62 | 15.15 | 0.989 | `null` | 2 519 | **failed — 98.9 % of the volume called tissue** |
| I58 (DANDI) | 2.12 | 16.93 | 0.587 | `null` | 1 453 | **failed** |
| I61 | 6.80 | 10.42 | 0.742 | `null` | 1 839 | **failed** |

Two readings of that table are easy to get backwards. First, **`valley_ratio` is small when the mask is
good** — it is the valley depth relative to the shallower of the two peaks, and the threshold *accepts* when it
falls below 0.5. So I57's 0.0631, I62's 0.0869, I46's 0.1161 and I38's 0.1984 are all clean separations, and
I48's 0.4737, the only value near the limit, is the corpus's worst. All five are recorded fields; **do not
print any of them as missing.** Second, **`null` is a warning flag, not a verdict**: I55 also has
`valley_ratio: null` and its fallback threshold happened to land correctly (tissue fraction 0.240, 620.5 cm³).

#### 6.9.3 Why it is nonetheless the number to report on unlabelled data

Because there is nothing else. On Xiangrui's I58 brainstem pair there are no labels, no vessel annotations and
no reference transform — the shared folder contains exactly two files, 13 GB of OCT and 92 MB of cropped MRI.
The complete inventory of automatic evidence available on unlabelled data is:

| Signal | Value on the brainstem pair | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| structural restarts | **10/12**, corner-mean median 0.099 mm | the refinement basin around the chosen pose is narrow and reproducible |
| search margin `top1/top2` | 0.1247 / 0.1184 = **5.3 %** | the search was *decisive* — the one signal that would have flagged I48 (0.5 %) and DANDI-I58 (0.03 %) |
| vessel-channel NCC | **0.0055** | dead. Here the "vessels" are section seams, so the one independent verifier does not transfer |
| refined NCC | 0.1014, channels `[−0.0174, 0.2203]` | one of two class channels is *anti*-correlated |
| Dice / vessel distance | **do not exist** — `evaluation.final` for this run contains only `stretch_ijk` and `block_centre_mri_mm` | |

**The correct framing:** *restart consistency is a necessary-not-sufficient screen. 10/12 says the answer is a
well-defined local optimum. It says nothing about whether that optimum is the right one, and on this dataset
the wrong answers were the most stable ones.* Report it as a stability statistic alongside the search margin,
and never call it validation.

#### 6.9.4 The reject gates that should exist, and their honest cost

Two gates have been proposed and neither is implemented:

1. Reject if `top1/top2 < 1.02` or `top1 < 0.35` ("no separation").
2. Reject if the MRI "tissue" volume exceeds 1.5× the largest plausible hemisphere.

**Take the hemisphere number from the data, not from memory.** The MRI tissue volumes recorded in
`work/<SUB>/prep.json` (`tissue_fraction × grid volume`) span **386.3 – 805.8 cm³** across the six subjects
whose foreground mask behaves normally — I48 386.3, I57 518.0, I62 531.5, I55 620.5, I46 802.9, I38 805.8,
median 576 cm³ — and jump to 1 453.4 / 1 838.8 / 2 519.0 cm³ on the three whose mask failed. **Use 806 cm³ as
the expected upper end of a hemisphere everywhere in this document, and derive every threshold from it.** The
band is established and derived once, in chapter 4, The data, §4.3, which tabulates the same volumes alongside
the block geometry; state it from there. Any "≈600 cm³" or "≈900 cm³" hemisphere figure met in the project's
older prose is a from-memory number with no artefact behind it, superseded by this band.

Gate 2 re-derived on that number is `1.5 × 806 ≈ 1 210 cm³`, and it is clean: it catches I61 (1 838.8 cm³),
I58 (1 453.4 cm³) and I56 (2 519.0 cm³) with a factor of 1.2–2.1 to spare, and flags nothing known-good — the
largest normal mask, I38's 805.8 cm³, sits a third below the gate.

Gate 1 is **not** free, and this is worth stating before anyone ships it. Computing the ratio from the verified
scores in §6.3.1: it would reject I48 (1.005), I58 (1.0003), I57 (1.013) and I61 (1.012) — all four bad
cases — but it would **also reject I55 (1.004), the single best-validated subject in the corpus.** And the
absolute half of the rule (`top1 < 0.35`) would additionally reject I56 (0.3397), I62 (0.2872) and **the
brainstem run that is the project's only result on our own data (0.1247)**. A margin gate is the right
instinct — it is the only signal that discriminates the failures in advance — but as stated it is not a
usable rule. Whatever gate ships must be validated against I55 and the brainstem pair as negative controls.
(This paragraph is arithmetic on the verified `top1`/`top2` fields, not a claim from any source document.)

**A third gate must not ship at all: an absolute floor on `refine.final_ncc`.** The criterion
"`refine.final_ncc` ≥ ~0.35 for hemisphere runs" appears in the shipped documents, and it does not work.
**I61 scores 0.5020 and I57 0.5121 and both are wrong; I62 scores 0.2842 and is the strongest of the three
unresolved subjects.** The refined NCC is comparable *within* a subject — it is exactly what decides the class
polarity — and **not comparable across subjects**, because its level is set by how much structure the MRI side
happens to contain, which is precisely what the failed tissue masks inflate. Any document proposing a numeric
NCC acceptance threshold has to carry that counterexample in the same sentence.

The one thing that cannot be said is that the pipeline warned anybody: it returned 12/12 restarts on I58 and
I61, and 10/12 on I57.

---

### 6.10 The I46 deep-validation suite

A path correction first: `octreg/README.md` §4 and §6 refer to `scripts/validation_i46/` and `scripts/legacy/`.
**Neither directory exists**, on the server or locally. The validation scripts sit flat in `octreg/scripts/`:
`refine_validate.py`, `oracle_cv.py`, `scale_probe.py`, `nonrigid_stage.py`, `distill_oct_parser.py`,
`vessel_channel_refine.py`, `test_own_vessels.py`, `test_vessel_scales.py`, `label_offset.py`,
`profile_vessels.py`, `analyze_oracle.py`, `analyze_candidates.py`, `diag_candidates.py`. Their outputs are in
`work/runs/validate_real/`, `work/runs/nonrigid/`, `work/runs/vessel_channel/` and `work/runs/summary/`.

**Every experiment in this suite starts from the same `T0`** = `work/runs/crop_mixed_real/T_oct2mri.npy`, the
v0 label-free structural result, `stretch_ijk = [1.032, 1.004, 0.971]`. `T0` is therefore the common baseline
row in all the tables below, and it is *not* the shipped `I46_otsu` transform — it is the v0 machinery's
structural stage on the same subject. Keep the two distinct.

#### 6.10.1 Oracle affine — how far the structural stage is from the achievable optimum

`work/runs/validate_real/refine_validate.json`, log `logs/refine_validate_real.log`. "Oracle" = an affine
fitted *with* the manual MRI vessels and manual labels, which the pipeline never sees.

| row | vessel median µm | p75 | f150 | f300 | n_inside | Dice WM | Dice GM | anchor NCC | vs T0: centre / corner mean | OCTves→manual median µm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| T0 (label-free) | 276.5 | 624.4 | 0.254 | 0.541 | 3 935 | 0.805 | 0.837 | 0.726 | 0 / 0 mm | 665.2 |
| A: auto vessels + anchor | 268.4 | 709.7 | 0.274 | 0.550 | 5 397 | 0.806 | 0.823 | 0.725 | 1.27 mm / **2.04 mm** | 699.5 |
| A2: auto vessels only | 457.7 | 1 482.3 | 0.153 | 0.362 | 4 104 | **0.462** | **0.563** | **0.172** | 2.56 mm / 2.77 mm | 1 062.7 |
| **B1: ORACLE affine (manual)** | **171.5** | 706.9 | **0.466** | 0.612 | 4 945 | 0.802 | 0.831 | 0.713 | 0.93 mm / **1.36 mm** | 639.7 |
| B2: ORACLE nonrigid (manual) | — | — | — | — | — | 0.803 | 0.825 | — | disp mean 0.100 / p95 0.119 / max 0.124 mm | 641.3 |

(The rotation figures in this table's source — e.g. "91.2°" for the oracle — are products of the broken
rotation metric of §6.14.1 and have been omitted deliberately. A 91.2° rotation would force ≥ 17 mm of corner
motion against a reported 1.36 mm.)

**Proves:** the structural stage sits **~1.36 mm (corner mean) from the oracle affine**, and that residual is
worth 276 → 171 µm on the vessel metric while costing *nothing* in Dice (0.805/0.837 → 0.802/0.831). It also
proves that **automatic MRI vessel candidates are useless as an oracle substitute**: 64 192 candidates were
extracted (8 784 components, size ≥ 4), of which only **3 %** fall within 0.3 mm of a manual vessel and only
10 % of manual vessels are within 0.3 mm of a candidate; driving the refinement with them alone (row A2)
destroys the result — Dice 0.46/0.56, anchor NCC 0.17, 2.77 mm off. This is why the MRI side of the vessel
channel is a **soft local-darkness map**, not a binary vessel segmentation (§6.10.8).

#### 6.10.2 Cross-validation of the oracle — is it fitting, or is it real?

`work/runs/validate_real/oracle_cv.json`, log `logs/oracle_cv.log`. 2 folds × 3 seeds over **31 214** manual
vessel voxels in **2 922 connected components**; components are split between folds and the score is reported
on **held-out vessels only**.

| variant | held-out median µm (mean ± sd) | f150 (mean ± sd) | f300 mean | moved vs T0: centre / corner |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| T0 (label-free) | 273.3 ± 20.4 | 0.257 ± 0.033 | 0.544 | 0 / 0 |
| **oracle affine (labels + vessels)** | **197.1 ± 13.5** | **0.416 ± 0.041** | 0.604 | 0.917 / 1.399 mm |
| oracle **rigid** (labels + vessels) | 254.0 ± 24.7 | 0.304 ± 0.040 | 0.554 | 0.773 / 0.900 mm |
| oracle affine (**vessels only**) | 236.7 ± 33.2 | 0.342 ± 0.078 | 0.570 | 1.520 / 2.042 mm |
| oracle affine (**labels only**) | 269.3 ± 23.6 | 0.274 ± 0.024 | 0.546 | 0.191 / 0.241 mm |

**Proves:** (a) the oracle gain **survives held-out** — 197 µm / f150 0.416 against T0's 273 µm / 0.257 — so it
is not overfitting the 31 k annotation voxels; (b) **the improvement is affine, not rigid** (the rigid oracle
only reaches 254 µm), i.e. the residual is a *shape* error, not a placement error; (c) **the labels alone
cannot find it** — the labels-only oracle moves 0.19 mm and gains nothing (269 µm vs T0's 273 µm), so the
GM/WM geometry is blind to the residual; (d) vessels alone overfit, with the largest spread (sd 0.078).

The held-out ceiling **f150 ≈ 0.42** is the number the pipeline should be compared against; the full-fit
ceiling is 0.466 and the shipped run reaches 0.473. Read together: at, or statistically indistinguishable
from, the ceiling.

#### 6.10.3 Scale profile along each OCT array axis — the core negative result

`work/runs/summary/scale_profiles.json` (byte-identical to `work/runs/validate_real/scale_profiles.json`),
produced by `octreg/scripts/scale_probe.py`. It applies a single-axis scale `s ∈ [0.85, 1.30]` in steps of
0.025 about the block centre on top of T0. Columns are `[s, NCC-mixed, Dice WM, Dice GM, vessel median µm,
f150]`. **This is the canonical presentation of the three-axis scale probe** — other chapters state its
conclusion and point here. The numbers are the full-range values read back from `scale_profiles.json`; the
narrower ranges that circulate in the prose read only the ascending half of the depth-axis curve.

| OCT axis | NCC argmax | NCC at s = 1.0 | NCC range over 0.85–1.30 | **Δ NCC** | manual-Dice argmax (WM/GM) | vessel f150 argmax |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **i** — 627-axis, depth / serial-sectioning | **1.075** | 0.7258 | **0.7062 (s = 1.300) – 0.7274 (s = 1.075)** | **0.0212** | **1.100** (0.788 / 0.815) | 0.875 (0.258) |
| **j** — 1271-axis, in-plane | 1.025 | 0.7258 | 0.6720 – 0.7266 | 0.0546 | 1.025 | 1.000 (0.254) |
| **k** — 1230-axis, in-plane | 1.000 | 0.7258 | 0.5572 – 0.7258 | **0.1686** | 1.000 | 1.100 (0.317) |

**Proves the core claim:** along the depth axis the label-free objective is **flat** — 2.9 % NCC variation
across a ±22.5 % scale change, against 16.9 % along k, a factor of **8** — and the manual-label Dice varies by
0.007 over the same sweep. A one-sheet GM/WM block does not encode its own thickness scale, and neither do the
manual GM/WM labels. This is the same conclusion the labels-only oracle reached from the other direction
(§6.10.2c), by a completely different route.

Read carefully, the corrected numbers make the result **sharper** than the original write-up: along depth the
manual labels still resolve a maximum at s = 1.100 that the NCC essentially cannot see, its own maximum sitting
at 1.075 on a 0.021-wide plateau.

**The one inconsistency inside this story that is not resolved.** In `scale_profiles.json` the *vessel* metric
responds strongly on the **k** axis (f150 0.254 → 0.317 at s = 1.10) and **not** on the **i/depth** axis (f150
stays 0.226–0.258). Yet the pipeline's vascular stage stretches **i**, and that is what moves the vessel score
from 265 to 167 µm. Single-axis probes about the block centre and a full 12-DOF affine are different
experiments, so this may be pure axis coupling — but **the raw i-axis column does not, on its own, show the
vessel metric preferring a depth stretch.** Marked `[UNVERIFIED]`. To settle it: re-run `scale_probe.py`
starting from the **final** transform and report the i-axis profile of the **vessel-channel NCC**, not the
mixed NCC. ~30 min.

`scale_probe.py` also writes `work/runs/validate_real/T_free_affine.npy`, the label-free affine refined from T0
with the scale prior removed (`ls_clamp = sh_clamp = 0.35`, `reg = 0`). Its printed diagnostics were never
captured to a log; re-run to recover them.

#### 6.10.4 Vessel-channel design sweep — what the vascular stage is made of

`work/runs/vessel_channel/vessel_channel_refine.json` (`reg = 0.5`, `clamp = 0.3`), 22 variants. The MRI side is
either a local-median "dark spot" map or a Frangi vesselness; the OCT side is either a *density* of a vessel
segmentation or a raw Frangi map; `w` is the vessel-channel weight in the 3-channel NCC. **This is the
canonical presentation of the `vessel_channel_refine` sweep**; it is summarised elsewhere and tabulated in
full only here.

| variant | vessel median µm | f150 | Dice WM/GM | depth stretch | corner vs oracle |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| T0 (no vascular stage) | 276.5 | 0.254 | 0.805 / 0.837 | 1.032 | 1.362 mm |
| oracle affine (reference) | 171.5 | 0.466 | 0.802 / 0.831 | 1.177 | 0 |
| mri:dark / oct:density **w = 0.5** | 181.2 | 0.438 | 0.808 / 0.831 | 1.144 | 0.480 mm |
| mri:dark / oct:density **w = 1.0** | 167.3 | 0.476 | 0.805 / 0.827 | 1.208 | **0.349 mm** |
| mri:dark / oct:density **w = 2.0** (shipped) | **166.7** | **0.477** | 0.803 / 0.826 | 1.223 | 0.430 mm |
| mri:dark / oct:density w = 4.0 | 166.7 | 0.477 | 0.803 / 0.825 | 1.238 | 0.512 mm |
| mri:dark / oct:density, vessel channel **only** | 165.5 | 0.479 | 0.801 / 0.823 | 1.237 | 0.522 mm |
| mri:dark / oct:**frangi** w = 2.0 | 188.2 | 0.428 | 0.804 / 0.826 | 1.159 | 0.514 mm |
| mri:**frangi** / oct:density w = 2.0 | 165.1 | 0.479 | 0.804 / 0.828 | 1.211 | **0.316 mm** |
| mri:frangi / oct:frangi w = 2.0 | 240.6 | 0.345 | 0.802 / 0.826 | 1.116 | 0.877 mm |
| **CONTROL: WM/GM only, same schedule** (`reg 0.5, clamp 0.3`, no vessel channel) | **265.8** | **0.277** | 0.810 / 0.844 | 1.057 | 1.240 mm |

**Proves:** the gain is the **vessel channel**, not the looser regularisation — the identical optimisation
schedule without the vessel channel reaches only 266 µm / 0.277 and stays 1.24 mm from the oracle. It also
fixes the design: the MRI side must be a *local-darkness* or Frangi map and the OCT side must be a *density* of
a vessel segmentation; OCT-Frangi-as-a-map is markedly worse (188–241 µm). The weight `w` is insensitive
between 1 and 4, which is a good sign — the result is not perched on a tuned hyperparameter.

Note the Dice column across the whole table: 0.801–0.810 WM for every variant including the ones that are
100 µm apart on vessels. Another demonstration that the labels cannot discriminate.

#### 6.10.5 Which OCT vessel segmentation, and the scrambling controls

`work/runs/vessel_channel/test_own_vessels.json` (log `logs/test_own_vessels.log`):

| variant | vessel median µm | f150 | Dice WM/GM | corner vs oracle |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| T0 | 276.5 | 0.254 | 0.805 / 0.837 | 1.362 mm |
| oracle affine | 171.5 | 0.466 | 0.802 / 0.831 | 0 |
| oct `ves_seg` (DANDI Frangi @12 µm) \| mri dark | **167.3** | **0.476** | 0.805 / 0.827 | 0.349 mm |
| oct `ves_seg` \| mri frangi | 166.4 | 0.473 | 0.805 / 0.829 | 0.311 mm |
| **oct own Frangi @48 µm q99.0** \| mri dark | 174.6 | 0.454 | 0.806 / 0.828 | **0.301 mm** |
| oct own Frangi @48 µm q99.5 \| mri dark | 180.4 | 0.440 | 0.806 / 0.829 | 0.430 mm |
| oct own Frangi @24 µm q99.0 \| mri dark | 192.6 | 0.413 | 0.807 / 0.830 | 0.518 mm |
| oct own Frangi @24 µm q99.5 \| mri dark | 190.8 | 0.419 | 0.806 / 0.830 | 0.598 mm |
| **CONTROL: `ves_seg` density flipped along depth** | **269.5** | **0.269** | 0.809 / 0.834 | 1.362 mm |
| **CONTROL: `ves_seg` density k-slices permuted** | **266.2** | **0.275** | 0.807 / 0.838 | 1.271 mm |

**Proves:** (a) our own label-free Frangi segmentation reaches within 4 % of the DANDI manual `ves_seg`
(174.6 vs 167.3 µm; f150 0.454 vs 0.476) — **the pipeline does not need the provided segmentation**, which is
what makes the method label-free rather than merely annotation-light; (b) both scrambling controls collapse the
gain back to T0 level, so the signal is genuine vessel *correspondence* and not an artefact of the extra
degrees of freedom. These two scrambles are the strongest controls in the project and should always be quoted
alongside the 167 µm figure.

`work/runs/vessel_channel/test_vessel_scales.json` sweeps Frangi scale and quantile on the OCT side (16
variants: 24 µm vs 48 µm × σ ranges 1–2.2 / 2–4.4 × q98.5 / 99.0 / 99.5). Best own-segmentation variant is
`24 µm max(σ1–2.2, σ2–4.4) q99` at 182.9 µm / f150 0.436; `ves_seg @12 µm` at 167.3 / 0.476 is the ceiling;
plain 48 µm variants sit at 199–212 µm. Dice WM stays in 0.805–0.807 for **every** variant.

#### 6.10.6 The `ves_seg` depth-offset check

The DANDI `ves_seg.tif` for I46 has **561** z-slices while the OCT stack has **627**, so its alignment along
depth is ambiguous by 66 slices = 0.79 mm. Both hypotheses were scored in every `*_final*` run:

| run | `vessels_zoff0` median / f150 | `vessels_zoff66` median / f150 |
|---|---|---|
| crop_final2 | **166.8 / 0.469** | 301.9 / 0.187 |
| whole_final2 | **166.6 / 0.474** | 304.5 / 0.181 |
| crop_final | **179.0 / 0.440** | 294.1 / 0.196 |

`zoff0` (segmentation aligned to the *start* of the stack) wins by a wide margin. But note that the
structural-stage rows **invert** this (`struct zoff0` 276 µm vs `struct zoff66` 245 µm): before the vascular
stage the depth scale is wrong, so the offset test is not decidable there. **Only after the vascular stage does
the answer become unambiguous** — a small but real piece of evidence that the vascular stage is fixing a real
depth-axis error rather than absorbing one.

#### 6.10.7 Non-rigid ablation — measured, and deliberately excluded from v1

`work/runs/nonrigid/nonrigid_stage.json`, log `logs/nonrigid_stage.log`. Starting point is `crop_final`'s
transform; displacement grids are saved as `work/runs/nonrigid/disp_grid_*.npy`. **This is the canonical
presentation of the non-rigid ablation** — the design argument that rests on it (chapter 5, The method, as a
chain of reasoning) summarises these rows rather than repeating them.

| variant | vessel median µm | f150 | Dice WM | Dice GM | OCTves→manual median µm | disp mean / p95 / max (mm) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| structural affine | 276.5 | 0.254 | 0.803 | 0.830 | 665.2 | — |
| **vascular affine (the v1 result)** | 179.0 | 0.440 | 0.801 | 0.819 | 635.8 | — |
| oracle affine (manual) | 171.5 | 0.466 | 0.800 | 0.822 | 639.7 | — |
| label-free nonrigid 5×8×8, smooth 5 | 176.6 | 0.450 | 0.808 | 0.827 | 642.0 | 0.048 / 0.101 / 0.134 |
| label-free nonrigid 5×8×8, smooth 20 | 178.6 | 0.444 | 0.804 | 0.822 | 638.0 | 0.017 / 0.035 / 0.051 |
| label-free nonrigid 5×8×8, **smooth 1** | 172.7 | **0.458** | **0.816** | **0.838** | 648.9 | 0.116 / 0.223 / 0.355 |
| label-free nonrigid 4×6×6, smooth 5 | 178.2 | 0.445 | 0.805 | 0.823 | 638.5 | 0.029 / 0.056 / 0.077 |
| label-free nonrigid 7×12×12, smooth 5 | 175.3 | 0.453 | 0.814 | 0.835 | 647.0 | 0.086 / 0.175 / 0.292 |
| label-free nonrigid 5×8×8 smooth 5, **NO vessel channel** | 191.1 | 0.413 | 0.813 | 0.835 | 652.5 | 0.086 / 0.196 / 0.267 |
| ORACLE nonrigid 5×8×8 smooth 5 | 167.7 | 0.467 | 0.807 | 0.828 | 639.4 | 0.056 / 0.098 / 0.121 |
| **ORACLE nonrigid 5×8×8 smooth 1** | **159.8** | **0.480** | 0.816 | 0.838 | 643.6 | 0.103 / 0.182 / 0.291 |

**Proves:** on top of the vascular affine, the best label-free non-rigid buys **Dice +0.015 WM / +0.019 GM and
f150 +0.018** (0.440 → 0.458), at the cost of a 5×8×8 free-form grid and 0.36 mm of maximum displacement —
i.e. displacements smaller than one MRI voxel (0.15 mm) for the well-regularised settings. The **oracle**
non-rigid only reaches f150 0.480, so **there is at most 0.04 f150 of headroom in any deformation model on this
data.** Excluded from v1 on cost/benefit. The vessel channel is what carries the non-rigid stage too: removing
it costs 176.6 → 191.1 µm and f150 0.450 → 0.413.

This is the ablation to cite when someone asks "why is your method affine-only?" The answer is not that
non-rigid is hard; it is that the measured headroom on this data is smaller than the annotation's own
uncertainty.

#### 6.10.8 Self-distillation ablation — also excluded, and the most instructive negative result

`work/runs/summary/distill_log.json`, log `logs/distill_v1.log`. A 3D U-Net OCT parser trained on the MRI
parser's labels, then re-trained on its own registered output, 2 rounds of 2 000 iterations. **This is the
canonical presentation of the self-distillation ablation** — chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning,
and chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us, state its conclusion and point here.

| round | search top1 / top2 | final NCC | Dice WM (parser classes) | Dice GM | vessel median µm | f150 | vs T0: centre / rotation / corner mean / corner max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 0 (MRI-trained parser applied to OCT) | 0.7084 / 0.7083 | 0.7240 | 0.735 | 0.927 | 404.0 | 0.127 | 12.23 mm / **124.9°** / **17.98 mm** / 25.72 mm |
| **1 (distilled)** | **0.8626 / 0.8573** | **0.9566** | **0.959** | 0.952 | 265.2 | 0.270 | 0.207 mm / 12.9° / 0.508 mm / 0.755 mm |
| 2 (distilled again) | 0.8737 / 0.8565 | 0.9598 | 0.961 | 0.952 | 258.0 | 0.279 | 0.082 mm / 4.9° / 0.681 mm / 0.931 mm |

OCT class fractions after round 1: bg/WM/infra/supra `[0.007, 0.466, 0.296, 0.230]`; after round 2
`[0.005, 0.474, 0.299, 0.222]`.

**Proves:** distillation makes the *search* dramatically more decisive (top1 0.708 → 0.874, final NCC
0.724 → 0.960, "Dice" against its own class definition 0.735 → 0.961) **while the underlying registration
barely moves** (0.51 mm then 0.68 mm corner mean vs T0) and the vessel score stays at 258–265 µm / f150
0.27–0.28 — it never gets past structural-stage accuracy. **The high scores are self-consistency, not
accuracy: the metric is being distilled along with the parser.** Excluded from v1. The trained parser lives at
`work/oct_parser_v1`.

Keep this result in mind whenever a self-supervised or learned variant is proposed: on this problem, a method
can improve every internal score by 30 % and move the answer by half a millimetre.

#### 6.10.9 Two more ablations that shaped v1

**Feature representation** (I46 crop, `work/runs/runs_summary.json`, `bash octreg/scripts/run_ablations.sh`):

| features | top1 | refined NCC | Dice WM/GM | vessel median µm / f300 | vessels inside | restarts | in v1? |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---:|---|---|
| **otsu** (two-class after local-mean flattening) | 0.727 | **0.753** | 0.801 / 0.830 | 281 / 0.53 | 3 926 | 7/8 | **yes — shipped** |
| mixed (otsu + parser) | 0.733 | 0.731 | 0.798 / 0.829 | 297 / 0.51 | 4 023 | 8/12 | no — no gain over otsu |
| raw intensity | 0.594 | 0.693 | 0.800 / 0.832 | 275 / 0.54 | 3 945 | 4/8 | no — same answer, much weaker basin |
| parser (3D U-Net) | 0.650 | 0.710 | **0.442 / 0.696** | 230 / 0.68 | **242** | 5/8 | kept only as `--features parser` |
| **MIND (12 channels)** | **0.219** | **0.185** | 0.323 / 0.672 | n/a | **0** | 3/8 | **no — total failure** |

MIND is the one unambiguous negative: the search score never rises above 0.22, the refinement *decreases* it to
0.185, only 3/8 restarts converge, and the block lands 17.9 mm (corner mean) / 33.0 mm (corner max) from the
reference. MIND's rotational invariance appears to destroy exactly the signal this problem needs. Do not
revisit without a fundamentally different descriptor.

Note that raw intensity finds essentially the same answer as otsu (275 vs 281 µm) but with a much weaker basin
(4/8 vs 7/8 restarts). The contribution of the Otsu two-class construction is basin **width**, not a different
answer — which is consistent with the confirmed bias-flattening result: local-mean flattening before Otsu
takes I46's whole-hemisphere WM/GM Dice from **0.66 / 0.62 to 0.90 / 0.93**, driven by a measured 1.9×
intensity drift across the hemisphere. The precise re-derived pair is in §6.14.2; the mechanism is in
chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning.

**Mirror branch.** `crop_mixed_nomirror` (`--no-mirror`): top1 drops 0.733 → 0.685, refined NCC 0.731 → 0.685,
Dice 0.798/0.829 → 0.767/0.806, vessels 297 → 284 µm, and the recovered scale degenerates to
`[0.955, 1.0, 1.0]`. The mirror branch is **required** — 6 of the 9 DANDI subjects are mirrored — and it costs
exactly 2× the search (16 000 vs 8 000 orientations).

**Whole-hemisphere vs cropped search.** `crop_*` vs `whole_*` pairs converge to identical poses within noise
(crop_final2 stretch `[1.184, 0.973, 1.034]` vs whole_final2 `[1.195, 0.975, 1.035]`; vessels 166.8 / f150
0.469 vs 166.6 / 0.474). Cost: 12–14 s (crop, 4 000 rot) → 153 s (whole, 8 000 rot, parser features).
**The 30 mm crop prior buys nothing on I46.** v1 runs whole-hemisphere by default — which is a robustness and
capability argument, not an accuracy argument, and §6.15 N8 says why that distinction matters.

**MRI polarity robustness.** `crop_final_inv2` / `crop_final_inv2_w` feed a **tissue-inverted** MRI. The pose is
recovered (stretch 1.145–1.148, vessels 179–182 µm / f150 0.438–0.441, matching the non-inverted 179–181 µm)
and otsu-class Dice is unchanged, but `crop_final_inv2` recorded **0/12** structural restarts converged (its
`_w` re-parse recovered 8/12). Polarity handling is functional; the restart basin is fragile.

### 6.11 The strongest external validation: the ≈1.17 depth scale

#### 6.11.1 Why this beats every Dice value

A Dice value or a vessel distance is a *self-report*: we chose the metric, we chose the annotation, we chose
the point set. The depth-scale agreement is different in kind, for three reasons.

1. **It is a quantity our objective provably cannot see.** §6.10.3: a ±22.5 % stretch along the depth axis
   changes the structural objective by 2.9 % and the manual-label Dice by 0.007, against 16.9 % along an
   in-plane axis. A one-sheet GM/WM block does not encode its own thickness scale, and the manual GM/WM labels
   do not either (the labels-only oracle moves 0.19 mm and gains nothing).
2. **The number it is compared against was produced by someone else, from data we never used, by a method we
   did not run.**
3. **It is falsifiable, and it was tested in the right direction on a second subject** (§6.11.3) — though
   that second subject carries a coincidence of its own, stated there, which stops it being a clean null.

#### 6.11.2 Three independent routes to the same number (and one that was withdrawn)

| Route | Value | Provenance |
|---|---:|---|
| **Costantini et al.'s published affine** `results/mri2oct/affine.lta` (208 B, `github.com/neuroscales/biccn-broca-I46`, branch `main`), largest column norm | **1.17419** | fitted with their `ndot` vessel term against `vessels.manual.distance.nii.gz` — i.e. **hand-drawn vessels are what carry that number**. Singular values 1.21149 / 1.03593 / 0.98222, det 1.23270 |
| **Our oracle affine**, fitted by our optimiser to the same manual annotations in our own frame | **1.177** on the OCT depth axis | `refine_validate.json` B1 / `vessel_channel_refine.json`; never used by the method, ceiling only |
| **Sibling subjects' OCT sidecars** — I46 declares 12 µm *isotropic*; every other subject declares 30/30/35 or 12/12/14 µm, i.e. depth/in-plane = 35/30 = 14/12 | **1.1667** | `work/*/prep.json → oct.spacing_um_zyx`: I46 `[12,12,12]`, I55 `[14,12,12]`, the other seven all `[35,30,30]` |

**A fourth route was withdrawn; do not re-derive it.** I46's serial-section period measures **33 slices** (FFT
peak 33.0, autocorrelation r = 0.857 at lag 33, clean harmonics at 66/99/132/165/198). Combined with a 500 µm
vibratome cut that gives 500/33 = 15.15 µm per slice against a declared 12, i.e. ≈1.26, and it was written up
as a fourth confirmation. It fails on its own counter-example. **I56's measured period is 12 slices, so the
same arithmetic gives 500/12 = 41.7 µm against a 35 µm sidecar that two independent sources corroborate** — it
would convict a sidecar known to be right. Turned around and used consistently, I56 calibrates the true cut at
12 × 35 µm = 420 µm, and 420/33 = 12.7 µm on I46, a correction of only **≈1.06** — not 1.167, and not in
agreement with the three routes above. The period measurement itself is real and still matters, but as a
**slab-window** fact about `prep_subject.py` (§6.14.2), never as depth-spacing evidence. If any source counts
the section period as a route or as a line of evidence, recount without it and fix the ordinal.

**Three counts circulate in this document. They cover different sets, all three are correct within their own
scope, and the section period is excluded from every one of them** — that exclusion is the only thing the
withdrawal changed.

| where | count | what it covers |
|---|---:|---|
| **§6.11.2, here** | **three** | independent routes to the *value* ≈1.17, **none of them ours**: the sibling sidecars **1.1667**, the authors' published affine **1.17419**, an oracle affine fitted to their manual annotations in our frame **1.177** |
| chapter 4, The data, **§4.5.1** | **four** | lines of evidence that I46's *declared 12 µm is wrong*: (a) the sibling 7/6 convention, (b) no in-file spacing record for I46 at all, (c) the authors' affine, (d) our own pipeline's recovered **1.219**. (b) carries no number and (d) is our own measurement, so neither is an independent route in the sense of the row above |
| chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us, **§7.3.8** | **two** | *annotation-free anchors* — the specific numbers quotable without a manual annotation behind them: our pipeline's **1.219** and the sidecar ratio **14/12 = 1.167**. The authors' affine and the oracle affine both rest on hand-drawn vessels or labels, so neither is an anchor in this narrower sense |

Four lines, three routes, two anchors. If you meet "a fourth independent route" or "a fifth line", that is the
withdrawn one.

And the pipeline's own automatic recovery, with no annotation of any kind:

| configuration | depth stretch | vessel median | f150 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| structure only, no vessel channel (T0) | **1.032** | 276.5 µm | 0.254 |
| auto, `--vascular-w 0.5` | 1.144 | 181.2 | 0.438 |
| auto, `w = 1.0` | 1.208 | 167.3 | 0.476 |
| **auto, `w = 2.0` — the shipped default** | **1.223** | **166.7** | **0.477** |
| auto, `w = 4.0` | 1.238 | 166.7 | 0.477 |
| auto, MRI-Frangi × OCT-`ves_seg` | 1.183 | 166.4 | 0.473 |
| **shipped end-to-end `I46_otsu`** (`stretch_ijk[0]`) | 1.026 → **1.219** | 166.7 | 0.473 |

A useful sanity conversion: 1.219 × 12 µm = **14.6 µm** per slice, against the **14.0 µm** implied by the
sibling sidecars (35/30 = 14/12) and the **14.1 µm** implied by the authors' published affine (1.17419 × 12).
The three surviving routes agree the true spacing is ≈14 µm and that the I46 sidecar's 12 µm is wrong.

#### 6.11.3 The reverse test — what makes this evidence rather than coincidence

**I55's sidecar is correct**: it declares 14/12/12 µm, exactly the anisotropy I46's omits. Prediction: if the
1.22 on I46 is a real recovery of a missing metadata factor, then I55 should need **no** depth correction and
its vascular stage should barely move the block.

| | I46 (sidecar wrong) | I55 (sidecar correct) |
|---|---|---|
| `stretch_ijk[0]` structural → final | 1.026 → **1.219** | 0.920 → **0.913** |
| vascular stage displacement (corner mean) | **1.524 mm** | **0.334 mm** |
| vascular restarts within 0.3 mm | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| vascular NCC channels | `[0.729, 0.730, 0.296]` | `[0.766, 0.717, 0.083]` |

The prediction holds, in both directions: the subject that needs a correction gets one, the subject that does
not is left alone, and both have healthy vascular restart counts so neither result is a convergence artefact.
**A coincidence does not produce a correct negative control** — with one qualification that has to travel with
this test wherever it is quoted.

**I55 is not a clean null.** Its *structural* `stretch_ijk` is `[0.920, 1.084, 1.063]`, i.e. a recovered
depth-to-in-plane anisotropy of **0.8570** — and **6/7 = 0.8571**. That is the exact inverse, to four decimal
places, of the 7/6 = 1.1667 factor that I46 is supposed to be missing. So the subject whose job is to
demonstrate "no correction needed" in fact recovers, on the same axis, the reciprocal of the correction. Two
readings are open and the data does not choose between them: either the refinement is absorbing an unrelated
anisotropy that happens to land on 6/7, or something upstream is applying a 7/6 depth factor to I55's
already-correct sidecar and the refinement is quietly undoing it. What survives untouched is the *vascular
stage displacement* — 0.334 mm on I55 against 1.524 mm on I46 — because that is a measurement of how far the
vessel channel had to move the block, not of the scale itself. **State the 0.8570 wherever I55 is used as a
null result.** Resolving it is cheap: report I55's `stretch_ijk` against the OCT array axes with the sidecar
spacing divided out and check whether the 6/7 survives. `[OPEN]`

#### 6.11.4 The precision you may claim and the caveat you must carry

**Write this:** *"The authors' published affine, fitted with a hand-drawn-vessel term, has a largest-axis scale
of 1.174. An oracle affine fitted to those same manual annotations in our frame puts 1.177 on the OCT depth
axis. The sibling subjects' sidecars imply 1.167. Our fully automatic vessel channel recovers 1.18–1.24
depending on weight (1.22 at the shipped default) without using any annotation, while structure-only
registration gives 1.03 and provably cannot see the difference."*

**Never write** "we reproduce their affine", "we agree to three decimals", or any TRE derived from this.
Reasons, all verified:

- The authors' `affine.lta` lives in the FreeSurfer `flash20.mgz` frame, reachable from the DANDI NIfTI world
  only through `results/mri/raw2samseg.lta`. Different world coordinates, same grid.
- The OCT side has **no world coordinates at all** — the OME-XML `PhysicalSize` is the placeholder
  `1.0 pixel`, and the real 12 µm exists only in the JSON sidecar. Over 96 signed axis permutations the best
  conventions place the block correctly at millimetre scale but never achieve better than 260 µm median
  MRI-vessel-to-`ves_seg` agreement.
- Therefore **the axis identification of the authors' 1.174 column is `[UNVERIFIED]`.** It is magnitude
  evidence, not axis-resolved evidence.
- Our 1.219 exceeds the expected 1.1667 by **4.5 %**, and `--vascular-clamp 0.3` (≈ ±35 %) is a ceiling the
  recovered value has not been shown to be free of. So the sidecar is probably not the only thing that is off.
- The whole comparison is between scale *magnitudes* in two different coordinate conventions. It is
  **corroboration**, and it is **useless as a target registration error**.
- One loose end: several documents refer to a "true depth scale of ~1.18". **No artefact on disk carries
  1.18.** The two defensible anchors are the pipeline's own 1.219 and the sidecar-vs-siblings ratio
  14/12 = 1.1667. `[UNVERIFIED]` — ask the author which is meant.

Finally, the honest limit on generalisation: this recovery has been *needed* on exactly **one** subject and
*demonstrated absent* on exactly **one**, and the second of those two carries the unexplained 0.8570 = 6/7
anisotropy of §6.11.3. Nothing else in the dataset has a wrong sidecar to recover. n = 1 each way, and the
n = 1 on the null side is qualified.

### 6.12 Xiangrui's I58 brainstem pair — our own data

Runs: `work/runs/xiangrui_I58bs_novasc` (the reported result) and `work/runs/xiangrui_I58bs` (vascular on,
superseded). Logs `logs/reg_xiangrui_nv.log`, `logs/reg_xiangrui.log`, `logs/prep_xiangrui.log`,
`logs/test_polish.log`.

Data, and this is the whole of it: OCT `I58_Brainstem_mus_Slice_full_20um_corr.nii.gz`, 1457×2013×1595 @ 20 µm
isotropic, 13 025 490 607 bytes (md5-verified), pooled to 194×267×212 @ 0.15 mm; MRI
`I58_brainstem_MRI_cropped_to_OCT.nii.gz`, already cropped, 343×489×495 @ 0.08 mm, 92 207 321 bytes. Block
29.1 × 40.3 × 31.9 mm. **No labels, no segmentations, no vessel annotations, no reference transform.** The
promised 20+ subjects have not been uploaded.

#### 6.12.1 What worked

| | value |
|---|---|
| overlap gate | MRI tissue **13.3 cm³** vs OCT mask **28.9 cm³** → effective `min_overlap` **0.369** (requested 0.85). The gate adapts because the OCT mask includes agarose |
| 0.6 mm search grid | 42×61×61 @ 0.64 mm; block radius 29.3 mm; template 93³ |
| search | top1 **0.1247**, top2 0.1184 (margin **5.3 %**), converged by 4 000/16 000 orientations, **44.8 s** |
| polarity | WM-bright branch won (0.1247 → refined 0.1014) over GM-bright (0.1170 → 0.0851) |
| mirror | **no** |
| refined NCC | 0.1014, per channel `[−0.0174, 0.2203]` |
| structural restarts | **10/12** (corner mean min 0.093 / median 0.099 / max 8.04 mm) |
| block centre in MRI world | 5.03, −5.58, 20.74 mm |
| `stretch_ijk` | `[0.969, 0.988, 0.972]` — no pathological scaling |
| wall time | **362.3 s** total |

Worth noting: **this is the only run in the entire corpus where the adaptive overlap gate binds.** In all eight
DANDI runs that record it, `overlap_gate = {requested 0.85, effective 0.850}`, and `I46_otsu` has
`overlap_gate: null` because the feature did not exist when it ran. The gate formula (`register.py:111`), its
**0.15 floor** — which several shipped documents omit — and the reason the floor must always be quoted with
the formula are stated once, in full, in **chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning**. The result-level
point here is narrower: the adaptive gate is a brainstem-specific feature that has never been exercised on the
DANDI corpus, so do not present it as a validated component.

The human verdict (`results_inspection/INDEX.md`, the meeting document) is **"coarse correct"**: the specimen
outline, the dome-shaped section and a separate small tissue piece all land on their MRI counterparts. The
residual is described as "a few millimetres, larger toward the deep end" — but that magnitude is a **visual
estimate from the checkerboard panel** of `octreg/figures/fig_I58_brainstem.png`. **No numeric residual exists
for this pair**: `evaluation.final` for this run contains only `stretch_ijk` and `block_centre_mri_mm`; the
vessel and Dice blocks are absent because there is nothing to score against.
`[UNVERIFIED]` — no artefact quantifies the residual.

#### 6.12.2 What failed, and why

**1. The vessel channel is dead here.** `vascular.ncc_channels = [0.0013, 0.1844, 0.0055]` — the vessel channel
scores **0.0055**, and the WM channel collapses from −0.017 to 0.001. The stage moved the block **2.652 mm**
corner mean (4.005 mm max), and **0/8** vascular restarts landed within 0.3 mm (corner means 0.828 / 2.969 /
3.683 mm): the vascular objective has no basin here at all. It cost **4 778.4 s** of the 5 244.0 s total.

The cause is diagnosed and specific: the OCT "vessels" are dominated by the **serial-section seam artefact**.
`logs/prep_xiangrui.log` records 4 534 410 own-vessel voxels from the top-1 % dark-tube Frangi, on a stack with
strong vertical striping. The Frangi dark-tube detector fires on the seams, so the "vessel density" map is a
map of the **sectioning grid**, not of vasculature. The vascular stage is therefore switched off for this pair
(`--vascular off`), which is what makes `xiangrui_I58bs_novasc` the reported run.

**2. A raw-intensity fine polish is actively harmful.** `octreg/scripts/test_polish.py`, output
`work/runs/xiangrui_I58bs_novasc/T_polish.npy`, log `logs/test_polish.log`: `level 0.32 mm: NCC 0.033` →
`level 0.16 mm: NCC 0.030`, and the polish moved the block **centre 9.37 mm, corner mean 9.55 mm, corner max
12.3 mm** away from the structural solution. A raw-intensity fine channel between 20 µm OCT and 0.08 mm MRI is
not merely weak — it drags the block ~10 mm off a pose that was correct.

**3. Tissue/agarose separation by intensity is impossible.** `logs/prep_xiangrui.log`: `raw tissue thr 0.0`,
`oct150 tissue frac 0.779`, `octv tissue frac 0.772` — **77 %** of the block is called tissue because the
agarose scatters like tissue. This is why the OCT "tissue" volume (28.9 cm³) is more than twice the MRI's
(13.3 cm³), and why the overlap gate had to be made adaptive in the first place.

**Both failures share one root cause:** the fine-scale channels assume the OCT's high-frequency content is
anatomy. On this specimen it is section seams and embedding medium. That is the whole design brief for v1.1 —
a **texture-based specimen mask** (the tissue/agarose boundary is clearly visible, just not by intensity) plus
an **artefact-robust fine channel** built on the fibre texture that both modalities share. Exploratory work
exists: `octreg/scripts/test_texture_mask.py` → `work/texture_mask_test.png`; `octreg/scripts/diag_xiangrui.py`
and `diag2_xiangrui.py` → `xiangrui_diag.png`, `xiangrui_diag2.png` (local copies in
`/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/octreg/results/final/v1/`).

#### 6.12.3 What the brainstem run licenses

That the **coarse global pose** — position, orientation, mirror, approximate scale — is recoverable on a real
in-house specimen, from a 13 GB OCT volume and an MRI crop, in **six minutes**, with no prior, no labels and no
manual initialisation, and that the answer is a well-defined local optimum (10/12 restarts, median scatter
0.099 mm) reached from a decisive search (5.3 % margin). It licenses nothing about the residual, because
nothing numeric about the residual exists. And it does not license transferring the vascular stage to this
class of data — the one independent verifier the pipeline has is measurably dead here.

Naming trap to avoid in every future document: **"I58" means two different things.** DANDI subject I58 is a
failed whole-hemisphere run against a 10° MRI (`work/runs/I58_otsu`). Xiangrui's I58 brainstem pair is a
separate specimen and a *successful* coarse registration (`work/runs/xiangrui_I58bs_novasc`). They are
unrelated results.

---

### 6.13 The four bad cases, and how much of each is actually diagnosed

Three of the four have a mechanism behind them. **The fourth, I57, does not** — so the claim in §6.16 A7 that
the failures are diagnosable in advance has to be stated as *three of four*, never four of four.

#### 6.13.1 I48 — "uncertain": no score separation anywhere

Search `top1 = 0.2571` against `top2 = 0.2558`: a **0.0013 (0.5 %) margin** between the best and second-best
distinct pose. The refined NCC (0.2584) is barely above the search score, i.e. the affine cascade found nothing
to improve. The **losing polarity branch** scores 0.2422 → refined 0.2503, only 0.008 below the winner, so the
polarity decision is not separated either. The score plateaued early: 0.2558 at 4 000/16 000 orientations,
0.2571 at 8 000, unchanged to 16 000 — more search would not have helped.

Diagnosed cause, from `work/I48/prep.json`: the I48 MRI is `sub-I48_ses-MRI_flip-2_VFA.nii.gz` and **its JSON
sidecar was never downloaded**, so no FlipAngle can be read. MRI tissue fraction 0.156 (the lowest of the set),
two histogram peaks at 10.3 and 16.9 with `valley_ratio 0.474` — the **worst valley separation** in the corpus,
and a ratio near 0.5 means the two peaks are barely distinguishable. The WM/GM two-class split on the MRI side
therefore carries almost no contrast, which is exactly what a flat 0.257/0.256 landscape looks like.

**Evidence status, and the ordering matters. The "uncertain" verdict rests on that 0.0013 search-score
margin, and on nothing else.** The label evidence is not the reason and cannot be made into one: only **62.7 %**
of I48's whole-hemisphere labels and **64.2 %** of its BA labels sit on MRI tissue at all, so its
`frac_on_mri_labels` 0.575, its Dice 0.255 / 0.483 and the 36.5 % of on-label OCT-WM landing on MRI WM are
**untrustworthy in both directions** — they neither convict the pose nor clear it. `vessels_own` and
`vessels_vesseg` are both `n_inside = 0`; the manual vessel cloud (79 331 voxels, the largest in the dataset)
sits 50.7 mm from the block centre and the BA labels 51.1 mm away, but those distances are measured in the same
suspect frame.

**Do not file I48 with I62 and the large slabs.** Their empty cells have a specific label-coverage explanation:
I62 has no whole-hemisphere label on DANDI at all, so its `labels4` is the BA-only volume and any Dice against
it is arithmetic on the wrong object (§6.8.1). I48's problem is different in kind — it *has* whole-hemisphere
labels, they are simply half off-tissue, **and** its search never separated two poses. Lumping the two together
hides the only thing that would actually settle I48, which is a decisive search, not a better label volume.

#### 6.13.2 I61 — "wrong": the tissue mask kept the bath, and the search found it

| field | I61 |
|---|---|
| MRI file | `sub-I61_ses-MRI_flip-4_VFA.nii.gz`, FlipAngle **20** |
| grid | 1600×1400×640 @ 0.12 mm |
| `tissue_thresh` / intensity median | **6.80** / 10.42 — **the cut lands below the median** |
| `tissue_fraction` | **0.742** |
| histogram peaks | 8.72, 17.55 |
| `valley_ratio` | **null** — no valley found, so the fallback floor is used |
| MRI tissue volume passed to the search | **1 838.8 cm³**, about three hemispheres |
| top1 / top2 | 0.5172 / 0.5112 (margin 1.2 %) |
| refined NCC | 0.5020 |
| structural restarts | **12/12**, scatter 0.089 – 0.180 mm |
| vascular vessel-channel NCC | 0.0185 |
| frac_on_mri_labels | 0.000 |
| manual vessel cloud distance | **95.7 mm**, 0 % inside |
| whole-hemi label cloud distance | **94.5 mm**, 0 % inside |

The mechanism is the `valley_ratio: null` fallback of §6.9.2: a 28.8 cm³ OCT block finds a comfortable,
repeatable, meaningless correlation maximum inside a 1 839 cm³ field of homogeneous bath. The symptom is the
part worth remembering — a *respectable* refined NCC (0.5020), *perfect* restart stability (12/12 inside
0.18 mm), and a placement **95 mm from the labelled hemisphere**, which is not in the brain at all. It is the
cleanest demonstration in the corpus that neither the absolute NCC nor the restart count is an acceptance
criterion.

The diagnosis does not depend on the broken label mapping: `tissue_fraction`, `tissue_thresh` and
`valley_ratio` are computed from the MRI volume alone, before any label is touched. The 94–96 mm distances do
depend on it, but at that magnitude the mapping bug cannot account for them — the whole MRI grid measures only
192 × 168 × 76.8 mm.

#### 6.13.3 I57 — "wrong", and the failure has no explanation `[OPEN]`

I57 was written up alongside I61 as a second "bath-heavy, tissue-mask failure". **It is not one**, and the
pairing must be undone wherever it appears. Every foreground-mask field for I57 is normal:

| field | I57 | reading |
|---|---:|---|
| `tissue_thresh` | 15.77 | **above** the intensity median — if anything a conservative mask |
| intensity median (p50) | 13.80 | — |
| `tissue_fraction` | 0.209 | ordinary; I46 is 0.310, I62 0.215 |
| histogram peaks | 13.61, 23.86 | two clean peaks |
| `valley_ratio` | **0.0631** | a valley *was* found, and it separates better than I46's 0.1161 |
| MRI tissue volume | 518.0 cm³ | inside the normal 386–806 cm³ band (§6.9.4) |

The failure itself is not in doubt — top1 0.4394 / top2 0.4337, refined NCC 0.5121, `frac_on_mri_labels`
0.00048, manual vessel cloud 51.3 mm away, whole-hemisphere labels 44.5 mm away, BA labels 57.3 mm away,
10/12 restarts with two missing the 0.5 mm gate at 0.536 mm. **Its cause is unknown.** `[OPEN]`

What is ruled out, and what is still open:

- **Not the tissue mask.** See the table. Whatever went wrong did not go wrong in
  `histogram_tissue_threshold`, and I57 must not be counted in any "bath-heavy MRI" tally.
- **The labels cannot adjudicate it either way.** Only **6.56 %** of I57's BA labels and 57.9 % of its
  whole-hemisphere labels land on MRI tissue at all — the worst coverage in the corpus, which by itself
  explains its anomalous `labels_agreement_wholehemi_vs_ba = 0.671` and its Dice of 0.0. Every distance quoted
  above is measured in a frame that is independently suspect.
- **Still a live candidate: the block, not the MRI.** I57's OCT block is the largest and most sparsely filled
  in the corpus — 26.9 × 37.5 × 60.6 mm, 404 voxels at 0.15 mm along one axis, OCT tissue fraction 0.404, the
  lowest of the nine. `results_inspection/INDEX.md` describes it as "captured by a flat MRI region (two-piece
  slab)", which is a human reading of an overlay, not a measurement. If the block really is two disconnected
  pieces, scoring their **union** lets one piece sit on tissue while the other sits anywhere; requiring **each
  connected OCT component** to land on tissue would be the fix. This has never been tested.

The cheapest next step is the same one that unblocks I38/I56/I62: fix the label axis permutation, re-evaluate,
and see whether I57's annotations move onto the block. If they do not, I57 needs a diagnosis of its own. Until
then it is a failure with a symptom and no mechanism, and it is the reason this chapter does not claim that
the pipeline's failure modes are understood.


#### 6.13.4 DANDI I58 — "wrong": registered against a 10° flip angle

Verified from the sidecars on the box:
`data/costantini/dandi-000026/derivatives/EPIC/sub-I58/ses-MRI/anat/` contains exactly two volumes,
`sub-I58_ses-MRI_flip-1_VFA` with `"FlipAngle": "30"` and `sub-I58_ses-MRI_flip-3_VFA` with
`"FlipAngle": "10"`, both `RepetitionTime 0.045`, Siemens MAGNETOM Terra 7 T GRE. `work/I58/prep.json` confirms
the pipeline used the **flip-3, 10°** file. **There is no 20° volume for I58**, unlike every other subject.
(Some of the shipped prose has this inverted, with flip-1 = 10° and flip-3 = 30°; the sidecars say the
opposite, and the sidecars win. The *conclusion* — there is no 20° volume for I58 — is right either way.)

Symptoms: `tissue_thresh 2.12`, `tissue_fraction 0.587`, **one** histogram peak (`n_peaks: 1`,
`valley_ratio: null`), intensity p50/p99 = 16.9 / 40.8 — the narrowest dynamic range in the set. MRI tissue
volume 1 453.4 cm³. Search top1 0.2896 with top2 0.2895, a **margin of 0.0001**; refined NCC 0.2708 with wildly
unbalanced per-channel NCC `[0.344, 0.197]`. Placement 63.0 mm from the labelled hemisphere, 66.9 mm from the
manual vessel cloud, `frac_on_mri_labels = 0.000`.

Diagnosis: at a 10° flip a FLASH VFA volume is essentially proton-density weighted, so WM and GM have almost no
contrast and the Otsu two-class split on the MRI side is noise. Combined with the failed tissue mask this is
I61's failure mode plus a contrast failure on top.

**The free experiment that has never been run:** `sub-I58_ses-MRI_flip-1_VFA.nii.gz` (30°, **2 890 933 645 B**,
already on disk since 2026-08-20 11:49) has never been tried. Re-prepping and re-registering against it costs
~30 min and directly tests the diagnosis. Alternatively, synthesise a 20°-equivalent contrast by VFA T1 fitting
from the 10° + 30° pair — both volumes are downloaded.

A general trap this exposes, worth carrying: **`flip-N` is a per-subject file index, never an angle.** Seven of
nine subjects are 20° regardless of index (I38/I46/I55/I56 use `flip-2`, I57/I61 use `flip-4`, **I62 uses
`flip-3` and is 20°** — the same index as I58's 10° file). Always read the sidecar.

### 6.14 Discrepancies and broken fields a successor must know about

#### 6.14.1 `transform_diff(...).rotation_deg` is broken for mirrored transforms

```python
def polar_rotation(M):                      # octreg/octreg/common.py:94
    U, _, Vt = np.linalg.svd(M)
    R = U @ Vt
    if np.linalg.det(R) < 0:
        U[:, -1] *= -1                      # which column this is depends on the SVD ordering
        R = U @ Vt
    return R
```

For a mirrored transform (`det < 0` — I38, I46, I48, I56, I58, I62 and every I46 development run), forcing
`det > 0` negates the singular vector with the smallest singular value. When the singular-value ordering
changes between the two transforms being compared — which is exactly what a depth stretch of 1.19 does — a
*different* axis gets negated and the geodesic angle jumps by ~100°.

Direct check on I46 (`T_oct2mri_structural.npy` vs `T_oct2mri.npy`, both `det < 0`): det −1.0297 / −1.2277;
singular values of the relative linear map `M = A_final · A_struct⁻¹` are 1.1892, 1.0420, 0.9622; the **true**
relative rotation of `M` is **2.73°**; the reported `vascular.vs_structural.rotation_deg` is **129.02°**. The
geometric impossibility test: a 129° rotation about the block centre displaces a corner at
`|(7,7,7)| = 12.12 mm` by `2 × 12.12 × sin(64.5°) = 21.9 mm`, against a reported corner mean of 1.52 mm.

**41 such fields** fail an automated consistency scan across `work/runs/*/result.json` — in `I46_otsu`,
`I46_parser`, `I46_parser_wrongpol_v0`, `I58_otsu`, `I62_otsu`, `crop_final*`, `whole_final*`, `crop_mixed*`,
`crop_mind_v2`, `crop_intensity_v2`. Worst offenders: `vascular.vs_structural` (129.0° at 1.52 mm),
`evaluation.restarts.detail[2]` (176.0° at 8.07 mm), `refine.distinct_runner_up` (23.8° at 0.13 mm).

Consequences: **every `rotation_deg` quoted anywhere for a mirrored subject is meaningless**, including the
"129.0°" for I46's vascular stage, the "91.2°" for the oracle affine, and the 108–117° in
`evaluation.vs_author_coarse_placement` (that last one is not provably impossible given a 17.7 mm centre
offset, but it is computed by the same broken code on a mirrored transform and **must be recomputed** before
the "the authors disagree with us by 23 mm and 110°" sentence goes near a paper). **`centre_mm`,
`corner_mean_mm` and `corner_max_mm` are unaffected** — they are computed from the transforms directly — so
every restart-convergence count (`< 0.5 mm`) and vascular count (`< 0.3 mm`) in this chapter is valid. Fix:
compare `M = T1[:3,:3] @ inv(T2[:3,:3])`, take its polar factor once, and if `det(M) < 0` report "handedness
differs" rather than an angle.

#### 6.14.2 Other traps in the JSONs and prose

| Trap | Correct reading |
|---|---|
| `stretch_ijk` vs `final_transform.column_scales` | different orderings. `stretch_ijk[0]` is the OCT depth axis; `column_scales[2]` holds the same number. Several summaries print one and label it the other |
| Block sizes in the prose docs | unreliable; recompute from `prep.json` as `oct.shape_native × oct.spacing_um_zyx`. I46 is 7.5 × 15.3 × 14.8 mm (not 15×15×7); **I56 is 9.8 × 45.2 × 43.0 mm**, against the "33x49x44 mm slab" recorded in `results_inspection/INDEX.md` — **wrong by ≈3× on the first axis**. Never reproduce that INDEX.md line without the correction attached to it |
| `mri_vessels.npy` | the **manual MRI vessel label** (bool), loaded from `--mri-vessels …label-vessels_dseg.nii.gz` and used for **evaluation only**. It is *not* the local-median dark-blob map — that is `vascular.mri_dark_channel`, computed in RAM inside `register.py` and never written to disk. Getting this backwards would make the vessel evaluation look circular when it is not |
| "5 of 9 subjects are mirrored" | 6 of 9: I38, I46, I48, I56, I58, I62 |
| "DANDI 8 finished subjects" (`octreg/README.md:42`) | 9 were run: I38 I46 I48 I55 I56 I57 I58 I61 I62 |
| "15–40 min per subject" | 18.7 – 131.1 min; only 4 of 9 fall inside 15–40 min. Budget **2.5 h/subject** for large 30 µm slabs |
| "one section period ≈ 100 slices at 12 µm" (`prep_subject.py:125`) | measured period is **33 slices** (I46, 0.396 mm) and **12 slices** (I56, 0.420 mm) — ~3× smaller. The `window = max(10, round(1200/spacing_z))` formula happens to work for I46 (3.03 periods) but gives 2.83 periods for I56, i.e. **not an integer multiple**, leaving a residual sawtooth. The "≈100" traces to a profile inspected at 25-slice granularity, which aliases a 33-slice period to ≈100. This is a **slab-window** fact only: the same measurement was once used as a fourth line of evidence for the I46 depth-spacing correction, and **that use is withdrawn** (§6.11.2) |
| The README's whole-hemisphere Dice claim for bias-field flattening, "0.66/0.62 → 0.90/0.93" | **Confirmed.** No artefact carried it when the README was written, so it was re-derived directly on I46: raw Otsu **WM 0.6502 / GM 0.5987** against locally flattened **WM 0.9069 / GM 0.9343**, from a measured 1.9× intensity drift across the hemisphere — the README's rounding is right to ≤ 0.02. Quote the rounded pair in prose; this row is the one place the precise pair is needed |

### 6.15 What is NOT yet demonstrated

Ordered by how badly it would hurt if a reviewer asked.

| # | Not demonstrated | Exactly what exists instead |
|---|---|---|
| **N1** | **Sub-millimetre accuracy on our own data.** | Nothing numeric. `work/runs/xiangrui_I58bs_novasc/result.json → evaluation.final` contains **only** `stretch_ijk` and `block_centre_mri_mm`. The residual "a few millimetres, larger toward the deep end" is a visual estimate from the checkerboard panel of `octreg/figures/fig_I58_brainstem.png`. `[UNVERIFIED]` — no artefact quantifies it |
| **N2** | **Any quantitative accuracy metric that works without labels.** | Restart stability (§6.9), search margin, and the vessel-channel NCC. The first two are not accuracy; the third is dead on the brainstem (0.0055). The proposed fix — ask for ~20 matched anatomical points per pair, ~30 min of annotation, report TRE — has **not been requested** from the PI; the action item is open |
| **N3** | **Robustness on bath-heavy MRI.** | **3 of 3 subjects whose foreground mask failed produced a wrong or unconfirmed pose** — I61 (1 838.8 cm³), DANDI I58 (1 453.4 cm³) and I56 (2 519.0 cm³), all `valley_ratio: null`. No fix is implemented; exploratory work only, `octreg/scripts/test_texture_mask.py` → `work/texture_mask_test.png`. **I57 is not in this group**: its mask is normal (518.0 cm³, `valley_ratio 0.0631`, threshold above the median) and its failure has no explanation at all (§6.13.3) |
| **N4** | **Anything on the brainstem beyond global pose.** | The vascular stage is **switched off** there (NCC 0.0055, 0/8 restarts, 4 778 s cost, 2.652 mm move on a dead channel). A raw-intensity fine polish is **actively harmful** — NCC 0.033 → 0.030 while dragging the block 9.55 mm corner mean / 12.3 mm max off a correct pose. Tissue/agarose separation by intensity is impossible: 77.9 % of the block is called tissue |
| **N5** | **That 5 of 9 DANDI subjects are correct.** | Two are (I46, I55). Three (I38, I56, I62) rest on unverified visual QC that three quantitative checks contradict (§6.8). One (I48) has no score separation at all (0.2571 vs 0.2558). Honest count: **2 confirmed, 3 unresolved, 1 undecidable, 3 failed** |
| **N6** | **That the depth-scale recovery generalises.** | Needed on exactly **one** subject (I46), demonstrated absent on exactly **one** (I55). Nothing else in the dataset has a wrong sidecar to recover. n = 1 |
| **N7** | **Laminar / cortical-layer alignment.** | The labels carry infragranular vs supragranular; the evaluator collapses both to GM and the OCT side has only two classes. Nothing was ever measured about layers |
| **N8** | **That the whole-hemisphere search is needed.** | The PI stated on 2026-08-23 that a position prior *is* available in practice, and the I58 MRI he supplied is already cropped. §6.10.9 also shows the ±30 mm cropped search and the whole-hemisphere search converge to the same pose on I46. Global search is **robustness insurance and a paper capability**, not the value proposition |
| **N9** | **That the method beats the baseline.** | No head-to-head was run. Costantini's pipeline was never executed on our machine; the comparison is a feature-by-feature reading of their `mri2oct_affine.sh`. Their published pose for I46 disagrees with ours by **23.0–23.2 mm corner mean / 17.7 mm centre**, and that disagreement is **unresolved** |
| **N10** | **Generalisation beyond cortical blocks plus hemisphere MRI.** | 9 Broca's-area blocks from one study plus 1 brainstem pair from one specimen. One tissue type, two scanners, one species |
| **N11** | **That the reported figures are correct.** | The five-panel subject figures the PI approved on 2026-08-23 were generated by Claude Code and **have not been human-verified**; the action item is open |
| **N12** | **That the headline I46 numbers are reproducible with the code on disk.** | Five of the nine headline runs predate the current source; `I46_otsu` is the only run whose prep *and* registration both predate it, and its `overlap_gate` is `null` because the feature did not exist yet. The tree is unversioned, so the producing revision is **unrecoverable** (§6.3.4) |
| **N13** | **That the reject gates work.** | Neither the margin gate nor the tissue-volume gate is implemented, and the margin gate as proposed would also reject I55 and the brainstem run (§6.9.4) |
