### 6.16 How a skeptic would attack this, and the honest answer

| # | Attack | Honest answer |
|---|---|---|
| **A1** | *"Dice 0.80 is mediocre — same-modality registration gets 0.95."* | Concede the number, reject the comparison. This is cross-modality, cross-resolution (12 µm vs 150 µm), automatic-classes-vs-manual-labels, and the reference labels are interpolated between contours drawn every 1.5 mm and disagree with the authors' own second annotation of the same tissue on 6.8 % of voxels. Then pivot: Dice is not our accuracy metric and we can prove it is unusable as one — **0.857 WM Dice at a pose 71.1 mm from the truth** (§6.5.3, and chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning, for the full table). |
| **A2** | *"You are scoring against your own output."* | Half true, and say so first. `vessels_own` (122.8 µm) **is** the objective the vascular stage maximises and must never be quoted as accuracy — the tell is that its own ±3 mm control (212 µm) sits almost on top of its structural registered value (173 µm). The honest channel is `vessels_vesseg` (166.7 µm), the authors' manual OCT segmentation, which the pipeline never touches. The Dice labels are likewise the authors' and enter only at evaluation. |
| **A3** | *"Your random-placement control is a 3 mm nudge."* | Fully concede — this is the weakest link in the evidence. Give the real numbers immediately: ±3 mm shift → 352 µm; uniform random point inside the block → **530 µm / f150 0.117**; registered → 167 µm / 0.473. Then offer the three *strong* controls that do exist: depth-flip of the vessel density (269.5 µm), k-slice permutation (266.2 µm), and the identical optimisation schedule with the vessel channel removed (265.8 µm) — all three collapse the entire gain. Then state plainly that a random-pose-in-hemisphere control was not run and is the top missing experiment. |
| **A4** | *"f150 = 0.47 means you miss 53 % of vessels."* | The oracle affine — fitted to the very vessels being scored — reaches 0.466, and cross-validated on held-out vessel components 0.416 ± 0.041. The best *oracle non-rigid* deformation reaches 0.480. There is at most 0.014–0.04 of f150 left in any transform model. 0.47 is the annotation's ceiling and 4× the 0.117 chance level. |
| **A5** | *"Your two vessel rows are scored on different point sets (4 040 vs 4 999), so 265 → 167 µm is not like-for-like."* | Checked, and it works **against** us. On the 3 950-point intersection the improvement is **260 → 119 µm** and f150 **0.287 → 0.568**, and the p95 tail improves rather than worsens. The shipped 166.7 µm is the conservative figure. |
| **A6** | *"Restart consistency proves nothing."* | Agree completely and volunteer the damning statistic: two of the three runs with 12/12 restarts are the two marked wrong, the third is the most-contested "correct", and the two quantitatively confirmed subjects have the loosest scatter in the corpus (9/12 each). Mean 11.3/12 for wrong runs vs 10.2/12 for correct ones. Restarts are a stability screen. Also volunteer *why*: a bath-contaminated tissue mask produces a wide, smooth, very reproducible optimum. |
| **A7** | *"5 of 9 is a 56 % success rate."* | Reframe to 2 confirmed / 3 unresolved / 1 undecidable / 3 failed, then say **three of the four bad cases are diagnosable in advance from fields already in `result.json`** — search margin 0.0013 (I48) and 0.0001 (I58); `valley_ratio: null` with MRI tissue volume 1 453–1 839 cm³ (I58, I61). **The fourth, I57, is not.** Its mask is normal, its `valley_ratio` of 0.0631 is a *clean* separation rather than a warning, its tissue volume 518.0 cm³ is unremarkable, and its failure has no mechanism (§6.13.3). Say three, not four, and never repeat "bath-heavy" about I57. Do not oversell the gates either: the margin gate as proposed would also reject I55 and the brainstem run, and an absolute `refine.final_ncc` floor would pass I61 (0.5020) and I57 (0.5121) while failing I62 (0.2842) (§6.9.4). The one thing you cannot say is that the pipeline warned you — it returned 12/12 restarts on two of the three wrong runs. |
| **A8** | *"Your evaluation labels are broken for 6 of 9 subjects — how do you know anything?"* | Concede immediately. Then note the bug is in `map_labels_to_grid`, is entirely on the evaluation side, and cannot bias the registration: search and refinement run on the MRI's own voxel grid with isotropic spacing and an exhaustive orientation search, so a wrong world-axis labelling in a *label* header cannot reach the transform. The two subjects with lossless mapping (I46, I55) are exactly the two we quote. The fix is re-prep plus re-evaluation only — no re-registration, because `result.json` stores `final_transform`. |
| **A9** | *"Three of your 'successes' are 60 mm from their own annotations."* | Concede fully; it is the single most important open question. Then give the correlation: the six subjects with a broken label mapping are **exactly** the six with a distant annotation cloud, and the two with lossless mapping are **exactly** the two with a coincident one, across all nine subjects. That makes a header artefact the leading hypothesis — but it is a hypothesis, the H2 test costs ~1 h, and until it is run neither verdict may be claimed. |
| **A10** | *"The 1.17 agreement is a coincidence between numbers in incomparable frames."* | Concede the frame problem and refuse to turn it into a TRE. Then give the reverse test: I55, whose sidecar is correct, needs **no** depth correction (0.920 → 0.913) and its vascular stage moves the block **0.334 mm** against I46's 1.524 mm, with 8/8 vascular restarts in both cases. A coincidence does not produce a correct negative control. Then volunteer the qualification before it is extracted: I55's recovered depth-to-in-plane anisotropy is **0.8570 = 6/7**, the exact inverse of the 7/6 factor I46 is missing, and that is unexplained (§6.11.3). The 0.334 mm of block motion is the part of the control the coincidence does not touch; the 0.913 itself is not. |
| **A11** | *"The vessel channel is just extra degrees of freedom fitting noise."* | Three controls: the identical optimisation schedule with **no** vessel channel → 265.8 µm / f150 0.277 (no gain); vessel density flipped along depth → 269.5 / 0.269; vessel density with k-slices permuted → 266.2 / 0.275. The gain is the correspondence, not the freedom. |
| **A12** | *"Your own JSON reports a 129° rotation for a 1.5 mm move — your numbers are internally inconsistent."* | Found, diagnosed, and it is a metric bug, not a result bug. `common.polar_rotation` forces `det > 0` by flipping a singular-vector column, which is unstable for mirrored transforms. The true relative rotation between I46's structural and final transforms is **2.73°**, not 129.02°. **41 such fields exist.** Translations, corner distances and every restart count are unaffected. Fix or delete the field before publishing any rotation (§6.14.1). |
| **A13** | *"You claim a bias-flattening Dice jump of 0.66 → 0.90 and there is no artefact for it."* | There is one now, and it confirms the claim. The measurement was re-derived directly on I46 and reproduces the README to ≤ 0.02: local-mean flattening before Otsu takes WM/GM Dice from **0.66 / 0.62 to 0.90 / 0.93**, driven by a measured 1.9× intensity drift across the hemisphere. Quote it freely; the precise pair is in §6.14.2. |
| **A14** | *"You never ran the baseline."* | True — state it. The comparison is a reading of `mri2oct_affine.sh`, and their published pose for I46 is 23 mm from ours, unresolved. Getting their pipeline running is an open action item. |
| **A15** | *"Your best result comes from a code revision you cannot produce."* | True and it must be volunteered, not extracted. Five of nine headline runs predate the current source; `I46_otsu` is the only one whose prep and registration both do, and its `overlap_gate` is `null` because the gate did not exist. The tree is unversioned, so the producing revision is unrecoverable. The correct response is to `git init` the authoritative tree, re-run I46 with today's code, and report both numbers (§6.3.4). |
| **A16** | *"Your headline runtime is 150 s for a whole hemisphere; your own logs say 299 s."* | Both are real measurements of different things. 153.7 s is `run_demo_i46.py --features mixed`, whose MRI channels are the **trained parser's probabilities**; the label-free path is 298.9 s per polarity and 597.8 s with the shipped `--oct-wm-bright auto`. Quote 299 / 598 under any "label-free" heading. Also concede that search is not the bottleneck — the vascular stage is 72–91 % of wall clock on the worst runs. |

**The five experiments that would change these answers, cheapest first:**

| # | Experiment | Cost | What it settles |
|---|---|---|---|
| **E1** | Fix `map_labels_to_grid`, re-prep the six 0.12 mm subjects, re-run **evaluation only** | ~1 h, no re-registration | whether I38/I56/I62's 60 mm annotation gap is real or a header artefact — the biggest open question (§6.8) |
| **E2** | Re-run DANDI I58 on `sub-I58_ses-MRI_flip-1_VFA.nii.gz` (30°, already on disk, 2 890 933 645 B) | ~30 min | whether I58's failure is the 10° flip angle as diagnosed |
| **E3** | A true random-pose control: N random overlap-passing poses from the existing 16 000-orientation grid, scored with `vessel_distance_stats` | ~1 h | closes attack A3 permanently |
| **E4** | Re-run `scale_probe.py` from the **final** transform, reporting the i-axis profile of the **vessel-channel** NCC | ~30 min | resolves the §6.10.3 inconsistency in the depth-scale story |
| **E5** | Ask Xiangrui for ~20 matched anatomical points on the I58 brainstem pair (~30 min of his time) and report TRE | 1 email | the only route to a number on our own data |

Two more, cheap and worth doing: re-run `octreg/scripts/label_offset.py` (30 lines, output never persisted) to
measure whether the MRI vessel labels are systematically offset from the dark blobs they mark — this decides
whether 167 µm is a registration floor or an annotation floor; and fix `transform_diff`'s rotation metric
before any rotation number is published.

## 7. Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us

Nine DANDI subjects were registered end to end with identical flags. Three are marked **wrong** (I57,
I61, I58), one **uncertain** (I48), five **correct** — and of those five only two (I46, I55) have any
quantitative support. Everything in this chapter comes from the artefacts on the AutoDL box
(`~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration`, `work/runs/*/result.json`, `work/<SUB>/prep.json`, `logs/*.log`),
not from the prose docs, which are wrong on several of these numbers. Where the project's own prose
(`octreg/README.md`, `octreg/EXPLAINER_zh.md`, the meeting notes under `meeting_recordings/`) disagrees
with an artefact, the artefact wins, the corrected value is used, and the disagreement is named on the
spot; the consolidated list of such corrections is in chapter 12, Open questions and unverified claims.

The single most useful thing to know before reading further: **nothing in this project has ever failed
noisily.** Every wrong pose so far has a respectable objective value, tight restart convergence, and an
obviously wrong QC picture. Convergence is not correctness, and the failure detector is your eyes plus
the independent annotations — not the score.

**On the volume column, because the rest of this document depends on it.** These are

masks that are broken, and every rejection threshold quoted later in this chapter is derived from the
same band, not from memory.

Two corrections that matter and are already applied above. **I57's structural restarts are 10/12, not
12/12**: `work/runs/I57_otsu/result.json → evaluation.restarts.detail[].corner_mean_mm` gives min /
median / max of 0.381 / 0.388 / 0.536 mm, so two of the twelve restarts miss the 0.5 mm gate. Several of
the project's prose docs say 12/12 and contradict their own tables; the same per-run restart scatter is
tabulated in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.3.3. And **the `flip-N` filename index is
not the flip angle** — read `FlipAngle` out of the `.json` sidecar beside each NIfTI, never off the
filename. For I58 the sidecars read `flip-1` → FlipAngle **30**, `flip-3` → FlipAngle **10**, and the
pipeline ran on flip-3, i.e. 10°; the per-subject file-to-angle map is in chapter 4, The data, §4.4.

#### 7.1.2 I48 — "uncertain": the search landscape is flat, so there is no answer to believe

**Symptom.** `search.top1 = 0.2571`, `search.top2 = 0.2558`. The margin between the best and the
second-best *distinct* pose is **0.0013 (0.5 %)**. The refined NCC (0.2584) is barely above the search
score, meaning the 0.6 → 0.3 → 0.15 mm affine cascade found essentially nothing to improve. The score
plateaued early: 0.2558 at 4 000 of 16 000 orientations, 0.2571 at 8 000, unchanged to 16 000 — twelve
more minutes of search bought 0.0013. The losing polarity branch reaches 0.2422 search / 0.2503 refined,
only 0.008 below the winner, so **the polarity decision is unseparated as well**. Restarts look fine
(11/12), which is exactly the trap: the optimiser reliably returns to a maximum that means nothing.

**Independent evidence.** `vessels_own` and `vessels_vesseg` both report `n_inside = 0`. I48 has the
largest manual vessel annotation in the corpus (79 331 voxels) and it sits **50.7 mm** from the block
centre with 0.0 % inside; the BA labels sit 51.1 mm away, 0.0 % inside. Where labels do exist under the
slab (`frac_on_mri_labels = 0.575`) only **36.5 %** of on-label OCT-WM voxels land on MRI WM — below
chance for a two-class problem, the same signature as I38 and I56.

Read that in both directions, and do not file I48 with the large slabs. **I48's Dice is untrustworthy in
both directions.** It is not being suppressed by missing labels — coverage is 0.575, so the
label-coverage story that explains I62's zeros (§7.4.1, step 10) does not apply here — and it is not
usable as evidence *for* the pose either, because the run's whole problem is that no pose is
distinguishable from any other. **The "uncertain" verdict rests on the 0.0013 search-score margin, not on
any label statistic**, and I48 would still be uncertain if its labels were perfect.

**Diagnosed cause.** `work/I48/prep.json`: the MRI is `sub-I48_ses-MRI_flip-2_VFA.nii.gz` and **its JSON
sidecar is missing**, so no FlipAngle can be read and the file was used on the assumption that `flip-2`
means 20° as it does for the other subjects. The MRI histogram has two peaks at 10.3 and 16.9 with
`valley_ratio 0.474` — the worst valley separation in the whole set (a ratio approaching the 0.5 accept
threshold means the two modes are barely distinguishable). Tissue fraction 0.156, the lowest of all
subjects. So the MRI's two-class WM/GM split — the only thing the structural search actually correlates
against — carries almost no contrast. A flat 0.2571/0.2558 landscape is precisely what that produces.

**What would fix it.**

| Fix | Detail |
|---|---|
| Confirm the acquisition | Recover the true flip angle from the raw DANDI multi-echo data or the study protocol; if a 20° volume exists for I48, re-run against it. |
| A hard reject rule | Abort with "no separation" when `top1/top2 < 1.02`, instead of emitting a transform. An absolute-score clause (`top1 < 0.35`) has also been proposed and must not be used — see the [OPEN] note below. Chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.9.4 works through the same gates and their cost. |
| A better MRI two-class split | The real fix. Local-mean flattening + Otsu is not enough when the underlying contrast is this weak. |

**[OPEN] — do not implement that reject rule as written.** By arithmetic on the panel above it would
also reject **I55** (`0.6112/0.6089` = ratio 1.0038, margin 0.0023), which is the second-best-validated
subject in the project, and would reject **I56** (top1 0.3397) and **I62** (0.2872) on the absolute-score
clause. Achievable NCC falls as the block gets bigger, so any usable gate has to be conditioned on block
size and on restart convergence, not on a global constant. This calibration has not been done.

#### 7.1.3 I57 and I61 — two "wrong" whole-hemisphere runs with different causes, one of them unknown

These two share a data regime (0.12 mm, whole hemisphere, FlipAngle 20, `flip-4` files) and a verdict,
and almost nothing else. **I61 is a tissue-mask failure and is diagnosed. I57 is not a tissue-mask
failure, and its failure has no explanation at all — `[OPEN]`.** An earlier pass of this document filed
both under a single "the foreground mask fails" heading; that was wrong, and the two need different
fixes. Keep them apart.

| | I57 | I61 |
|---|---|---|
| MRI | `sub-I57_ses-MRI_flip-4_VFA.nii.gz`, FlipAngle 20 | `sub-I61_ses-MRI_flip-4_VFA.nii.gz`, FlipAngle 20 |
| grid | 1600×1400×640 @ 0.12 mm | 1600×1400×640 @ 0.12 mm |
| `tissue_thresh` | 15.77 | **6.80** |
| `tissue_fraction` | 0.209 | **0.742** |
| histogram peaks | 13.61, 23.86 | 8.72, 17.55 |
| `valley_ratio` | **0.0631** — a valley *was* found, the cleanest cut in the corpus | **null** (no valley found → fallback floor) |
| MRI intensity median (p50) | 13.80 — the threshold sits **above** it | 10.42 — the threshold sits **below** it |
| MRI tissue volume handed to the search | 518.0 cm³ — inside the measured 386–806 cm³ band (§7.1.1) | **1 838.8 cm³** — 2.3× the top of it |
| OCT block | 768×1251×2021 @ 35/30/30 µm = 26.9 × 37.5 × 60.6 mm, **two-piece slab** | 608×1067×1407 @ 35/30/30 µm = 21.3 × 32.0 × 42.2 mm |
| search top1 / top2 | 0.4394 / 0.4337 | 0.5172 / 0.5112 |
| refined NCC | 0.5121 | 0.5020 |
| struct restarts | 10/12 (0.381 / 0.388 / 0.536 mm) | **12/12** (0.089 / 0.165 / 0.180 mm) |
| vascular restarts ≤ 0.3 mm | 1/8 | 4/8 |
| vascular vessel-channel NCC | **−0.0020** | 0.0185 |
| distance to labelled hemisphere | 44.5 mm, 0 % inside | **94.5 mm**, 0 % inside |

**Symptom.** The block lands with a *respectable* NCC (0.50–0.51, higher than several runs marked
correct) and *stable* restarts, and has zero overlap with any annotation. I61's placement is ~95 mm from
the labelled hemisphere — it is not in the brain at all.

**Diagnosed cause — I61: the tissue mask ate the bath.** The MRI "tissue" volumes actually recorded in
`prep.json` for the six subjects whose mask is sane run **386.3–805.8 cm³** (§7.1.1). I61's mask is
**1 838.8 cm³**, 2.3× the top of that band, and its threshold of 6.80 sits *below* its own intensity
median of 10.42 — the signature of a cut that never happened. The mechanism is in
`octreg/octreg/common.py::histogram_tissue_threshold` (lines 214–238): starting at the rightmost
prominent histogram peak it walks left over prominent peaks and cuts at the first valley whose height is
below `0.5 ×` the smaller of the two neighbouring peaks; **if no such valley exists it records
`valley_ratio: null` and falls back to `thr = min(p1, 0.5 × multiotsu[0])`**, a floor designed to keep
everything (the right behaviour for a cropped, all-tissue field of view, the wrong one here). I61 lands
exactly on that fallback: threshold 6.80, 74.2 % of the volume declared tissue. The 0.6 mm two-class map
then contains a large field of homogeneous bath fluid, and a 21–24 cm³ OCT block finds a comfortable,
repeatable, meaningless correlation maximum inside it.

**I57 has no diagnosed cause — `[OPEN]`.** Every mechanism that explains I61 is absent here, and this
must be said plainly rather than papered over. I57's mask is not over-inclusive: 518.0 cm³, comfortably
inside the measured 386–806 cm³ band, tissue fraction 0.209. Its threshold of 15.77 sits *above* its
intensity median of 13.80, the opposite of I61's signature. And a valley genuinely was found —
`valley_ratio 0.0631`, the cleanest separation of any subject in the corpus — so the peak-walk never fell
through to its fallback floor. By every diagnostic the pipeline records, **I57's MRI foreground is the
healthiest in the set**, and the pose is still 51.3 mm from the manual vessel cloud with 0.0 % of it
inside the block.

The only thing on record is a human impression:
`~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration/results_inspection/INDEX.md` notes the verdict as "captured by a flat
MRI region (two-piece slab)". That is a description of the QC picture, not a diagnosis — no artefact
tests it. The one structural peculiarity worth chasing is real and checkable: I57's OCT block is 60.6 mm
along its long axis and consists of **two separate tissue pieces**, and the search scores the **union**
of those pieces, so a pose that puts the union over a large homogeneous region can score well without
either piece being anatomically right. Nobody has measured whether that is what happened. **I57 is the
one failure in the corpus with no explanation, which makes it the most informative thing left to
explain.**

**Which subjects the tissue-mask story actually covers.** It covers **I61** (threshold 6.80 below its
median, tissue fraction 0.742, 1 838.8 cm³, `valley_ratio: null`) and **DANDI I58** (threshold 2.12,
fraction 0.587, 1 453.4 cm³, `valley_ratio: null`, §7.1.4). **I56's mask is broken by the same
mechanism** (`null`, threshold 3.62, 98.9 % of the volume called tissue, 2 519.0 cm³) and yet the run was
marked correct. So a broken mask is neither necessary for a wrong pose (I57 is wrong with a clean mask)
nor sufficient for one (I56 survived a badly broken mask). The story does **not** cover **I57**, for the
reasons just given, and it does not cover **I48**, whose problem is contrast rather than foreground
(§7.1.2).

**The `null` flag is a warning, not a verdict.** I55 also has `valley_ratio: null` and its fallback
threshold happened to land correctly (tissue fraction 0.240, verdict correct); I56's `null` produced a
98.9 % mask and the result still survived, real anatomy outvoting a broken mask. Treat `null` plus a
tissue fraction above ~0.45 on a whole hemisphere as "look at this now", not "this run is dead".

**What would fix I61 — and, with §7.1.4's contrast fix, I58. None of it is known to touch I57.**

| Fix | Detail | Status |
|---|---|---|
| A tissue mask that is not a global intensity threshold | Bath and tissue differ in **texture**, not in mean intensity. This is the same fix the brainstem pair needs (§7.1.6). | Exploratory only — `octreg/scripts/test_texture_mask.py`, output `work/texture_mask_test.png`; the recorded conclusion in `octreg/EXPLAINER_zh.md` §4 is that pure texture thresholding fails on both datasets and texture must be **fused** with intensity |
| A sanity gate on mask volume | Reject/flag when the "tissue" volume exceeds ~1.5× the top of the measured band, i.e. **> ~1 210 cm³** (`1.5 × 806`). On this corpus that flags I61 (1 838.8), I56 (2 519.0) and I58 (1 453.4) and clears all six sane masks, the largest being I38 at 805.8 cm³ | Not implemented |
| Multi-piece slab handling — the only lead on I57 | Require **each connected OCT component** to land on tissue, instead of scoring the union. This is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis: nothing has measured whether it is what went wrong | Not implemented |
| Manual override, available today | `prep_subject.py --mri-tissue-thresh <value>` after eyeballing the histogram, then re-run `register.py` | Works now; the immediate remedy for a bad `tissue frac` |

#### 7.1.4 I58 (DANDI) — "wrong": only a 10° flip angle exists, so there is no GM/WM contrast to correlate

Do not confuse this with Xiangrui's I58 brainstem pair (§7.1.6). They are different specimens and
different results; the DANDI subject I58 is a failed whole-hemisphere run, the brainstem pair is a
successful coarse registration. Runs: `work/runs/I58_otsu` versus `work/runs/xiangrui_I58bs_novasc`.

**Symptom.** `tissue_thresh = 2.12`, `tissue_fraction = 0.587`, **one** histogram peak (`n_peaks: 1`,
`valley_ratio: null`), intensity p50/p99 = 16.9 / 40.8 — the narrowest dynamic range in the corpus. MRI
"tissue" volume 1 453.4 cm³. Search `top1 = 0.2896`, `top2 = 0.2895`: a margin of **0.0001**, the worst
in the project. Refined NCC 0.2708 with wildly unbalanced per-channel NCC `[0.344, 0.197]`. Restarts
12/12. Placement 63.0 mm from the labelled hemisphere, 66.9 mm from the manual vessel cloud,
`frac_on_mri_labels = 0.000`, Dice 0/0.

**Diagnosed cause.** `data/costantini/dandi-000026/derivatives/EPIC/sub-I58/ses-MRI/anat/` contains
exactly two volumes: `sub-I58_ses-MRI_flip-1_VFA.nii.gz` with `"FlipAngle": "30"` (2 890 933 645 bytes,
on disk since 2026-08-20 11:49) and `sub-I58_ses-MRI_flip-3_VFA.nii.gz` with `"FlipAngle": "10"`. **There
is no 20° acquisition for I58**, unlike every other subject, and `work/I58/prep.json → mri.file` confirms
the pipeline used the 10° file. At a 10° flip a FLASH VFA volume is essentially proton-density weighted:
WM and GM have almost no contrast, so the Otsu two-class split on the MRI side is noise. On top of that
the tissue mask failed the same way I61's did (1 453 cm³, `valley_ratio: null`). It is I61's foreground
failure **plus** a contrast failure.

**What would fix it.**

| Fix | Detail |
|---|---|
| Use the 30° volume | `sub-I58_ses-MRI_flip-1_VFA.nii.gz` is downloaded and **has never been tried**. This is the cheapest experiment in the whole backlog. |
| Synthesise 20°-equivalent contrast | VFA T1 fitting from the 10° + 30° pair; both volumes exist locally. |
| Texture-based tissue mask | Same fix as §7.1.3. |
| Margin reject gate | A margin of 0.0001 would have been caught automatically by any separation test (subject to the calibration caveat in §7.1.2). |

#### 7.1.5 The three "correct" subjects that may also be failures — I38, I56, I62 [OPEN]

This is the most important unresolved question in the results, and it belongs in a failures chapter
because it may move three subjects across the line.

Every OCT block in DANDI:000026 is a `sample-BrocaAreaS01` block, and the `ba_labels` volume marks
Broca's area in the same EPIC MRI space. For I46 and I55 the registered block sits on the BA label
(12.8 % and 59.0 % of BA voxels inside the block; centroids 9.6 mm and 7.8 mm away). For **I38, I56 and
I62 the registered block contains 0.0 % of the BA labels and sits 57–65 mm away** — the same 55–66 mm
that the manual vessel annotations give, from a completely independent annotation. For I38 and I56 the
block *is* inside the labelled hemisphere (12.0 % / 5.4 % of hemisphere labels inside it,
`frac_on_mri_labels` 0.607 / 0.450) but the OCT WM class lands on MRI **GM** about twice as often as on
MRI WM: **35.0 %** and **36.8 %** of on-label OCT-WM voxels land on MRI WM
(confusion matrices `evaluation.final.gmwm.confusion_oct_rows_mri_cols`: I38
`[[0,0,0],[1488359,843559,1570140],[3402369,1969290,3169824]]`, I56
`[[0,0,0],[725859,285654,491373],[1417125,406327,570784]]`). That is worse than chance, not a coverage
artefact.

The "correct" verdicts for these three rest **entirely** on visual inspection of
`octreg/figures/fig_I38.png`, `fig_I56.png`, `fig_I62.png` and `work/runs/*/qc_vessels.png`. Two
independent quantitative checks — and for I38/I56 a third — point the other way.

The concrete test to run first: open `results_inspection/I38_otsu/{mri_region.nii.gz,
oct_in_mri_region.nii.gz, mri_labels_region.nii.gz}` in Freeview and check whether the BA label patch is
visible anywhere near the slab. If the annotations are 60 mm away while the overlay looks right, then
either the label volume is in a different space than assumed, or the OCT slab is not from Broca's area
for these subjects, or the pose is wrong. Related and unresolved `[UNVERIFIED]`: a 0.12 mm label-axis
mis-pairing has been reported that would invalidate Dice for I38/I48/I56/I57/I58/I61 — the check is
`octreg/scripts/label_offset.py`, and chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.14 lists the
evaluation fields already known to be broken. If that report is right, the Dice-based half of this
argument weakens, but the 57–65 mm annotation distances do not.

Until this is settled, the honest headline is **two subjects quantitatively verified, three visually
plausible, one uncertain, three wrong** — not "five correct".

#### 7.1.6 I58 brainstem (our own data) — a successful run with two failed stages inside it

`work/runs/xiangrui_I58bs_novasc` is the reported result: search top1 0.1247 / top2 0.1184 (5.3 %
margin), converged by 4 000 of 16 000 orientations in **45 s**, refined NCC 0.1014, 10/12 structural
restarts, `stretch_ijk = [0.969, 0.988, 0.972]`, total wall time **362 s**. The human verdict is "coarse
correct": specimen outline, the dome-shaped section, and a separate small tissue piece all land on their
MRI counterparts. Residual is described as "a few millimetres, larger toward the deep end" — that is a
visual estimate from the checkerboard panel of `octreg/figures/fig_I58_brainstem.png`.
**[UNVERIFIED — no artefact quantifies the residual.** There are no labels, no annotations, and
`evaluation.final` for this run contains only `stretch_ijk` and `block_centre_mri_mm`; the vessel and
Dice blocks are absent.]

Three things failed inside or around that run, and all three are the lab's own data, so they matter more
than the DANDI failures for what comes next:

| Failure | Numbers | Cause | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| **The vascular stage has no basin here** | `vascular.ncc_channels = [0.0013, 0.1844, 0.0055]` — the vessel channel scores 0.0055 and the WM channel collapses from −0.017 to 0.001; the stage moved the block **2.652 mm** corner mean (max 4.005 mm), rotation 14.6°; **0/8** vascular restarts within 0.3 mm (0.828 / 2.969 / 3.683 mm); it cost **4 778 s** of the 5 244 s total | The OCT "vessels" are the serial-section seam artefact. `logs/prep_xiangrui.log` records 4 534 410 own-vessel voxels from the top-1 % dark-tube Frangi on a stack with strong vertical striping — the dark-tube detector fires on the seams, so the "vessel density" is a map of the sectioning grid, not of vasculature | **`register.py --vascular off`.** `xiangrui_I58bs_novasc` supersedes `xiangrui_I58bs`; identical structural result, 362 s instead of 5 244 s |
| **Raw-intensity fine polish is actively harmful** | `octreg/scripts/test_polish.py` → `logs/test_polish.log`: `level 0.32mm: NCC 0.033`, `level 0.16mm: NCC 0.030`; it moved the block centre **9.37 mm**, rotation 15.79°, corner mean **9.55 mm**, corner max 12.3 mm away from a correct pose | 20 µm OCT scattering intensity and 0.08 mm ex-vivo FLASH signal are not a monotone function of each other | Not used. See §7.3.4 |
| **Tissue/agarose separation by intensity is impossible** | `logs/prep_xiangrui.log`: `raw tissue thr 0.0`, `oct150 tissue frac 0.779`, `octv tissue frac 0.772` — 77 % of the block called tissue because agarose scatters like tissue; OCT mask 28.9 cm³ vs MRI tissue 13.3 cm³ | Embedding medium has the same scatter statistics as tissue | The overlap gate had to become **adaptive**. It relaxed from the requested 0.85 to an effective **0.369** on this pair, and only then was the correct pose reachable at all. The formula and its floor are given once, in full, in chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning, §5.2 |

Two facts about that gate a successor will otherwise get wrong: it is bounded below by a hard floor, and
**it never binds on DANDI** — all eight DANDI runs that record it show
`{requested 0.85, effective 0.850}`, so the brainstem pair is the only place it has ever done anything.
`work/runs/I46_otsu/result.json` has `overlap_gate: null` because the gate did not exist when I46 was run.
Chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning, §5.2 states the formula and the floor.

Both the vascular and the polish failures share one root cause: **the fine-scale channels assume the
OCT's high-frequency content is anatomy.** On this specimen it is section seams and embedding medium.

#### 7.1.7 The general lesson

Every registration failure listed above **that has an explanation at all** is an MRI-side foreground or
contrast problem, not a search problem. The exception is I57 (§7.1.3), which has no explanation — but
nothing points at the search there either. The evidence:

1. **The search machinery converges hard on the wrong answers.** I58 12/12 restarts and I61 12/12; I57
   10/12 with corner-mean scatter of 0.381–0.536 mm. Tight convergence is not evidence of correctness:
   the only other 12/12 run in the corpus is I38, whose "correct" verdict rests on visual inspection
   alone (§7.1.5). Nothing is being lost to a coarse grid, a bad optimiser, or an unlucky seed.
2. **The wrong poses come with respectable objective values.** I61 refines to NCC **0.5020** and I57 to
   **0.5121**, both *higher* than I56 (0.3661) and I62 (0.2842), which are visually correct. There is
   therefore **no numeric acceptance threshold on `refine.final_ncc` that works**: any cut low enough to
   pass I62 at 0.2842 also passes both wrong runs, and any cut high enough to fail them also fails two
   subjects that are right. Absolute NCC does not separate right from wrong across subjects, and no
   "a good result scores above X" rule should appear anywhere in this project. The absolute score is
   mostly a function of block size.
3. **Where the margin collapses, the MRI contrast has collapsed with it.** I48 margin 0.0013 with
   `valley_ratio 0.474`; I58 margin 0.0001 with `n_peaks: 1` on a 10° flip. The search is faithfully
   reporting that its input contains no information.
4. **Where the mask over-includes, the volume says so before anything else does.** 1 838.8 cm³ (I61) and
   1 453.4 cm³ (I58) against the **386–806 cm³** that the six sane masks in this corpus actually measure
   (§7.1.1). That check costs nothing and is not implemented. It would not have caught I57, whose mask
   volume is 518.0 cm³ and whose failure is still unexplained.
5. **The fix list is entirely MRI-side**: a texture-based (or texture-fused) tissue mask, a mask-volume
   sanity gate, the right flip angle or a VFA-synthesised contrast, and a separation gate on the search
   margin. Not one of them is a change to the search.

The corollary for planning: adding orientations, restarts, or a non-rigid stage will not rescue any of
these subjects. Whole-hemisphere search at 16 000 orientations already finds the same pose as a 30 mm
crop prior (§7.3.8), so the search is not the bottleneck anywhere in this project.

### 7.2 Bugs hit and fixed

#### 7.2.1 Summary

| # | Bug | Symptom you would see | Fix, and where it lives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | float16 overflow in OCT slab normalisation | `inf` in `octv.npy`, poisoning every downstream statistic | gain trick: put the tissue median at ~16 384 and clip at 60 000 — `octreg/octreg/common.py:201-208` |
| 2 | non-finite voxels in the MRI | `ValueError: autodetected range of [..., inf] is not finite` — prep dies | `np.nan_to_num` + logged count at `octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py:69-70`, plus two more guards |
| 3 | naive tissue threshold | wrong pose, absurd `tissue frac` | histogram **peak-walk**, `common.py:214-238` — still not universal |
| 4 | Frangi gamma computed per chunk | stripes along z in the OCT vessel map | one gamma per scale for the whole volume, `features.py:169` + `prep_subject.py:153-158` |
| 5 | GPU OOM | `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError`, or a run that dies in the output stage | voxel budgets derived from in-plane size at 6 places; `result.json` written twice |
| 6 | `DEVICE` import bug | `NameError: name 'DEVICE' is not defined`, ~2 minutes into a multi-hour run | add `DEVICE` to the `from octreg.common import (...)` list in `register.py` |
| 7 | corrupted download with the correct size | `gzip.BadGzipFile: CRC check failed` | delete + re-fetch the one asset; verify with DANDI's `dandi:sha2-256`, never with size |

#### 7.2.2 Bug 1 — float16 overflow in the OCT slab normalisation, and the gain trick

**Symptom.** OCT stacks are stored as `uint16` with values around 10 000–60 000. The slab normaliser
divides each slice by its tissue median and re-multiplies by a running reference, then casts to
`float16`. `float16` maxes out at **65 504**, so bright specular and edge voxels became `inf`, and the
`inf` propagated into every downstream statistic.

**Why float16 at all.** `octv.npy` for I57 is 768×1251×2021 = **1.94 G voxels**. At float32 that is
7.8 GB for a single array; float16 halves it. On a box with 24 GB of VRAM and volumes of 0.2–2 G voxels,
that halving is not optional.

**Fix** — `octreg/octreg/common.py:201-208`, inside `oct_slab_normalize()`:

```python
# float16 output must not overflow (max 65504): put the tissue median at ~16k and cap bright outliers.
gain = 1.0
if np.dtype(out_dtype) == np.float16:
    gain = 16384.0 / max(float(np.nanmedian(ref)), 1e-3); cap = 60000.0
out = np.empty(oct_zyx.shape, dtype=out_dtype)
for i in range(z):
    v = np.asarray(oct_zyx[i], dtype=np.float32) * (scale[i] * gain)
    if gain != 1.0: np.clip(v, 0, cap, out=v)
    out[i] = v.astype(out_dtype, copy=False)
```

The gain is recorded in `work/<SUB>/prep.json`, so you can always recover the physical scale.

#### 7.2.3 Bug 2 — `inf` sanitisation of the MRI

**Symptom**, from `logs/run_all.log` on 2026-08-20 — this killed the I38 and I55 preps outright:

```
[prep I38 FAILED]
  File ".../numpy/lib/histograms.py", line 323, in _get_outer_edges
ValueError: autodetected range of [4.306451161461322e-18, inf] is not finite
[prep I55 FAILED]
ValueError: autodetected range of [2897.099853515625, inf] is not finite
```

**Cause.** The EPIC-corrected VFA NIfTIs contain `inf`/`nan` voxels; `np.histogram` refuses them — and
the histogram is the first thing the tissue threshold needs.

**Fix** — `octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py:69-70`, sanitise immediately after load and *log the count*, so
a silently-bad input becomes visible instead of being silently zeroed:

```python
nbad = int((~np.isfinite(mri)).sum())
if nbad: np.nan_to_num(mri, copy=False, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0); say(f"sanitized {nbad} non-finite MRI voxels -> 0")
```

Two more guards were added behind it: inside `histogram_tissue_threshold()` itself
(`common.py:222`: `sub = sub[np.isfinite(sub) & (sub > 0)]`) and in the OCT Otsu path
(`prep_subject.py:124`). After the fix, I38/I55/I56 were re-prepped — `chain_after_batch.sh` does
`rm -rf work/I38 work/I55 work/I56` first — and all completed. **Diagnostic value for a successor:** if
your prep log does *not* contain the line `sanitized N non-finite MRI voxels -> 0`, you are running a
stale `prep_subject.py`.

#### 7.2.4 Bug 3 — the tissue threshold, three generations, ending in the histogram peak-walk

The MRI foreground mask is the single most failure-prone step in the pipeline, and §7.1 is mostly a
catalogue of its remaining failure modes. Evolution (`octreg/EXPLAINER_zh.md` §5):

| Gen | Method | How it broke |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | plain Otsu | dragged off by bright artefacts |
| 2 | multi-Otsu (3 classes) + valley test | I38's "air \| bath fluid" valley fooled it — it cut in the wrong valley |
| 3 | **histogram peak-walk** (current) | still not universal — I61 defeats it |

Current implementation, `octreg/octreg/common.py:214-238`,
`histogram_tissue_threshold(sub, bins=256, prom=0.05, deep=0.5)`:

1. Drop non-finite and non-positive samples; clip above the 99.5th percentile.
2. 256-bin histogram, smoothed with `uniform_filter1d(size=5)`.
3. `find_peaks(prominence=0.05 * max, distance=5)`.
4. Start at the **rightmost prominent peak** (the tissue mode) and walk left over prominent peaks; cut at
   the first valley whose height is `< 0.5 ×` the smaller of the two neighbouring peaks.
5. If no deep valley exists (an all-tissue field of view, e.g. a cropped MRI), fall back to a floor
   `min(p1, 0.5 × multi-Otsu[0])` that keeps everything.

Step 5 is the correct behaviour for Xiangrui's already-cropped brainstem MRI and the wrong behaviour for
a bath-heavy whole hemisphere; that single branch is the proximate cause of the I61 and I58 failures.

The diagnostic you must read is `tissue frac` in `logs/prep_<SUB>.log` — the per-subject values are in
the §7.1.1 panel. **Rule of thumb: `tissue frac` above ~0.45 on a whole-hemisphere MRI means the
bath/embedding medium is inside the mask.** It does not always break the result (I56 at 0.989 survived),
but it is the first thing to check when the pose is wrong. Manual override:
`prep_subject.py --mri-tissue-thresh <value>`.

#### 7.2.5 Bug 4 — Frangi chunk-wise gamma produced stripe artefacts

**Symptom.** The OCT vessel map showed banding along z, and the top-1 % threshold then carved the mask
into bands at the slab boundaries.

**Cause.** Frangi's structureness term needs a constant `c`. The original code used
`c = 0.5 * max(S)` **per processing chunk**. The volume is processed in z-slabs of 8–64 slices, so every
slab got a different normaliser and identical vessels scored differently in different slabs.

**Fix.** Compute **one `c` per scale for the whole volume** before any chunking.
`octreg/octreg/features.py:169` — `frangi_gamma(vol, sigmas_vox, q=99.9)` returns `0.5 ×` the 99.9th
percentile of the scale-normalised Hessian norm, estimated from **6 strided full-resolution slabs**
spread over the depth (`prep_subject.py:153-158`); that tuple is passed down through
`frangi_chunked(..., gamma=gam)` to every slab. Every subject's `frangi_gamma` is now recorded in
`work/<SUB>/prep.json`. The old behaviour is still reachable (`gamma=None` → per-chunk `0.5*S.max()`);
do not use it.

**The re-run this forced.** `octreg/scripts/run_all.sh` opens with
`rm -f work/I46/octv_vessels.npy   # re-prep I46 with the final prep code (global Frangi gamma)` — the
headline subject had to have its vessel channel rebuilt.

**Related tuning, worth keeping in the same place in your head:** Frangi runs at the **24–35 µm vessel
level, never at native 12 µm** — at 12 µm the filter locks onto speckle rather than vessels
(`EXPLAINER_zh.md` §5; the measured consequence is in §7.3.9: a raw 12 µm Frangi map scores a
vessel-channel NCC of 0.007 and is useless). Sigmas are physical: `sig_um = (24, 36, 53, 72, 106)`,
converted per subject (I46 → `[1.0, 1.5, 2.21, 3.0, 4.42]` vox; the 30–35 µm subjects
I38/I48/I56/I57/I61/I62 → `[0.76, 1.14, 1.67, 2.27, 3.35]` vox).

#### 7.2.6 Bug 5 — GPU OOM, and the slab voxel budget

24 GB of VRAM against volumes of 0.2–2 G voxels. Three separate places needed a budget, and all of them
are now *derived from the in-plane size* rather than hardcoded:

| Location | Budget | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Frangi vesselness over the OCT vessel level | ~**30 M voxels per z-slab** | `prep_subject.py:152` — `zc = clip(30e6 // (H*W) - 2*ov, 8, 64)`, `ov = ceil(3*max(sigma))+1` overlap |
| gamma-estimation subsample | ~**20 M voxels** | `prep_subject.py:154` — `nsl = clip(20e6 // (H*W), 4, 8)` slices × 6 positions |
| Hessian eigen-decomposition inside Frangi | **4 M matrices** | `features.py:169,189` — `chunk = 4_000_000` |
| generic world-space resampling | **8 M points** | `common.py:140` — `resample_to_grid(..., chunk=8_000_000)` |
| whole-MRI feature maps | kept on the **CPU as float16**; only pooled levels and block-sized crops go to the GPU | `register.py` class `MRIFeatures` (`.pooled()` / `.region()`) — a 0.12 mm hemisphere is 1.4 G voxels |
| final output resampling | **64 z-slices at a time** | `register.py:258-263` |

The last one was a real failure: `octreg/scripts/tail_fixups.sh`'s header reads
`redo any subject missing result.json (e.g. I57 output-OOM)`, and `recover2.log` shows
`[register otsu I57] 22:26:01` → `[otsu I57 FAILED]`. The re-run after the z-slab chunking succeeded in
2 831 s. The failing log itself was overwritten by that successful re-run, so what survives is the
`tail_fixups.sh` header and the `recover2.log` timestamps, not the traceback.

Two defensive measures survive from this and are worth preserving. `register.py` writes `result.json`
**twice** — once immediately after the transform is computed, once after the heavy NIfTI/QC outputs — so
an OOM in the output stage cannot destroy a good registration:

```python
write_json(log, a.out / "result.json")   # write the result BEFORE the heavy QC/NIfTI outputs (they must not lose it)
```

And there are explicit `del` + `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` calls at six points in `register.py`
(lines 144, 153, 159, 179, 200, 217).

#### 7.2.7 Bug 6 — the `DEVICE` import bug, and why it cost a full run

**Symptom**, `logs/reg_I46_otsu2.log` — a whole-hemisphere run died shortly after loading:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../octreg/scripts/register.py", line 107, in <module>
    PM06, A06 = MF.pooled(0.6); PT06, _ = MF.pooled(0.6, "tissue"); ...
  File ".../octreg/scripts/register.py", line 80, in pooled
    Dp, Hp, Wp = D // f, H // f, W // f; out = torch.empty((len(srcs), Dp, Hp, Wp), device=DEVICE); ...
NameError: name 'DEVICE' is not defined
```

**Cause.** `MRIFeatures.pooled()` was added to `register.py` and used `DEVICE`, but `register.py`'s
import list from `octreg.common` never included it. Nothing catches this at import time: the class body
compiles fine and the name is only resolved when `.pooled()` is first called — roughly two minutes into
the run, *after* the expensive MRI load and Otsu split.

**Fix.** Add `DEVICE` to the `from octreg.common import (...)` list in `register.py`.
`DEVICE = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")` is defined once at
`octreg/octreg/common.py:23` and is the single source of truth; `features.py:76-77` already does the
right thing (`from .common import DEVICE`; `device = device or DEVICE`).

**Lesson.** A `NameError` in a lazily-executed branch costs a full re-run. Smoke-test the entry point on
a small crop before launching a multi-hour batch:

```bash
python octreg/scripts/register.py --work work/I46 --out /tmp/smoke \
  --crop-centre -6.1,25.7,8.3 --crop-half-mm 30 --n-rot 200
```

#### 7.2.8 Bug 7 — a corrupted download that had exactly the right size

**Symptom**, `logs/recover2.log`, 2026-08-21 01:01:

```
[prep I58] Fri Aug 21 01:01:24 CST 2026
[prep I58 FAILED]
  File ".../gzip.py", line 525, in _read_eof
    raise BadGzipFile("CRC check failed %s != %s" % (hex(crc32), ...
gzip.BadGzipFile: CRC check failed 0xa8730787 != 0x23de8525
```

**Cause.**
`data/costantini/dandi-000026/derivatives/EPIC/sub-I58/ses-MRI/anat/sub-I58_ses-MRI_flip-3_VFA.nii.gz`
was **exactly 2 811 331 089 bytes**, matching the manifest, so every size-based check
(`fetch_manifest.sh`, `run_all.sh`'s skip test, `chain_after_batch.sh`) declared it complete. The bytes
were wrong — almost certainly an aria2 restart across a **6-hour pre-signed-S3-URL expiry** writing a
fresh S3 error body into an offset range (§7.2.10).

**Fix.** Delete and re-fetch that single asset. `logs/redo_I58.log` shows the re-download (2.6 GiB,
average **2.0 MiB/s**, connections ramping from 19 KiB/s to 1.5 MiB/s over 8 connections);
`logs/redo_I58b.log` then shows `[prep I58] 03:33:57 → [register otsu I58] 03:54:47 → [done I58] 04:24:47`.
Verified 2026-08-23: on-disk `sha256sum` = `f6f56ee3b3cbea2b661275a98b800b43dea4f0b27e670d484660653c4a461047`
= DANDI's `dandi:sha2-256` for asset `7b454919-fff2-4e58-a111-1515df2a5959`. The file is good now.

**Standing lesson: file size is not integrity.** DANDI does publish a SHA-256, just not on the `/info/`
endpoint (which returns `digest: null`):

```bash
curl -s https://api.dandiarchive.org/api/assets/<uuid>/ \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["digest"]["dandi:sha2-256"])'
```

Running that loop over all 81 lines of `data/manifest_multisub.txt` is the single highest-value
hardening left undone. Cheap partial check for gzipped NIfTIs in the meantime: `gunzip -t <file>`, or
`python -c "import nibabel; nibabel.load(p).dataobj[0,0,0]"`. Note that the pinned sub-I46 subset in
`download_costantini.sh` already carries `path|asset_uuid|bytes|sha256` for its **16** assets (lines
27–42; the count of 17 that circulates in the prose docs is wrong — count the lines in the file) and
verifies offline via
`PROJECT_ROOT=$PWD ./download_costantini.sh verify`.
