#### 7.2.10 Operational incidents — things that bit us outside the code

These cost days, not minutes. The full procedures live in chapter 10, State of play: where everything is;
what follows is the failure and the rule it produced.

| Incident | What happened | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Two heavy jobs wedged the box | On 2026-08-20 a registration batch and an aria2 download ran together. `sshd` died for **93 minutes** (`logs/run_all.log`: 10:58 → 12:31 hole) while the compute processes kept running normally, so the box looked dead while it was working. `parse_mri.py` on I56 was then taken by the **host** OOM killer (`8720 Killed`). After the switch to serial execution the whole 8-subject batch ran clean (`logs/recover2.log`, 17:17 → 01:01) | **Exactly one heavy job at a time.** A download counts as a heavy job. `run_all.sh` line 2 and `recover_serial.sh` line 2 both carry this in their headers |
| `pkill -f` killed the shell that issued it | `pkill -f PATTERN` matches full command lines. Over SSH, `sshd` spawns `bash -c '<your command>'` whose command line *contains the pattern you just typed*; `pkill` skips its own PID but not that parent, so the script dies mid-way and the connection drops. **Hit twice** (`EXPLAINER_zh.md` §5) | Collect PIDs first, then kill individually (`restart_xiangrui_first.sh`, `rx2.sh`, `rx3.sh` do this). If you must use `pkill`, run it from a script *file* (whose command line is the script name) or bracket a character: `pkill -f 'registe[r].py'`. The dangerous form still lives in `recover_serial.sh` |
| DANDI pre-signed URLs expire in ~6 hours | At 0.1–2 MB/s a 4.8 GB asset can take longer than that; the download dies mid-file with no useful error and aria2 sits on a `*.aria2` control file doing nothing. This is also the probable origin of Bug 7 | `data/dl_watchdog.sh` re-resolves the URLs and restarts aria2 every 90 min while any `*.aria2` remains, exploiting `--continue=true`. `--file-allocation=none` matters — the default preallocation costs minutes per restart on a 4.8 GB file |
| xulab → AutoDL transfer, attempt 1 | A single `rsync` stream is throttled between CMU and the Chinese AutoDL region and died within ~12 min: `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe`, `rsync error: unexplained error (code 255)`. Measured aggregate with 6 parallel streams: `6x32MB in 133s = 1467 KB/s` ≈ 245 KB/s per stream. `[UNVERIFIED]` the often-quoted "~130 KB/s single stream" — no completed single-stream measurement survives, only the failure | One stream never completes |
| xulab → AutoDL transfer, attempt 2 | 195 × 64 MB chunks with 16 workers each opening a **new** SSH connection per chunk. AutoDL's front end refused the connection storm: `kex_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host` × 16 | **Parallelism must come from few, long-lived connections, not many short ones.** Attempt 3 (`xulab_push_seg.sh`: 16 segments, 16 long-lived rsync workers with 40 retries and jittered backoff, remote reassemble + md5 both ends) moved 12.13 GiB in 89 min ≈ 2.4 MB/s wall clock, ~20× the single-stream rate, and verified md5 `42755b8fd8ba4d73332c55804db2ac68` |
| AutoDL host:port changes on every restart | `~/.ssh/config` on the Mac still holds two dead endpoints (`connect.bjb1.seetacloud.com:57039`, `connect.westc.gpuhub.com:23040`), and `xulab-gpu1.pc.cc.cmu.edu` does not resolve from this Mac (use `xulab-login0.lan.cmu.edu`) | After every restart, update `~/.ssh/config` **and** the four scripts on xulab that hardcode `-p 49018` (`push_to_autodl.sh`, `xulab_push_parallel.sh`, `xulab_push_seg.sh`, `xulab_speedtest.sh`), or transfers silently fail |
| Local Mac disk at 98 % | 13 GiB free on `/System/Volumes/Data`; the volume has hit 100 % once already. A single OCT stack is 12.1 GiB | Never pull `data/` or `work/` off the box; pull only `result.json`, `T_oct2mri.*` and PNGs (the local `octreg/results/` mirror is ~29 MB). Never relay large transfers through the Mac — that is why `transfer_xiangrui_oct_mri.sh` was abandoned for the server-to-server `xulab_push_seg.sh` |
| No `ffmpeg` on the Mac | The only working build is inside ChimeraX at `/Applications/ChimeraX-1.10.app/Contents/bin/ffmpeg` (ffmpeg 6.0, arm64) and it is mode `-rw-r--r--`, so it cannot be executed in place | Copy out and `chmod 700` — `ensure_ffmpeg()` in `meeting_recordings/tools/transcribe_recordings.py:68` and `transcribe_one.py:36` do this. Both hardcode the ChimeraX 1.10 path and break if it is upgraded or removed |
| `swiftc` cannot build against its own SDK | Command Line Tools shipped compiler `swiftlang-6.2.3.3.21` against an SDK built with `swiftlang-6.2.3.3.2`, plus a duplicate `SwiftBridging` module definition. Anything importing a system framework fails | Any plan needing native macOS APIs (Apple `Speech` ASR, AVFoundation) needs full Xcode. This is why local ASR went the Python/Whisper route |

---

### 7.3 Dead ends, with the measured reason for rejecting them

The I46 ground-truth block centre is `[-6.1, 25.7, 8.3]` mm; all comparisons below are against it or
against `T0 = work/runs/crop_mixed_real/T_oct2mri.npy`, the v0 label-free structural result.

#### 7.3.1 Non-rigid free deformation — rejected: the gain is sub-voxel, the cost is a whole stage

Script `octreg/scripts/nonrigid_stage.py`; log `logs/nonrigid_stage.log`; results
`work/runs/nonrigid/nonrigid_stage.json` (mirrored locally at
`octreg/results/final/summary/nonrigid_stage.json`). Seven label-free variants and two oracle variants on
I46, all starting from `crop_final`'s transform. **The full ablation table is in chapter 6, What we
found, and what it means, §6.10.7**; what belongs in a dead-ends chapter is the reason for rejection.

**Measured reason.** The best label-free variant buys **Dice +0.015 WM / +0.019 GM and f150 +0.018**
(0.440 → 0.458 over the shipped vascular affine), with total displacement ≤ 0.36 mm — smaller than one
MRI voxel (0.15 mm) for the well-regularised settings. It is sub-voxel polishing bought with an extra
stage, two new hyper-parameters (grid, smoothness) and a new failure mode. And the **oracle** non-rigid,
fitted with manual annotations, only reaches f150 0.480 against the oracle affine's 0.466 — so there is
at most ~0.04 f150 of headroom in *any* deformation model on this data. Excluded from v1
(`octreg/README.md` §4.4); the code survives as `octreg/octreg/nonrigid.py` for I46 validation only and
v1 never calls it.

**When to revisit.** When the affine residual stops being the limiting term — i.e. after the MRI-side
foreground/contrast problems in §7.1 are fixed and the pipeline is routinely landing within ~1 mm on
multiple subjects — or on a specimen with genuine physical deformation (a slab that visibly bent or
compressed during sectioning), which I46 is not. Note also that the vessel channel is what carries the
non-rigid stage: removing it costs 176.6 → 191.1 µm and f150 0.450 → 0.413, so a non-rigid revival on
data with no usable vessel channel (Xiangrui's brainstem, §7.1.6) would be optimising on nothing.

#### 7.3.2 Cross-modality self-distillation of an OCT parser — rejected: the metric is distilled along with the model

Script `octreg/scripts/distill_oct_parser.py`; log `logs/distill_v1.log`; results
`work/runs/summary/distill_log.json`; trained model `work/oct_parser_v1`. The idea: take the current
transform, pull the MRI's WM/GM labels through it as pseudo-labels on the OCT, train a 3D parser on the
OCT itself, re-register, iterate. Two rounds of 2 000 iterations. **The full round-by-round table, rotation
column included, is in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.10.8**; what belongs in a dead-ends
chapter is the reason for rejection.

**Measured reason.** The scores look spectacular and are **self-referential**. Search top1 rises
0.708 → 0.874, refined NCC 0.724 → 0.960, and "Dice" against the parser's own class definition reaches
0.961 — because the parser has been trained to reproduce whatever the current transform says, including
its errors. The one metric that is not in the loop does not move: vessel median stays at 258–265 µm and
f150 at 0.27–0.28, against **166.7 µm / f150 0.473** for the plain vascular-affine v1
(`I46_otsu`, `evaluation.final.vessels_vesseg`). The registration itself
barely moves (0.51 mm then 0.68 mm corner mean vs T0), i.e. it never gets past structural-stage accuracy.
Round 0 also records the honest baseline failure: an MRI-trained parser applied directly to OCT lands
**12.23 mm and 124.9°** away. Distillation inherits the initial depth-axis scale error and cannot correct
it — which is exactly the error the vascular channel exists to fix.

**When to revisit.** Only with an evaluation metric that is provably outside the distillation loop
(manual vessels, an independent modality, a physical fiducial), and ideally with a *different* subject's
transform providing the pseudo-labels so the self-reference is broken. As a way to make the search more
decisive on low-contrast subjects it is genuinely attractive — the top1/top2 margin rises from 0.0001 to
0.0053 in round 1 — but a decisive search that is confidently wrong is what §7.1 is already full of.

#### 7.3.3 The trained 3D U-Net structural parser — rejected: flattening + Otsu is better *and* free

Code `octreg/octreg/parser.py`, `octreg/octreg/synth.py`, `octreg/scripts/train_parser.py`; ablation
table `octreg/results/runs_summary.md`. Two generations: synthetic-data training, then real-MRI training
with polarity-inversion augmentation. All against the same I46 crop:

| Run | features | search top1 / top2 | final NCC | centre found (mm) | Dice WM / GM vs manual (otsu maps) | restarts |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| `crop_otsu_v2` | **otsu (v1)** | 0.7271 / 0.6968 | **0.7529** | **[−6.2, 25.9, 8.1]** correct | **0.801 / 0.830** | 7/8 |
| `crop_parser_v2` | parser (real-trained) | 0.6495 / 0.6375 | 0.7101 | [−15.8, 40.3, 19.6] — ~19 mm off | 0.442 / 0.696 | 5/8 |
| `crop_parser_v1` | parser (synthetic) | 0.6208 / 0.6189 | 0.7689 | [−13.8, 34.6, 4.0] wrong | 0.453 / 0.703; scales collapsed to 0.76 / 0.73 / 0.77 | 5/12 |
| `crop_parser_vessel_v1` | parser + vessel | 0.6208 / 0.6189 | 0.4834 | [−13.5, 37.2, 36.0] wrong | 0.453 / 0.674 | 5/12 |

**Measured reason.** The parser's class maps score well against *its own* label space (`dice_*_parser`
0.68–0.91) but land the block in the wrong place — 19 mm off in the best generation, with half the
restarts diverging. The training-free alternative (divide the MRI by its local mean, σ = 10 mm, to kill
the bias field, then plain Otsu) gets the pose right, needs no training data, no labels and no GPU
minutes, and the whole-hemisphere run `I46_parser` reproduces the same pose as `I46_otsu` only because
the *search* is robust, not because the parser helps: its refined NCC is **0.7218 vs otsu's 0.7564**.
There is also an operational cost — `parse_mri.py` on I56 was killed by the host OOM killer
(`run_all.log`: `8720 Killed`) — and a documented failure mode at `parser.py:188`, that whole-volume
normalisation *"mislabels air-dominated windows as tissue because their statistics never occur in
training"*. The parser is kept only as `--features parser` for ablation.

**The headline justification is confirmed — quote it.** `octreg/README.md` claims that local-mean
flattening (divide the MRI by its local mean, σ = 10 mm, before Otsu) raises whole-hemisphere WM/GM Dice
from **0.66/0.62 to 0.90/0.93**. An earlier pass of this handoff could not locate the artefact behind
those numbers and told readers not to quote them. **That doubt is withdrawn.** The improvement has since
been re-derived, and this is the one place the precise pair is worth writing down: **0.6502 / 0.5987
before flattening, 0.9069 / 0.9343 after**, which is exactly what the project's prose rounds to
0.66/0.62 → 0.90/0.93. Use the rounded pair in prose. Do not confuse it with the other whole-hemisphere
Dice values you will meet in the logs, which belong to different maps and are not a before/after of
anything: the trained parser's (`logs/parse_I46.log`: WM 0.485, GM 0.586) and the polarity probes'
(0.181–0.227 WM). The *head-to-head* otsu-versus-parser comparison in the table above is verified
independently and does not rest on these numbers at all.

**When to revisit.** When there is real cross-subject training data with labels — the current parser was
trained on I46's own labels, so it was never going to generalise — or if a foundation-style segmentation
model can produce WM/GM maps on ex-vivo VFA without per-dataset training. Note the failure being fixed
would have to be an MRI-side one (§7.1.7), which is precisely where a *good* parser could help: a
segmentation robust to bath fluid would solve I61 and I58 at the same time as it solves the contrast
problem. That is the strongest argument for a future revisit, and it is an argument about the tissue
mask, not about the WM/GM split.

#### 7.3.4 Raw intensity NCC across modalities — rejected: it only works where you already know the answer

| Setting | Result |
|---|---|
| I46, **40 mm crop** around the true location (`crop_intensity_v2`) | search 0.5940 / 0.5919 (**margin 0.0021**), final NCC 0.6931, centre `[−6.2, 25.8, 8.1]` — correct, but only **4/8** restarts converge (vs 7/8 for otsu) |
| Xiangrui I58 brainstem, intensity polish started from the **correct** structural pose (`octreg/scripts/test_polish.py`, `logs/test_polish.log`) | `level 0.32mm: NCC 0.033` → `level 0.16mm: NCC 0.030`; it moved the block centre **9.37 mm**, rotation **15.79°**, corner mean **9.55 mm**, corner max 12.3 mm |

**Measured reason.** OCT scattering intensity and ex-vivo FLASH signal are not a monotone function of each
other, so their correlation carries almost no cross-modality information — NCC ≈ 0.03 on real data. On a
tight crop the tissue *outline* alone is enough to fake success, with a 0.002 search margin and half the
restarts diverging; on real data, started from a pose that was correct, it dragged the block ~10 mm off.
This is the reason the pipeline reduces **both** sides to the same two-class structure map before
correlating anything.

**When to revisit.** Not as a similarity metric on raw intensity. The live successor idea is an
**artifact-robust fine channel built on the fibre texture both modalities share** — the v1.1 plan in
`octreg/README.md` §3 and the "Next" section of the 2026-08-23 meeting notes under `meeting_recordings/`.
It is a shared *derived* representation, which is the same lesson stated positively. Chapter 11, What to
do next, carries it as a work item.

#### 7.3.5 MIND-SSC modality-independent descriptors — rejected: the worst variant ever measured

`crop_mind_v2`, `logs/run_crop_mind_v2.log`: search top1 **0.2185** / top2 0.2160, final NCC **0.1846**
(the refinement *decreased* the score), centre `[−17.5, 10.6, 31.6]` — **17.9 mm** off (corner max
33.0 mm), **3/8** restarts, **0** manual vessels inside the block, Dice 0.323 / 0.672. The 12-channel
descriptors also make the FFT search ~3× slower (31 s vs 11 s on the same crop). Code retained at
`octreg/octreg/features.py:26 mind_ssc()`.

**Measured reason.** MIND's rotational invariance appears to destroy exactly the signal this problem
needs: the whole task is finding an orientation, and a descriptor built to be insensitive to local
orientation removes the discriminative content. **Do not revisit without a fundamentally different
descriptor.**

#### 7.3.6 Automatic MRI vessel detection — rejected: ~8 % precision

`work/vesselness_check/vesselness_check.json` (`octreg/scripts/check_vesselness.py`), Frangi
dark-vesselness thresholded at several quantiles and scored against dilated manual labels:

| map | threshold | precision vs dilated labels | recall | n predicted |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MRI q99.0 | 0.0219 | **0.079** | 0.396 | 139 647 |
| MRI q99.5 | 0.0460 | 0.078 | 0.253 | 69 824 |
| MRI q99.8 | 0.0893 | 0.075 | 0.119 | 27 930 |
| OCT q95.0 | 0.0092 | 0.285 | 0.130 | 9 991 (vs 14 303 in `ves_seg`) |
| OCT q98.0 | 0.0277 | 0.261 | 0.053 | 3 997 |
| OCT q99.0 | 0.0467 | 0.265 | 0.028 | 1 999 |

Consistent with `logs/refine_validate_real.log`: of 64 192 automatic MRI vessel candidates (8 784
components, size ≥ 4), only **3 %** fall within 0.3 mm of a manual vessel, and only 10 % of manual
vessels are within 0.3 mm of a candidate. Driving the refinement with them alone (row A2 of
`work/runs/validate_real/refine_validate.json`) destroys the result: vessel median **457.7 µm**, f150
0.153, Dice **0.462 / 0.563**, anchor NCC **0.172**, 2.77 mm off T0.

**This is why the shipped design uses a soft local-darkness map on the MRI side rather than a binary
vessel segmentation.** The measured design sweep confirms the choice: MRI-dark or MRI-Frangi with an
OCT *density* reaches 165–167 µm / f150 0.476–0.479, while OCT-Frangi-as-a-map only reaches
188–241 µm. Do not replace the soft map with a detector until a detector exists whose precision is
better than 0.08.

#### 7.3.7 Pure texture-based specimen mask — not a dead end, open work for v1.1

`octreg/scripts/test_texture_mask.py` (server-only; figure at `work/texture_mask_test.png` and
`octreg/results/final/v1/texture_mask_test.png`): local standard deviation in a 7-voxel window,
Gaussian-smoothed, Otsu, closing + fill + largest component. Tried on both `work/xiangrui_I58bs` and
`work/I46`. The recorded conclusion (`EXPLAINER_zh.md` §4) is that **pure texture thresholding fails on
both datasets and texture must be fused with intensity**.
`[UNVERIFIED — the script prints its mask fractions to stdout and no log file was kept; only the PNG
survives.]` Listed here so nobody re-runs it expecting it to work as-is; the fusion version is the actual
v1.1 item and it is the fix for I61, I58 and the agarose problem simultaneously.

#### 7.3.8 Two negative results that are not dead ends but change what you should build

| Result | Measurement | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **The 30 mm crop prior buys nothing** | `crop_mixed_v2` vs `whole_mixed_v2`, `crop_final` vs `whole_final`, `crop_final2` vs `whole_final2` all give identical poses to within noise (e.g. `crop_final2` stretch `[1.184, 0.973, 1.034]` vs `whole_final2` `[1.195, 0.975, 1.035]`; vessels 166.8 µm / 0.469 vs 166.6 / 0.474) | v1 runs whole-hemisphere by default. Do not add a position prior for accuracy — only for cost. The PI has stated a position prior exists; using it is legitimate and makes the search-memory problem disappear, but it will not fix any of §7.1 |
| **The manual GM/WM labels cannot see the depth scale** | Along the OCT depth axis the label-free NCC varies by only **0.0212** over a scale sweep `s ∈ [0.85, 1.30]` (0.7062 at s = 1.300 to 0.7274 at s = 1.075), against **0.1686** along the in-plane k axis — 8× less sensitive. The labels-only oracle in `oracle_cv.json` moves 0.19 mm and gains nothing (269.3 µm vs T0's 273.3 µm) | This is why the vascular channel exists. Beware the span "0.713–0.727" quoted in some of the prose docs: 0.713 is the value at s = 0.85, i.e. only the ascending half of the curve was read. The corrected full-range numbers make the negative result **stronger**, not weaker. The full three-axis scale-probe table is in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.10.3 |

**[UNVERIFIED] tension to be aware of before you re-tell the depth-scale story.** In
`work/runs/validate_real/scale_profiles.json` the *vessel* metric responds strongly on the **k** axis
(f150 0.254 → 0.317 at s = 1.10) and not on the **i/depth** axis (f150 stays 0.23–0.26), while the
pipeline's vascular stage stretches the **i** axis (1.026 → 1.219) and that is what moves the vessel
score (265 → 167 µm). Single-axis probes about the block centre and a full 12-DOF affine are not the
same experiment, so this may be axis coupling — but the raw single-axis numbers do not, on their own,
show the vessel metric preferring a depth stretch. To settle it, re-run `scale_probe.py` from the
*final* transform and report the i-axis profile of the **vessel-channel NCC**, not the mixed NCC. The
same tension is set out beside the full table in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.10.3.
Related [UNVERIFIED] item: the "true depth scale ≈ 1.18" quoted in some sections has no artefact behind
it; the two defensible anchors are the pipeline's own **1.219** and the sidecar-vs-siblings ratio
14/12 = **1.167**. A third anchor — the 33-slice serial-section period — was once offered alongside
these and has been **withdrawn**; see §7.2.9 for why it does not survive I56. **That "two" is the
narrowest of three counts this document keeps, and it contradicts neither of the others.** Two
*annotation-free anchors*: the two numbers above, the only ones that do not rest on the authors'
hand-drawn vessels or labels. **Three** independent routes to the value ≈1.17, none of them ours — the
sibling sidecars 1.1667, the authors' published affine 1.17419, and an oracle affine fitted to their
manual annotations 1.177 (chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.11.2). **Four** lines that
I46's declared 12 µm is wrong — chapter 4, The data, §4.5.1 (a)–(d), which adds the absence of any
in-file spacing record for I46 and our own recovered 1.219. The withdrawn section period is in none of
the three; if a source counts it, recount without it and fix the ordinal.

#### 7.3.9 Vessel-channel variants that were measured and discarded

Kept here so nobody re-derives them. All on I46, from `work/runs/vessel_channel/`. **The full 22-variant
design sweep and the scrambling controls are in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.10.4 and
§6.10.5**; this section keeps only the discards and the conclusion that generalises.

Four things were tried and dropped. Frangi run on the **raw 12 µm OCT** as a map is useless — vessel
median 227.5 µm, f150 0.349, vessel-channel NCC **0.007**; at native resolution the filter locks onto
speckle rather than vessels. Frangi at 24 µm is better but still weak (206.7 µm, channel NCC 0.092).
Using a Frangi *map* on the OCT side instead of a *density* is the worst of the four map/density
combinations (240.6 µm, f150 0.345). And the DANDI `ves_seg` manual annotation at 12 µm → density is the
ceiling (166.8 µm, f150 0.469, channel NCC 0.159) but it is an annotation, so it is evaluation-only. What
shipped is own-Frangi at 48 µm → density: 179.0 µm, f150 0.440, channel NCC 0.142. The controls that
turn this into a finding rather than a coincidence — WM/GM only on an identical schedule, and `ves_seg`
density scrambled two different ways, all collapsing back to roughly T0's 276 µm — are tabulated in
chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.10.5.

The takeaway that generalises: **what works is a *density* pooled to a scale comparable to the MRI's
(48 µm / 0.15 mm), not a raw high-resolution vesselness map**, and the vessel-channel weight `w` is
insensitive between 1 and 4 (shipped at 2.0).

---

### 7.4 Troubleshooting decision trees

#### 7.4.1 "The registration produced a wrong pose" — check in this order

Everything you need is in `work/runs/<RUN>/result.json` and `logs/reg_<SUB>_otsu.log`.

**Step 1 — is there any search margin?** Read `search.top1` and `search.top2`.

```bash
python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('work/runs/I48_otsu/result.json'));print(d['search']['top1'],d['search']['top2'])"
```

A margin below ~0.01 means the search cannot distinguish its answer from the runner-up; do not believe
any number downstream, open the QC figure. Reference values: I46 0.7259/0.7039 (0.0220), I38 (0.0512),
I62 (0.0106), I56 (0.0082), I61 (0.0060), I57 (0.0057), I55 (0.0023), I48 (0.0013), I58 (0.0001).
**Do not use a low absolute score as the failure criterion** — large slabs legitimately score 0.29–0.34
(I38 0.3145, I56 0.3397, I62 0.2872) and are visually correct; the achievable NCC falls as the block
grows. **And do not use a high one as a success criterion either.** There is no numeric acceptance
threshold on `refine.final_ncc` that works on this corpus: **I61 refines to 0.5020 and I57 to 0.5121 and
both are wrong, while I62 refines to 0.2842 and is right.** Any cut that passes I62 passes both wrong
runs; any cut that fails them fails I62 and I56 as well. Absolute NCC does not separate right from wrong
across subjects — if you find a "good result means NCC above X" rule anywhere in this project's prose,
it is wrong. Note also that I55 sits at a 0.0023 margin and is one of the two best-validated subjects, so
margin alone is not sufficient either. Judge on **margin + restart convergence + the picture**, never on
the raw score.

**Step 2 — did the restarts converge?** `evaluation.restarts.n_converged` of `n = 12`, or the log line
`structural restarts converged to the solution: N/12`. 9–12 of 12 is healthy (I46 9/12, I38 12/12,
I57 10/12). Below ~8/12 the basin is not well defined. **Remember this cuts both ways:** tight
convergence is not correctness — I58 and I61 are 12/12 and both wrong.

**Step 3 — is the MRI tissue mask sane?** `logs/prep_<SUB>.log`, field `tissue frac`. Above ~0.45 on a
whole hemisphere means bath fluid or embedding medium is inside the mask (I61 0.742 → wrong; I56 0.989 →
survived by luck). Cross-check the absolute volume against the **386–806 cm³** that the six sane masks in
this corpus actually measure (§7.1.1); I61's 1 838.8 cm³ and I58's 1 453.4 cm³ are immediately
disqualifying, and anything above ~1 210 cm³ should be. A sane volume does **not** clear the run — I57's
is 518.0 cm³, its valley ratio is the cleanest in the corpus, and it is still wrong for reasons nobody
has established (§7.1.3). Fix with
`prep_subject.py --mri-tissue-thresh <value>` after looking at the histogram, then re-run `register.py`.

**Step 4 — does the MRI have any GM/WM contrast at all?** Check which flip angle you actually fed it, by
reading the **sidecar JSON**, not the filename. `flip-N` is a file index, not an angle: for I58,
`flip-1` is 30° and `flip-3` is 10°, while I62's `flip-3` and I57/I61's `flip-4` are all 20°. The correct
per-subject file, from `run_all.sh` line 5:

| Subject | file | Subject | file |
|---|---|---|---|
| I46, I38, I55, I56, I48 | `flip-2` | I62, I58 | `flip-3` |
| I57, I61 | `flip-4` | | |

If `prep.json` shows `n_peaks: 1` or an intensity p99 under ~50, the two-class split is noise and the run
is meaningless regardless of what it scored.

**Step 5 — polarity and handedness.** Both vary *within the same dataset*. Check `oct_wm_bright` and
`mirror` in `result.json`. Six of nine DANDI subjects are mirrored — **I38, I46, I48, I56, I58, I62**;
not mirrored: I55, I57, I61 and both brainstem runs — the widely-copied five-name list that circulates in
the prose docs dropped I48, so read `mirror` out of `result.json` rather than trusting any list. I46 is
GM-bright + mirrored, I55 is WM-bright + not mirrored. If either came out wrong, pin it:
`--oct-wm-bright yes|no` and/or `--no-mirror`.

The thing to internalise: **neither the 0.6 mm coarse search nor the manual GM/WM Dice can separate the
two polarities.** On `I46_otsu` the *wrong* polarity wins the coarse search (0.7411 against 0.7259) and
only the refined NCC separates them; and the fully-run wrong-polarity control lands ~70 mm away while
scoring *higher* WM Dice than the correct run. The only independent verifier is the vessel channel. That
counterexample is laid out in full, with its table and the vessel-channel numbers, in chapter 5, The
method, as a chain of reasoning, §5.2.5 — read it once before you trust any Dice value in this project.
If `--oct-wm-bright auto`
picked the wrong branch, look at `polarity_trials` in `result.json`. And remember `auto` is **not** the
default (`register.py:32` defaults to `"no"`); only `run_subject.sh` passes it.

**Step 6 — the overlap gate.** Log line
`overlap gate: MRI tissue X cm3, OCT mask Y cm3 -> effective min_overlap Z (requested 0.85)`. The
effective value is derived from the ratio of those two volumes and is bounded below by a floor; the
formula is stated once, in full, in chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning, §5.2. What you need
at the troubleshooting bench is when it bites: it **never binds on DANDI** (effective 0.850 in all eight
runs that record it; `I46_otsu` has `overlap_gate: null` because it predates the feature). It matters
when the OCT mask is
over-inclusive (agarose) or the MRI is a crop: the brainstem pair auto-relaxed to **0.369** and only then
found the correct pose.

**Step 7 — the depth-axis scale.** `stretch_ijk` before → after the vascular stage
(`stretch_ijk[0]` is the OCT depth / serial-sectioning axis; `final_transform.column_scales` is a
*different* ordering — `column_scales[2]` holds the same number). A large jump (I46 1.026 → **1.219**)
means the OCT sidecar's depth spacing is wrong or missing; a tiny one (I55 0.920 → **0.913**, only
0.334 mm of block motion) means the sidecar was right. Read I55's numbers straight from
`work/runs/I55_otsu/result.json`: **0.913** is the depth (i) axis and **1.097** is the in-plane j axis,
and several of the project's prose docs quote the latter as if it were the former — chapter 12, Open
questions and unverified claims, records that correction. The sidecar values are in `prep.json`
`oct.spacing_um_zyx`: I46 `[12,12,12]` (the anomaly), I55 `[14,12,12]`, everything else `[35,30,30]` —
depth/in-plane = 1.167 for all the healthy ones. Tissue geometry is blind to this axis, so with
`--vascular off` you will never recover it.

**One thing to say out loud every time I55 is used as the reverse control.** I55 is the subject normally
cited as the null result: its sidecar depth spacing is right, so there is no large depth correction to
recover, and the pipeline duly recovers none. But its *recovered* depth/in-plane anisotropy is
**0.8570**, which is 6/7 to four decimal places — **exactly the inverse of the 7/6 = 1.167 factor that
I46 is supposed to be missing**. That may well be a coincidence, and no artefact resolves it either way,
but it has to be stated wherever I55 is presented as a clean null, because the one number the control
exists to show as "nothing here" is numerically the I46 factor turned upside down. Until someone explains
it, call I55 a *qualified* reverse control, not a clean one.

**Step 8 — is the vascular channel helping or hurting?** `vascular.ncc_channels` `[wm, gm, vessel]`. A
vessel channel near zero means the OCT "vessels" are artefacts, not vessels: Xiangrui's brainstem gives
`[0.0013, 0.1844, 0.0055]` with **0/8** vascular restarts, and the stage dragged the block 2.652 mm the
wrong way at a cost of 4 778 s. **Turn it off for such data:** `register.py --vascular off`. On DANDI,
`I56 0/8`, `I62 1/8`, `I57 1/8` and `I58 1/8` vascular restarts are all warning signs on runs that are
either wrong or unverified.

**Step 9 — look at the picture.** Every failure so far is obvious in the QC figure; nothing has ever
failed quietly.

```bash
python octreg/scripts/viz_result.py --work work/<SUB> --run work/runs/<SUB>_otsu
# then open work/runs/<SUB>_otsu/qc_vessels.png and qc_oct_space.png
# or load the pair in Freeview / ITK-SNAP:
#   work/runs/<SUB>_otsu/mri_region.nii.gz  +  oct_in_mri_region.nii.gz   (same grid)
```

Recorded human verdicts for every run: `~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration/results_inspection/INDEX.md`.

**Step 10 — do not read Dice unless the labels cover the block.** Dice 0.000 is usually a label-coverage
artefact, not a registration error: I62 has effectively no whole-hemisphere labels (`labels4 counts
{0: 1430249220, 1: 1403085, ...}`, ~0.2 % labelled) and is visually correct. Read
`gmwm.frac_on_mri_labels` first (Dice is computed with the full OCT class count in the denominator, so it
collapses toward 0 when coverage is low). The *informative* label statistic is the confusion matrix: if
on-label OCT-WM lands on MRI WM only 35–37 % of the time (I38 35.0 %, I56 36.8 %, I48 36.5 %), that is
below chance and is evidence against the pose, not a coverage artefact.

**The coverage explanation belongs to I62 and the other large slabs only — do not extend it to I48.**
I48's labels do cover its block (`frac_on_mri_labels = 0.575`), so nothing is suppressing its Dice; what
is wrong with I48's Dice is that it is untrustworthy in *both* directions, because on that subject no
pose is distinguishable from any other. **I48's "uncertain" verdict rests on its 0.0013 search-score
margin (§7.1.2), not on any label artefact**, and it would still be uncertain with perfect labels.

**Step 11 — the independent checks, when annotations exist.** Distance from the block centre to the
manual MRI vessel centroid and to the BA label centroid, and the fraction of each inside the block
(§7.1.1). Correct subjects: 4.6–9.6 mm with 12.8–59.0 % inside. Everything else in the corpus is
50–96 mm away with 0.0 % inside. If `vessels_own`/`vessels_vesseg` report `n_inside = 0`, that is not a
zero score — `vessel_distance_stats` in `octreg/octreg/evaluate.py` returns only `{"n_inside": n}` when
fewer than 20 points survive, and every downstream metric is `null` (printed as `nan` in logs, `—` in
`summary.md`). Dashes in the summary tables are missing data.

#### 7.4.2 "Prep failed" — check in this order

1. **Read the tail of the log first.** `run_subject.sh` prints only 5 lines on failure:
   `tail -40 logs/prep_<SUB>.log`.
2. **`ValueError: autodetected range of [..., inf] is not finite`** → non-finite MRI voxels; you are
   running a **stale `prep_subject.py`**. The current one prints
   `sanitized N non-finite MRI voxels -> 0`. Sync the code from the authoritative tree.
3. **`gzip.BadGzipFile: CRC check failed`** → corrupted download, *even if the file size matches the
   manifest exactly*. Re-verify against DANDI's `dandi:sha2-256` (§7.2.8) and re-fetch that one asset.
4. **`FileNotFoundError: .../mri_prob_wm.npy`** → you passed `--features parser` without running
   `parse_mri.py` first (this is `logs/reg_I56_parser.log`). Use the default `--features otsu`.
5. **`Killed` with no traceback** → the **host** OOM killer, not CUDA. Seen on `parse_mri.py`
   (`run_all.log`: `8720 Killed`). Almost always a second heavy job running concurrently.
6. **Missing sidecar or wrong spacing** → `prep_subject.py` reads `PixelSize` from the OME-TIFF's `.json`
   sidecar and `header.get_zooms()` for NIfTI. Override explicitly with `--oct-spacing-um z,y,x`
   (e.g. `--oct-spacing-um 35,30,30`). **Always sanity-check the logged line**
   `OCT (D,H,W) dtype spacing um (z,y,x) [...]` — a wrong depth spacing is the single most consequential
   silent error in the pipeline (it is the whole I46 story).
7. **Re-running prep is idempotent per stage.** `run_subject.sh` skips prep when both
   `work/<SUB>/octv_vessels.npy` and `work/<SUB>/mri_tissue.npy` exist. To force a re-prep of one side:
   `rm -f work/<SUB>/octv_vessels.npy` (OCT), or use `--skip-mri` / `--skip-oct`.
8. **Know when it is merely slow.** Prep runs 190 s (I46, 12 µm block) to 1 460 s (I57,
   768×1251×2021 at 30 µm); the Frangi vessel step is the long pole (I57: 766 s → 1 324 s into the log).

#### 7.4.3 "Out of memory" — what to change, in order

First decide **which** memory ran out:

| Signal | Which memory |
|---|---|
| `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError` / `CUDA error: out of memory` | 24 GB VRAM (RTX 4090) |
| bare `Killed` in the log, no traceback | 503 GB host RAM (OOM killer) — note there is **no swap** |
| `[Errno 28] No space left on device` | check `df -h /` — the container overlay is only 30 G. Everything must be written under `~/autodl-tmp` (1.5 T) |

**If VRAM, in this order:**

1. **Confirm you are the only job.** `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv`. A
   leftover process from a previous run holding 20 GB is the most common cause.
2. **Frangi slab budget** — `octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py:152`, lower the constant:
   `zc = int(np.clip(30e6 // (H*W) - 2*ov, 8, 64))` → try `15e6`. Also `nsl` on line 154 (`20e6`).
3. **Hessian eigen chunk** — `octreg/octreg/features.py:169,189`, `chunk = 4_000_000` → `1_000_000`.
   This is `N×3×3` float32 plus intermediates and is the peak allocation inside Frangi.
4. **Resampling chunk** — `octreg/octreg/common.py:140`, `resample_to_grid(..., chunk=8_000_000)`.
5. **Output stage** — `octreg/scripts/register.py:259`, `for z0 in range(0, mri_out.shape[0], 64)` → 32
   or 16. This is the stage that OOM'd on I57.
6. **The FFT search itself** — `octreg/octreg/search.py` holds `FI`, `FI2` (per channel) and `Ftis` as
   complex `rfftn` transforms of the *padded* MRI grid; padding is half a template on every side
   (`self.pad = n//2 + 1`), so a 50 mm block against a 0.12 mm hemisphere is the worst case. Reduce by
   registering against a crop: `--crop-centre x,y,z --crop-half-mm 30`. The PI has stated a position
   prior exists, so using one is legitimate — and §7.3.8 shows the crop costs nothing in accuracy.
7. **Last resort:** lower `--n-rot` (default 8 000, doubled to 16 000 by the mirror branch). This trades
   the accuracy of the initial pose for memory and time; prefer 1–6 first.

**If host RAM / `Killed`:** it is almost always two heavy jobs at once, or `parse_mri.py` on a 0.12 mm
hemisphere. Serialise the jobs and avoid `--features parser`.

**If it is slow rather than out of memory**, check the expectation before you change anything. The
per-branch wall-clock reference for every run — seconds per 4 000 orientations, the full search per
polarity, each polarity trial, the vascular stage and the total — is tabulated in chapter 6, What we
found, and what it means, §6.3.1 and §6.3.2. What you need at the bench is the shape of it: over the nine
DANDI otsu runs the total ranges from **1 124.7 s (18.7 min, I46) to 7 864.1 s (2 h 11 min, I38)**, so
**budget 2.5 h per subject** for large 30 µm slabs; only four of the nine fall inside the "15–40 min"
quoted in the 2026-08-23 meeting notes under `meeting_recordings/`. And the time is not where the prose
says it is: on the worst runs the **vascular stage is 72–91 % of wall clock**, not the search.

One number to distrust on sight. The 153–154 s "whole hemisphere" figure in `octreg/README.md` and
`octreg/EXPLAINER_zh.md` is a real measurement of a *different* entry point —
`run_demo_i46.py --features mixed`, a parser-probability configuration `register.py` cannot even run.
The label-free shipped search is **298.9 s per polarity** on the identical subject and grid, 597.8 s with
the `--oct-wm-bright auto` that every DANDI run used.

Two levers: pin `--oct-wm-bright yes|no` once you know the protocol polarity, which halves the time by
removing the second polarity branch; and turn the vascular stage off when its channel NCC is near zero,
which on the brainstem pair took 5 244 s down to 362 s.

## 8. How this compares to the published method

Everything this project calls "the baseline", "the authors", or "the reference method" is one paper and one code repository:

> Costantini et al. 2023, *A cellular resolution atlas of Broca's area*, **Science Advances 9, eadg3844**, published 12 October 2023.
> Data: **DANDI:000026**. Code: `github.com/neuroscales/biccn-broca-I46`.

That paper is simultaneously (a) the source of the only public dataset on which `octreg v1` can be validated, (b) the method `octreg` is trying to beat on human input, and (c) the source of the one external number our results can be checked against. A successor who does not understand the Costantini pipeline cannot defend a single design decision in `octreg`, because almost every one of them is either an inheritance from it or a deliberate removal of something it requires.

**Where the evidence in this chapter comes from.** The acquisition facts were read off page renders of the paper at `/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/tmp/pdfs/costantini/full_render/page-09.jpg` (p.9), `page-10.jpg` (p.10), and `/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/tmp/pdfs/costantini-method-11.png` / `costantini-method-12.png` (pp.11–12). The registration recipe was fetched live from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neuroscales/biccn-broca-I46/main/scripts/registration/*` on 2026-08-23. The `nitorch register2` flag semantics come from `nitorch/cli/registration/register/parser.py` at submodule commit `785093620b1475b66e26346af9471560c56611aa` of `balbasty/nitorch` — the branch named in `.gitmodules`, `refactor-registration-preproc`, **no longer exists**, but the commit is still reachable. The published affine is `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neuroscales/biccn-broca-I46/main/results/mri2oct/affine.lta`, decomposed locally with numpy. Our own numbers come from `/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/octreg/results/final/summary/*.json` and, where a figure was re-derived, from `work/runs/*/result.json` and `work/runs/summary_all/summary.md` on the AutoDL compute server (see chapter 10, State of play: where everything is, for how to reach it).

**Corrections applied in this chapter.** Several figures that circulate in the project's own prose are wrong, and this chapter uses the corrected values throughout. The headline ones: the whole-hemisphere search is **299 s label-free**, not 154 s; end-to-end per-subject runtime is **18.7–131.1 min**, not 15–40 min; **3 of 9** DANDI subjects fail, not 3 of 8; the serial-section period is **33 slices**, not ≈100 (and the inference once drawn from it is withdrawn — §8.1.1); the depth-scale NCC plateau spans **0.706–0.727**, not 0.713–0.727; I55's depth stretch is **0.913**, not 1.10. Each is flagged at the point of use so that a reader holding an older copy of the prose can see exactly what changed and why.

---

### 8.1 What the authors actually did

#### 8.1.1 Three modalities, three scales, one hemisphere

One human hemisphere is imaged three times, at three scales, and **each imaging step destroys some of the geometry the previous one had**. That sentence is the whole reason the modality chain has the shape it does.

The full acquisition parameters for all three modalities — scanner, sequence, echo and flip-angle lists, the OCT optics, stages and vibratome, the light-sheet optics, and the clearing and staining protocols — are tabulated once in **chapter 4, The data** (§4.8.1 for the OCT rig) and compared modality-against-modality in **chapter 3, The scientific problem and why it matters** (§3.3.1). They are not repeated here. What follows is only the handful of acquisition facts that a design decision in `octreg` or in the baseline actually rests on.

**Ex-vivo MRI — the global reference frame** (p.9, left column, "Magnetic resonance imaging"). Three facts carry weight downstream:

- **The readout gradients are bipolar**, so odd and even echoes are distorted in opposite directions under B0 inhomogeneity and the echoes misalign. The authors correct this with a group-sparsity edge-preserving intensity-correction algorithm that uses the B0 field map together with all the FLASH images. The DANDI derivatives folder is literally named `EPIC` (`derivatives/EPIC/sub-I46/ses-MRI/anat/sub-I46_ses-MRI_flip-2_VFA.nii.gz`), matching reference 16 of the paper, Varadarajan et al., "Edge-preserving B0 inhomogeneity distortion correction for high-resolution multi-echo ex vivo MRI at 7T". **The MRI we register against is therefore already a derived, corrected, synthesized FLASH contrast, not raw scanner output.**
- **There is no body coil on that 7 T scanner** — reception is a custom-built 31-channel phased array — so the receive bias field was never removed at acquisition, only modelled, by a likelihood-based cost that jointly segments tissue type and estimates the intensity bias. That residual is precisely what `octreg` has to flatten before Otsu can work (§8.4, contribution 2). It is the single acquisition fact that the whole label-free branch depends on.
- The corrected whole-hemisphere structural image is what the authors use "to generate a brain surface and provide a reference coordinate system for registration purposes" (p.9). **The MRI is the reference frame by construction**, not by choice of our project.

**Serial-sectioning block-face OCT — the geometric bridge** (p.9, right column, and p.10, left column). Two facts, both load-bearing:

- **The stitching / stacking convention is the single most important fact about this dataset:** tiles are stitched in 2D using the average intensity projection; once each tile's coordinate is known they are linearly blended in x and y; **and then stacked in z**. There is **no z-direction image-based registration between slabs** — the z stacking is done from the motorized stage coordinates, accurate to 10 µm along z. This is what makes the OCT block one rigid, undistorted 3D object (chapter 4, The data, §4.8.2) and therefore something that can be affinely related to the MRI at all.
- **The vibratome cuts a nominally 500 µm superficial slice** after each surface is fully scanned, so the reconstructed volume carries a periodic intensity modulation along z — each slab's own within-slab depth attenuation. **This is the direct justification for `octreg`'s per-z-slice depth normalization**; any raw-intensity similarity, LCC included, is corrupted by it. Our own audit found the modulation independently (`/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/costantini_b0/reports/costantini_i46_data_audit.md` §3).

> **The section period: measured, and one inference withdrawn.** The audit reported the period as **≈100 slices** (peaks at 0/100/200…, troughs at 25/125/225…), and that figure propagated into `octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py:125` as the comment `# ~1.2 mm of depth = one section period at 12 um`, and from there into several prose sections. **The measured period is 33 slices for I46 (0.396 mm) and 12 slices for I56 (0.420 mm)** — about 3× smaller. The ≈1200 µm figure came from inspecting the mean-intensity profile at 25-slice granularity, which aliases a true 33-slice period to ≈100; its origin is `costantini_b0/reports/costantini_i46_data_audit.md:43`. The period itself was obtained by FFT plus autocorrelation on the raw OME-TIFFs and is `[NOT RE-MEASURED]` for this document (it requires decoding a 987 MB OME-TIFF). The full measurement, with harmonics and the per-subject window arithmetic, is in **chapter 4, The data** (§4.8.3).
>
> One arithmetic observation survives, and it bears on §8.6.4: 33 slices × the sidecar's declared 12 µm = **0.396 mm**, which is exactly the slab z extent the authors themselves hard-code in `lsfm_slide_center_and_scale.py` (z voxel size `0.396 / 50` mm). That the authors' LSFM z-scale therefore inherits the same 12 µm assumption is an inference, not a finding — the arithmetic coincidence is exact, the causal claim is `[UNVERIFIED]`.
>
> **What does not survive is the 500 µm cut as a line of evidence for the I46 depth-spacing bug.** 500 µm / 33 slices = 15.15 µm per slice against a declared 12, and that was once counted as an independent confirmation that I46's sidecar is wrong. **It is withdrawn, and must not be presented as confirming evidence anywhere.** The identical computation on I56 gives 500 µm ÷ its ≈12-slice period = **41.7 µm** per slice against a 35 µm sidecar that is corroborated twice inside the file (ImageJ `spacing=0.035`, `XResolution 33.3333`) and by a recovered depth stretch of 0.998. Both cannot hold. Read consistently — I46's 0.396 mm period against I56's 0.420 mm, whose spacing is the corroborated one — the actual cut is ≈0.40–0.42 mm rather than the nominal 500 µm, in which case the period implies a **1.06** correction for I46, not 1.167, and the argument runs *against* a large correction rather than for it. The depth-spacing bug's other lines of evidence are untouched by this; see §8.6.4 and chapter 4, The data (§4.5).

**LSFM — the cellular layer** (p.10, right column, and p.11). One fact matters for this chapter: the input is **the 500 µm slices the vibratome removed** — cleared with SHORT, immunostained (NeuN, CR, Calb2, SST), mounted between a quartz coverslip and a glass holder, imaged on a custom inverted dual-objective light sheet whose objectives sit at **45°** to the sample-holder plane, deskewed and downsampled to 3.3 µm isotropic, and stitched with **ZetaStitcher**. Vessels are segmented from the 561 nm channel, and the paper says those reconstructions "were used to visualize and segment the blood vessels to perform the alignment of the three modalities" — i.e. **vessels are the authors' own cross-modal landmark**, which is the point §8.5 concedes. The stereology that the whole atlas rests on (Optical Fractionator, 150 × 150 µm counting frame, 800 × 800 µm grid, 15 usable slices of 16) is described in chapter 3, §3.3.1 and chapter 4.

#### 8.1.2 Why the chain is LSFM → OCT → MRI and not LSFM → MRI

This is the structural fact a newcomer must internalize before reading either codebase.

**OCT is self-consistent because the block never leaves the stage.** The block is fixed on the motorized xyz stages, the top surface is imaged, the vibratome shaves off a slice *in place*, and the next surface is imaged with the stage coordinates still valid. Stacking in z is a bookkeeping operation at 10 µm stage accuracy, not a registration problem. The reconstructed OCT volume is one rigid, undistorted 3D object that can be affinely related to the MRI.

**LSFM slices are physically removed, so they lose their geometry.** Each 500 µm slice is picked up by hand ("the 500-µm slices were manually captured to reserve the sequence"), stored between two TDE-rinsed gauze pads in a plastic shell, labelled, stacked, sealed in a bag and shipped to another site (p.10). It is then cleared (SDS, 55 °C, 4 days), antigen-retrieved at 95 °C, stained for 7 days, TDE-graded, and sandwiched between a coverslip and a spacer. Between the block face and the light sheet the slice has been detached, transported, swollen, shrunk, folded and squashed. Whatever coordinate system it had is gone.

**Therefore OCT is the geometric reference for LSFM.** For every slice `i`, the OCT block still contains the exact slab that slice came from, in its correct place. The authors exploit this literally: `scripts/registration/oct2lsfm_affine.sh` loops `for i in {08..23}` and registers each LSFM slice to `oct/slices/unstack/oct.${i}.masked.nii.gz` — the *unstacked* corresponding OCT slab.

**The authors did NOT reconstruct LSFM across slices.** Verified from their scripts:

- `oct2lsfm_affine.sh` uses `@affine affine -2d` — the affine is forced 2D about the default axis. There is no inter-slice 3D pose estimation.
- `oct2lsfm_nonlin.sh` uses `@nonlin svf 1 -2d …` — the deformation is also 2D per slice.
- `lsfm_slide_center_and_scale.py` *assigns* each LSFM slice a z position by copying the corresponding OCT slab's centre: it resizes the slide crop to exactly 50 z-samples, sets the z voxel size to `0.396 / 50` mm (= 7.92 µm) and re-centres the affine on `centeroct`, the centre of `oct/slices/unstack/oct.{i}.nii.gz`. **The LSFM slice's z geometry is imported from OCT, not measured.**
- `lsfm2oct_make_lsfm_volume.py` builds a 3D LSFM-like volume only by pulling every slice through its own `oct2lsfm` transform into a common OCT-derived grid at `[0.0099, 0.0099, 0.00792]` mm. It is a warp-and-accumulate into OCT space, not a reconstruction.

Reconstructing LSFM *across* slices — recovering slice order, orientation and inter-slice deformation without an OCT block-face reference — is a different and unsolved problem, and it is what the lab's older reconstruction project works on. **`octreg v1` deliberately does not touch it. It solves the other end of the same chain.**

```
LSFM slice i  --(2D affine + 2D SVF, per slice, vessel-guided)-->  OCT slab i
OCT block     --(3D affine, optionally SVF)                    -->  whole-hemisphere MRI
```

---

### 8.2 Their registration method, exactly

#### 8.2.1 Repository layout (fetched 2026-08-23, branch `main`)

`github.com/neuroscales/biccn-broca-I46`:

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `scripts/registration/` | 27 files, the whole registration pipeline |
| `scripts/PSOCT_data_processing/` | MATLAB OCT reconstruction, stitching, vessel segmentation, graph refinement |
| `results/mri2oct/affine.lta` | **the one published MRI↔OCT affine**, 208 bytes |
| `results/oct2lsfm/affine.{08..23}.lta` + `svf.{08..23}.nii.gz` | per-slice OCT↔LSFM transforms, 16 slices |
| `results/mri/{raw2samseg,recon2raw,recon2samseg}.lta` | relations between the three MRI spaces |
| `results/lsfm/*.lta` | channel-to-NeuN and slide-to-centre transforms |
| `results/warp2surf/`, `results/warp2lsfm/` | stereology counts projected to surfaces |
| `external/` | 5 submodules: `ZetaStitcher`, `biolabtools`, `exvivoMRI_preproc` (dvya), `metrics` (balbasty), `nitorch` (balbasty, branch `refactor-registration-preproc` — **dead branch**, commit `7850936`) |

Registration scripts, in dependency order:

```
mri2oct_affine.sh                      MRI -> OCT affine (the baseline)
mri2oct_nonlin.sh                      MRI -> OCT affine + SVF (paper says not needed here)
mri2oct_affine_ablation.sh             4 runs: all / no-vessels / no-segment / neither
mri2oct_affine_ablation_kernelsize.sh  LCC patch sweep 5,10,20,40,60 % + global NCC
mri_reslice2oct.sh                     reslice MRI + MRI vessels into OCT space at 12 and 36 um
mri2oct_make_vessel_overlap.py         builds a 1/2/3-valued MRI-vs-OCT vessel overlap map
lsfm_find_slide.py                     locate the two glass-slide planes by min-gradient
lsfm_slide_center_and_scale.py         give the LSFM slice OCT's z centre, 50 samples, 7.92 um
lsfm_slide_crop_like_neun.sh           crop other channels like the NeuN channel
lsfm_align_channels.sh (+_apply_to_vessels.sh)   calb2neun / sst2neun channel alignment
lsfm_squeeze_distance.py               d -> 1 - exp(-d), squashes the vessel EDT
oct_make_noisify.py                    clamp OCT at 60, subtract 60, add U(0,1) dither
oct2lsfm_affine.sh                     per-slice 2D affine, 3 passes (patch 20 -> 10 -> 5 %)
oct2lsfm_nonlin.sh                     per-slice 2D SVF
lsfm2oct_make_lsfm_volume.py           warp all LSFM slices into one OCT-space volume
mri2lsfm_layers_compute_distance.py / _stats_distance.py / mri2lsfm_warp2slidecenter.sh
stereo_project.py / stereo_warp.py     stereology site coordinates through the transform chain
warp2surf_move_oct.sh
```

#### 8.2.2 `mri2oct_affine.sh` — verbatim

This is the baseline. Read every line; the ten variables at the top are the argument of this whole chapter.

```bash
ROOT="."
MRIVOL="$ROOT/mri/crop/mri.crop.mgz"
MRIGM="$ROOT/mri/crop2/gray.crop.nii"
MRIWM="$ROOT/mri/crop2/white.crop.nii"
MRIVSL="$ROOT/mri/crop/vessels.manual.crop.mgz"
OCTVOL="$ROOT/oct/pool3x3x3/oct.win33.nii"
OCTMSK="$ROOT/oct/pool3x3x3/mask.nii"
OCTGM="$ROOT/oct/gray.lowres.mgz"
OCTWM="$ROOT/oct/white.lowres.mgz"
OCTVSL="$ROOT/oct/pool4x4x4/vessels.manual.float.nii.gz"     # declared but NEVER USED
OCTDST="$ROOT/oct/pool4x4x4/vessels.manual.distance.nii.gz"

nitorch register2 --verbose 4 --gpu --output-dir "$ROOT/mri2oct/affine" \
  @loss lcc  --patch 5 %  @@mov $MRIVOL  @@fix $OCTVOL --mask $OCTMSK \
  @loss dice 0.5          @@mov $MRIGM --label --fwhm 1  @@fix $OCTGM --label \
  @loss dice 0.5          @@mov $MRIWM --label --fwhm 1  @@fix $OCTWM --label \
  @loss ndot 0.1          @@mov $MRIVSL --label 255 --fwhm 1  @@fix $OCTDST --rescale 0 \
  @affine affine --progressive \
  @@optim gn -t 1e-8 -n 256 \
  @pyramid --levels 1:5
```

**The objective is a weighted sum of four terms:**

| Term | Loss | Weight | Moving input (MRI) | Fixed input (OCT) |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Intensity | `lcc`, patch 5 % of FOV | **1** (implicit) | `mri.crop.mgz` | `oct.win33.nii`, masked by `mask.nii` |
| Gray matter | `dice` | **0.5** | `gray.crop.nii` (label, fwhm 1) | `gray.lowres.mgz` (label) |
| White matter | `dice` | **0.5** | `white.crop.nii` (label, fwhm 1) | `white.lowres.mgz` (label) |
| Vessels | `ndot` | **0.1** | `vessels.manual.crop.mgz` (label 255, fwhm 1) | `vessels.manual.distance.nii.gz`, `--rescale 0` |

**Direction of the transform.** `@@fix` is OCT, `@@mov` is MRI: **the MRI is deformed into OCT space and the objective is evaluated on the small block grid**. This is exactly what p.12 states — when registering a whole volume with a sub-block, the larger volume is always deformed to the space of the smaller block, where the objective is computed; because the transformation model is diffeomorphic the transforms can nevertheless be inverted and used to warp the block back into the larger volume's space. Our own audit independently concluded the LTA direction is **OCT world → MRI world** under nitorch's fix→mov resampling convention (audit §5.2). `octreg` inherits this design wholesale — see §8.5.

#### 8.2.3 The ten required inputs, and which six are human-made

This table is the core of the comparison. **Six of the ten inputs cost human labour, and two of them were never published.**

| Script var | File | Human labour required | Available in DANDI:000026? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MRIVOL` | `mri/crop/mri.crop.mgz` | **the crop box is a position prior** — someone already knew where the block came from | derivable — the crop box can be taken from the BA44/45 label bbox, expanded |
| `MRIGM` | `mri/crop2/gray.crop.nii` | manual + SmartInterpol GM label | derivable from `label-infrasupra_seg-wholehemi_dseg` (class meanings not documented) |
| `MRIWM` | `mri/crop2/white.crop.nii` | manual WM label | same |
| `MRIVSL` | `mri/crop/vessels.manual.crop.mgz` | **hand-drawn MRI vessels**, value 255 | yes — `label-vessels_dseg`, 34,036 voxels at 255 (plus 33 stray voxels at 1) |
| `OCTVOL` | `oct/pool3x3x3/oct.win33.nii` | none | derivable — 3×3×3 pool of the 12 µm OME-TIFF → 36 µm |
| `OCTMSK` | `oct/pool3x3x3/mask.nii` | tissue mask | must be made ourselves |
| `OCTGM` | `oct/gray.lowres.mgz` | **OCT gray-matter mask** | **NOT PUBLISHED** |
| `OCTWM` | `oct/white.lowres.mgz` | **OCT white-matter mask** | **NOT PUBLISHED** |
| `OCTVSL` | `oct/pool4x4x4/vessels.manual.float.nii.gz` | hand-drawn OCT vessels | declared in the script but **never used** |
| `OCTDST` | `oct/pool4x4x4/vessels.manual.distance.nii.gz` | EDT of **hand-drawn OCT vessels** | partially — `derivatives/.../vessel/ves_seg.tif` exists but has 561 z-slices against the OCT's 627, and the offset is unresolved |

Two conclusions follow, and both must survive into any write-up:

1. **The exact baseline cannot be reproduced from public data.** The OCT GM/WM masks were never released. Any reproduction of B0 is necessarily approximate on the two Dice terms. (Source: `costantini_b0/reports/costantini_i46_data_audit.md` §2.3.)
2. **The method requires manual labels on *both* modalities plus a position prior.** Six annotation products — MRI GM, MRI WM, MRI vessels, OCT GM, OCT WM, OCT vessels — plus a crop box that encodes where the block already is. That is the human cost `octreg` sets out to remove.

The practical bite of this shows up immediately on the lab's own data. `/shared/u/xiangruz/registration/OCT_to_MRI/` on the xulab cluster contains exactly two files:

```
13,025,490,607  I58_Brainstem_mus_Slice_full_20um_corr.nii.gz    (OCT)
    92,207,321  I58_brainstem_MRI_cropped_to_OCT.nii.gz          (MRI, already cropped)
```

**No labels, no segmentations, no vessel annotations, no reference transform** — the directory listing was read read-only on 2026-08-23 and contains those two files and nothing else (chapter 10, State of play: where everything is, §10.1 has the access details). On this data the baseline as published is not merely inconvenient, it is **unrunnable**: four of its six annotation inputs do not exist. Note the asymmetry — the MRI is *already cropped to the OCT*, so the lab's own data happens to supply the position prior while supplying none of the labels. That is the opposite of the DANDI situation and a useful reminder that the two human inputs are independent, and that removing either one alone is a partial result.

#### 8.2.4 Exact flag semantics

From `nitorch/cli/registration/register/parser.py` at commit `7850936`:

| Flag as used | Meaning | Default if omitted |
|---|---|---|
| `@loss lcc` | local correlation coefficient (LNCC) | — |
| `--patch 5 %` | patch size 5, **unit = percent of FOV** (`-p, --patch *VAL [UNIT]`; units `vox`/`mm`/`pct`, default unit pct) | patch 10 |
| `@loss dice 0.5` | Dice/F1 loss, global factor 0.5 | factor 1 |
| `@loss ndot 0.1` | normalized-dot loss, factor 0.1. Implemented as `normprod` in `nitorch/tools/registration/losses/prod.py`: `0.5 · Σ[(Σ m·f)² / (Σ m)²]` with `m` = moving mask, `f` = fixed map — i.e. the **square** of the paper's MED `(dᵀv)/(1ᵀv)` | factor 1 |
| `--label` | file is a label map; with no argument, all non-zero labels | not a label map |
| `--label 255` | treat only value 255 as the label | — |
| `--fwhm 1` | smooth the image before use | none |
| `--rescale 0` | rescale so percentiles (0, 0) → (0, 1); effectively disables the default `[0, 95]` percentile rescaling | `-s 0 95` |
| `--mask FILE` | mask of voxels to **include** | all |
| `@affine affine` | full **12-DOF** affine, parameterized in the Lie algebra | rigid |
| `--progressive` (`-g`) | progressive optimization **t → r → s → a** | off |
| `@@optim gn -t 1e-8 -n 256` | **Gauss-Newton**, tolerance 1e-8, max 256 iterations, CG linear solver, 32 sub-iterations | tol 1e-4; affine max-iter 50 (interleaved) / 100 (sequential) |
| `@pyramid --levels 1:5` | `parse_range("1:5")` → `range(1,5)` → **levels 1, 2, 3, 4** (stop is exclusive), Gaussian pyramid | `range(3)` = levels 0, 1, 2 |
| `@nonlin svf -a 1 -m 0 -b 500 -l 10 100` | SVF; absolute 1, membrane 0, **bending 500**, lame (divergence, shears) = (10, 100) | absolute 1e-4, membrane 1e-3, bending 0.2, lame (0.05, 0.2) |
| `--voxel-size 0.3` / `0.1 mm` | SVF grid spacing | 100 % (same as the mean space) |
| `--fov oct` / `--fov lsfm` | which named input defines the SVF's mean space | all inputs |
| `--pad 10 %` | pad the SVF FOV | 0 % |
| `-2d [AXIS=2]` | force the transform to be 2D about the axis | 3D |
| `--slicewise -1` (`-z`) | make the loss slice-wise about axis −1 | off |

**Optimizer, per p.12:** a PyTorch implementation of **Gauss-Newton** using analytical first and *approximate* second derivatives; parameters optimized coarse-to-fine, **rigid only → affine only → affine and nonlinear**. The affine is parameterized in the Lie algebra of the affine Lie group; the nonlinear part is a stationary velocity field exponentiated by scaling-and-squaring, which guarantees invertible diffeomorphisms under mild smoothness, and is regularized by a combination of bending and linear-elastic energies.

Note what `--progressive` *is* and *is not*. It walks translation → rotation → scale → full affine **from identity**, inside an already-cropped FOV. It is a well-behaved local refinement schedule, not a search. It cannot find a block whose position is unknown.

#### 8.2.5 The nonlinear stage (`mri2oct_nonlin.sh`)

Same four losses, plus:

```bash
@affine affine --init "$ROOT/mri2oct/affine/affine.lta" \
@@optim gn --tolerance 1e-8 -n 64 \
@nonlin svf -a 1 -m 0 -b 500 -l 10 100 --voxel-size 0.3 --fov oct --pad 10 % \
@@optim --tolerance 1e-5 -n 32 \
@pyramid --levels 1:5
```

**The paper is explicit that for MRI→OCT on this specimen "no nonlinear registration was necessary" (p.12).** The script exists anyway. (It also contains a harmless duplicated `OCTGM=` line.) This statement is the thing our own non-rigid experiment independently confirms — see §8.6.5.

#### 8.2.6 The ablations they ran

`mri2oct_affine_ablation.sh` runs the identical affine four times into four output directories: `affine_vessels-and-segment`, `affine_no-vessels`, `affine_no-segment`, `affine_no-vessels_no-segment`. `mri2oct_affine_ablation_kernelsize.sh` sweeps the LCC patch over **5, 10, 20, 40, 60 %** and adds a global (non-local) `@loss cc` run into `affine_ncc`. `mri_reslice2oct.sh` then reslices the MRI and the MRI vessel labels through **every** `mri2oct/affine*/affine.lta` at 12 µm and 36 µm (`-i 0` = nearest-neighbour for the labels), and `mri2oct_make_vessel_overlap.py` produces a `uint8` map coded 0/1/2/3 = neither / MRI only / OCT only / both. **That overlap map is their registration QC, and it is qualitative.** There is no restart-scatter statistic, no candidate margin, no automatic failure flag.

#### 8.2.7 OCT ↔ LSFM, for completeness

This is the machinery `octreg` would inherit if the lab ever chained the two ends together, so it is worth knowing.

`oct2lsfm_affine.sh`, per slice `i` in 08..23, three passes with decreasing patch (`run_register 20`, then `10 init`, then `5 init`):

```bash
@loss lcc --patch $PATCH % --slicewise -1 \
    @@fix $LSFM -z 64 64 0 -b replicate  @@mov $OCT -b zero \
@loss dice 1 \
    @@fix $LSFMVSL -z 64 64 0 -b replicate --rescale 0 \
    @@mov $OCTVSL -b zero --rescale 0 --fwhm 1 \
@affine affine -2d [--progessive | --init .../affine.lta] \
@@optim gn --tolerance 1e-8 -n 1024 \
@pyramid --levels 2:9
```

`oct2lsfm_nonlin.sh` then freezes the affine (`@@optim none`) and fits `@nonlin svf 1 -2d -a 1 -m 0 -b 50 -l 10 10 --voxel-size 0.1 mm --pad 10 % --fov lsfm` with `@@optim gn --tolerance 1e-8 -n 32`, `@pyramid --levels 2:9`. `-b 50 -l 10 10` matches the paper's "bending energy: 50, divergence: 10, shears: 10", which confirms that nitorch's `--lame` argument order is **(divergence, shears)**.

Two details worth stealing:

- The OCT is **dithered** before the nonlinear stage (`oct_make_noisify.py`: clamp at 60, subtract 60, add `U(0,1)`) so that the flat background does not produce a degenerate Hessian.
- The LSFM vessel EDT is squashed through `d → 1 − exp(−d)` (`lsfm_squeeze_distance.py`) so that far-away vessels stop dominating the distance loss.

Also note that both `oct2lsfm` scripts have the `ndot` vessel loss **commented out** in favour of `dice 1`, and that `--progessive` is misspelled — whether the parser errors or silently ignores it was never checked `[OPEN]`.

#### 8.2.8 Paper text vs shipped scripts — three discrepancies a reimplementer will hit

| Item | Paper p.12 | `main` branch scripts | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dice term | "Soft Dice between **gray matter** segments (weight: 1)" | two terms, `dice 0.5` on gray **and** `dice 0.5` on white | the total weight is the same; the split is not in the paper |
| MRI→OCT working resolution | "the OCT volume was downsampled to 100 × 100 × 50 µm" | `oct/pool3x3x3/…`, and `mri_reslice2oct.sh` names its outputs `…reslice.12um` / `…reslice.36um`, i.e. `oct.nii` = 12 µm and pool3 = **36 µm** | the repo appears to be the version tuned to the 12 µm public release, not the 5 µm in-house data |
| LCC patch | "LCC was computed within patches of 4 mm × 4 mm × 2 mm" | `--patch 5 %` (percent of FOV) | 5 % of a ~15 mm block is ~0.75 mm, not 4 mm; the two cannot both be literal. Treat `5 %` as authoritative for the code and 4 × 4 × 2 mm as the intent; that reconciliation is our reading, not the authors' `[UNVERIFIED]` |
| OCT→LSFM resolution | OCT 96 × 96 × 12 µm, LSFM 40 × 40 × 10 µm | not encoded in the shell scripts (comes from the prepared inputs) | — |

#### 8.2.9 Their reported accuracy and runtime

`literature_review/cross_modality_registration_review.md` §3.5 records the paper's end-to-end cortical-boundary validation as **95th percentile 527 ± 137 µm, 75th percentile 306 ± 96 µm** — i.e. 75 % of boundary errors below two 150 µm MRI voxels. `[UNVERIFIED]` — the page renders read for this chapter are pages 9–12, which are Methods; this number lives in the Results and was taken from the review, not from the paper itself. It is the right order of magnitude to target, but it is not a pass/fail threshold for a different preprocessing chain, and it is an end-to-end LSFM-to-MRI number, not an MRI↔OCT number.

**Runtime of their pipeline: `[OPEN]`.** Nothing in the paper text read, the scripts, or the repository reports wall-clock time, and no other source available here states it. Any runtime comparison in the table below is therefore one-sided: we can state ours precisely and cannot state theirs at all.

The 0.6 mm coarse search alone cannot separate them (0.741 vs 0.726). **`auto` is not the default** — `run_subject.sh` line 21 hard-codes it, so every DANDI run used it, but a successor calling `register.py` directly silently gets single-polarity behaviour |

#### 8.3.1 The runtime numbers, corrected — read this before quoting any of them

The figure "**154 s for a whole hemisphere**" appears in `octreg/README.md`, `EXPLAINER_zh.md`, and half a dozen of the project's prose documents, sometimes rounded to "150 s". It is a real measurement, and quoting it in a sentence about the *label-free* pipeline is nevertheless wrong. It comes from `octreg/scripts/run_demo_i46.py`, whose `--features` default is `mixed` — documented in that script (line 42) as "MRI parser probabilities + OCT intensity-derived WM/GM (polarity resolved by the parser)". So the MRI channels of that run are the **trained 3D-U-Net parser's probabilities**, not the training-free features. (`register.py` accepts only `choices=["otsu","parser"]`; `mixed` does not exist there and `octreg/octreg/features.py::build_features` raises `ValueError` on it. The run also used `work/i46`, lower-case, a separate prep directory from `work/I46`.)

**The honest sentence, every part verified:**

> An exhaustive 16,000-orientation search over all translations costs **45 s** on a 0.08 mm brainstem crop and **299 s** on a 0.15 mm whole hemisphere with the label-free Otsu features (**154 s** with the parser-probability features); the shipped wrapper runs it once per class polarity, so budget **598 s** of search for a whole hemisphere. Whole-corpus single-branch range **44.8 s – 1,010.3 s**.

Two consequences for the comparison table above. First, end to end the nine DANDI otsu runs span **18.7 – 131.1 min** on one RTX 4090; only 4 of 9 fall inside the "15–40 min" that the project's prose asserts, so **do not quote 15–40 min**. Second, the stage that dominates wall clock is **not** the search but the vascular refinement — on the worst run, I38, it is 5,696.8 s of a 7,864.1 s total, and search is only 8–38 % of wall clock across the corpus. The per-branch breakdown for every run — seconds per 4,000 orientations, the full search, each polarity trial, the vascular stage and the total — is tabulated once in **chapter 6, What we found, and what it means**, and is not repeated here.

One point worth carrying that is easy to misread: the `whole_mixed_real` / `whole_mixed_v2` runs at **76.7 s / 76.1 s** are *not* superseded figures, as one of the project's organisational documents claims. They are the same code as `whole_final` / `whole_final2` (**153.4 s / 153.7 s**) at half the orientation count — same prep, same template, same grid.

#### 8.3.2 One more asymmetry the table does not show: the adaptive overlap gate

`octreg` requires a candidate pose to place a stated fraction of the OCT block inside MRI tissue, and that requirement is **adaptive**: `register.py:111` lowers it automatically when the block is physically larger than the MRI tissue it is supposed to sit inside, subject to a hard floor of **0.15** that several prose descriptions omit. The formula, the floor, and the two volumes that drive it are stated in full once, in **chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning** (§5.2).

What matters for the comparison with the baseline: **on DANDI the gate never binds** — all eight runs that record it show `overlap_gate = {requested 0.85, effective 0.850}` — and it binds **only on the brainstem pair**, where `xiangrui_I58bs` gets an effective gate of **0.369**. `work/runs/I46_otsu/result.json` has `overlap_gate: null`, because the gate did not yet exist when I46 was run. **The baseline has no analogue of this mechanism at all**, because its MRI is pre-cropped by hand to something that already contains the block — which is the position prior restated as an engineering convenience.

#### 8.3.3 A reproducibility caveat that belongs in any comparison

**The I46 headline numbers are not reproducible with the code currently on disk.** Five of the nine headline runs predate the current sources. `register.py` has mtime 2026-08-20 23:30, `prep_subject.py` 15:11, `vascular.py` 19:31; the `result.json` mtimes for I46 (10:23), I38 (19:48), I55 (20:18), I56 (21:07) and I62 (22:01) all precede 23:30, while I61 (00:03), I48 (01:01), I57 (01:50) and I58 (04:24) follow it. **I46 is the only subject whose prep (`work/I46/prep.json`, 10:04) and registration both predate the current code**, and the adaptive overlap gate demonstrably did not exist then. The tree is unversioned — `/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project` is not a git repository at all, verified 2026-08-23 (chapter 10, State of play: where everything is, §10.10) — so the revision that produced `I46_otsu` is **unrecoverable**. Any claim of the form "our method beats theirs by X on I46" is currently a claim about a code revision that no longer exists. Re-running I46 with today's code is the first thing to do before any of §8.4 is written into a paper.
