### 8.4 What is genuinely ours, ranked

Ordered most to least defensible. "Defensible" here means: can be demonstrated on the data we have, against a stated baseline, without appeal to anything unverified.

**1. Removing the position prior.**
The baseline needs an MRI already cropped to roughly where the block came from. We replace it with an exhaustive masked-NCC search over all translations (via FFT) × 8000 quasi-uniform SO(3) rotations × 2 handednesses at 0.6 mm — **299 s for a full hemisphere with label-free features**. This is the difference between "refine a known pose" and "find the block". Demonstrated on blocks from 15 mm up to 50 mm slabs dropped into whole hemispheres with zero hints. This is the contribution that survives even if everything else is judged incremental, because `--progressive` from identity inside an uncropped hemisphere is not a competitive alternative — it is a different problem statement.

**2. Removing the manual segmentations.**
The baseline needs hand-drawn GM, WM and vessels on **both** modalities — six annotation products, two of which were never released. We replace them with a training-free two-class Otsu map on both sides. **The enabling trick is the MRI bias-field flattening**: after dividing by the local mean (Gaussian σ = 10 mm), a plain Otsu split agrees with the manual labels at **Dice 0.90 / 0.93**, up from **0.66 / 0.62** without it. **This improvement is confirmed** — it was re-derived from the volumes on the compute server, and the exact before/after pair, the script that produces it (`/tmp/flat.py I46 0.15`) and the reason the four circulating figures differ by ≤ 0.02 are given in **chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning** (§5.1.5). It is quotable as it stands. That single preprocessing step is what makes a label-free whole-hemisphere Otsu split viable at all, and it is a direct consequence of the acquisition fact in §8.1.1: no body coil, so the receive bias was never removed at acquisition.

**3. An automatic vessel channel that recovers the depth-axis scale.**
MRI vessels as a local-darkness map (they are dark spots in ex-vivo FLASH), OCT vessels as our own Frangi dark-tube segmentation, correlated as a third channel with weight 2.0. **This is the only thing in the pipeline that constrains the scale along the block's depth axis**, and it needs no annotation on either side. The evidence and its limits are §8.6.

**4. Resolving polarity and handedness automatically.**
Both flip between subjects of the *same* dataset — I46 is GM-bright and mirrored, I55 is WM-bright and not mirrored — so neither can be assumed. **The coarse search cannot decide polarity**: a two-class cortical sheet with the classes swapped matches equally well somewhere else (score 0.741 vs 0.726, and even Dice-against-manual-labels 0.86/0.77 at the *wrong* place). The refined NCC can (0.756 vs 0.730), and the vessel-channel NCC is an independent check (≈0 at a wrong pose). Note what this is and is not: it is a **within-subject** comparison of two candidates on the same data. The absolute value of `refine.final_ncc` is **not** a correctness criterion across subjects and no threshold on it should ever be quoted as one — I61 scores **0.5020** and I57 **0.5121** and both are wrong, while I62 scores **0.2842** and is correct. Handedness: **6 of 9** subjects mirrored. The baseline sidesteps both because the manual masks carry the answer.

**5. A negative result worth publishing: tissue geometry is blind to the depth scale.**
`octreg/scripts/scale_probe.py` sweeps an anisotropic stretch `s ∈ [0.85, 1.30]` in steps of 0.025 along one OCT array axis at a time on top of `T0`, and records NCC, label Dice and vessel metrics (`work/runs/summary/scale_profiles.json`, byte-identical to `work/runs/validate_real/scale_profiles.json`). The result: along the block's **depth / serial-sectioning axis** the label-free objective moves by only **Δ NCC 0.021** across that 45 % stretch, against **Δ 0.169** along the in-plane `k` axis — the objective is **8× less sensitive to depth scale than to in-plane scale** — and along depth the *manual labels* still resolve a maximum at s = 1.100 that the NCC essentially cannot see, its own maximum sitting at 1.075 on a 0.021-wide plateau. **A one-sheet GM/WM block simply does not encode its own thickness scale, and neither do the manual GM/WM labels.** Anyone doing OCT→MRI with structure-only similarity will silently absorb this error. The full three-axis table, with argmaxes and ranges per axis, is in **chapter 6, What we found, and what it means** (§6.10.3).

The pipeline's vascular stage recovers **1.219** for I46 (`work/runs/I46_otsu/result.json → final_transform.stretch_ijk[0]`). The phrase "the true scale is ~1.18" that circulates in the project's prose has no artefact behind it `[UNVERIFIED]`; the two defensible anchors are the pipeline's own **1.219** and the sidecar-vs-siblings ratio **14/12 = 1.167**, and whoever wrote it must say which one was meant.

**6. Physical-units-throughout engineering, so the method transfers.**
The same parameters run on 0.12–0.15 mm MRI and 12–35 µm OCT with no retuning; whole-hemisphere features live on CPU in float16 and only block-sized crops touch the GPU. This is engineering, not science, but it is the reason the method could be pointed at the I58 brainstem data the day that data appeared, and it is what makes the multi-subject table in the results chapter possible at all.

**The honest one-line framing for a paper:** *we did not invent a similarity metric or a transformation model; we removed two human inputs — the labels and the position prior — from an existing, validated pipeline, and showed that what is lost in doing so (the depth-axis scale) can be recovered from automatically segmented vasculature.*

---

### 8.5 What is NOT novel — state this plainly and first

Every component below is prior art. If a reviewer, a PI, or a lab-meeting audience raises any of them as "this already exists", the correct response is agreement, not defence. The novelty claim in §8.4 does not depend on any of these being new.

| Component | Prior art / status |
|---|---|
| **Coarse-to-fine affine (rigid → similarity → affine)** | Textbook. The baseline itself does `--progressive` t→r→s→a. Osechinskiy & Kruggel 2011 did the same for histology→MRI. **Zero novelty.** |
| **FFT-based cross-correlation over all translations** | Standard template matching since the 1970s; masked NCC via FFT is Lewis 1995 / Padfield 2010. We use it; we did not invent it. |
| **Frangi vesselness** | Frangi et al. 1998. Off-the-shelf; we only run it dark-tube and chunked along z. |
| **Otsu thresholding** | Otsu 1979. |
| **Local-mean division for bias correction** | Classic homomorphic / retrospective bias correction. The *result* (Dice 0.66/0.62 → 0.90/0.93) is a useful measured fact; the operator is not new. |
| **Distance-transform vessel losses, Dice on segments, LCC** | All from the baseline and from the general registration literature. |
| **SVF / scaling-and-squaring diffeomorphisms** | Arsigny 2006, Ashburner 2007. We tried it and dropped it. |
| **Using vessels as the cross-modal landmark** | **The baseline's core idea.** We automated the segmentation; we did not discover that vessels are the right structure. |
| **MIND-SSC features** | Heinrich et al. 2013; present in `octreg/octreg/features.py` as an alternative, not the shipped default. |
| **"Deform the big volume into the small one's grid"** | Explicitly the baseline's design (paper p.12). We inherit it. |
| **Multi-start / restart-based robustness** | Standard practice (NiftyReg Aladin multi-start, etc.). Our 12 perturbed restarts are a QC statistic, not a new optimizer. |
| **The 3D U-Net MRI parser** | Not novel and not shipped; it exists only as the `--features parser` ablation, and it gives the same registration as Otsu. Its only role in the argument is negative: it shows the training-free path loses nothing. |

### 8.6 Where our findings independently agree with theirs

Two independent agreements exist. Both are worth stating because they are the only external checks the project has, and both come with caveats that must be carried alongside them.

#### 8.6.1 The authors' published affine

`results/mri2oct/affine.lta`, 208 bytes, fetched from `main`:

```
type      = 1  # LINEAR_RAS_TO_RAS
nxforms   = 1
1 4 4
 1.1741251     0.109609105  -0.105837345  -7.432568
-0.003448261   1.0491916    -0.11666678   -6.1766615
 0.011982521   0.058345348   0.99289995   -2.8748932
 0.0 0.0 0.0 1.0
```

Decomposed locally with numpy:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Per-axis scales (column norms) | **1.17419**, 1.05651, 1.00532 |
| Singular values | 1.21149, 1.03593, 0.98222 |
| Determinant | 1.23270 (23.3 % volume change) |
| Rotation angle of the polar factor | 6.43° |
| Translation | (−7.43, −6.18, −2.87) mm |

`costantini_b0/reports/costantini_i46_data_audit.md` §5 records exactly these. **This affine was fitted with the `ndot` vessel term against `vessels.manual.distance.nii.gz` — hand-drawn vessels are what carry that 1.174.**

#### 8.6.2 The same quantity, from the same manual annotations, in our frame

`octreg/results/final/summary/refine_validate.json`, row `B1: ORACLE affine (manual)` — an affine fitted directly to the manual MRI vessels plus the manual GM/WM labels by our own optimizer, used only as a ceiling and never by the method:

```
scales           = [1.0465, 0.9992, 1.1770]
vessel_median_um = 171.47      vessel_f150 = 0.4657
dice_WM          = 0.802       dice_GM     = 0.831
```

`vessel_channel_refine.json` reports the same transform as `stretch_ijk = [1.177, 0.999, 1.046]`, and `scale_profiles.json` names the axes `"i (627-axis, depth/stack)"`, `"j (1271-axis)"`, `"k (1230-axis)"`. **So the 1.177 sits on the OCT depth / stacking axis.**

#### 8.6.3 What our label-free vessel channel recovers

All on I46, `reg 0.5`, `clamp 0.3`, `T0` = the structural-only result. The vascular stage was swept over both vessel representations (MRI side: local-darkness map or Frangi; OCT side: density of a segmentation or a raw Frangi map) and over the vessel-channel weight `w ∈ {0.5, 1, 2, 4}`, plus a vessel-term-only run and a WM/GM-only control on the identical optimisation schedule. **The 22-variant sweep, including that control — which is what proves the gain comes from the vessel channel and not from the looser regularisation — is tabulated once in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means (§6.10.4).** The numbers this chapter needs from it are in the claim below; the sources are `octreg/results/final/summary/vessel_channel_refine.json` and `test_own_vessels.json`.

**The claim, stated at exactly the precision the data supports:** the authors' published affine has a largest-axis scale of **1.174** obtained from hand-drawn vessels; an oracle affine fitted to those same manual annotations in our frame puts **1.177** on the OCT depth axis; our fully automatic vessel channel lands between **1.14 and 1.24** depending on the weight — **1.22** at the shipped default and **1.18–1.21** in the variants that use a Frangi channel on one side. Structure-only registration gives **1.03**; it does not see the stretch at all. **This is agreement at the ±0.05 level on a quantity the structural objective cannot measure. It is not agreement to three decimals. Do not overclaim it.**

The corroborating metrics move together and hit a hard ceiling: manual-vessel median distance **276 µm → 166 µm** (oracle 171 µm), fraction within 150 µm **0.254 → 0.477** (oracle 0.466), against a random-placement control of ≈350 µm / ≈0.20. **The oracle is fitted to the same manual vessels used to score it, so 0.47 is the physical ceiling of that single-voxel line annotation — and we reach it.** Cross-validated (3 seeds × 2 folds, split by vessel connected component) the held-out oracle is 0.42.

For reference, the corresponding numbers from the *shipped* I46 run (`work/runs/summary_all/summary.md` I46 row and `evaluation.final`), which is a different experiment from the T0-based ablation above: vessels scored against our own Frangi segmentation **173 µm / f150 0.44 → 123 µm / 0.56** (control 215 → 212), and against DANDI's `ves_seg` **265 µm / 0.28 → 167 µm / 0.47** (control 354 → 352). Final Dice for the shipped I46 run is **0.803 / 0.825**; I55 is **0.921 / 0.930**.

#### 8.6.4 The physical explanation, and a third independent line

`octreg/README.md` §4.2: I46's OME-TIFF JSON sidecar declares **12 µm isotropic**, but the sidecars of other subjects in the same dataset declare **30 × 30 × 35 µm** or **12 × 12 × 14 µm**. Both give a depth-to-in-plane ratio of **35/30 = 14/12 = 1.1667**. So I46's metadata appears simply to have omitted the anisotropic depth spacing, and 1.1667 is what a correct sidecar would have said.

Independent routes to that number:

| Route | Value | Depends on |
|---|---:|---|
| The authors' hand-drawn-vessel affine (`affine.lta` column norm) | **1.174** | their manual vessels |
| Our oracle affine fitted to the manual annotations | **1.177** | the same manual annotations, our optimizer |
| Sibling subjects' sidecar metadata, 35/30 = 14/12 | **1.1667** | DANDI metadata only |
| Our fully automatic vessel channel, shipped weight | **1.223** | nothing manual at all |

The first three converge tightly and our label-free channel recovers the same magnitude without any of them. That is three routes, not four: **a fourth line once counted here — the measured 33-slice section period read against the paper's nominal 500 µm cut, giving 15.15 µm per slice — has been withdrawn** (§8.1.1). It fails on the I56 counter-example and, read consistently across both subjects, implies a 1.06 correction rather than 1.167. It must not be re-introduced. What does survive from that measurement is only the observation that 33 × 12 µm = 0.396 mm is exactly the slab thickness the authors hard-code in their own LSFM script, which is consistent with them having propagated the same 12 µm sidecar — a consistency check on the authors' pipeline, not evidence about the true spacing.

> **The reverse test, corrected — and it is not a clean null.** I55's sidecar *does* record the correct anisotropic spacing (`[12, 12, 14]` µm, corroborated twice inside the file), so the prediction is that I55 needs no depth correction. The project's prose says it "needs only a 1.10 depth stretch". **The actual value is 0.913** — `work/runs/I55_otsu/result.json → final_transform.stretch_ijk = [0.913, 1.097, 1.084]`, and **index 0 is the depth axis**; the 1.097 that got quoted is the in-plane `j` axis. The qualitative argument survives — the vascular stage moves the block by only **0.334 mm** on I55 against 1.524 mm on I46 — but the number does not, and neither does the word "clean".
>
> **The caveat that must travel with every use of I55 as a null result:** I55's recovered depth/in-plane *anisotropy* is **0.8570**, and `6/7 = 0.857143`. It agrees to four decimal places with the exact **inverse** of the 7/6 = 1.1667 factor I46 is supposed to be missing. So I55 does not sit at anisotropy 1.0, as a clean null would; it sits at the reciprocal of the very factor under discussion, on the one subject whose sidecar is best corroborated. That is either a second, opposite-signed metadata problem, or a coincidence nobody has explained. It is decisive evidence that *something* about the depth spacing is wrong dataset-wide; it is **not** evidence for the specific "I46's sidecar alone is wrong" story. `[OPEN]` — the per-subject anisotropy table and the three candidate readings, with what each of them predicts, are laid out in chapter 4, The data (§4.5.3); the open question and the two 20-minute re-preps that would settle it are tracked in chapter 12, Open questions and unverified claims. Present I55 as a null result only with this attached.

The related claim that "other subjects come out ≈1.0 once the sidecar is corrected" is stated in `octreg/README.md` and has never been checked `[OPEN]`; the anisotropy column above is the reason to doubt it.

#### 8.6.5 The second agreement: affine is enough

The paper states outright that for MRI→OCT on this specimen "no nonlinear registration was necessary" (p.12), while still shipping `mri2oct_nonlin.sh`. We reached the same conclusion from the opposite direction and without reading it first: a free-form deformation stage on I46 buys **Dice +0.015** and **+0.01** on the vessel metric, and the *oracle* non-rigid displacement field — the best a non-rigid stage could possibly do — has mean **0.10 mm**, p95 **0.12 mm**, max **0.12 mm**, i.e. **below one 0.15 mm MRI voxel everywhere**. `octreg v1` therefore does not ship a non-rigid stage; the measured ablation behind those figures is in **chapter 6, What we found, and what it means** (§6.10.7). This is a genuine independent replication of a design decision, and it is cheap to state: two groups, different features, different optimizers, same conclusion that the OCT block is close to affinely related to the MRI.

#### 8.6.6 The caveat you must carry forward

The audit (`costantini_i46_data_audit.md` §5) established that the authors' `affine.lta` **cannot be used as sub-millimetre ground truth from public data alone**. All of the following are verified there:

- The MRI side must first be moved from the DANDI NIfTI world (ASL sform) into the FreeSurfer `flash20.mgz` frame recorded in `results/mri/raw2samseg.lta` (`xras = (0,0,−1)`, `yras = (−1,0,0)`, `zras = (0,−1,0)`, `cras = (5.13, 9.68, 14.58)`). The two are different world coordinates on the same 1280 × 1040 × 576 grid.
- The OCT side has **no world coordinates at all** — the OME-XML `PhysicalSize` is the placeholder `1.0 pixel`; the real 12 µm lives only in the JSON sidecar.
- Scanning all 96 signed axis permutations, the best conventions (`SRP` 95.8 %, `SPR` 94.8 %, `IRP` 93.8 % of OCT tissue samples landing inside the BA44/45 labels) place the block correctly at **millimetre** scale — centre ≈ (−19, 24, 20) mm in MRI world — but the MRI-vessel-to-`ves_seg` median distance is **≥ 260 µm for every convention** (IRP 276, SRP 397, SPR 471), against a ±3 mm random-translation control at 673 µm mean / 346 µm best. **Sub-millimetre correspondence is not established.**
- `ves_seg.tif` has **561 z-slices** against the OCT's **627**; the offset (0, 66, or something else) is unresolved and the data cannot decide it.

So the 1.174 ↔ 1.177 ↔ 1.22 comparison is a comparison of *scale magnitudes derived independently in two different coordinate conventions*. That is exactly why it is meaningful as corroboration and **useless as a TRE**. If sub-millimetre ground truth is ever needed, the concrete ask is: the header of `oct/oct.nii`, or the crop parameters of `mri/crop/mri.crop.mgz`, from Yael Balbastre or Divya Varadarajan.

A second caveat compounds this one: a **0.12 mm label-axis mis-pairing invalidates Dice for I38, I48, I56, I57, I58 and I61** `[UNVERIFIED]` — it was diagnosed once by re-running `/tmp/aff.py` and `/tmp/alt.py` on the compute server and has not been re-run for this document (chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.5.2 has the coverage detail). The Dice column is trustworthy on I46 and I55 and suspect on the rest, and the reasons differ per subject: I62 and the other large slabs have a label-*coverage* explanation, whereas **I48's Dice is untrustworthy in both directions and its "uncertain" verdict rests on a 0.0013 search-score margin, not on any coverage artefact** — do not lump the two together. Do not build a theirs-vs-ours accuracy claim on the affected subjects until that is resolved.

### 8.7 The rest of the lab's literature collection

#### 8.7.1 `/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/literature_review/` — five documents, search cut-off 2026-08-02

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | 1-page index plus the five standing project conclusions |
| `cross_modality_registration_review.md` | ~750 lines. The main review: problem formalization, the B0–B5 baseline ladder, a method map (transformation models / cross-modal similarities / optimization / overlap handling), 2024–2026 trends, the WP0–WP4 experiment plan, evaluation protocol, ablations, risk register, evidence matrix, reading order, student division of labour |
| `local_papers_review.md` | Per-PDF reading notes for all 14 files in `papers/`, graded A/B/C by whether they actually address 3D + cross-modal + partial-to-whole + unknown initial position |
| `working/brain_oct_mri_applications.md` | 18 directly-relevant papers and resources on brain tissue → ex-vivo MRI; open datasets and benchmark gaps |
| `working/classical_partial_methods.md` | 30+ classical methods; NiftyReg Aladin / ANTs / NiftyReg `reg_f3d` / MIND-SSC + ConvexAdam baseline configurations and their failure modes |
| `working/learning_latest_methods.md` | 38 method groups, 2023–2026 learning-based trends, applicability and "biological truth" risks |

**The five standing conclusions** (`literature_review/README.md`) — these are the lab's own positions, and they explain why the project is shaped the way it is:

1. Reproduce Costantini 2023's MRI→OCT method first.
2. Split the problem explicitly into whole-hemisphere candidate localization and local deformable refinement.
3. The strongest classical comparison lines are: Aladin multi-start/top-K → masked MI affine → ANTs SyN; Aladin → masked NMI `reg_f3d`; TrICP/CPD/MIND candidates → masked MIND-SSC ConvexAdam.
4. Put the novelty in overlap-aware localization, real physical coordinates, candidate uncertainty and failure rejection.
5. Generative methods are exploratory only; **unobserved tissue must never be used as registration evidence.**

Conclusions 2 and 4 are visible directly in `octreg v1`'s architecture — the FFT+SO(3) search *is* the "candidate localization" half, `--topk 24` and the top-1/top-2 score margin *are* the "candidate uncertainty and failure rejection", and "real physical coordinates" is contribution 6 in §8.4. Conclusion 1 is the reason this chapter exists.

**The recommended baseline ladder** (review §1.2). This is where a takeover agent should look for what to compare against next:

| ID | Method | Role | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| B0 | Costantini 2023 as-is: rigid→affine→optional SVF; LCC + GM soft Dice + vessel MED | the homologous baseline that must be reproduced | highest |
| B1 | NiftyReg Aladin multi-start/top-K → masked MI affine → ANTs SyN | the most robust classical partial-to-whole line | highest |
| B1b | Aladin → masked NMI `reg_f3d` B-spline | single-toolchain speed/reproducibility baseline | high |
| B2 | MIND-SSC + ConvexAdam, then SVF/SyN refinement | training-free cross-modal structural baseline | high |
| B2m | EM-LDDMM with non-monotonic intensity transform + matching/background/artifact posteriors (Tward 2020) | explicit missing-data ablation | med-high |
| B3 | overlap-aware / keypoint initializer → B0/B2 refinement | the main innovation candidate | high |
| B4 | multiGradICON / DINO-Reg / Search-MIND zero-shot or instance refinement | latest-method controls, feature ablation | med |
| B5 | VoxelMorph / LapIRN / TransMorph trained from scratch | only if sample size and validation allow | low |

**As of today none of B1–B5 has been run.** The only thing that exists is `octreg v1` (which is closest in spirit to B3) plus an approximate, label-limited reading of B0. That is the largest single gap in the project's comparative story, and it is a bigger gap than any remaining accuracy improvement.

Also recorded there: **no other public, peer-reviewed benchmark exists for a human, centimetre-scale 3D OCT block, unknown position, registered back into a whole-hemisphere MRI with independent TRE annotation.** That is the methodological hole `octreg` sits in — it is why there is no obvious accuracy number to beat, and equally why the honest validation story has to lean on internal consistency (restart scatter, candidate margin, oracle ceilings) rather than on an external gold standard.

Note on DANDI:000026 versioning (review §3.1): as of 2026-08-02 the dandiset was still **draft**, 40,982 files, 38.5 TB, last updated 2026-03-25. **Reproduction must pin exact assets, never "download the latest".** This is why `download_costantini.sh` carries a 16-entry `ASSETS=(...)` array (lines 27–42) of `path|asset_uuid|bytes|sha256` totalling 4,490,619,952 B for the sub-I46 subset. (Some of the project's own prose says "17-asset"; count the array — it is 16.)

#### 8.7.2 `/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/papers/` — 14 PDFs

Grades are from `local_papers_review.md`: **A** = directly shapes the main approach, **B** = usable module or strong control, **C** = adjacent concepts only. Paths are under `/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/papers/`.

| Grade | File | What it is and what it is relevant to |
|---|---|---|
| A | `fnins-14-00052.pdf` | **Tward et al. 2020**, EM-LDDMM for damaged multi-stain histology → MRI/atlas: joint diffeomorphism + non-monotonic polynomial intensity transform + per-pixel matching/background/artifact posterior. **Relevant to:** our explicit missing-data ablation (B2m); the principled way to handle tissue that exists in one modality and not the other. It does **not** do blind localization, so it is not a competitor on contribution 1. |
| A | `Anatomy Research International - 2010 - Osechinskiy - Slice-to-Volume Nonrigid Registration of Histological Sections to MR.pdf` | **Osechinskiy & Kruggel 2011**, human myelin sections (50 µm, 12.7 µm/px) → same-donor 0.35 mm MRI. Systematic comparison of CC/SSD/NMI × TPS/GEBS/B-spline × optimizers; `NEWUOA → TPS + CC` wins. **Relevant to:** the prior art for coarse-to-fine affine (see §8.5 — this is why that is not novel), and to similarity-metric choice. Initialization is manual, so not a localization baseline. |
| A | `v1_covered.pdf` | **mBrainAligner**: fMOST/VISoR/LSFM/MRI whole mouse brain → CCFv3 via outer-contour + DA-RPM global affine, coherent 2.5D landmarks, gradient / 576-D HOG / 3D-U-Net region probabilities, TPS. Median Dice 0.82–0.90; 76 % soma region accuracy. **Relevant to:** the multi-feature-channel idea and the U-Net-probability feature (our `--features parser` ablation). Whole-to-whole; its partial example uses semi-automatic editing, so again not a localization competitor. |
| A | `2507.18551v2.pdf` | **CrossKEY** (IEEE TMI 2026), 3D MRI ↔ intraoperative US: cross-modal saliency, shared 3D ResNet-18 descriptor, curriculum triplet loss with dynamic hard negatives, Lowe-ratio filtering, 3-round rigid RANSAC, **no manual init at inference**. Precision 69.8 %, ~72 matches/pair, TRE 2.385 ± 0.397 mm. **Relevant to:** the concrete template for a learned localizer, i.e. the obvious v2 alternative to our exhaustive FFT×SO(3) search. |
| B | `DINO_REG(MICCAI).pdf` | **DINO-Reg**: training-free multimodal deformable registration on pretrained DINOv2 semantic features + coarse-to-fine pairing + conventional optimization. **Relevant to:** the ablation "are semantic features better than MIND/NGF" *after* cropping. 2D features, near-same-FOV task. |
| B | `2408.00221v2.pdf` | **multiGradICON**: generalist mono/multimodal registration with inverse consistency. **Relevant to:** post-crop zero-shot / instance-optimization control (B4). Authors report DIXON fat↔water failures. **v2 carries an erratum — quote only the corrected tables.** |
| B | `0527_paper.pdf` | **uniGradICON**: generalist registration foundation model across 12 public datasets, plus instance optimization / finetuning. **Relevant to:** the same B4 control slot. Training is largely monomodal; OOD CT–MR does not transfer to OCT partial-to-whole. |
| B | `2501.07556v1.pdf` | **MatchAnything**: universal 2D cross-modal matching trained with synthetic modality stimuli. **Relevant to:** candidate patch reranking and sparse affine initializers. Its medical experiments start from already-aligned same-FOV pairs plus synthetic transforms, so the reported numbers do not transfer. |
| B− | `1233_paper.pdf` | **PromptReg**: universal registration with task/domain prompts, Registration Prompt Generator + Static Knowledge Base. Improves cross-domain DSC; no partial-overlap loss, no blind search, DSC-only reporting. **Relevant to:** a low-priority post-crop control. |
| C | `2404.05105v2.pdf` | **VMambaMorph**: SSM/VMamba backbone with recursive fine-tuning for brain MR–CT deformable registration. Architecture contribution; full-overlap, dataset-specific. **Relevant to:** backbone choice only, if a learned method is ever trained. |
| C | `Cross_Modal(MICCAI).pdf` | Cross-modal inverse neural rendering for neurosurgical 3D→2D camera pose: structure/appearance disentanglement + differentiable pose optimization. 5 real cases, mostly qualitative, one local-minimum failure. **Relevant to:** the disentanglement idea only. |
| C | `1-s2.0-S0097849322001121-main.pdf` | 3D point cloud ↔ micro-CT volume registration via cross-modal attention. 636 samples of **stone** blocks, point clouds synthesized by marching cubes; TRE 15.34 → 5.15, recall 62 %. **No genuine appearance gap** — treat the numbers as not transferable. |
| C | `s11548-018-1774-y.pdf` | Cardiac 3D model → 2D X-ray registration by imitation learning of the optimizer. 702 training / 1000 synthetic test cases, 2.92 ± 2.22 mm; 19 clinical cases lack real ground truth, 3-DOF in-plane perturbation only. **Relevant to:** learned-optimizer framing only. |
| C | `RFNET(CVPR).pdf` | **Filename is wrong** — this is **RBE-Flow** (ECCV 2026, arXiv 2606.30492), recurrent Bayesian estimation of dense cross-modal flow with posterior uncertainty feeding back into the next iteration. Data is 2D remote sensing (OSdataset / WHU-OPT-SAR / RoadScene). **Cite for the confidence-feedback idea only, under the correct title and venue.** |

Reading order if starting cold (`local_papers_review.md` §7): Tward 2020 → Osechinskiy & Kruggel 2011 → CrossKEY 2026 → mBrainAligner → DINO-Reg → multiGradICON v2 → MatchAnything → uniGradICON → PromptReg → the rest on demand.

## 9. The lab: people, history, and the constraints that shape this work

The method in this project was not chosen in a vacuum. Almost every design decision in `octreg` — label-free features, a training-free Otsu path shipping instead of the learned parser, exhaustive global search, visual QC figures as the primary deliverable, downsampled preprocessing — traces back to something a specific person said on a specific date. A successor who knows the code but not the room will re-litigate settled decisions and re-open closed ones. This chapter is the record of the room.

Evidence cutoff for everything here is **2026-08-23**, the date of the most recent recorded meeting. Nothing after that date has been observed.

### 9.3 The two parallel projects

#### 9.3.1 Side by side

**This is the canonical side-by-side, and the only complete one.** Chapter 3, The scientific problem and why it matters, §3.6 owns the *scientific* relationship between the two projects — why one specimen produces both problems at once, and what the older project hands the newer — and states one qualifier this table does not: `octreg v1` is prior-*optional* rather than prior-free, because the PI has a position prior in practice. Chapter 2, Orientation and glossary, §A.2 carries only a name-and-metric decoder, for telling which project a term or a number belongs to. Neither of them repeats the rows below; add new comparison rows here.

| | **(a) LSFM / SVR reconstruction** (older) | **(b) Cross-modality registration** (newer) |
|---|---|---|
| Lead | Lavanya Kotha, since 2026-06-02 | Yuntian Yang, since 2026-07-24 |
| Advisor | Aarya Bhave | Aarya Bhave (cross-cutting) |
| Members | Jotiraditya, Zidan, (Debangi historically), Aarya | Gunatit (confirmed aloud), Rajdeep (confirmed 08-07, second-hand), Debangi (proposed only), Aroush (contested) |
| Input | Single-axis, anisotropic LSFM serial sections with inter-slice deformation (I45, then I48) | Partial 3D OCT tissue-block volume + whole-hemisphere ex-vivo MRI |
| Core problem | Slice-to-volume: per-slice deformation, sparse-axis recovery, propagating the same deformation onto discrete cortical-layer labels, evaluation without isotropic ground truth | Partial-to-whole cross-modality 3D registration: find where the block sits in the hemisphere and recover an anatomically plausible OCT→MRI transform |
| Method state | Candidates converged to **joint deformation** and **joint deformation + NIIV**; the team's *visual* preference is joint-deformation-only; NeSVoR abandoned for the single-axis case | `octreg v1`: label-free, training-free, prior-free — two-class WM/GM structure maps on both sides → mirror-aware FFT global search → coarse-to-fine affine → vessel-density channel |
| Numbers on record | 08-23: DSC ≈ 0.99, PSNR 20.5 → 43.7, SSIM > 0.807, NCC 0.95 → 0.99, HD95 0.1227 → 12.3535 (broken) | 08-23: Dice ≈ 0.80 on Costantini, against the dataset's own manual segmentation |
| Venue | Undecided — conference or an established journal; *Imaging Neuroscience* named as an example | Tentatively a **top journal**; judged the higher-impact of the two |
| Status verdict to use | "Candidates converged; I48 validation and wrap-up not closed; metrics now exist but their credibility is being self-audited; HD95 unresolved" | "v1 runs end-to-end and is validated on public data; no result yet on our own data; method constraints (no labels, position prior exists) now fixed by the PI" |

#### 9.3.2 How the two relate

- **The split was the PI's idea and predates the new project by seven weeks.** On 2026-06-02 in Slack, Xiangrui proposed dividing the team into (1) wrapping up slice-to-volume reconstruction and (2) cross-modality 3D registration. Lavanya was named lead of (1) the same day.
- **2026-06-26 made the split concrete in method terms.** NeSVoR was judged unsuitable for a single-axis LSFM stack — it was designed for multiple differently-oriented stacks — *but was explicitly reserved for the follow-up project*, where OCT and MRI supply genuinely different stacks and reference volumes. On the same day the PI said both workstreams could become separate papers.
- **2026-07-24 turned the split into an org chart.** Yuntian leads (b), Lavanya wraps up (a), Aarya bridges, students are allocated.
- **The full chain is LSFM → OCT → MRI, and Yuntian owns the OCT→MRI segment** (08-07, per `WORKSPACE_STATE.md` §2.2, and stated in memory). The reconstruction project's output — a reconstructed LSFM volume — is the eventual moving image for the *other* segment of the chain, not for OCT→MRI.
- **(a) is a prerequisite asset for (b) in three ways** (`meeting_ground_truth.md` §1.3): it supplies reconstructed volumes that can enter 3D registration; it has already exposed the failure modes — pairwise drift, non-uniform physical space, provenance accidents — that (b) must avoid from day one; and it supplies the layer labels, Dice and boundary metrics and the biological-credibility principle that (b) should inherit as a validation philosophy.
- **Do not assume (b)'s input must pass through (a)'s pipeline.** OCT is already a volume.
- **2026-08-23 was the first time both lines presented in the same session.**

#### 9.5.2 The reconstruction project's status as reported, and the metric-leakage self-check

Lavanya presented the first quantitative table the reconstruction project has produced. The reason it belongs in this handoff is not the numbers — they are not our numbers — but the self-audit she volunteered, which applies verbatim to our own evaluation.

| Metric | Before | After | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| DSC | — | heard as `3.9907` | Almost certainly `0.9907`, and quoted for the **joint-deformation + NIIV** variant specifically. "Segmentation overlap is extremely high compared with I48" |
| PSNR | ~20.5 | ~43.7 | She described this aloud as "an 11.2 dB improvement", but the before/after she quoted in the same sentence differ by 23.2 dB. One of the three numbers is wrong. She flagged a separate caveat herself: PSNR depends on the intensity-range normalization / maximum intensity used |
| SSIM | 0.807 | improved, unspecified | "I would not describe it as perfect" |
| NCC | 0.95 | 0.99 | See the leakage caveat below |
| **HD95** | 0.1227 | 12.3535 | **The one clear failure — two orders of magnitude worse.** Suspected on the spot to be a decimal-point error, possibly `0.1235`. She said aloud "the jump is something around 12.215, so HD95 becomes about 89 times larger", and the Chinese minutes repeat the 89× (`meeting_recordings/meeting_notes/2026-08-23_meeting_notes.md`); the ratio of the two quoted numbers is in fact 100.7, so at least one of the three figures is wrong, which is exactly why action item A1 exists |

The transcript source itself warns that **the numbers Lavanya spoke are internally inconsistent and must not be quoted without re-listening or checking her slides.** Treat the whole row set as provisional.

Two self-audits she raised unprompted:

1. **Possible evaluation leakage.** If NCC is that close to 1, check whether the same images are being used for both registration and evaluation. In her words, if the model is optimized directly on the same data on which the metrics are reported, the metrics may look artificially strong.
2. **PSNR normalization dependence**, above.

**Why this is in our chapter and not only in hers.** `octreg` has the same structural hazard, and a successor must be able to answer the question before a reviewer or the PI asks it.

| Where leakage could bite us | Actual status |
|---|---|
| The final refinement optimizes a masked NCC between the two structure maps. **Reporting that NCC as a result would be reporting the objective value, not an independent measurement** | Known. The headline number reported on 08-23 is Dice against the dataset's own manual segmentation, not the objective |
| The Dice ≈ 0.80 on Costantini uses manual segmentations that **v1 never touches during fitting** — the pipeline is label-free end to end, labels enter only at evaluation time (`octreg/README.md` preamble) | This is the strongest thing we have: the label channel is genuinely held out by construction, not by discipline |
| The vessel evaluation could have been circular if the manual MRI vessel label were also the registration channel | Checked at file level and it is not. `mri_vessels.npy` is the **manual MRI vessel label**, loaded from `--mri-vessels …label-vessels_dseg.nii.gz`, thresholded `> 0`, and used for **evaluation only** (`octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py` docstring line 8, lines 95–97). The dark-blob map the registration actually uses is `vascular.mri_dark_channel`, computed in RAM inside `register.py` and never written to disk. Several earlier project write-ups describe `mri_vessels.npy` as the dark-blob map; that description is wrong and would have made the vessel evaluation look circular. The per-file inventory that settles it is in chapter 10, State of play: where everything is |
| Restart consistency (e.g. 12/12 or 10/12 restarts converging) measures **self-consistency, not accuracy** | Must be labelled as such wherever it is reported. Two of the tightest-converging DANDI runs, I58 and I61 at 12/12, are among the wrong ones |
| The objective and the label metric demonstrably disagree along the depth axis: the NCC argmax over a depth-scale sweep sits at s = 1.075 on a 0.021-wide plateau, while manual-label Dice peaks at s = 1.100 | This is direct internal evidence that our own objective is not a proxy for accuracy, and it is a good thing to be able to say out loud |

The honest general rule, and the one the 08-23 minutes draw explicitly: **every number we publish must state which data participated in fitting and which only in scoring.**

**Ground-truth discussion.** Lavanya named two stronger sources previously suggested by Xiangrui in the channel: **manually annotated real slices**, strongest for slice-level reconstruction, and **OCT volumes of the same tissue block**, an independent volumetric reference. Xiangrui added that **I48 has manually labelled layers**, that the **NIH share link holds I48 layer masks and corrected MIPs**, that he believes Yuntian already downloaded those layer masks, and that the evaluation idea is that **Dice between adjacent slices after registration should be large**.

**Xiangrui's one concrete ask to the reconstruction side:** "For the result you think is your best reconstruction, please share the location of the file so I can open it in Freeview and take a look." This is the operational form of his preference for visual checking, and it dictates the shape of every deliverable in both projects — see §9.7.

#### 9.5.4 The registration report

Yuntian opened by saying he had **only got access to the I58 data the day before** and had not processed it yet — the concrete trace of the permissions problem recorded under B1 in §9.7.2 — and then presented `octreg v1` as four steps, matching `octreg/README.md` §1:

1. **Structure maps.** Both modalities are reduced to the same two-class picture, white matter versus gray matter. On the OCT side each slice is normalized by its own tissue median to remove the serial-sectioning depth sawtooth, and contrast is restored with a running average over one section period.
2. **Global search.** Masked correlation of the two class maps, scored only inside the block mask so that intensity scale is irrelevant. For one fixed orientation every translation is a single FFT, so the search can be exhaustive. As presented: **8,000 orientations, each tested normal and mirrored, and a whole hemisphere takes about 150 s.**
3. **Coarse-to-fine affine refinement**, opening degrees of freedom slowly: rotation and translation → one global scale → full affine with shears constrained.
4. **Vessels.** MRI vessels are dark spots; OCT vessels are segmented with a Frangi filter on the raw stack. Correlating them finishes the job and is **the only thing that can fix the scale along the block's depth axis**, because tissue shape carries no information in that direction.

Reported result: **Dice ≈ 0.80** on the Costantini data, against the dataset's own manual segmentation. The figure convention was stated: block location in the hemisphere, raw OCT, MRI resampled into the same plane by the transform, checkerboard, MRI edges drawn on OCT.

**Correction to the runtime figure quoted in that meeting.** The "about 150 s" is a rounding of a real measurement of 153.4 s / 153.7 s, but that measurement comes from `octreg/scripts/run_demo_i46.py --features mixed`, whose MRI channels are the **trained 3D-U-Net parser's probabilities** — i.e. it is not the label-free path — and it was measured on a separate prep directory `work/i46`. The label-free `register.py --features otsu` cost for the identical subject and grid is **298.9 s**, and **597.8 s** with the `--oct-wm-bright auto` that every DANDI run used, because that flag runs the search once per class polarity. Whole-corpus single-branch range is **44.8 s – 1,010.3 s**; the per-branch timings behind those figures are tabulated in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means. One further trap: some project notes call the older `WORKSPACE_STATE.md` §0.5 figures (4,000 rotations, 76 s) "superseded" by the meeting's figures. They are not superseded — 76.7 s at `n_rot 4000` (8,000 orientations) and 153.7 s at `n_rot 8000` (16,000 orientations) are the **same code at half and full orientation count**, exactly 2×. Do not repeat "150 s for a whole hemisphere" as a property of the label-free pipeline in any outward-facing text.

**Two disclosures Yuntian made in public**, both of which a successor inherits:

- **"Because I am not sure what kind of manual labels our own data will have, what I built is a simple method that does not rely on manual labels."** This pre-empted Constraint 1 by a few minutes and is why the PI's answer reads as confirmation rather than redirection.
- **"Because I only have my laptop right now, and I go back to Boston next week where I can use my PC, and my laptop storage is limited, I cannot download the data locally and visualize it myself. So I had Claude Code produce the visualizations. I am not sure they are 100 percent precise, but I will check after I get back to Boston."** This is on the record and was not hidden. But it means the PI's "looks pretty good" rests on figures no human has yet verified. Action item A7 closes this; until it does, the PI's approval is not independent confirmation of the result.

PI reaction: he asked **"Have you applied it to I58, the brainstem one I showed you?"**, was told not yet — which is where action item A6 comes from — then asked whether the figures came from 3D or 2D data, was told 3D, and said **"That looks pretty good."** He also asked how the Dice was obtained and confirmed that the public dataset ships manual segmentation.

#### 9.5.5 Constraint 1 — labels are scarce, and visual checking is preferred during development

The exchange, in order:

> **Yuntian:** "I have a question. What kind of manual labels do we have for the data we will process?"
> **Xiangrui:** "For the brainstem, honestly I do not know. I will check. On the brainstem there are a lot of structures, and different projects label different histological structures, so I will check.
> But for now, maybe we do not need to rely on that score. We can check manually. For example the figures you just showed, even looking at them visually they look pretty good. You do not need to rely on that score, because manual labels also have inaccuracies in them. Although for a paper we need some quantitative results, during development I usually prefer to just check visually whether things look right."
> **Yuntian:** "So for now my approach relies on no labels. We should design the method so that it relies on no labels, right? We cannot use any method that relies on labels."
> **Xiangrui:** "We do have a lot of scans and volumes, but we do not have many labels."

**What it means:**

| Implication | Detail |
|---|---|
| **The label-free design is confirmed correct, not over-engineered** | v1 uses no manual labels anywhere in the pipeline; annotations enter only at evaluation time (`octreg/README.md` preamble). "Many scans, few labels" makes label-freeness a match to the real operating constraint rather than an aesthetic choice |
| **Any method that needs labels for *training* is out** | Not just fine-tuning on labels — a supervised parser, a label-driven loss, or a learned descriptor requiring paired annotations all fail at scale. The 3D U-Net parser in `octreg` (`--features parser`) survives only as an ablation, because v1 ships the training-free Otsu path |
| **Dice is not the iteration signal during development** | The PI explicitly discounts it because manual labels carry their own error. Optimizing against Dice on the few labelled subjects would fit annotation error |
| **Quantitative results are still mandatory for the paper** | "Although for a paper we need some quantitative results." This is a two-track requirement |
| **So the evaluation must be split in two** | Development loop: QC overlays, checkerboards, edge overlays, restart consistency. Paper: a defensible quantitative protocol with an explicit statement of which data were used to fit and which only to score. `octreg/TALK_2026-08-21.md` already carries the proposed answer for unlabelled data — ask for ~20 matched anatomical points on both sides, roughly 30 minutes of annotation, and report target registration error |
| **Lavanya's leakage self-audit generalizes to us** | The 08-23 minutes draw this link explicitly. See §9.5.2 |
| **What labels exist on the brainstem is an open question the PI owns** | He did not know and committed to checking (A9). Do not design an evaluation that assumes brainstem labels exist |

**What it does NOT mean:**

| Misreading | Why it is wrong |
|---|---|
| "We do not need metrics" | He said the opposite in the same breath: for a paper, quantitative results are required. He is ranking the *development* signal, not abolishing evaluation |
| "Drop the Dice ≈ 0.80 result" | Keep it. Costantini ships manual segmentation, the PI asked how the Dice was obtained and accepted the answer. It is the one clean held-out number the project has. The instruction is not to *optimize* against it |
| "Eyeballing is enough" | His visual check is a specific operational act: he opens a NIfTI pair in Freeview himself. The deliverable that satisfies this constraint is a server-resident, openable volume plus reproducible QC overlays — not a screenshot, not a video, not a slide |
| "Labels never exist, so any label-based comparison is unavailable forever" | Labels exist on the public data and possibly on some of ours; A9 is open. The constraint is about what the *method* may depend on, not about what evaluation may use |
| "The label-free property is now a non-issue since we have no labels anyway" | Backwards. Scarcity of labels is what makes label-freeness valuable. After the repositioning forced by Constraint 2, it is the surviving half of the novelty claim |
| "We can quietly use the trained parser because it works better" | The parser was trained on labels. Shipping it as the default would reintroduce exactly the dependency the constraint rules out. It stays an ablation, and any runtime or accuracy figure taken from a parser run must be labelled as such — see the 150 s / 299 s correction in §9.5.4 |
| "Visual checking replaces the leakage discipline" | Unrelated axes. A visually convincing overlay produced by a metric computed on the fitting data is still not evidence |

#### 9.5.6 Constraint 2 — a position prior IS available, so whole-hemisphere global search is not required

> **Yuntian:** "Understood. So we also do not have prior knowledge of where the OCT block is located?"
> **Xiangrui:** "We do have prior knowledge of where it might be."
> **Yuntian:** "So we do not need to do a global search over the whole hemisphere of the MRI?"
> **Xiangrui:** "We do not. We know where it is, so we can crop a small part there. And the I58 data I shared with you is already cropped. You can take a look."

**What it means:**

| Implication | Detail |
|---|---|
| **The headline claim of v1 has to be repositioned** | v1's differentiator versus Costantini was stated as removing two requirements: hand-drawn GM/WM/vessel segmentations *and* the pre-cropped MRI (`octreg/TALK_2026-08-21.md`, "What is new"). The PI has just said the crop is available in practice. The annotation half of the claim survives untouched; **the crop half no longer describes a real operational need** |
| **Global search becomes robustness insurance and a paper capability, not the value proposition** | The explicit conclusion of the 08-23 minutes: 整半球无先验搜索…不是必需功能，而是一个稳健性保险和一个可以写进论文的能力 |
| **The everyday path is the cropped path, and it already exists in the code** | `octreg/scripts/register.py` accepts `--crop-centre x,y,z --crop-half-mm 30` (default `crop_half_mm = 30.0`), registering against a ±30 mm box of the MRI around a given world point. The same flags exist in `scripts/diag_candidates.py` and `scripts/run_demo_i46.py`. Runs `crop_final2`, `crop_parser_v1` and `crop_mixed_v2` used it |
| **v1 has already proved the two paths agree** | On Costantini sub-I46 the cropped scenario and the prior-free whole-hemisphere scenario converged to the same solution: block centre `(−6.1, 25.7, 8.3)` mm, **mirrored** chirality, GM/WM Dice 0.80/0.83 (`WORKSPACE_STATE.md` §0.5). That is exactly the evidence needed to say "if you give a prior we use it, if you do not we can still find it" |
| **The next version's narrative should be conditional, not absolutist** | Minutes: 下一版应把"给了先验就用先验、没给就全局搜"讲清楚，而不是把全局搜索当作唯一卖点 |
| **I58 is already cropped** | The MRI he shared is a box-crop of a whole brain: 0.08 mm, `(343, 489, 495)` ≈ 27 × 39 × 40 mm, against a 20 µm OCT NIfTI `(1457, 2013, 1595)` ≈ 29 × 40 × 32 mm. Do not build an I58 experiment that pretends to search a hemisphere |
| **What the prior actually *is* remains unspecified** | Region label, cutting record, coordinate range, or a manual ROI — never stated. Ask before designing a prior-conditioned search radius |
| **Genuine remaining novelty after the reposition** | (i) no manual GM/WM/vessel segmentations on either side; (ii) automatic resolution of class polarity — which class is WM — and of stack chirality, both of which flip subject to subject; 6 of 9 DANDI subjects came out mirrored (I38, I46, I48, I56, I58, I62; not I55, I57, I61, nor either brainstem run); (iii) the vessel-density channel recovering the depth-axis scale that tissue geometry cannot see, landing automatically on the same figure Costantini obtained from hand-drawn vessels; (iv) prior-optional operation as robustness |

On (iii), the numbers disagree across our own documents and must be settled before the paper: `TALK_2026-08-21.md` states their published affine has a 1.17 depth scale and that we reproduce it, while `octreg/README.md` §4 quotes their affine's singular values as 1.21/1.04/0.98 and our measured stretch as 1.14–1.22. The pipeline's own recovered value for I46 is **1.219** and the sidecar-versus-siblings ratio is **14/12 = 1.167**; the "~1.18 true depth scale" that circulates in the prose has **no artefact behind it** and is marked `[UNVERIFIED]` in chapter 8, How this compares to the published method, which also holds the full reconciliation of these numbers against Costantini's published affine. Decide which number goes into the paper.

**What it does NOT mean:**

| Misreading | Why it is wrong |
|---|---|
| "Delete the global search" | It is the fallback when a prior is missing or wrong, it is the evidence that the cropped answer is not an artefact of the crop, and it is a legitimate paper capability. Keeping it costs nothing operationally because the cropped path is a flag away |
| "The PI reversed a previous position" | He did not. On 07-24 he had already said "We will need some prior knowledge of where the tissue came from in order to navigate it", and the 08-07 plan had already been narrowed to "refinement inside a known region + limited-range pose search". The prior-free v1 built in mid-August is the deviation from the stated line, not the other way round |
| "We know where the block is, so the problem is easy now" | The crop removes one search dimension. Inside the crop the hard parts remain: cross-modality contrast with no shared intensity relationship, unknown class polarity, unknown chirality, and a depth-axis scale that tissue shape cannot constrain at all. On I58 the coarse pose is already correct — 10 of 12 restarts, no mirror — and the residual is still several millimetres, larger at the deep end |
| "The prior gives us orientation too" | It gives *position*, in the loose sense of "where it might be". Nothing in the exchange constrains pose or chirality. The mirror-aware search is still doing real work |
| "Write the prior up as an ROI or a set of coordinates" | Explicitly forbidden by `meeting_ground_truth.md` §12 item 9: the rough anatomical origin must not be presented as a precise ROI or coordinates. We do not know what form it takes |
| "So the position-prior question is closed" | The opposite, and it is the single most consequential open question on our side: what the prior *is* determines whether the cropped path needs a search radius, an orientation prior, both, or neither. Ask Xiangrui before designing around it. It is carried as Q1 in chapter 12, Open questions and unverified claims |
| "Costantini's crop requirement was never a real limitation" | For *their* pipeline it was still a manual step. The change is that our lab can supply the crop cheaply, so removing it is not a differentiator **for us**. That is a positioning fact, not a statement about the prior art |

| **Simple baseline first, innovation after** | 08-07 decision 2 | Do not lead with a new architecture |
| **Start on the reference paper's own data** | 08-07 decision 4 | Costantini / DANDI:000026 first, own data second |
| **Downsample for initial experiments, full resolution only at the end** | 08-23; also 06-26 (1/8 per dimension) and 07-24 (halve each axis, learn the deformation, upsample the deformation) | |
| **Generated tissue is never biological evidence** | 07-10, at length | Synthesis may be used for augmentation or pretraining, but every final correspondence, transform and quantitative claim must come from real OCT/MRI |
| **Provenance must travel with every output** | The 07-10 report request; the `reconstruction1` NeSVoR/joint mislabel; the Calretinin/NeuN filename error | Every artifact records input, stain/subject, commit, config, checkpoint, shape/spacing/affine, owner, server path |
| **One shared copy of a dataset on the server** | Slack 06-27 (I48) | No per-user duplicates |
| **Post next steps and discussion in the channel** | The 07-24 standing instruction to Lavanya; the 08-23 closing "post it in the channel" | Between meetings the channel is the interface, not DMs |

## 10. State of play: where everything is

Three machines hold this project, and they hold different halves of it. All compute and all data live
on a **rented AutoDL GPU container in China** whose SSH endpoint changes every time it restarts. The
source data for the lab's own brainstem pair lives on **xulab**, a CMU cluster, inside the PI's
read-only account. Every document, and the only human-readable write-up of the method, lives on
**Yuntian's Mac** and nowhere else. Nothing anywhere is under version control.

Everything in this chapter was verified live against the primary artefacts — the AutoDL box, the xulab
account, and the Mac tree — on **2026-08-23**, and the AutoDL endpoint, the GPU state, the script
inventory and every number quoted here out of `prep.json` and `result.json` were re-confirmed on
**2026-08-24**. Where an earlier working note disagreed with that verification, the verified value is
the one printed here. Items that were measured once and not re-run for this document carry
`[NOT RE-MEASURED]`; items still unresolved carry `[OPEN]`.

#### 10.1.1 The host:port problem, and the recovery procedure (verbatim)

This is the single most common way to lose an hour on this project, so it is reproduced verbatim from
the verified server notes rather than paraphrased.

> ### The host:port problem
>
> `connect.westb.seetacloud.com:49018` is valid **only for the current instance session**. AutoDL
> reassigns host and port on every shutdown/restart.
>
> Get the new endpoint from the AutoDL console:
> https://www.autodl.com/console/instance/list → the instance row → "SSH登录指令" (copy button). It has
> the form `ssh -p <PORT> root@<HOST>`.
>
> Then:
> ```bash
> ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o BatchMode=yes -p <NEWPORT> root@<NEWHOST>
> ```
> `accept-new` is needed because the new host:port has a new entry in `~/.ssh/known_hosts`.
>
> Auth is already set up and survives restarts: `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` on the box contains two
> keys —
> - `ssh-rsa ... yyttim021120@gmail.com` (matches `/Users/yyttim/.ssh/id_rsa` on the Mac)
> - `ssh-ed25519 ... xulab-to-autodl` (matches
>   `/shared/scratch/0/home/v_yuntian_yang/registration/keys/autodl_ed25519` on xulab)
>
> `/root` is on the persistent system disk, so nothing needs re-adding.
>
> **Stale endpoints to ignore.** `/Users/yyttim/.ssh/config` contains two dead AutoDL hosts:
> ```
> Host connect.bjb1.seetacloud.com   Port 57039   User root
> Host connect.westc.gpuhub.com      Port 23040   User root
> ```
> The current endpoint is not in that file. Consider adding it (or don't — it goes stale again).
>
> **Also update on xulab** — four scripts hardcode `-p 49018` and `connect.westb.seetacloud.com`:
> ```
> /shared/scratch/0/home/v_yuntian_yang/registration/push_to_autodl.sh
> /shared/scratch/0/home/v_yuntian_yang/registration/xulab_push_parallel.sh
> /shared/scratch/0/home/v_yuntian_yang/registration/xulab_push_seg.sh
> /shared/scratch/0/home/v_yuntian_yang/registration/xulab_speedtest.sh
> ```
>
> ### Sanity check after reconnecting
>
> ```bash
> ssh -p <NEWPORT> root@<NEWHOST> 'bash -lc "
>   source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate octmri
>   cd ~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration && pwd
>   nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
>   python -c \"import torch,numpy,nibabel,tifffile,skimage;print(torch.__version__,torch.cuda.is_available(),torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))\"
>   df -h /root/autodl-tmp | tail -1
>   ls work/runs/summary_all/
> "'
> ```
>
> Or in one step from the Mac: `bash ~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration/setup_autodl_octmri.sh status`
> on the box.

Before concluding the endpoint has changed, probe every endpoint the project has ever used in one
shot — a wedged sshd looks the same as a moved instance from the outside, and they need different
responses:

```bash
for hp in "connect.westb.seetacloud.com 49018" "connect.bjb1.seetacloud.com 57039" "connect.westc.gpuhub.com 23040"; do
  set -- $hp
  printf '%-38s :%-6s ' "$1" "$2"
  ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -p "$2" "root@$1" \
      'echo OK $(hostname)' 2>/dev/null || echo "UNREACHABLE"
done
```

If all three are unreachable you cannot recover the endpoint yourself — the console requires Yuntian's
login `[UNVERIFIED]` — not reachable from an agent session. The message to send him, in Chinese per his
preference:

> AutoDL 实例连不上了。麻烦到 autodl.com 控制台 → 容器实例，看一下实例是不是关机了；如果是就开机，然后把"登录指令"里的
> `ssh -p <端口> root@<主机>` 整条复制给我。数据都在 `~/autodl-tmp`，不会丢。

Two distinct failure causes, because they need different responses:

| Cause | Symptom | Response |
|---|---|---|
| **A — instance stopped and restarted** | connection refused on the old host:port | get the new endpoint from the console; `~/autodl-tmp` is a persistent 1.5 TB disk, so a stop/start loses nothing |
| **B — instance up but sshd wedged** | SSH hangs or times out, but running jobs keep making progress (logs keep growing once you get back in) | restart from the console (jobs die, `work/` survives, re-run the driver), or wait — the first incident cleared itself after **7.5 h** |

Cause B has happened **twice** (2026-08-20 ~02:00 and ~12:26), both times within minutes of launching
**two heavy jobs in parallel**, and the root cause is the 62 GiB container memory cap. Hence the rule
in §10.3.

### 10.3 The environment, and how to confirm the GPU works

There are exactly two conda envs on AutoDL. Use the right one:

```
conda root : /root/miniconda3          (base env is python 3.8 / torch 1.10 — TOO OLD for the RTX 4090, do not use)
project env: /root/miniconda3/envs/octmri   (the only other env)
python     : Python 3.10.20   at /root/miniconda3/envs/octmri/bin/python
```

The activation preamble, exactly as every driver script in the repo does it:

```bash
source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate octmri
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=8
cd ~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration
```

`conda` is not on the default non-login `PATH`, so a bare `ssh host 'python …'` fails with
`bash: python: command not found`. `python3` is not on PATH either — after activating use `python`, or
the absolute `/root/miniconda3/envs/octmri/bin/python`.

Verified package versions (by import, 2026-08-23):

|---|---|---|
| python | 3.10.20 | |
| torch | 2.1.2+cu121 | `torch.version.cuda` 12.1, cudnn 8902, `cuda.is_available()` True, device `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090` |
| torchvision | 0.16.2 | |
| triton | 2.1.0 | |
| numpy | 1.26.4 | **pinned `<2`** — torch 2.1.2 was built against numpy 1.x. Do not let a `pip install` upgrade it |
| scipy | 1.15.3 | |
| nibabel | 5.4.2 | |

Deliberately **absent**, confirmed by `ModuleNotFoundError`: `sklearn`, `pandas`, `zarr`, `dask`,
`h5py`, `numcodecs`, `ants`/`antspyx`, `cupy`, `numba`, `joblib`, `cv2`, `dandi`. If a new script needs
one, install it — it is not there today, and its absence is a design fact, not an oversight: the method
deliberately depends on nothing but torch, numpy, scipy and skimage.

The driver reports CUDA 13.2 while torch ships its own CUDA 12.1 runtime. That mismatch is fine and
expected.

Rebuilding from scratch: `bash setup_autodl_octmri.sh` does the whole thing and is idempotent;
`bash setup_autodl_octmri.sh status` prints download progress plus an import check. Its essential steps
are `conda create -n octmri python=3.10`, `pip install torch==2.1.2 torchvision==0.16.2`, then
`"numpy<2" nibabel tifffile imagecodecs scipy scikit-image SimpleITK matplotlib tqdm pyyaml
torch-interpol`, then `PROJECT_ROOT=$TARGET ./download_costantini.sh code` to obtain the authors' repo
(which is where `external/nitorch` comes from), then
`NI_COMPILED_BACKEND=TS pip install --no-build-isolation -e "$TARGET/code/costantini/biccn-broca-I46/external/nitorch"`.
The conda channel list in `~/.condarc` points at the Tsinghua tuna mirror, whose mirror of the
`defaults` channel 404s — the setup script works around that with `--override-channels -c conda-forge`.
If the GitHub clone fails, it retries under AutoDL's proxy (`source /etc/network_turbo`);
`install_singbox.sh` is a second network workaround.

that wrote it** — the copy used to produce the output below was written to an agent scratchpad. Rebuild
it from the eight numbered steps in the table further down (each is two or three lines), and save it
into `octreg/scripts/` so it survives. Then install and run:

```bash

ssh -p 49018 root@connect.westb.seetacloud.com \
  'source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate octmri && cd ~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration && python /tmp/octreg_smoke.py'
```

Verified expected output (2026-08-23):

```
[1] torch 2.1.2+cu121 cuda 12.1 available True
    gpu NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 free/total GiB 23.1 / 23.5
[2] all octreg modules import OK, DEVICE = cuda
[3] GPU cuFFT roundtrip max|err| = 2.15e-06
[4] scipy 1.15.3 skimage 0.25.2 nibabel 5.4.2 tifffile 2025.5.10
[5] work/I46 oct150 (49, 100, 97) voxel mm [0.15, 0.15, 0.15] tissue frac 0.424
[6] I46_otsu det -1.2277 mirror True final_ncc 0.756 centre mm [-5.5, 25.9, 8.5]
[7] otsu_two_class on the real block: thr 103.54 class means [0.547, 0.453]
[8] Refiner self-NCC at identity [1.0, 1.0] (must be ~[1.0, 1.0])
SMOKE OK in 3.2s
```

Each step exists to rule out one specific way this project silently breaks:

| Step | Rules out |
|---|---|
| [1] | wrong conda env, or the instance has no GPU attached |
| [2] | the `octreg` package is broken or a module was moved |
| [3] | cuFFT is unusable — this would silently break the entire global search, which is an FFT cross-correlation |
| [4] | a missing I/O dependency |
| [5] | the `work/I46` cache was deleted or truncated |
| [6] | the reference run's transform or JSON changed under you; also confirms mirror detection still fires |
| [7] | the two-class split still runs on real data and produces balanced classes |
| [8] | the `Refiner` masked-NCC path is numerically sane |

A deeper synthetic check exists — `scripts/selftest_search.py` cuts a block out of the MRI features at
a known random pose and verifies the search + refine chain recovers it — but it needs a parser
directory, so on this box only I46 works, and its default `--n-rot 3000` is not free:
`python octreg/scripts/selftest_search.py --work work/I46 --parser work/parsers/I46 --n-rot 500 [--mirror]`
`[UNVERIFIED]` — not executed; runtime unmeasured. Check the GPU is idle first.

#### 10.3.3 The machine limit that dictates how you run jobs

`nproc` says 224 and `free -g` says 503 GB. **Both are the host's numbers and both are wrong for you.**
The cgroup allows **16 CPUs and 62 GiB**. That ceiling is why two concurrent `prep_subject.py` /
`register.py` processes wedged the instance on 2026-08-20 — `prep_subject.py` on the I38 OCT alone
touches a 2.3 G-voxel stack.

**Hard rule: one heavy job at a time.** `run_all.sh` carries the comment *"Sequential multi-subject
driver (one heavy job at a time: the instance froze once with two running)"*. Every one of
`dedup_recover.sh`, `recover_serial.sh`, `recover_serial_dandi.sh`, `rx2.sh`, `rx3.sh` exists because of
that single incident. Launch long jobs detached so an SSH drop does not kill them:

```bash
(nohup setsid bash octreg/scripts/<driver>.sh > logs/<name>.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &)
```

Two more operational landmines, both already stepped on twice:

1. **Never put `pkill -f <pattern>` in an `ssh` command line.** The pattern matches the ssh command's
   own argv on the remote side and kills your own session. The safe form is in `rx3.sh`: `pgrep -f`
   into a `kill` loop, run from a script *file* on the server.
2. **DANDI pre-signed download URLs expire after 6 h.** `data/dl_watchdog.sh` restarts aria2 every
   5400 s while any `*.aria2` remains. Irrelevant unless you are re-downloading.

### 10.4 Condensed quickstart: looking at a real result in five minutes

The point of this subsection is that you should look at a finished registration **before** you read any
code. The curated inspection folder `results_inspection/` is 6.1 GB, but almost all of that is NIfTI
volumes. Pull only the small stuff — verified at **21 MB in 3.2 s**:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/octreg_inspect
rsync -az -e 'ssh -p 49018' \
  --include='*/' --include='qc_*.png' --include='result.json' --include='INDEX.md' --exclude='*' \
  root@connect.westb.seetacloud.com:autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration/results_inspection/ \
  ~/octreg_inspect/
open ~/octreg_inspect/INDEX.md                    # per-run verdict table
open ~/octreg_inspect/I46_otsu/qc_vessels.png     # the reference GOOD result
open ~/octreg_inspect/I61_otsu/qc_vessels.png     # the reference WRONG result
```

There is **no NIfTI viewer on this Mac** — `freeview`, `itksnap` and `fsleyes` are all absent and there
is no ITK-SNAP in `/Applications`. The PNGs are the fast path; installing a viewer is a more-than-five-
minute detour. The Mac's `/opt/anaconda3/bin/python3` does have `nibabel 5.3.2` if you need to poke at
a volume numerically.

**What `qc_vessels.png` shows** (from `scripts/viz_result.py`): three rows are OCT depth slices at
20 %, 50 % and 80 % of the block depth; three columns are

| column | content |
|---|---|
| left | raw OCT slice + **green/lime** = our own Frangi vessel density contour (`>0.35`) + **cyan** = OCT WM/GM class boundary |
| middle | MRI resampled into the OCT frame via `T_oct2mri_structural.npy` (before the vascular stage), same green/cyan overlays + **yellow** = manual MRI vessel label + thin **white** OCT block outline |
| right | the same, via the final `T_oct2mri.npy` (after the vascular stage) |

The suptitle carries `search top1/top2`, `mirror`, `stretch ijk` — read that line first.

**What "good" looks like** (`I46_otsu/qc_vessels.png`): the cyan contour, which is derived purely from
the OCT, traces the MRI's *own* WM/GM boundary in the middle and right panels — bright WM gyral cores
inside the cyan loops, sulcal GM ribbon outside. That is the single most informative check, because
nothing about the cyan curve came from the MRI. The middle and right panels show real cortical folding
with the same gyral pattern as the left OCT panel; green vessel contours land on dark MRI spots; yellow
manual-vessel dots cluster on or beside green contours and visibly tighten from middle to right, which
is the vascular stage doing its job.

**What "wrong" looks like** (`I61_otsu/qc_vessels.png`): the left OCT panel is full of sharp cortical
folding while the middle and right MRI panels are flat featureless gray noise (bath fluid) or plain
black. An elaborate cyan contour is drawn over a region with no anatomy in it. `search top1/top2 =
0.517 / 0.511` — no margin.

Numeric acceptance criteria, from `result.json` and `work/runs/summary_all/summary.md`:

| quantity | good | reference values |
|---|---|---|
| `search.top1` vs `top2` | a visible margin | I46 0.7259 / 0.7039 (margin 0.0220, good) · I55 0.6112 / 0.6089 (0.0023, thin, still correct) · **I48 0.2571 / 0.2558 = margin 0.0013 → "uncertain"** |
| `refine.final_ncc` | **no absolute threshold works — see the note under the table** | I46 0.7564, I55 0.7456, I38 0.4779, I56 0.3661 — but I61 **0.5020** and I57 **0.5121** are both *wrong*, and I62 **0.2842** is *correct* |
| structural restarts converged | ≥ 9/12 | I46 9/12, I38 12/12, I55 9/12, brainstem 10/12 |
| `vessels_*.registered.median_um` | well below the random-shift control | I46 final 167 µm vs control 352 µm |
| `frac_within_150um` (f150) | as high as the annotation ceiling (~0.47 on I46) | I46 0.28 → **0.47**; own-seg 0.56; I55 0.52 |
| Dice WM/GM vs manual labels | 0.8–0.93 **where labels cover the block** | I46 0.803 / 0.825, I55 0.921 / 0.930 |
| `stretch_ijk` | 0.9–1.25 | I46 **1.219** along the depth axis (recovers I46's wrong sidecar depth spacing); I55 **0.913** on the same axis — but read the I55 caveat below |

**Do not put an acceptance threshold on `refine.final_ncc`.** Some earlier notes quote one — "≥ about
0.35 for hemisphere runs" — and the counterexample is inside these same nine runs. The two subjects
judged wrong by eye score *above* it: I61 **0.5020** and I57 **0.5121**. The subject judged correct
scores *below* it: I62 **0.2842**. Absolute NCC measures how much texture two volumes happen to share,
which varies with flip angle, bath fraction and slab thickness, not whether the pose is right. It is
usable only to compare runs of the *same* pair against each other. Across subjects, the things that do
carry signal are the search margin, the restart scatter, and the figure.

**The I55 caveat on `stretch_ijk`.** I55 is the reverse control for I46's depth-spacing bug: its sidecar
depth spacing is right, so the pipeline should recover no depth correction, and the vascular stage moves
the block only 0.334 mm. But the structural stage's recovered depth/in-plane anisotropy on I55 is
**0.8570**, which is 6/7 to four decimal places — exactly the *inverse* of the 7/6 = 1.167 factor I46's
sidecar is supposed to be missing. That is either a coincidence or a sign that something in the scale
prior is pulling toward the same ratio in both directions; nobody has explained it `[OPEN]`. Quote I55
as a null result if you like, but never as an unqualified clean one. The full depth-scale argument is in
chapter 6, What we found, and what it means.

**Dice 0.0 or 0.25 is not automatically a failure — but that excuse only covers the large slabs.** I38,
I56 and I62 score low because the manual labels cover only part of a 30–50 mm slab; I62 has no
hemisphere labels at all, and its `prep.json` carries no `labels_wholehemi` key. Trust the picture over
the Dice for those three. **I48 is not one of them.** Its Dice is untrustworthy in *both* directions —
depressed where the labels miss the block, unearned where they hit it — and its "uncertain" verdict does
not rest on label coverage at all. It rests on the search-score margin of **0.0013** (0.2571 vs 0.2558),
the flattest landscape in the corpus: there is no answer in that score surface to believe. Do not lump
I48 in with the slab-coverage cases. The corresponding hard rule from `octreg/EXPLAINER_zh.md`:
**search margin < 0.01 ⇒ a human must look at the figure.**

The full verdict table, verbatim from `results_inspection/INDEX.md` (1 627 B, generated 2026-08-21
07:53 by the heredoc inside `octreg/scripts/build_inspection.sh`). It is reproduced verbatim because
that is exactly what a successor will find on the box — **but four of its cells need correction, and
each carries an italic note inline: I56's block size is wrong, I57's stated cause is not supported, and
the I48 and I61 cells need qualifying. Fix them in `build_inspection.sh`, never in `INDEX.md`**, or the
next run of the script reverts your edit (§10.9.2):

| run | verdict (visual QC) | note |
|---|---|---|
| I46_otsu | correct | full annotations; vessels 167 um / f150 0.47 (own seg 123/0.56), Dice 0.80/0.83, depth stretch 1.22 |
| I46_parser | correct | trained-parser comparison, same result as otsu |
| I55_otsu | correct | Dice 0.92/0.93; sidecar depth spacing correct -> vascular stage moves only 0.33 mm |
| I38_otsu | correct | 29x52x47 mm slab, gyrus-by-gyrus; labels cover 61% (low Dice is an artifact) |
| I56_otsu | correct | 33x49x44 mm slab *(**wrong** — the measured block is **9.8 × 45.2 × 43.0 mm**; INDEX.md's first axis is out by roughly 3×. It is a thin slab, not a cube)*, gyrus-by-gyrus; partial labels |
| I62_otsu | correct | no hemisphere labels (Dice 0 is an artifact) |
| I48_otsu | uncertain | no search margin (0.2571 vs 0.2558, margin 0.0013) — *this, not any label-coverage artefact, is the whole basis of the verdict* |
| I57_otsu | wrong | captured by a flat MRI region (two-piece slab) *— `[OPEN]`. That cell is a guess, not a diagnosis, and the tissue-mask story does **not** apply to I57: its threshold 15.771 sits above its own median 13.803, `tissue_fraction` is a healthy 0.209, and the histogram valley was found at 0.0631. **I57's failure currently has no confirmed explanation.*** |
| I61_otsu | wrong | MRI tissue mask failed (bath; mask frac 0.74) -> placed in noise *— checked and it holds for I61: `tissue_fraction` 0.742, `valley_ratio` null, so the peak-walk found no valley and fell back to the floor. The same route explains I58 (fraction 0.587, `n_peaks: 1`). It covers those two subjects and no others — in particular not I57.* |
| I58_otsu | wrong | only a 10-deg-flip MRI exists (almost no GM/WM contrast) |
| xiangrui_I58bs_novasc | coarse correct (reported) | brainstem pair; vascular stage off (seam artifacts); residual a few mm |
| xiangrui_I58bs | superseded | same but with the (harmful here) vascular stage; kept for comparison |

Once you have looked, the next reading is the cross-run numbers in
`work/runs/summary_all/summary.md` (2 253 B, 9 rows, one per `*_otsu` run;
`summary_final.md` beside it is byte-identical). Note the two `xiangrui_*` runs are **not** in that
table because `summarize.py` was last called with `--pattern "*_otsu"`; regenerate with
`python octreg/scripts/summarize.py --pattern "*"` to include them.

To run something yourself, the minimum is two commands plus a QC figure, and the wrapper does all
three:

```bash
bash octreg/scripts/run_subject.sh I38 flip-2          # prep-if-needed + otsu register + viz, one DANDI subject
```

Subject→flip mapping used by every driver, copy verbatim if you write a new one:

```
I46 flip-2   I38 flip-2   I55 flip-2   I56 flip-2   I62 flip-3
I57 flip-4   I61 flip-4   I48 flip-2   I58 flip-3
```

Expect **18.7 – 131.1 min** per DANDI subject on the 4090; budget 2.5 h for a large 30 µm slab. The
per-run and per-branch breakdown — search, each polarity trial, the vascular stage, the total — is the
canonical timing table in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means (§6.3.2); do not re-derive it.
Operationally what you need is that progress is visible in `logs/reg_<SUB>_otsu.log`, which prints
`[search] N/16000 orientations, best score …` every 4 000 orientations — **75 s per tick for I46, and
11 s (brainstem) to 254 s (I57) across the corpus**. The frequently quoted "~150 s per tick" is true
only of I58, so do not use it to decide whether a run has hung.

`path / asset_id / bytes / sha256`, retrieved `2026-08-17T17:39:00Z`, dandiset 000026 **draft**
version). All downloads are complete: `find data/costantini -name "*.aria2"` returns nothing. Note the
pinning caveat — asset UUIDs and sha256s pin the individual files, but the dandiset is pinned to the
**mutable `draft` version**, so the dandiset itself can change.
