#### 10.5.4 What is reclaimable, and what is not

If disk is ever needed, in order of safety: `results_inspection/` 6.1 G (it is a `cp -n` copy —
regenerate with `bash octreg/scripts/build_inspection.sh`), `work/i46` 6.8 G (superseded), the six
`work/parser_real*` / `work/parser_v1` dirs ~26 G (but see the symlink trap), the Aug-18/19
`work/runs/crop_*` and `whole_*` ablations ~1.7 G. `~/autodl-tmp/speedtest_{0..5}` are six
33 554 432 B leftovers from `xulab_speedtest.sh`.

What is **not** reclaimable and not reproducible on any sane budget: `work/` per-subject caches and run
outputs represent weeks of GPU time, and `octreg/` (4.2 M) plus `logs/` (656 K) are the single copy of
the science. That asymmetry is the whole subject of §10.10.

### 10.6 The code map

Read `octreg/{common,features,search,refine,vascular}.py` and
`scripts/{prep_subject,register,viz_result,summarize}.py`. **That is the entire v1 method.** Everything
else is an optional parser ablation, I46 validation evidence, or dead.

#### 10.6.1 The package — `octreg/octreg/`, 10 modules

Shared conventions, true in every module: a volume is a torch tensor `[C, D, H, W]` (or numpy
`[D, H, W]`) plus a 4×4 affine mapping voxel index `(i,j,k)` to **world millimetres**; NIfTI arrays are
kept in `(i,j,k)` order with `img.affine` verbatim, no transposition; every inter-volume transform is a
4×4 **world → world** matrix in mm; `sample_at_world` is the single sampling primitive that search,
refinement, evaluation, output resampling and QC all go through; `DEVICE` is a module-level global in
`common.py` imported by everything.

| module | what it is | when you open it |
|---|---|---|
| `__init__.py` | version string + module map docstring, `__version__ = "0.1.0"` | never, except to bump the version |
| `common.py` (328 lines) | affines, world↔voxel resampling, pooling, OCT slab normalisation, tissue thresholding, NIfTI/JSON/LTA I/O | whenever a geometry or convention question comes up — it is the foundation of everything |
| `features.py` (238 lines) | the registration representations: MIND-SSC, Otsu two-class (full and low-memory), parser-probability features, Frangi dark-tube vesselness and its γ calibration | when you want to change *what* is being matched rather than *how* |
| `search.py` (152 lines) | `FFTSearcher` — masked-NCC global pose search over all translations × N rotations × both handednesses, with NMS over pose space | when the global search misses the right pose, or you want to change the orientation budget |
| `refine.py` (148 lines) | `Refiner` — differentiable rigid/similarity/affine masked-NCC refinement with Adam | when the pose is right but the fit is not |
| `vascular.py` (98 lines) | the label-free vascular third channel: MRI dark-blob map, OCT Frangi vessel mask, vessel density on a target grid, 3-channel affine refinement | when depth-axis scale is wrong, or when the vascular stage is misbehaving (as on the brainstem pair) |
| `evaluate.py` (117 lines) | annotation-based metrics (vessel distance, GM/WM Dice), `transform_diff`, the `qc_figure` | when interpreting numbers — **never used by the method itself** |
| `nonrigid.py` (81 lines) | free-form displacement grid on top of the affine | only to reproduce the non-rigid validation — **not part of v1** |
| `parser.py` (227 lines) | 3D U-Net structural parser (4 classes) + training loop + sliding-window inference | only for the `--features parser` ablation branch |
| `synth.py` (155 lines) | SynthSeg-style synthetic image generator used to train `parser.py` | ablation branch only |

#### 10.6.2 The live path — scripts you will actually run

| script | role | where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| `prep_subject.py` (190 lines) | **entry point 1** — build the per-pair cache in `work/<S>/` | both |
| `register.py` (271 lines) | **entry point 2** — the v1 pipeline → `work/runs/<run>/`. Short enough to read in full; its module docstring is the authoritative five-stage description and the argparse block is the authoritative flag list | both |
| `viz_result.py` | the per-run QC figure `qc_vessels.png` (3 depth slices × 3 columns) | both |
| `summarize.py` | glob `work/runs/*/result.json` → `work/runs/summary_all/summary.{md,json}` (13-column table) | both |
| `run_subject.sh` | prep-if-needed + otsu register + viz for one DANDI subject; **hard-codes `--oct-wm-bright auto` on line 21** | **server only** |
| `run_all.sh` | the 9-subject sequential driver, then `summarize.py`; its line 5 carries the subject→flip mapping | **server only** |
| `run_xiangrui.sh` | prep + register the PI's brainstem pair (uses `--min-overlap 0.5`) | **server only** |
| `build_inspection.sh` | assembles `results_inspection/` and writes `INDEX.md` from a heredoc | **server only** |
| `recover_serial_dandi.sh`, `recover_serial.sh`, `rerun_xiangrui_fixed.sh`, `restart_xiangrui_first.sh`, `rx2.sh`, `rx3.sh`, `tail_fixups.sh`, `chain_after_batch.sh` | crash/freeze recovery drivers written during the Aug 20–21 incident | **server only** |

Booby traps in the drivers, all confirmed:

- **`run_all.sh` starts with `rm -f work/I46/octv_vessels.npy`** — it re-preps I46 (~25 min) every time.
- **`rx2.sh` and `rx3.sh` end by relaunching `recover_serial_dandi.sh` in the background.** Running
  either to redo the brainstem pair silently starts an 8-subject batch too. Delete that last line if
  you only want the brainstem run.
- **`--oct-wm-bright auto` is not the default.** `register.py:32` reads
  `choices=["auto","yes","no"], default="no"`. Every DANDI run passed `auto` *explicitly* because
  `run_subject.sh` hard-codes it. The 2× runtime doubling is a property of the shipped wrapper, not of
  `register.py`; **a successor calling `register.py` directly will silently get single-polarity
  behaviour.**

#### 10.6.3 The optional parser branch (`--features parser`)

`train_parser.py` (train the U-Net from `labels4.npy` + `mri.npy`) then `parse_mri.py` (cache
`mri_prob_{wm,gm,tissue}.npy`), then `register.py --features parser --parser-dir …`. Both training
steps **require manual labels**, so this branch cannot run on a new subject without annotations —
which is exactly why v1 ships without it. Only `work/parsers/I46` actually holds all three
probability arrays. `parse_mri.py --auto-polarity` decides GM-bright vs WM-bright with a *geometric*
cue — "cortex borders the background/CSF, WM does not", scored as `gm_near - wm_near` after a 7³
max-pool dilation of the predicted background — because parser confidence turned out not to be
discriminative.

#### 10.6.4 The I46 validation suite — the evidence for the design

Run these only to reproduce §4 of `/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/octreg/README.md` (D1 in
§10.8). **Every one takes `--work` and `--parser`, reads
`oct150_prob.npy` / `mri_prob_*.npy`, and therefore needs a trained parser and the I46 manual
annotations. None is runnable on a new subject.**

| script | what it established |
|---|---|
| `scale_probe.py` | the label-free NCC and the manual-label Dice are both **flat** along the OCT depth axis; the manual vessels are not. Unregularised affine (`reg=0`, `clamp=0.35`) drifts |
| `oracle_cv.py` | splits the manual MRI vessels into folds **by connected component**, fits an oracle on the training folds, scores the held-out fold — this is what showed the ~1.4 mm residual after the structural stage is real, and that a held-out oracle reaches f150 ≈ 0.42 |
| `refine_validate.py` | variants A (automatic symmetric vessel distance), A2 (vessels only), B1 (oracle affine), B2 (oracle nonrigid). Established that nearest-vessel-distance between two *automatic* segmentations does not work |
| `vessel_channel_refine.py` | swept MRI channel {dark, frangi} × OCT channel {density, frangi} × weight {0.5, 1, 2, 4}, plus vessel-only and no-vessel controls. **This is what chose `dark` + `density` and `w = 2`** |
| `test_own_vessels.py` | our own Frangi segmentation vs the DANDI `ves_seg`, restart robustness, and the **negative controls** (density flipped along depth, k-slices permuted) that must show no gain |
| `test_vessel_scales.py` | which Frangi sigmas/level for the OCT vessel channel |
| `test_soft_density.py` | soft vs binary vessel density (hard-coded paths) |
| `nonrigid_stage.py` | the free-form stage and its oracle ceiling; concluded v1 stays affine |
| `distill_oct_parser.py` | cross-modal self-distillation of an OCT parser through the current `T`; stronger search but inherits the initial scale, so not adopted |
| `analyze_oracle.py` | decomposes `T0` vs oracle; MRI vessel appearance statistics |
| `profile_vessels.py` | shifts `T` along each OCT axis, plots the vessel-distance profile |
| `check_vesselness.py` | Frangi precision/recall vs manual vessel labels |

**This table says what each script established, not what it measured.** The numbers themselves — the
three-axis scale-probe table, the `vessel_channel_refine.py` parameter sweep, and the non-rigid ablation
results — are canonical in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means (§6.10). Read the outcome there
and come back here only to find the script that produced it.

#### 10.6.5 Ignore these unless asked to reproduce a pre-2026-08-19 result

- `run_demo_i46.py` (352 lines) and `run_ablations.sh` — the pre-v1 monolithic driver, superseded in
  every respect by `register.py`. Its only unique feature is that the non-rigid stage is wired in
  (`--nonrigid on`, in a `try/except` so it can never lose the affine result). **It is also the source
  of the "154 s whole-hemisphere search" number** that circulates in the prose docs: its `--features`
  default is `mixed` (parser probabilities + OCT-derived WM/GM), a mode `register.py` does not accept
  at all — see §10.4's timing note.
- `summarize_runs.py` — reads the `run_demo_i46.py` `result.json` schema; **broken on v1 runs**.
- `prep_i46.py`, `prep_vessels.py`, `prep_large_vessels.py`, `prep_oct_fine.py`, `prep_oct_vessels.py`
  — the I46-only prep chain. They read/write `oct12_affine.npy`, `oct24.npy`, `oct_ves_dist48_z0.npy`,
  `oct_ves_dist48_z66.npy`, `oct_largeves_*`, **none of which `prep_subject.py` produces**. They will
  `FileNotFoundError` on any current `work/<SUBJ>`.
- `find_reference_pose.py`, `find_reference_pose2.py`, `refine_author_init.py`,
  `analyze_candidates.py`, `diag_candidates.py` — the 2026-08-18 forensics of "where is the block
  really" for I46, from when the authors' `affine.lta` was the only reference. All need
  `ref_author_T.json` and/or the authors' code checkout.
- `viz_parser.py`, `viz_pose.py`, `viz_region.py`, `viz_vascular.py` — I46 figure scripts superseded by

- `label_offset.py`, `parse_oct150.py`, `eval_parser_maps.py` — hard-coded paths (`work/i46`,

- `selftest_search.py` — genuinely useful as a convention check, but hard-codes the I46 centroid

### 10.7 The data contract

Two directory types carry everything. A **work directory** is a per-pair cache; a **run directory** is
one registration's output. `prep_subject.py` writes the first, `register.py` reads it and writes the
second. The split exists because prep is expensive (188 s – 1 459 s) and deterministic, while
registration is the part you re-run with different flags.

#### 10.7.1 `work/<SUBJ>/` — what `prep_subject.py` writes

All arrays are `.npy`, C-order; every `_affine.npy` is a 4×4 voxel→world-mm matrix, 256 B on disk.

| file | dtype | shape | content | I46 | brainstem |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mri.npy` | float32 | MRI native `(D,H,W)` | the MRI, non-finite sanitised to 0 | (1280,1040,576), 3.07 GB | (343,489,495) |
| `mri_affine.npy` | float64 | (4,4) | the NIfTI affine **verbatim** | — | — |
| `mri_tissue.npy` | bool | = MRI | air/fluid vs tissue | frac 0.310 | frac 0.313 |
| `labels4.npy` | uint8 | = MRI | *optional, eval only.* 0 bg, 1 WM, 2 infra GM, 3 supra GM | present | absent |
| `ba_labels.npy` | uint8 | = MRI | *optional, eval only.* BA44/45, same coding | present | absent |
| `mri_vessels.npy` | bool | = MRI | *optional, **evaluation only**.* The **manual MRI vessel label**, loaded from `--mri-vessels …label-vessels_dseg.nii.gz`, thresholded `> 0`, mapped to the MRI grid | 34 069 vox | absent |
| `oct150.npy` | float32 | `shape150` | slab-normalised OCT on an isotropic `--target-mm` grid, in the OCT frame | (49,100,97) | (194,267,212) |
| `oct150_affine.npy` | float64 | (4,4) | that grid's voxel→OCT-world affine | — | — |
| `oct150_mask.npy` | bool | `shape150` | OCT tissue mask (largest connected component) | frac 0.424 | frac 0.779 |
| `octv.npy` | float16 | vessel level | slab-normalised OCT pooled to `≥ --vessel-level-um` | (313,635,615) @ 24 µm, 233 MB | (728,1006,797) @ 40 µm |
| `octv_affine.npy`, `octv_mask.npy` | float64 / bool | — / vessel level | the affine; the 0.15 mm mask nearest-resampled | — | — |
| `octv_vessels.npy` | bool | vessel level | **our own** OCT vessel segmentation (top-1 % Frangi dark-tube inside tissue) | 491 472 vox | — |
| `oct_ves_dist48_own.npy` (+ `_affine`) | float32 | vessel level `// k` | EDT in **µm** to the nearest own vessel | (156,317,307) @ 48 µm | (728,1006,797) @ 40 µm |
| `oct_ves_dist48_vesseg.npy` (+ `_affine`) | float32 | native `// k` | *optional.* the same from `--oct-vesseg` (only I38, I46, I48 have one) | (156,317,307) | absent |
| `oct_native_affine.npy` | float64 | (4,4) | affine of the **raw** OCT array | — | — |
| `prep.json` | JSON | — | all prep diagnostics | 2 241 B | 1 422 B |

Two things that matter more than they look:

> **Naming trap.** `oct_ves_dist48_*` is *not* always a 48 µm grid. The pooling factor is
> `k = max(1, round(48/spacing))`, so a 40 µm vessel level gives `k = 1` and the EDT sits on the 40 µm
> grid (the brainstem case). **Always trust the companion `_affine.npy`, never the filename.**

> **`mri_vessels.npy` is the manual label, not a computed map.** If you believed otherwise you would
> conclude the vessel evaluation is circular. It is not: the local-median dark-blob map the *method*
> uses is `vascular.mri_dark_channel`, computed in RAM inside `register.py` and **never written to
> disk**.

`run_subject.sh` treats `work/<S>/octv_vessels.npy` and `work/<S>/mri_tissue.npy` as the "prep already
done" sentinels — delete them (or the whole directory) to force a re-prep.

`prep.json` is the first thing to read after a prep, because it decides whether registering is worth an
hour. Its structure:

```
mri: {file, shape, voxel_mm, tissue_thresh, tissue_fraction,
      n_peaks / peak_pos / valley_ratio (from histogram_tissue_threshold), intensity_p50_p99}
labels_wholehemi, labels_ba, labels_agreement_wholehemi_vs_ba, labels4_counts, mri_vessels
oct: {file, shape_native, spacing_um_zyx, layout, raw_tissue_thresh, slab_window, shape150,
      tissue_frac150, vessel_level_spacing_um, shape_v, own_vessel_voxels, own_vessel_frac48,
      frangi_sigmas_vox, frangi_gamma, per_slice_median_head, vesseg:{file, frac48, z_slices}}
```

Older `prep.json` files on the server also carry `multiotsu3`, `frac_below_first_split`,
`separate_low_mode` from an earlier `histogram_tissue_threshold`; the current code emits `n_peaks` /
`peak_pos` / `valley_ratio` only. **Do not depend on the older keys.**

The three diagnostics that predict failure are `tissue_thresh`, `tissue_fraction` and `valley_ratio`.
**The per-subject panel of them is canonical in chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us
(§7.1.1)**, where all nine DANDI subjects plus the brainstem pair appear with the search margin, the
refined NCC, the restart count and the verdict alongside. Read it there rather than re-deriving it; what
follows is only what you need to interpret a fresh `prep.json` in front of you.

**`tissue_fraction` around 0.31 is healthy** — I46 0.310, I38 0.325, brainstem 0.313. I56 0.989,
I61 0.742 and I58 0.587 are the three where the MRI tissue mask is dominated by bath/fluid; I61 and I58
failed, I56 nevertheless registered correctly, so the fraction is a warning, not a verdict. The knob to
reach for is `--mri-tissue-thresh`. **I57 is not in that group and must not be described as a mask
failure**: its threshold 15.771 sits above its own median 13.803, its `tissue_fraction` is 0.209, and
the peak-walk did find a valley, at 0.0631. Whatever went wrong on I57 is something else, and it is
`[OPEN]`.

`valley_ratio` is a real number for **I46 (0.1161)** and **I38 (0.1984)** — notes that print those two
as missing are wrong. It is `null` only where the peak-walk found no valley at all (I55, I56, I58, I61),
which is itself the warning sign.

The same fields give a sanity check on the mask that costs nothing: multiply shape × voxel volume ×
`tissue_fraction`. Across the six DANDI hemispheres whose masks are not obviously bath-contaminated that
lands at **386–806 cm³** of MRI "tissue" (I48's 386 cm³ is itself an under-inclusive mask; the
well-behaved four sit at 518–806 cm³). Anything far outside that band is a mask problem, not anatomy:
the three failures read 1 453 cm³ (I58), 1 839 cm³ (I61) and 2 519 cm³ (I56). The per-subject volumes
are in chapter 7's table.

On the OCT side `prep.json` records `shape_native`, `spacing_um_zyx`, `layout`, `raw_tissue_thresh`,
`slab_window`, `shape150`, `tissue_frac150` (0.42–0.78 across all working pairs; the brainstem's 0.779
is high because agarose cannot be separated from tissue by intensity — expected, and handled by the
adaptive overlap gate), the vessel level, `own_vessel_voxels` and `own_vessel_frac48`, the five Frangi
sigmas and the per-scale `frangi_gamma`, and `per_slice_median_head` (the first five slice medians —
for the brainstem these are all `0.0`, which is the embedding-medium problem showing up in the
metadata).

Also recorded: `labels_agreement_wholehemi_vs_ba` (I38 0.900, I46 0.932, I48 0.937, I55 0.909,
I56 0.882, **I57 0.671**, I58 0.939, I61 0.940) and `mri_vessels.n_voxels` (I38 10 236, I46 34 069,
I48 79 331, I55 13 899, I56 6 513, I57 15 650, I58 33 745, I61 33 670, I62 16 287).

**I46's sidecar is wrong.** It declares 12×12×12 µm while every other subject's is 30×30×35 or
12×12×14 — the depth spacing is 1.167× larger than declared. That is exactly the depth stretch the
vascular stage recovers (1.219 for I46). The pipeline's own `stretch_ijk[0]` and the sidecar-vs-siblings
ratio 14/12 = 1.167 are the two defensible anchors; the figure "≈1.18" that appears in some notes has
no artefact behind it `[UNVERIFIED]`.

#### 10.7.2 `work/runs/<run>/` — what `register.py` writes

| file | dtype/format | content |
|---|---|---|
| `T_oct2mri.npy` | float64 (4,4) | **the deliverable.** OCT world → MRI NIfTI world, after the vascular stage |
| `T_oct2mri_structural.npy` | float64 (4,4) | the same, before the vascular stage |
| `T_oct2mri.lta` | text, ~315 B | FreeSurfer `LINEAR_RAS_TO_RAS` of the final transform, headers `# src: OCT world (oct150 affine)` / `# dst: MRI NIfTI world` |
| `oct_class150.npy` | uint8, `shape150` | 0 bg, 1 WM, 2 GM on the oct150 grid (Otsu split + chosen polarity) |
| `result.json` | JSON, 12–19 KB | the full log. Written **twice** — once before the heavy outputs, so a late OOM cannot lose it |
| `qc_oct_space.png` | PNG | `evaluate.qc_figure`, 3×4 |
| `qc_vessels.png` | PNG | written by `viz_result.py`, **not** by `register.py`. Older runs have `qc_vascular.png` instead |
| `oct_in_mri_region.nii.gz` | float32 NIfTI | the OCT block warped into MRI space, on an MRI box `bc ± BOX` |
| `mri_region.nii.gz` | float32 NIfTI | the MRI for the same box |
| `mri_labels_region.nii.gz` | uint8 NIfTI | *optional*, only when `labels4.npy` exists |

The `mri_region.nii.gz` + `oct_in_mri_region.nii.gz` pair is **on a common grid** and is the intended
way for the PI to check a result himself: open both in Freeview or ITK-SNAP and slide the opacity.

`result.json` top-level keys, verified against `work/runs/I46_otsu/result.json`:

```
args.*                       every argparse value (Paths as strings)
mri_region_ijk               [lo, hi]
mri_otsu_thresh              (features=otsu only)
oct_otsu_thresh
overlap_gate                 {requested, effective, V_mri_tissue_cm3, V_oct_mask_cm3}
polarity_trials.{"False","True"}.{search_top1, search_top2, refined_ncc, centre, mirror, seconds}
oct_wm_bright                bool — the polarity that won
search.{n_rot, mirror, n_orientations, scales, seconds, template_n, top1, top2, candidates[]}
refine.{final_ncc, final_ncc_channels, distinct_runner_up, level015_candidates}
vascular.{ncc_channels, vs_structural, stretch_ijk_structural, stretch_ijk_vascular, seconds,
          restarts:{n, "n_within_0.3mm", detail}}     |  {"mode":"off"}
evaluation.final.{stretch_ijk, block_centre_mri_mm, vessels_own, vessels_vesseg, gmwm, vs_reference}
evaluation.structural.{same}                (null when the vascular stage is off)
evaluation.restarts.{n, n_converged, detail}
final_transform.{T_oct2mri_world, T_structural, block_centre_mri_mm, column_scales, det, mirror,
                 stretch_ijk}
total_seconds
```

Three schema facts a successor will trip on:

- **`overlap_gate` is `null` in `work/runs/I46_otsu/result.json`** — the adaptive gate did not exist
  when I46 was run.
- Its four sub-keys are `{requested, effective, V_mri_tissue_cm3, V_oct_mask_cm3}`. `effective` is
  derived at `register.py:111` from `requested` and those two volumes. **The formula is stated once, in
  full and with its 0.15 floor, in chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning (§5.2.3)** — quote it
  from there, because dropping the floor is the standard way it gets mis-cited.
- **The gate never binds on DANDI.** All eight DANDI runs that record it show
  `{requested 0.85, effective 0.850}`. It binds only on the brainstem pair: `xiangrui_I58bs` →
  **effective 0.369** (V_mri_tissue 13.3 cm³ vs V_oct_mask 28.9 cm³). Presenting it as a live feature of
  the DANDI results overstates it; it is a feature the brainstem data forced into existence.

#### 10.7.3 What the transforms mean, and in which world space

**MRI world.** `mri_affine.npy` is the source NIfTI `img.affine`, unmodified, and the array is kept in
`(i,j,k)` order. For the DANDI EPIC volumes this is the subject's RAS mm space; I46's is a
permuted/flipped 0.15 mm grid:

```
[[ 0,     0,    -0.15,  48.3283],
 [ 0.15,  0,     0,    -86.1671],
 [ 0,     0.15,  0,    -63.2689],
 [ 0,     0,     0,      1     ]]
```

Every region affine used internally (`A_reg`, `A_v`, `A_q`, `A_out`) is this matrix with only `[:3,3]`
moved to the world position of the crop's `lo` corner — **the linear part is never changed**, so world
coordinates are always the same MRI NIfTI RAS mm no matter which crop you are looking at.

**OCT world.** Purely synthetic, built by `layout_affine(shape, spacing_mm, --oct-layout,
center_origin=False)`. Voxel `(0,0,0)` of the *raw* array sits at world `(0,0,0)`. All four OCT levels
share one world frame and differ only in sampling grid and voxel-centre offset; for I46:

```
oct_native_affine  x = .012·k,  y = -.012·j,  z = .012·i          origin (0, 0, 0)
oct150_affine      x = .15·k,   y = -.15·j,   z = .15·i           origin (.066, -.066, .066)
octv_affine        x = .024·k,  y = -.024·j,  z = .024·i          origin (.006, -.006, .006)
oct_ves_dist48_own x = .048·k,  y = -.048·j,  z = .048·i          origin (.018, -.018, .018)
```

**The RAS letters carry no anatomical meaning.** The global search covers all of SO(3) *and* both
handednesses, so `--oct-layout` (default `SPR`) only fixes the arbitrary labelling of the OCT world
axes. It matters in exactly one sense: every OCT cache file must have been built with the same value.

**The transform.** `T_oct2mri` is a 4×4 row-major world→world matrix,
`x_mri_mm = T[:3,:3] @ x_oct_mm + T[:3,3]`, both sides in millimetres. I46's:

```
[[-0.0654,  0.2949,  1.1682,  -7.1325],
 [ 0.9390, -0.3561,  0.2132,  15.6256],
 [-0.4196, -0.8611,  0.2767,   4.0908],
 [ 0,       0,       0,        1     ]]
```

| quantity | meaning |
|---|---|
| `det(T[:3,:3]) < 0` | the OCT stack has the **opposite handedness** to physical space (`final_transform.mirror`). **6 of the 9 DANDI subjects are mirrored: I38, I46, I48, I56, I58, I62.** Not mirrored: I55, I57, I61, and both brainstem runs |
| `final_transform.column_scales` | `‖T[:3,:3][:,q]‖`, the per-**world**-axis column norms. **Not anatomically interpretable** |
| `final_transform.stretch_ijk` | `‖T[:3,:3] @ R_axes[:,q]‖` where `R_axes` are the normalised `A_oct` columns — the per-**OCT-array-axis** scale, i.e. `[depth, in-plane j, in-plane k]`. **This is the meaningful one.** I46 `[1.219, 0.977, 1.031]`, I55 `[0.913, 1.097, 1.084]`, brainstem `[0.969, 0.988, 0.972]`. Before quoting either of the first two, read the I55 caveat in §10.4 |
| MRI → OCT | invert: `np.linalg.inv(T)` |
| OCT **voxel index** → MRI mm | `T @ oct150_affine` (or `@ octv_affine` at the fine level) |

**The LTA caveat.** `T_oct2mri.lta` writes the same matrix in FreeSurfer's `LINEAR_RAS_TO_RAS` text
format, and it is **only valid if the consuming tool treats both volumes' spaces as their NIfTI world
spaces**. FreeSurfer's own "RAS" is a different (tkreg / scanner-RAS-recentred) convention, so do not
feed this to `mri_vol2vol` without checking. `scripts/refine_author_init.py` contains the explicit
`vox2ras_fs` / `fs_to_nifti` conversion for the I46 case if that ever has to be done again.

### 10.9 The figure system, and how to regenerate a figure

Every figure in every document follows one convention, and there is exactly one current generator.

| script | location | bytes | mtime | role |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| `fig_doc2.py` (78 lines) | **server only** | 5 086 | 2026-08-21 09:47 | **current** generator of all 6 document figures (5-panel A–E) |
| `fig_doc.py` (61 lines) | **server only** | 4 118 | 2026-08-21 08:03 | superseded 4-panel version with in-figure titles |
| `fig_bs.py` (35 lines) | **server only** | 2 558 | 2026-08-21 09:32 | superseded brainstem-only 4-panel one-off |
| `viz_result.py` | both | 4 548 | 2026-08-19 21:19 | per-run QC figure `qc_vessels.png` (3×3) |
| `viz_vascular.py` | both | 4 061 | 2026-08-19 00:39 | vascular-stage comparison `qc_vascular.png` |
| `octreg/evaluate.py::qc_figure` | both | (in 7 204 B module) | 2026-08-18 02:30 | `qc_oct_space.png`, written by `register.py:254` |
| `diag_xiangrui.py` / `diag2_xiangrui.py` / `test_texture_mask.py` | **server only** | 1 450 / 1 673 / 1 713 | 2026-08-20 | brainstem diagnostics |

The five-panel convention, verbatim from `fig_doc2.py`'s docstring:

> `A MRI slice with the located block (red);  B OCT mid-depth slice;  C registered MRI, same plane;`
> `D checkerboard of B|C;  E edges of C (Canny) over B.  Grayscale, robust windowing, physical scale bars.`

| panel | frame | content | overlay |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | MRI native grid, axis-0 slice `i0` | the MRI slice through the transformed OCT block centre | red contour of the OCT tissue mask pulled into that plane through `T⁻¹`, level 0.5, `linewidths=1.6`. **10 mm scale bar** |
| **B** | OCT-150 grid, `z = D//2` | raw OCT mid-depth slice | none. **5 mm scale bar** |
| **C** | OCT-150 grid, same `z` | raw MRI resampled into the OCT frame by `T` | none |
| **D** | OCT-150 grid, same `z` | checkerboard of B and C | none |
| **E** | OCT-150 grid, same `z` | panel B with the Canny edges of panel C on top | orange RGBA `(1.0, 0.45, 0.05, 1.0)`, `interpolation="nearest"` |

Why these five and not others, since you will be asked: the checkerboard forces a hard discontinuity at
every tile border, so a misalignment is visible and its size is readable in tiles — a colour blend hides
misalignment inside a gradient and its apparent quality depends on the alpha you picked. The Canny edges
are computed from **raw intensity of the registered MRI**, so panel E does not depend on the WM/GM
classifier the registration itself optimises — it is a check with a different failure mode than the
objective. Anatomy is grayscale so that each colour carries exactly one meaning, and that palette is
fixed across every figure and QC image in the project: **red** = registered block outline (or MRI WM
label contour in `qc_oct_space`), **cyan** = OCT WM/GM class boundary (or MRI GM label contour),
**lime/green** = our own automatic OCT vessel density, **yellow** = manual MRI vessel annotation,
**orange** = Canny edges of the registered MRI, **white** = block outline. Scale bars are physical
because the figures span 12 µm to 0.15 mm voxel sizes and a bar computed from the affine is the only
annotation that stays true across all of them. Only panel letters go inside the axes; everything else
lives in the caption, which is what let the panels survive the D2 → D5 rewrite unchanged.

The tile-size rule is `t = max(8, min(on.shape) // 6)` — one sixth of the shorter in-plane dimension of
the OCT-150 slice, floor of 8 px. That gives ≈6 tiles across the narrow axis **regardless of block
size**, which is what makes a 15 mm I46 block and a 45 mm I56 slab produce visually comparable
checkerboards. At 0.15 mm/voxel, `t = 8` is 1.2 mm; for a 300-voxel-wide slice `t = 50` → 7.5 mm tiles.
The two superseded scripts use different rules and are **not** the current convention (`fig_bs.py`
hardcodes `t = 32`; `evaluate.qc_figure` uses a fixed 12-voxel tile).

**One documentation inaccuracy to be aware of:** D2 and D5 both say "robust 1–99 % windowing per
volume". That is exactly true for panel C, but panels B/D/E's OCT half use `x / p99` with the low end
pinned at 0, and panel A uses `x / p99.5`. The images are fine; the sentence is a simplification.

#### 10.9.1 Regenerating a document figure

```bash

source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate octmri
cd ~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration     # cwd MATTERS: the script does sys.path.insert(0,\"octreg\") and uses relative work/ paths
python octreg/scripts/fig_doc2.py
ls -la octreg/figures/
"'
# then pull them back
rsync -az -e 'ssh -p 49018' root@connect.westb.seetacloud.com:autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration/octreg/figures/ \
  /Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/octreg/figures/
```

`fig_doc2.py` has **no CLI**. The case list is hard-coded at the top and running the script regenerates
**every** case in it, about 10 s each:

```python
CASES = [
    ("I46",           "work/I46",            "work/runs/I46_otsu"),

```

**Add a new subject by appending a `(name, work_dir, run_dir)` tuple**; the output filename is

#### 10.9.2 Regenerating the per-run QC figure, the summary table and the inspection folder

```bash
# one run's 3x3 QC figure -> <run>/qc_vessels.png (override with --out)
python octreg/scripts/viz_result.py --work work/I46 --run work/runs/I46_otsu

# the cross-run markdown table -> work/runs/summary_all/summary.{md,json}
python octreg/scripts/summarize.py                      # defaults: --runs work/runs --out work/runs/summary_all --pattern '*'
python octreg/scripts/summarize.py --pattern 'I*_otsu'  # what produced the current summary.md

# the curated inspection folder + INDEX.md
bash octreg/scripts/build_inspection.sh
```

`build_inspection.sh` copies ten files per run (`T_oct2mri.npy`, `T_oct2mri_structural.npy`,
`T_oct2mri.lta`, `result.json`, `qc_vessels.png`, `qc_oct_space.png`, `mri_region.nii.gz`,
`oct_in_mri_region.nii.gz`, `mri_labels_region.nii.gz`, `oct_class150.npy`) for the twelve runs listed
inside it. **Two behaviours that will surprise you:** it copies with `cp -n`, so existing files are
never replaced — a genuine refresh needs the targets deleted first; and it **rewrites
`results_inspection/INDEX.md` from a heredoc inside the script**, so the verdict table must be edited in
`build_inspection.sh`, never in `INDEX.md`, or your edits revert to the 2026-08-21 text.

`viz_result.py` needs `T_oct2mri_structural.npy`, `result.json`, `octv_vessels.npy`, `octv_affine.npy`,
and optionally `mri_vessels.npy` and `oct_class150.npy`. `fig_doc.py` (superseded) additionally needs
`octv_vessels.npy`, `octv_affine.npy` and `oct_class150.npy`.

**Nothing under `figures/` or `results/final/v1/` can be regenerated on the Mac** — every generator
needs the `work/` volumes (`mri.npy`, `oct150.npy`, …), which exist only on the AutoDL box. That is the
practical reason the box's `work/` directory is not disposable.

### 10.10 Risks to the handoff itself

Everything above describes a project that works. This subsection describes how it could stop existing.
These three items come from the first-hand verification pass and outrank anything softer said elsewhere
in this document.

#### Risk 1 — the project is effectively UNVERSIONED

| Location | VCS state |
|---|---|
| `/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project` | **NOT a git repository at all.** This is where the newest code and all docs live |
| `/Users/yyttim/workspace/oct-mri-registration` | git repo, remote `git@github.com:yyttim/oct-mri-registration.git`, **1 commit** (`88013e5 Add reproducible Costantini data setup`), **only 3 tracked files**. `octreg/` is listed as untracked (`?? octreg/`). `download_costantini.sh` is modified and uncommitted |
| AutoDL `~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration/octreg` | no VCS, but is the box where everything actually runs |

**There is no commit history, no branches, no diff trail. The only redundancy is that two or three
copies of the tree exist.** The one `.git` anywhere under `lsfm-project` is `proj-lsfm/.git`, a clone of
a *different* lab member's third-party repo, which must not be vendored in.

This is not a hygiene complaint. It has already cost a concrete result: **five of the nine headline
runs predate the current source.** `register.py` has mtime 2026-08-20 23:30, `prep_subject.py` 15:11,
`vascular.py` 19:31, while `result.json` mtimes are I46 10:23, I38 19:48, I55 20:18, I56 21:07,
I62 22:01 — all *before* 23:30 — against I61 00:03, I48 01:01, I57 01:50, I58 04:24 after it. **I46 is
the only subject whose prep (`work/I46/prep.json`, 10:04) and registration both predate the current
code**, and the revision that produced `I46_otsu` is **unrecoverable**. The adaptive overlap gate alone
did not exist then (`I46_otsu`'s `overlap_gate` is `null`), so a re-run with today's code should be
expected to give a different number. That is the price of no VCS, paid once already.

**The fix — but write the `.gitignore` first, because a secret in history survives deletion.** The tree
contains a private Slack export, 14 copyrighted PDFs and four `.m4a` recordings of identifiable
colleagues; committing it wholesale would publish all of that.

```bash
cd /Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project
# 1. write .gitignore FIRST — at minimum:
#    meeting_recordings/{source_audio,raw_recognition,voice_memos_raw}/  slack_archive/  papers/
#    tmp/  project_plan/qa/  proj-lsfm/  literature_review/**/*.pdf
#    data/ work/ results_inspection/ logs/ *.nii *.nii.gz *.tif *.tiff *.npy *.npz *.pt *.ckpt
#    __pycache__/ .venv/ .ipynb_checkpoints/ .DS_Store  .env .env.* *.pem *.key credentials* secrets*
git init
# 2. dry-run the index and eyeball it. Expect NO .m4a, NO .pdf, NO slack_archive.
git add -An . | sort | tee /tmp/would-commit.txt | wc -l

#### Risk 3 — the README references two directories that do not exist

`octreg/README.md` §4 and §6 reference `scripts/validation_i46/` and `scripts/legacy/`. **Neither
directory exists**, on the server or locally — `ls -A octreg/scripts` on the box returns 59 flat
entries with no subdirectories at all. The README is describing an intended reorganisation that was
never carried out, which means a successor following §6 to find the validation evidence will conclude
it is missing.

The I46 validation scripts are flat files directly in `scripts/`: `analyze_oracle.py`, `oracle_cv.py`,
`scale_probe.py`, `nonrigid_stage.py`, `distill_oct_parser.py`, `refine_validate.py`,
`analyze_candidates.py`, `test_own_vessels.py`, `vessel_channel_refine.py`.

**Fix the README** (preferred — one line in each of §4 and §6, and the directory names carry no
functional meaning):

grep -n 'validation_i46\|scripts/legacy' README.md      # find the two references

```

**Or create the directories**, if you would rather the layout match the prose:

Caveat if you take the second option: these scripts do `sys.path.insert(0, "octreg")` and use paths
relative to the **cwd**, not to `__file__`, so they keep working when launched from
`~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration` — but anything that referenced them by their old flat path breaks,
and moving files in an unversioned tree is exactly the operation that has no undo. Do Risk 1 first.

#### Two more errors in the shipped documents worth fixing in the same pass

Neither threatens the handoff, but both are in documents the PI or a successor will read:

- **`octreg/README.md:42` says "DANDI 8 个已完成 subject" and then lists 5 correct + 1 uncertain +
  3 wrong = 9.** Fix the count to 9. The same line says I55's depth stretch is 1.10; the measured value
  is **0.913** (`stretch_ijk = [0.913, 1.097, 1.084]`, index 0 = depth — 1.097 is the in-plane *j*
  axis). The argument it supports survives: I55's sidecar depth spacing is right, so no depth correction
  is needed, and the vascular stage moves it only 0.334 mm. Carry the caveat with it, though — I55's
  structural depth/in-plane anisotropy is **0.8570 = 6/7**, the exact inverse of the 7/6 factor I46 is
  missing, so I55 is a qualified null result and not a clean one (§10.4).
- **`EXPLAINER_zh.md:13` says 5 of 9 subjects are mirrored**; the measured answer is **6 of 9**
  (I38, I46, I48, I56, I58, I62). And **`EXPLAINER_zh.md:50`'s "整半球 154 秒"** is a real measurement
  but of a *different* configuration — `run_demo_i46.py --features mixed`, which uses the trained
  parser's probabilities as MRI channels. The label-free path that v1 actually ships costs **298.9 s**
  for the same subject and the same 16 000-orientation grid, and **597.8 s** with the
  `--oct-wm-bright auto` that every DANDI run used. Quoting 154 s under a "label-free" heading
  attributes a parser-assisted runtime to the training-free pipeline.

## 11. What to do next

Two sentences spoken by the PI on **2026-08-23** determine everything in this chapter. Both are transcribed
verbatim in `meeting_recordings/cleaned_transcripts/2026-08-23_beijing_yuanmingyuan_garden.md`; the
surrounding exchange is reconstructed in chapter 9, The lab: people, history, and the constraints that shape
this work, §9.5.5 and §9.5.6:

1. *"We do have a lot of scans and volumes, but we do not have many labels."* — and, on how development should
   be judged, *"I usually prefer to just check visually whether things look right… Although for a paper we need
   some quantitative results."*
2. *"We do have prior knowledge of where it might be… we can crop a small part there. And the I58 data I shared
   with you is already cropped."*

Constraint 1 confirms the method's core design and forbids anything that needs labels in order to **run**.
Constraint 2 removes the operational need for the one capability the project has been leading with. The
roadmap, the repositioning, the code defaults and the paper plan below are all consequences of those two
sentences.

**Conventions and provenance.** Every number and path in this chapter was checked against a primary artefact
— a file on the compute server under `~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration/`, a file in the local repo, a meeting
transcript under `meeting_recordings/`, or a published paper — on **2026-08-23** and **2026-08-24**. The three
provenance markers `[UNVERIFIED]`, `[NOT RE-MEASURED]` and `[OPEN]` are used with the meanings given in
chapter 2, Orientation and glossary. Where a passage is a judgement rather than a measurement, it says so in
words.

**Corrections applied in this chapter.** Several figures that circulate in the project's own README, talk and
meeting notes are wrong, and this chapter uses the corrected values throughout. The full correction register is

### 11.1 Honest state of play

#### 11.1.1 The one-paragraph version, unsoftened

`octreg v1` is a complete, label-free, training-free OCT→MRI affine pipeline that runs unchanged on
0.08–0.15 mm MRI and 12–35 µm OCT, has been executed end to end on 9 public subjects and one of the lab's own
specimens, and contains one result that is a genuine scientific finding rather than engineering: a scale factor
along the block's serial-sectioning axis that the structural objective provably cannot see (NCC span **0.021**
over a ±22.5 % sweep, against **0.169** along an in-plane axis — the three-axis probe behind those two numbers
is tabulated in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.10.3) is recovered automatically from vasculature at
**1.219**, against **1.174** from the authors' hand-drawn-vessel affine, **1.177** from an oracle fitted to the
same annotations, and **1.167** from sibling metadata. Against that:

- **The evaluation is broken on six of the nine public subjects.** `prep_subject.py::map_labels_to_grid` pairs
  a 640-voxel label axis against a 1400-voxel MRI axis; 31.7–41.6 % of labels are dropped and only 36–40 % of
  the MRI grid ever receives a lookup. Every `dice_WM`/`dice_GM` for I38, I48, I56, I57, I58, I61 is computed
  against a corrupted label volume.
- **Only two subjects have quantitative support at all** — I46 and I55. "5 of 9 correct" is a visual verdict,
  and three independent checks contradict it on I38/I56/I62.
- **The one specimen the lab actually cares about has no numeric residual whatsoever.** The brainstem result is
  a coarse pose judged by eye; `evaluation.final` for `xiangrui_I58bs_novasc` contains only `stretch_ijk` and
  `block_centre_mri_mm`.
- **The headline numbers are not reproducible with the code on disk.** `register.py` has mtime
  **2026-08-20 23:30**, `prep_subject.py` 15:11, `vascular.py` 19:31; the `result.json` files for **I46, I38,
  I55, I56, I62** are all older. `work/runs/I46_otsu/result.json` even has `overlap_gate: null` — the adaptive
  gate did not exist when the project's single most-cited subject was run. The tree is unversioned, so the
  revision that produced `I46_otsu` is **unrecoverable** (chapter 10, State of play: where everything is,
  §10.10, Risk 1).
- **The code is effectively unversioned and 21 files exist only on a rented GPU container** that reassigns
  `host:port` on every restart.
- **The method has no reject rule of any kind.** Every diagnosed failure was caught by a human opening a
  figure.
- **The framing the PI heard on 08-23 leads with the half of the claim he then told us was unnecessary.**

Nothing in that list is a search-localisation failure. That fact is the entire argument for the ordering in
§11.3.

### 11.2 The strategic repositioning

This section comes before the roadmap because it decides what the effort is *for*.

#### 11.2.1 What happened

`octreg/TALK_2026-08-21.md`, "What is new", states the delta against Costantini as removing **two**
requirements: hand-drawn GM/WM/vessel segmentations on both modalities, *and* the pre-cropped MRI. Minutes
after that was presented on 08-23, the PI said a position prior is available in practice and that the I58 MRI
he supplied is already cropped.

Both halves of the claim are true statements about the *method*. Only one of them is a statement about a
problem anybody has.

#### 11.2.2 The corrected claim ladder

| Rank | Claim | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Label-free.** The baseline needs hand-drawn GM, hand-drawn WM and hand-drawn vessels on **both** modalities — six annotation products. We need two files and their voxel sizes. Enabled by one measured fact: after dividing by the local tissue mean at σ = 10 mm, a plain Otsu split agrees with the manual labels at Dice **0.90 / 0.93**, up from **0.66 / 0.62** — confirmed by re-derivation; precise values in chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning, §5.1.5 | **The selling point.** It is exactly what the PI's constraint 1 says the lab needs, and it is the reason the method runs at all on a specimen that has two files and nothing else |
| **2** | **The vessel channel recovers a scale the structural objective provably cannot see.** A ±22.5 % depth stretch moves the structural NCC by **0.021** (against 0.169 along an in-plane axis) and the manual-label Dice by 0.007, while the true factor is ~1.17. Automatic recovery: **1.219**, against 1.174 / 1.177 / 1.167 from three independent human-derived sources, with an apparent null on I55 | The intellectual core — the only part of the project that is a finding rather than an engineering choice. **But see H13.** The I55 null is not clean: that subject's own recovered depth/in-plane anisotropy is **0.8570 = 6/7**, the exact inverse of the factor I46 is supposed to be missing, and I38's 0.861 is the clamp bound `exp(−0.15)` rather than a measurement. The scale story has three readings and none is clean. Do not write this up before P1.8 |
| **3** | **Automatic resolution of polarity and handedness.** Both flip between subjects of the same dataset. Neither can be assumed, neither can be reached by a gradient, and the coarse search *prefers the wrong polarity* on I46 | Small but genuinely necessary, and unhandled by the baseline. There is now indirect external support: the authors' own `stereo_warp.py` clamps a Jacobian determinant they know has the wrong sign, with the comment *"for some reason all my determinants are negative, which cannot be right FIXME"* — almost certainly the same chirality problem, undiagnosed. Reading their FIXME that way is an interpretation, not something they state. The file is `scripts/registration/stereo_warp.py` in `github.com/neuroscales/biccn-broca-I46` (chapter 8, How this compares to the published method, §8.2.1) |
| **4** | **A publishable negative result:** a one-sheet two-class cortical block does not encode its own thickness scale, and neither do manual GM/WM labels. Anyone doing OCT→MRI with a structure-only similarity absorbs this silently | Stands on its own |
| **5** | **Prior-optional operation.** Whole-hemisphere search when no prior is given; a ±30 mm crop when one is | **Robustness insurance and a paper capability — not the value proposition.** Frame it conditionally |

#### 11.2.3 What changes in the story told to the lab

1. Lead with **"it needs no annotations"**, not **"it needs no prior"**. The first matches a stated operational
   constraint; the second solves a problem the PI says he does not have.
2. Say the prior sentence in the conditional form, every time: *"if you give us a prior we use it; if you do
   not, we can still find the block."* Never as a single absolutist selling point.
3. Do **not** describe the prior as a precise ROI or a coordinate range. Nobody has said what it is
   (§11.12 Q1), and `project_plan/working/meeting_ground_truth.md` §12 item 9 — the project's own "never claim this" list — forbids writing it up as one.
4. Report **2 confirmed, 3 unresolved, 1 undecidable, 3 failed** rather than "5 of 9", until P1 settles it —
   and then report whatever P1 says. Downgrade I56 further: it has the worst MRI tissue mask in the dataset
   (`tissue_fraction` 0.989, threshold 3.62 against a median of 15.1) and 0/8 vascular restarts converged; its
   "correct" is unsupported (chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.4.3; chapter 7, Failures, dead
   ends, and things that bit us, §7.1.5).
5. Volunteer the failures with their causes. Three of the four bad cases are diagnosable in advance from fields
   already written into `result.json` and `prep.json`; the honest and much stronger statement is *"the failures
   are mostly not mysterious, and the reject gates were simply not implemented"* — not *"56 % success rate"*.
   The fourth, **I57, is genuinely unexplained** `[OPEN]`; say so rather than repeating the mask-failure story,
   which its own numbers contradict.
6. Say plainly that the specimen size varies 80-fold across the nine subjects, and that the hard version of the
   problem — a 0.09 % block in a whole hemisphere — has been demonstrated on **one** subject.
7. Carry the "what must be true before submission" list in §11.11.5 into every outward-facing document. In particular: no TRE for any subject including the brainstem, no "we reproduce their affine", no
   Dice for the six subjects with a broken label mapping, no `rotation_deg` for a mirrored subject.

#### 11.2.4 What changes in the code

The temptation is to flip `--crop-centre` on by default. That is the wrong move, and the measured reason is
that the crop **buys nothing in accuracy**: `crop_final2` vs `whole_final2` give `stretch_ijk`
[1.184, 0.973, 1.034] vs [1.195, 0.975, 1.035] and vessels 166.8 µm / f150 0.469 vs 166.6 µm / 0.474. What the
crop buys is speed and a smaller space in which the margin gate is more discriminative.

State the speed honestly, because both halves of the usual comparison come from the **parser-assisted**
`run_demo_i46.py --features mixed` path, not the shipped label-free one: crop **12–14 s** at 4 000 rotations
(= 8 000 orientations) `[NOT RE-MEASURED]` against **76.7 s** whole at the same orientation count
(`whole_mixed_real`) and **153.7 s** whole at 16 000 (`whole_final2`). The shipped label-free whole-hemisphere
search is **298.9 s per polarity** on I46. The canonical per-branch timing table is in chapter 6, What we
found, and what it means, §6.3.2. The crop-versus-whole accuracy evidence above is likewise from
`--features mixed` runs and has **never been repeated on the label-free path** `[UNVERIFIED]` — an experiment
that costs one afternoon and belongs with P1.

So the design proposal is: **run cropped as the answer, whole as the certificate, and report both.**

| Change | Concretely | Argument |
|---|---|---|
| Add `--prior-mode {auto,crop,global}`, default `auto` | `auto` = use `--crop-centre`/`--crop-half-mm` when supplied, otherwise whole-hemisphere. Today the prior is an optional flag with no status in the output | Makes the prior a first-class input matching the operational reality, without ever making it mandatory |
| When a prior is given, run the global search too and record both poses in `result.json` | It costs 45 s–17 min depending on the subject, and it is now the *robustness experiment* rather than the product | Every subject then ships its own prior-free regression. That is the paper's robustness table, generated for free |
| Wire H6's reject gates into the return value, not just the log | `result.json` gains `accepted: bool` and `reject_reasons: [...]` | Constraint 1 says the development loop is visual. A visual loop needs the pipeline to say which figures to open |
| Surface `valley_ratio: null` as a first-class warning | One line. It is the single cleanest automatic red flag in the pipeline — three of the four problem subjects have it — and it appears in no `result.json` field, no `INDEX.md` verdict and no figure. I55 is its one false positive, so it warns, it does not reject | chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us, §7.1.1 |
| Keep `--vascular` defaulted **on**, but auto-disable it when the vessel-channel NCC at the structural pose falls below ~0.05 | On the brainstem it scored **0.0055**, moved the block 2.652 mm, returned 0/8 restarts and consumed **4 778.4 s of a 5 244.0 s** run. On I38 the vascular stage is **5 696.8 s of 7 864.1 s** | The vascular stage is 72–91 % of wall clock on the runs where it does not work. This is the single largest compute saving available. **Read the vessel-channel NCC out of all eleven `result.json` before fixing the threshold** — only the brainstem value is quoted anywhere `[OPEN]` |
| **Make `--oct-wm-bright auto` the actual default in `register.py`** | `register.py:32` currently reads `default="no"`. Every headline run got `auto` only because `run_subject.sh` line 21 hard-codes it. A successor calling `register.py` directly gets single-polarity behaviour **silently** | It doubles the structural stage (I46: 2 × 388.4 s) and the alternative is a 70 mm error that *every* structural metric endorses. Cheapest insurance in the pipeline; pass `yes`/`no` only when the protocol is known |
| Measure the section period in `prep_subject.py` instead of asserting 1 200 µm | §11.6 P2.4 | Physical units are necessary but not sufficient — the physical quantity has to be measured, not asserted |
| Write the frame into the transform | Copy `oct.layout`, `oct.spacing_um_zyx`, `oct.shape_native` from `prep.json` into `result.json → final_transform`, and emit them as `#` comments from `common.lta_text()` | H14. Until it lands, **never hand out a `.npy` or `.lta` without the matching `prep.json`** |

### 11.3 The ordering principle, stated once

The PI's two constraints are not two independent notes. Together they say: **stop spending on the thing v1 does
best, and start spending on the things v1 has not solved, plus the one human ask that produces a paper number.**

The decisive test for the ordering is to cross-tabulate every known failure against "does a position prior fix
this?":

| Known failure | Root cause | Does a position prior fix it? |
|---|---|---|
| **I61** wrong (`tissue_fraction` 0.742, 1 839 cm³ of "tissue", threshold 6.80 against a median of 10.4, `valley_ratio: null`) | `histogram_tissue_threshold` fails open | **No.** A crop of a hemisphere whose mask is wrong is still a crop of a wrong mask |
| **I58** wrong (`tissue_fraction` 0.587, 1 453 cm³, threshold 2.12 against a median of 16.9, `valley_ratio: null`) — *and* registered against the **10°** `flip-3` volume | mask failure **and** a contrast failure | **No** on both counts |
| **I56** mask degenerate (`tissue_fraction` 0.989 — the mask is essentially the whole field of view, 2 519 cm³), currently marked "correct" | same | **No** |
| **I57** wrong — **cause unknown** `[OPEN]`. Its mask is one of the *best* in the corpus (fraction 0.209, threshold 15.77 above its median 13.8, `valley_ratio` 0.0631). Confounded with contrast: it is one of only two `flip-4` runs, and of the four non-`flip-2` runs three are wrong | unknown | **Unknown.** Nothing can be claimed until it is diagnosed |
| **I48** undecidable (search top1 0.2571 vs top2 0.2558, margin **0.0013**, ratio 1.0051). Its verdict rests on that margin and on nothing else; its Dice is untrustworthy in **both** directions because of the label-mapping bug in H1. It is **not** an instance of the label-coverage artefact that explains I62 and the other large slabs — do not lump it in with them | flat objective | **Partly.** A smaller space raises the margin; the objective is unchanged |
| Brainstem: OCT mask includes agarose (**77.9 %** "tissue", raw threshold 0.0) | intensity cannot separate agarose from tissue | **No** |
| Brainstem: vessel channel dead (NCC **0.0055**, 4 534 410 seam voxels) | Frangi fires on section seams | **No** |
| I46 depth scale off ~17 % | two-class geometry is degenerate along depth | **No** |
| Nothing on this list | wrong search localisation | — |

**Not one of the project's failures is a search-localisation failure.** That is the whole argument for the
order below: the prior removes the problem v1 solved best, and leaves every problem v1 has not solved.

Two further ordering rules follow from the constraints:

- **Fix the measuring instrument before re-measuring anything.** Six of nine subjects are evaluated against a
  corrupted label volume, and the single largest open question in the results (the 55–66 mm annotation gap on
  I38/I56/I62) is *confounded with that exact bug*. Any experiment run before H1 is fixed produces a number
  nobody can interpret.
- **Anything that needs a human decision starts now and runs in parallel.** The meeting cadence is biweekly
  (next ≈ **2026-09-06**). A question asked on 09-06 is answered on 09-20. The list lives in chapter 12, Open
  questions and unverified claims, C.2 and C.3, with three additions in §11.12; the successor sends all of them
  at once, in `proj-lsfm`, this week.

### 11.6 P2 — v1.1: foreground separation and artefact-resistant features

This is where the effort that used to go into global search now goes. The reasoning: foreground separation is
the common root cause of I56, I58 and I61 on the MRI side and of the agarose problem on the OCT side; it is the
one thing on the list a position prior does not help with; and it stands between the project and a result on
**our own data**, which is what the PI asked for next.

The three engineering items below are stated with the files to change, the experiment that validates them, and
the metric that shows success. **None of the three has been started beyond a prototype.**

#### 11.6.1 P2.1 — the bath-heavy MRI tissue mask

The MRI is scanned with the hemisphere in fluid. Bath and tissue differ in **texture**, not in mean intensity,
so a histogram method has nothing to cut on: `histogram_tissue_threshold` walks left from the rightmost
prominent peak looking for a valley below `0.5 ×` the smaller neighbouring peak, finds none, and **falls back to
a floor that keeps almost everything** while writing `valley_ratio: null`.

The full per-subject `prep.json` diagnostic table — `tissue_thresh`, `tissue_fraction`, `valley_ratio`, MRI
"tissue" volume, search scores, refined NCC, restart counts and verdict for all nine DANDI subjects and the
brainstem pair — is canonical in **chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us, §7.1.1**. Read it
there; it is not repeated here. Three readings of it drive this section.

**The fail-open signature covers exactly three subjects: I56, I58 and I61.** Each has `valley_ratio: null` and
a `tissue_thresh` far *below* its own median intensity — I56 3.62 against 15.1, I58 2.12 against 16.9, I61 6.80
against 10.4 — with "tissue" fractions of 0.989, 0.587 and 0.742.

**It does not cover I57, and it does not cover I48.** I57's threshold 15.77 sits *above* its median 13.8, its
fraction is 0.209, and it found a valley at 0.0631. I48's fraction is 0.156 with the largest `valley_ratio` in
the corpus, 0.4737. Both have a `valley_ratio` printed, not missing — as do I46 (**0.1161**) and I38
(**0.1984**). I57 is wrong anyway, for a reason nobody has `[OPEN]`; I48 is undecidable on its 0.0013 search
margin, which is a different problem again.

**The size of the failure, in the only units that matter.** Take the expected volume of a hemisphere from the
data rather than from memory. The MRI tissue volumes recorded in `work/<SUB>/prep.json` on the compute server
(`tissue_fraction × grid volume`) run **386.3 – 805.8 cm³** across the six subjects whose mask behaves normally
— I48 386.3, I57 518.0, I62 531.5, I55 620.5, I46 802.9, I38 805.8 (the band is established and derived once,
in chapter 4, The data, §4.3). **806 cm³ is the expected upper end of a hemisphere used everywhere in this
document, and every threshold below is derived from it.** Against that band
I58's mask is 1 453.4 cm³, I61's is 1 838.8 cm³ — 2.3× the top of the band — and I56's is 2 519.0 cm³, 3.1×.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Files to change** | `octreg/octreg/common.py` — `histogram_tissue_threshold`, lines 214–237 (the fail-open branch); `octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py` — MRI mask construction and the `prep.json` fields it writes. Prototype already on the server: `octreg/scripts/test_texture_mask.py` → `work/texture_mask_test.png` (7-px uniform-filter variance → σ = 2 Gaussian → Otsu → closing ×2 → fill holes → largest connected component) |
| **The design constraint** | `octreg/EXPLAINER_zh.md` §4 records that **pure texture thresholding failed on both datasets**. The fix is texture *fused with* intensity, not texture instead of it. Do not repeat the prototype as-is |
| **Experiment** | Re-prep I56, I58, I61 with the fused mask; re-prep I46, I55, I38, I48, I57, I62 as no-regression controls; re-register all nine with flags identical to `logs/reg_*_otsu.log` |
| **Success metric** | (a) `mri.tissue_fraction` for I56/I58/I61 lands in the 0.15–0.35 band the six healthy subjects occupy, and their tissue volume falls below the **≈1 210 cm³** gate and inside the measured **386–806 cm³** band; (b) `valley_ratio` is non-null for all three, or the fused mask makes the field obsolete; (c) I61 and I58 move to a pose with non-degenerate BA-label containment and Dice; (d) **no regression**: I46 stays at 0.803/0.825 and I55 at 0.921/0.930 within ±0.01, and I46's vessel median stays at 166.7 µm / f150 0.473 within noise |
| **What it does not settle** | I57. Its mask is fine and it still fails, and nothing here explains it `[OPEN]`. Treat it as a separate investigation: open `results_inspection/I57_otsu/` and check whether the `flip-4` contrast has usable GM/WM separation at all, which is exactly why I58 failed. §11.12 carries no question for it because it is ours to answer rather than the PI's; it is logged as C1.3 in chapter 12, Open questions and unverified claims |

#### 11.6.2 P2.2 — agarose versus tissue on the brainstem OCT

`logs/prep_xiangrui.log` records `raw tissue thr 0.0` and `oct150 tissue frac 0.779`. The OCT "tissue" volume
is **28.9 cm³** against the cropped MRI's **13.3 cm³** — the OCT mask is more than twice the volume of the
thing it is supposed to match, because the block is embedded in agarose and intensity cannot tell agarose from
tissue. That is why the overlap gate had to become adaptive at all: on this pair it relaxes from the requested 0.85
to an effective **0.369**, and without that relaxation a fixed 0.85 rejects **every** pose. The formula and its
0.15 floor are written out once, in full, in chapter 5, The method, as a chain of reasoning, §5.2.3.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Files to change** | the same threshold path — `octreg/octreg/common.py::histogram_tissue_threshold` and the OCT branch of `octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py`; and once it works, revisit the adaptive floor in `octreg/scripts/register.py:111` |
| **Experiment** | Re-prep `data/xiangrui/OCT_to_MRI/I58_Brainstem_mus_Slice_full_20um_corr.nii.gz` (13 025 490 607 B, 1457 × 2013 × 1595 at 20 µm isotropic) with the fused texture+intensity mask; re-run `register.py` with the `xiangrui_I58bs_novasc` flags; compare `overlap_gate`, the accepted pose and the refined NCC |
| **Success metric** | (a) OCT tissue volume drops from 28.9 cm³ toward the MRI's 13.3 cm³ — concretely, `V_OCT ≤ 15.2 cm³` raises the effective gate from **0.369 to ≥ 0.70**, and `V_OCT ≤ 12.5 cm³` restores the requested 0.85; (b) the gate stops binding, i.e. `overlap_gate.effective == overlap_gate.requested`; (c) the refined NCC at the accepted pose rises; (d) visually, the block face no longer carries an agarose rim in `results_inspection/` |
| **Why it matters beyond this pair** | Every specimen the lab scans itself will be agarose-embedded. This is not an I58 problem, it is a *our-data* problem, and D12's adaptive gate is a workaround that hides it |

#### 11.6.3 P2.3 — section seams defeating the vessel channel

On the brainstem the OCT "vessels" are not vessels. The top-1 % dark-tube Frangi response returns
**4 534 410 voxels**, the vessel-channel NCC at the structural pose is **0.0055**, **0 of 8** vascular restarts
converged, the stage moved the block 2.652 mm in the wrong direction, and it consumed **4 778.4 s of a
5 244.0 s** run. The `novasc` variant of the same pair finishes in **362.3 s** and is the result the PI was
shown.

The physical cause is that serial-sectioning leaves a periodic intensity discontinuity at every cut face, and a
dark-tube filter cannot distinguish a planar seam from a tubular vessel when the seam is thin.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Files to change** | `octreg/octreg/features.py` — `frangi_dark_vesselness` and the top-1 % dark-tube selection; `octreg/scripts/prep_subject.py:125` — `window = max(10, int(round(1200.0 / sp[0])))`, the per-slice normalisation window; `octreg/octreg/vascular.py` and `octreg/scripts/register.py` — the auto-disable rule from §11.2.4 |
| **The ordering inside this item** | Seams are **periodic**. Measure the period *first* (per-slice in-tissue median, detrend with a 301-slice running mean, then FFT + autocorrelation — the method is in chapter 4, The data, §4.8.3, and `/tmp/period.py` survives on the box), then notch it out of the normalisation, then re-test whether Frangi finds anything vessel-like. Doing it in the other order wastes GPU on a filter that is looking at an artefact |
| **Experiment** | (1) measure the brainstem seam period and compare against the asserted `slab_window = 60` at 20 µm, which has never been checked `[UNVERIFIED]`; (2) set the window to an integer multiple of the measured period; (3) re-prep and re-run with `--vascular on`; (4) run the same three scrambling controls used on I46 (depth-flip, k-slice permutation, channel removed) so the result is non-circular if it works |
| **Success metric** | (a) top-1 % dark-tube voxel count falls from 4 534 410 to a physiologically plausible number — for scale, I46's vessel channel supports a median vessel distance of 166.7 µm; (b) vessel-channel NCC at the structural pose rises from 0.0055 above the ~0.05 auto-disable floor; (c) vascular restarts converge > 0/8; (d) the vascular stage improves rather than degrades the pose, judged by the same checkerboard panels; (e) the run stops spending 91 % of its wall clock on it |
| **The honest fallback** | If seams cannot be separated from vessels on this specimen, the correct outcome is that the auto-disable rule fires and the brainstem ships as a structural-only affine — which is what `xiangrui_I58bs_novasc` already is. That is a legitimate result. It is not a reason to leave a 4 778-second stage running |

#### 11.6.4 P2.4 — per-subject section period

Replace the asserted `1 200 µm` in `prep_subject.py:125` with a measured period × an integer. The comment
`# ~1.2 mm of depth = one section period at 12 um` is wrong by ~3×; its origin is
`/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/costantini_b0/reports/costantini_i46_data_audit.md:43`, a mean-profile
inspection at 25-slice granularity that
aliased a 33-slice period to ≈100. I46 survives by luck (window 100 ≈ 3 periods); **I56's window is 2.83
periods**, leaving a residual sawtooth in the very channel the registration reads.

Measure it on all nine DANDI subjects and the brainstem pair (~10 min CPU each, read-only). The measurement is
worth more than the window fix, because `period × declared_spacing` is **0.396 mm** for I46 and **0.420 mm** for
I56 — which says the vibratome cut is ≈0.40–0.42 mm, not the nominal 500 µm, and therefore that the period
argument implies only a **1.06** correction for I46's depth spacing rather than 1.167. That line of evidence is
already **withdrawn** — see the corrections table at the head of this chapter, and chapter 4, The data, §4.8.3.
If the same product comes out at 0.40–0.42 mm across all nine, it is withdrawn formally rather than quietly
wrong, and the depth-scale story is left standing on its three surviving anchors.

#### 11.6.5 P2.5 — where a learned model is allowed, and where it is not

If a learned model is used anywhere in this project, it is in the foreground/bath discriminator. It needs
**coarse masks, not layer labels**, so it does not violate constraint 1 — unlike the 3-D U-Net parser, which
needs `labels4.npy` from a manual whole-hemisphere segmentation that our own specimens will never have
(chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us, §7.3.3).

**Do not enable the non-rigid stage during P2.** A free-form deformation would improve the loss on exactly the
runs that are in the wrong place, and the QC figure would look *better*, not worse. An affine cannot do that.
Re-enable it after the foreground problem is fixed — the code is written and its ceiling is measured (D9), so
it is a fifteen-minute change whenever it becomes appropriate.

### 11.11 What would make this publishable

#### 11.11.1 What is supportable today, in one paragraph

On **two** subjects of one public dataset, a label-free, training-free, prior-optional pipeline places an
OCT specimen into a whole hemisphere, and two independent manual annotations agree at the millimetre scale. On
one of those two, hand-drawn vessels agree at a **166.7 µm median / 47.3 % within 150 µm**, which is the
annotation's own ceiling (an oracle affine fitted directly to those annotations reaches f150 0.466;
cross-validated on held-out vessel components, 0.416 ± 0.041). A scale factor the structural objective provably
cannot see is recovered automatically and lands where three independent human-derived sources say it should,
with an apparent null on the control subject — apparent, because that control subject's own recovered
anisotropy is **0.8570 = 6/7**, the exact inverse of the factor in question. That is a workshop paper. It is
not yet a top-journal paper: one of its supporting legs, the 33-slice section-period anchor, has been
**withdrawn outright**, and another, the claim that I55 is a clean null, is under revision.

#### 11.11.2 The gaps between here and submittable

| Gap | Why a reviewer stops | Cost to close |
|---|---|---|
| **G1. n = 2.** Evaluation is valid on two subjects out of nine | "Validated on 9 subjects" is not true. And the *hard* version of the problem — a 0.09 % block in a whole hemisphere — is demonstrated on **one** subject; the other eight are 0.5–7.2 % chunks, which is a materially easier retrieval | P1.1 (fixes six subjects' labels) + P4.2 (adds I45, I60, which carry OCT vessel segmentations). Realistically 4–5 subjects with tier-1 evidence |
| **G2. No baseline was run.** The comparison is a reading of `mri2oct_affine.sh`, and their published pose disagrees with ours by 23 mm | It is the first table a methods reviewer looks for | P4.1. State the honest blocker: the OCT GM/WM masks were never published, so exact reproduction is impossible — say so, run the approximation, and run MI |
| **G3. No TRE anywhere,** including on our own data | Registration papers report a distance in millimetres | P3.1. One message and ~30 min of a human's time |
| **G4. The random-placement control is a ±3 mm nudge** | It is the weakest link in the evidence chain | P3.3, ~1 h |
| **G5. The scale story has three readings and none is clean** | It is the paper's intellectual core, and I55 — the subject offered as the decisive control — returns an anisotropy of exactly 6/7, the inverse of the factor I46 is supposed to be missing | P1.8, two 20-minute jobs. **This is the cheapest high-stakes experiment in the project** |
| **G6. NCC is not comparable across subjects, in either stage** | The project's own tables put `top1` side by side as if 0.726 (I46), 0.611 (I55) and 0.257 (I48) were commensurable. The template volume differs by 40×, and — this is a reading of the numbers, not a measured law — a small homogeneous specimen scores higher masked NCC than a large heterogeneous slab almost regardless of correctness. The same holds for the refined score, and there the counterexample is decisive: **I61 scores `refine.final_ncc` 0.5020 and I57 scores 0.5121 and both are wrong, while I62 scores 0.2842 and is correct.** No numeric acceptance threshold on `refine.final_ncc` may be stated anywhere without that sentence beside it | A size-normalised statistic, or drop the cross-subject comparison. It also explains why score magnitude has been such a poor guide to correctness |
| **G7. No independent benchmark exists for this task**, so every number had to be argued from first principles | Cuts both ways — see §11.11.4 | — |

#### 11.11.3 Three things that are already written and would strengthen the paper more than new experiments

1. **The Jacobian argument — the motivation paragraph the project does not have.** The authors'
   `stereo_warp.py` multiplies every stereology counting-frame volume by the determinant of the composed
   registration Jacobian, and `stereo_project.py` then computes `density = counts / volumes`. Therefore **a
   systematic error ε in the depth scale of the OCT→MRI affine is a systematic error ε in every published cell
   density**. For I46 the disputed factor is 1.17–1.22 — a 17–22 % error in the census's headline number, not a
   cosmetic misplacement. This converts "why does registration accuracy matter" from an assertion into
   arithmetic. `[UNVERIFIED]` on the last link: that the `warp2surf/` outputs are what the paper's figures were
   made from — settle it by reading the figure captions. The two files are `scripts/registration/stereo_warp.py` and
   `stereo_project.py` in `github.com/neuroscales/biccn-broca-I46` (chapter 8, How this compares to the
   published method, §8.2.1).
2. **The two physical alternatives to the metadata story, ruled out quantitatively in one table.** A reviewer
   with OCT experience will ask whether the 1.17 is clearing-induced shrinkage or a refractive-index error.
   Isotropic dimensional change predicts **1.072 on all three axes** at det = 1.2327; the measured spectra are
   one-axis on all three routes that produce a spectrum at all (authors' `affine.lta` singular values 1.2115 / 1.0359 / 0.9822; our
   oracle 1.177 / 0.999 / 1.046; our label-free 1.219 / 0.977 / 1.031). Refractive index would require
   `n_true = 1.4 / 1.17 = 1.197`, below water and impossible for TDE-equilibrated tissue — and it has the wrong
   sign. Population-level: the geometric mean of the absolute determinant over the five correct runs is **0.983**, so there is no
   dataset-wide shrinkage signature at all. The honest residual: two axes sit at 1.03–1.05 rather than 1.00, so
   a few-percent isotropic component is compatible and cannot be separated from registration error
   (chapter 4, The data, §4.5.2).
3. **The authors believed the 12 µm.** `lsfm_slide_center_and_scale.py:30` hard-codes `vx_new[2] = 0.396 / 50`
   — exactly 33 slices × 12 µm. They kept the sidecar spacing and let the affine absorb the entire 1.174 as a
   registration parameter. That means **their 1.174 and our 1.219 measure the same thing in the same units**,
   which is what makes the agreement an agreement rather than a coincidence of conventions (chapter 8, How this
   compares to the published method, §8.6.4). Note what this argument is and is not: it is about **units and
   conventions**, and it is *not* the withdrawn 33-slice period line of evidence.

#### 11.11.4 Three framings, and which one the evidence supports

| Framing | What it needs | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **Method paper** ("a better OCT→MRI registration") | G1 + G2 + G3 | Weakest fit. The components are all prior art: coarse-to-fine affine, FFT translation search, masked NCC, Frangi, Otsu, local-mean bias correction, MIND, and the idea of vessels as the cross-modal landmark — which is **the baseline's own idea**. The defensible one-line framing is *"we removed two human inputs from an existing validated pipeline and showed that the one thing lost — the depth-axis scale — can be recovered from automatically segmented vasculature"* |
| **Negative-result / analysis paper** ("structure-only similarity is blind along one axis, and here is what to do about it") | Mostly done: the sweep, the independent estimates of ~1.17, the reverse control on I55 (carried with its 0.8570 = 6/7 caveat), the oracle ceiling, the scrambling controls — plus §11.11.3's two ruled-out physical alternatives | Strongest fit to the evidence that already exists. Claims #2 and #4 of the ladder both live here. Small venue. **Gated on P1.8**: the I55 anisotropy has to be explained before this paper can be written honestly |
| **Benchmark + method** ("the first end-to-end label-free pipeline *and* the first public evaluation protocol for cm-scale OCT specimen → whole-hemisphere MRI") | G1 + G2 + G3 + G4, plus publishing the transforms and the protocol | **Best fit.** The lab's own review records the gap: no public, peer-reviewed benchmark exists for a human, centimetre-scale 3-D OCT specimen, of unknown position, registered into a whole-hemisphere MRI with independent TRE annotation. We hold the only worked example, and the two things we lack (a TRE protocol and baseline runs) are exactly what a benchmark paper has to provide anyway. It converts the project's biggest weakness — no ground truth — into its subject. It also makes U11 (block-to-block consistency) a first-class contribution rather than a nice idea |

The PI has said the cross-modality line is *tentatively a top journal* and the higher-impact of the lab's two
workstreams (chapter 9, The lab: people, history, and the constraints that shape this work, §9.3.1). Of the
three framings only the third is plausibly a top-journal object — and **nobody has decided**, which is why Q6
in chapter 12, Open questions and unverified claims, C.2 is the highest-value question on the whole list.

#### 11.11.5 What must be true before submission

- Every Dice quoted is from a subject with a lossless label mapping.
- Every number quoted was produced by a version of the code that still exists (H10).
- No `rotation_deg` appears anywhere until H7 is fixed.
- The vessel numbers are always the `vessels_vesseg` channel — the authors' manual OCT segmentation, which the
  pipeline never sees — never `vessels_own`, the channel the vascular stage optimises.
- Restart consistency is reported as a **stability** statistic, with the damning fact volunteered: the two
  tightest-converging runs, **I58 and I61 at 12/12**, are both marked wrong, and mean convergence is 11.3/12 for
  wrong runs against 10.2/12 for correct ones. (Do **not** include I57 in that list — it is 10/12, not 12/12.)
- The depth-scale agreement is presented as **corroboration between scale magnitudes in two different
  coordinate conventions**, never as a TRE and never to three decimals — and it is presented with I55's
  **0.8570 = 6/7** anisotropy stated and I38's **0.861** labelled as the clamp bound `exp(−0.15)`, not omitted.
- The specimen-size table (0.09 % to 7.19 % of a hemisphere) appears wherever "partial-to-whole" is claimed.
- The figures have been opened by a human.
