| Work | What it does | Relation to this project | Why it is not the same problem |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Costantini et al. 2023**, *Sci Adv* 9 eadg3844; DANDI:000026; `github.com/neuroscales/biccn-broca-I46` | The direct predecessor. Their registration pipeline is transcribed flag by flag in chapter 8, How this compares to the published method, §8.2, and their acquisition parameters in chapter 4, The data, §4.1 — neither is repeated here | **The baseline.** Same data, same specimen, same modality pair | Needs an MRI **pre-cropped by a human** and **six hand-drawn annotation products**. Their end-to-end cortical-boundary validation is p95 **527 ± 137 µm**, p75 **306 ± 96 µm** `[UNVERIFIED]` — not checked against the page renders. Their OCT GM/WM masks were never released |
| **Tward et al. 2020**, EM-LDDMM (`papers/fnins-14-00052.pdf`, grade A) | Joint diffeomorphism + non-monotonic polynomial intensity transform + per-pixel matching/background/artifact posteriors, damaged multi-stain histology → MRI/atlas | The explicit missing-data ablation, and the right model of "part of the moving image is not in the fixed image" | Does **not** do blind localisation. Initialisation is given |
| **Osechinskiy & Kruggel 2011** (grade A) | Human myelin sections (50 µm) → same-donor 0.35 mm MRI; systematic CC/SSD/NMI × TPS/GEBS/B-spline comparison; `NEWUOA → TPS + CC` wins | The closest classical histology→MRI precedent, and the source of the "coarse-to-fine affine is textbook" claim | 2-D sections, manual initialisation, no partial-to-whole search |
| **mBrainAligner** (`papers/v1_covered.pdf`, grade A) | Whole mouse brain fMOST/VISoR/LSFM/MRI → CCFv3: outer-contour + DA-RPM global affine, coherent 2.5-D landmarks, 3-D U-Net region probabilities, TPS. Median Dice 0.82–0.90 | The nearest multi-modality microscopy→reference pipeline that works | **Whole-to-whole.** Its partial example uses semi-automatic editing. Mouse, not human |
| **CrossKEY**, IEEE TMI 2026 (`papers/2507.18551v2.pdf`, grade A) | 3-D MRI ↔ intraoperative US: shared 3-D ResNet-18 descriptor, curriculum triplet loss, 3-round rigid RANSAC, no manual init at inference. TRE **2.385 ± 0.397 mm** | The concrete template if a learned localizer is ever wanted | Needs training pairs of exactly the kind our target specimens do not have; rigid only |
| **Mancini 2020 / NextBrain** (in the lab's own review) | Whole hemisphere cut into ~1.5 cm coronal blocks, blockwise registration with inter-block overlap/gap regularisation, shared initialisation across the cutting hierarchy, L1 Bayesian consensus | **The template for U11**, the jigsaw constraint nobody has exploited | Its blocks are cut on a known grid, ours arrive one at a time |
| **DINO-Reg**, **multiGradICON**, **uniGradICON**, **MatchAnything**, **PromptReg** (grades B/B−) | Training-free or generalist cross-modal registration on pretrained features | Post-crop controls and feature ablations | All assume near-same-FOV pairs. None does blind partial-to-whole localisation; `multiGradICON` v2 carries an erratum — quote only the corrected tables |
| The lab's own **B0–B5 ladder** (`literature_review/working/classical_partial_methods.md`) | B0 Costantini as-is; B1 Aladin multi-start → masked MI affine → ANTs SyN; B1b Aladin → masked NMI `reg_f3d`; B2 MIND-SSC + ConvexAdam; B2m Tward EM-LDDMM; B3 overlap-aware initializer; B4 zero-shot generalists; B5 trained-from-scratch | The comparison plan, already written | **None of B0–B5 has been run.** B2 is the only one measured, indirectly, and it failed badly (MIND top1 0.219) |

### 11.13 If a successor only does six things

1. **Rescue and version the code** (P0). Twenty-one files exist only on a rented container that reassigns its
   address on every restart, and the tree has no commit history of any kind.
2. **Fix `map_labels_to_grid` and re-evaluate the six 0.12 mm subjects** (P1.1). It costs an hour, needs no
   re-registration, and it is the difference between "5 of 9 correct" and "2 of 9 confirmed".
3. **Implement the two reject gates and surface `valley_ratio`** (P1.3). Twenty lines that turn three silent
   failures into three flagged ones, using fields already written into `result.json` and `prep.json`.
4. **Re-prep I46 at 14 µm and I55 at 12 µm** (P1.8). Forty minutes of GPU that decide whether the project's
   intellectual core survives contact with its own control subject.
5. **Ask for the twenty matched points** (P3.1; chapter 12, Open questions and unverified claims, C.2 Q3), and
   send the authors' email in its four-part form (§11.12 Q8) in the same hour. One
   message each; between them they are the only route to a number on the lab's own data and the only route to a
   sub-millimetre external check on the public data.
6. **Move the effort from global search to foreground separation** (P2). It is the common root cause of every
   failure a position prior does not fix, and it is the last thing standing between this project and a
   defensible result on our own specimen.

## 12. Open questions and unverified claims

Nothing in this chapter is new measurement. It is the residue of the verification passes that produced
this handoff, collected in one place so that a successor does not have to rediscover which numbers in
the project's own files are stale, which claims rest on a single unrepeated measurement, and which
questions nobody has answered.

Why a chapter like this is necessary here specifically: **the project is unversioned.**
`/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project` is not a git repository at all, and
`/Users/yyttim/workspace/oct-mri-registration` has exactly one commit (`88013e5`, "Add reproducible
Costantini data setup") and three tracked files — `.gitignore`, `README.md` and
`download_costantini.sh`. The 55-module `octreg/` tree is tracked by nothing anywhere. There is
therefore no diff trail, no blame, and no way to ask "when did this number change and why". Numbers
propagated between `octreg/README.md`, `EXPLAINER_zh.md`, `octreg/MEETING_2026-08-21.md`,
`octreg/TALK_2026-08-21.md`, `octreg/results_inspection/INDEX.md`, `WORKSPACE_STATE.md` and the PI's
Google Doc by copy-paste, and several of them were wrong at the point of first writing. A stale number
that has been copied into five documents looks like five independent confirmations. §A exists to break
that illusion.

**How disagreements were settled.** Every row in §A was re-checked against a primary artefact — a file
on the compute server (`ssh -p 49018 root@connect.westb.seetacloud.com`, tree
`~/autodl-tmp/oct-mri-registration`), a file in the local repo, a meeting recording, or the published
paper — and the primary artefact wins over any prose that quotes it, including prose written earlier in
this project's own working notes. Where two artefacts genuinely disagree, both are shown and the
disagreement is recorded as open rather than resolved by fiat; those cases are §A.8 and §C.6. The
provenance markers `[UNVERIFIED]`, `[NOT RE-MEASURED]` and `[OPEN]` are used throughout with the
meanings given in chapter 2, Orientation and glossary.

A practical consequence worth stating before the tables: **the corrections below have been applied to
this handoff document, and have NOT been applied to the project's own files.** `octreg/README.md`,
`EXPLAINER_zh.md`, `prep_subject.py`'s comments, `common.py`'s docstring, `results_inspection/INDEX.md`
and the Google Doc still say the old things. §A.10 is the edit list for those files.

#### A.4 Evaluation validity and metric bugs

This is the most consequential group. Two of the four "successful" verdicts and all four failure
diagnoses rest on Dice numbers that are computed against a corrupted label volume.

| # | Claim as written | Where it appeared | Verified value | How verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A4.1** | The label-loss audit flags only I56 and I48 **vessel** labels as lossy | the data notes' label-quality audit | **Incomplete.** The **whole-hemisphere** labels lose **31.7–41.6 %** on all six 0.12 mm subjects. I46 and I55 (0.15 mm) are **exactly lossless** (111 293 541 and 127 943 011 nonzero, source count = mapped count) | Source label counts against `work/*/prep.json → labels4_counts` on the compute server |
| **A4.2** | The cause is "the label box covers only ~68 % of the MRI FOV" | a diagnosis proposed during the audit and rejected | **Wrong, and the truth is worse: the axis pairing itself is wrong.** `prep_subject.py::map_labels_to_grid` lines 42–53 computes `M = inv(A_label) @ A_ref`, takes `perm[r] = argmax\|M[r,:3]\|`, and zeroes every MRI voxel whose label index is out of range. The two 0.15 mm subjects get `perm = [2,0,1]`, pairing **equal-length axes** (576↔576, 1280↔1280, 1040↔1040) — lossless. The six 0.12 mm subjects get `perm = [1,2,0]`, pairing a **640-voxel** label axis against a **1400-voxel** MRI axis; only **36–40 %** of the MRI grid ever receives a label lookup. The shape-consistent `transpose(1,2,0)` is lossless and puts **99.0 %** of labels on tissue against **87.8 %** now. Root cause is in the headers: for I38 the label world box is 76.8 × 192 × 168 mm assigned L–R / A–P / I–S (anatomically sensible for a hemisphere) while the MRI header assigns 168 mm to L–R and 76.8 mm to A–P (not sensible). **The EPIC MRI affine is the broken one for the 0.12 mm subjects** | Raw headers of the label and MRI volumes on the compute server, plus the four throwaway scripts `/tmp/aff.py`, `/tmp/bb.py`, `/tmp/ov.py`, `/tmp/alt.py`. I38 alternative mapping retains **3 856 521** labels vs **2 528 749** (ratio 1.525, matching the 1.521 count ratio) and scores 0.9900 vs 0.8782 on tissue, with **all eight** flip variants beating the current mapping |
| **A4.3** | The three "correct (visual only)" verdicts for I38/I56/I62 are contradicted by the label evidence | the results and interpretation drafts | **The contradicting evidence is itself invalid.** Every `dice_WM`, `dice_GM` and `frac_on_mri_labels` for **I38, I48, I56, I57, I58, I61** in `work/runs/*/result.json` and `results_inspection/` is computed against a corrupted label volume. **Not invalidated: the registrations themselves.** Search and refinement never touch the labels — they run on the MRI's own voxel grid with isotropic spacing and an exhaustive orientation search, so a wrong world-axis labelling in a *label* header cannot bias the transform. **I46 and I55 Dice (0.803/0.825 and 0.921/0.930) are unaffected** and are the only two Dice values in the project that may be quoted | The `perm` derivation of A4.2 applied to each subject. The fix costs ~1 h and needs **re-prep + re-evaluation only**, no re-registration, because `result.json` stores `final_transform` |
| **A4.4** | I57's low scores are caused by the MRI foreground mask | the failure-diagnosis prose, and `octreg/results_inspection/INDEX.md` | **Two separate corrections.** (a) Only **6.56 %** of I57's BA labels and **57.9 %** of its whole-hemisphere labels land on MRI tissue, which alone explains `labels_agreement_wholehemi_vs_ba = 0.671` and Dice 0.0 — I57's evaluation is untrustworthy either way. The full per-subject diagnostic panel is in chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us (§7.1.1) |

##### A.4a One number used document-wide: the expected volume of a human hemisphere

Several rows above and the reject gate of §C.7 depend on knowing how big a hemisphere is. **This
document fixes that figure once, from the MRI tissue volumes this pipeline actually measured**, and the
band is established and derived in full in **chapter 4, The data, §4.3**. In brief:
`work/<SUBJ>/prep.json`'s `mri.tissue_fraction` × field of view gives
**386–806 cm³** across the six subjects whose mask behaves sensibly — I48 386.3, I57 518.0, I62 531.5,
I55 620.5, I46 802.9, I38 805.8, median 576 — and that band, anchored on its **806 cm³** top, is what the
document uses wherever an expected-hemisphere figure is needed. The three broken masks sit far outside it:
I56 2 519.0, I61 1 838.8, I58 1 453.4 cm³. Every threshold in this chapter that derives from a hemisphere
volume derives from that 806 cm³ top and from nothing else, giving the single reject gate
`1.5 × 806 ≈ 1 210 cm³`.

#### A.5 Code, pipeline behaviour and documentation

| # | Claim as written | Where it appeared | Verified value | How verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A5.1** | "with the **default** `--oct-wm-bright auto` … the search runs twice" | the first audit pass, and early drafts of this document | **`auto` is not the default.** `register.py:32`: `choices=["auto","yes","no"], default="no"`. Every DANDI run passed it **explicitly** — `run_subject.sh` line 21 hard-codes `--oct-wm-bright auto`. The 2× doubling is a property of the shipped wrapper, not of a bare `register.py` invocation. **A successor calling `register.py` directly will silently get single-polarity behaviour** and, on I46, the *wrong* polarity, since the coarse search prefers it (0.7411 vs 0.7259) and only the refined NCC separates them (0.7564 vs 0.7300) | `grep -n add_argument octreg/scripts/register.py`; `cat octreg/scripts/run_subject.sh`; `args.oct_wm_bright == "auto"` in all nine `result.json` |
| **A5.2** | I46's headline numbers are reproducible with the code on disk | implied everywhere. #### A.8 Corrections that correct other corrections

Five places where the audit trail itself needed care, because a first pass got something wrong and a
second pass reversed it. Each is stated here as a finished adjudication, not as a running argument.

| # | Dispute | Adjudication |
|---|---|---|
| **A8.1** | The provenance offered for the "150 s" figure | The first explanation — that 150 s was the 8 000-of-16 000 halfway progress tick — is **replaced**. See **A1.3**: 153.7 s is a real logged measurement of the parser-feature entry point and "150 s" is a rounding of it. The corrected numbers (299 / 598 / 44.8–1010.3 s) are unaffected |
| **A8.2** | The restatement of the nine-run range as "1 082–7 864 s" | **Wrong at the low end.** See **A1.7**: 1 082.2 s is `I46_parser`, which is not one of the nine otsu runs. The minimum is 1 124.7 s |
| **A8.3** | **The "33-slice section period" line of evidence for the I46 depth-spacing bug.** It was written up as a third, then promoted to a fourth, independent confirmation: a 500 µm vibratome cut divided by a measured 33-slice period gives **15.15 µm per slice**, therefore I46's 12 µm sidecar is too small | **WITHDRAWN. Do not present it as confirming evidence anywhere, and do not re-derive it.** The identical arithmetic on I56 gives 500 µm / 12.17 slices = **41.7 µm** against a **35 µm** sidecar that is corroborated **twice inside the file** (ImageJ `spacing=0.035`, `XResolution 33.3333`) *and* by registration — I56's recovered depth stretch is **0.998**, i.e. the pipeline finds no error at all. The premise cannot hold for both subjects. Read consistently, the two measured periods say the real cut is **≈0.40–0.42 mm**, not 500 µm; applying I56's 0.42 mm to I46 gives 420/33 = **12.7 µm**, a correction of only **1.06** — not the **1.167** the sidecars give. The 500 µm premise is itself `[UNVERIFIED]` (B2.1). **If a document counts "a fourth independent line" or "a fifth" for the I46 depth-spacing bug, recount without this one and fix the ordinal: there are three.** The three that survive — the sibling sidecars' exact 7/6, the authors' 1.17419 affine column, and an oracle affine fitted to manual labels and vessels — are laid out in chapter 4, The data (§4.5) and chapter 6, What we found, and what it means (§6.11.2). **The I46 sidecar bug does not depend on the withdrawn line** and stands without it. The measured period remains a true and useful fact *about the de-sawtooth window* (A3.3) — that is all it is |

Two further qualifications that are not disputes, but that nobody had drawn and that change how two
frequently quoted results should be read:

| # | Qualification | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **A8.4** | **I55 is presented as "the decisive comparison" — a clean reverse control** supporting the I46 sidecar bug: its sidecar depth spacing is right, so the pipeline should find no depth correction, and its vascular stage moves the block only 0.334 mm | **It is not clean, and the qualification must travel with it every time I55 is used as a null result.** I55's recovered depth/in-plane anisotropy is **0.8570, which equals 6/7 to four decimal places** — the exact *inverse* of the 7/6 factor I46 is supposed to be missing — on the subject whose sidecar `[12,12,14]` is corroborated twice inside its own file. That is decisive evidence that *something* is systematically wrong with depth in this dataset; it is **not** evidence for the current story. Three readings exist — (A) an I46-only sidecar bug; (B) the 7/6 sidecars are the erroneous ones; (C) ±15 % anisotropy is registration error absorbed by the least-constrained direction — and **none of the three is clean**. The handoff's prose presents (A) as settled; it is not. See **C5.4** |
| **A8.5** | The 1.17 depth factor is discussed only as a metadata question | The two **physical** alternatives are never named and both are ruled out quantitatively: isotropic clearing-induced change predicts 1.072 on *all three* axes at det 1.2327, against an observed spectrum of 1.21 / 1.04 / 0.98; refractive-index mismatch would need `n_true = 1.20`, below water. Also: the authors themselves **hard-code `vx_new[2] = 0.396 / 50`** in their `scripts/registration/lsfm_slide_center_and_scale.py:30` — exactly 33 slices × 12 µm — so they believed the 12 µm and let the affine absorb the whole 1.174 as a registration parameter. **Their 1.174 and our 1.219 are therefore measuring the same thing in the same units** |

Also confirmed, and worth restating because it is easy to mis-read: **the depth-scale negative result
is stronger than the prose says, not weaker.** The three-axis scale probe (canonical table and full
discussion in **chapter 6, What we found, and what it means, §6.10.3**) shows the objective's
sensitivity to a 45 % stretch is about **8× smaller along depth than along the k axis** — Δ NCC 0.021
against 0.169 — and the widely quoted "the whole 0.85–1.30 range spans only 0.713–0.727" is wrong
because the writer read only the ascending half; the true depth span is **0.706–0.727**. Along depth
the *manual labels* still resolve a maximum at s = 1.100 that the NCC essentially cannot see, its own
maximum sitting at 1.075 on a 0.021-wide plateau.

### B — Claims carried without independent verification

Every `[UNVERIFIED]` and `[NOT RE-MEASURED]` claim in the material, with what it would take to settle
each. **None of these is known to be false.** They are claims for which no artefact was found, or which
rest on a single measurement that was recorded and then trusted. **Do not silently promote any of them
to fact.** The markers themselves are defined in chapter 2, Orientation and glossary.

#### B.1 Claims about our own method and results

| # | Claim | Where it is asserted | What is actually established | What would verify it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B1.1** | "the true depth scale is **~1.18**" `[UNVERIFIED]` | the depth-scale prose | **No artefact on disk carries 1.18.** The two defensible anchors are the pipeline's own recovered **1.219** (`work/runs/I46_otsu/result.json → final_transform.stretch_ijk[0]`) and the sidecar-vs-siblings ratio **14/12 = 1.1667** | Ask Yuntian which one was meant (C4.1). There is nothing to measure — this is a writing ambiguity, not an experiment |
| **B1.2** | "the vascular channel sees the depth scale that the tissue geometry cannot" `[UNVERIFIED]` as a single-axis claim | the method rationale and every forward plan built on it | The **end-to-end** result supports it: turning the vascular stage on moves I46's depth stretch 1.026 → 1.219 and the honest `ves_seg` vessel metric 265 → **167 µm**, f150 0.283 → 0.473, against an oracle ceiling of 0.466. The **single-axis probe does not**: in `work/runs/summary/scale_profiles.json` the vessel metric responds on the **k** axis (f150 0.254 → 0.317 at s = 1.10) and stays flat at 0.23–0.26 on **i**. Single-axis probes about the block centre and a full 12-DOF affine are different experiments, so this is plausibly axis coupling — but the raw i-axis column does not, on its own, show the vessel metric preferring a depth stretch. Chapter 6, What we found, and what it means (§6.10.3) has the full profile | Re-run `octreg/scripts/scale_probe.py` starting from the **final** transform, and report the i-axis profile of the **vessel-channel NCC**, not the mixed NCC. **Blocked on the A5.6 shim** — `scale_probe.py` needs `work/oct_ves_dist48_z0.npy`, which the current prep does not write |

| **C3.3** | The actual vibratome cut thickness for I46, and whether the DANDI OME-TIFF was produced by anisotropic pooling of the native reconstruction (and at what factors) | Settles B2.1 and, via the pooling question, the depth-scale story outright — including which of the three readings in C5.4 is right |

#### C.5 Questions the research could not settle

These need an experiment or a reading, not a person's decision. Ordered by consequence.

| # | Question | State of the evidence | Cheapest way to settle it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C5.1** | **Why does the authors' published pose for I46 disagree with ours by 23 mm?** | `crop_final`, `crop_final2` and `whole_final` all record `evaluation.vs_author_coarse_placement`: **centre 17.7–17.8 mm, rotation 108–117°, corner mean 23.0–23.2 mm, corner max 32.8–33.2 mm**. The two poses are nowhere near each other. The working interpretation is that the author placement is a coarse/initialisation pose, not a gold standard — but that is a convenient reading and it is **unresolved**. It is the only external check on absolute placement that exists | Needs C3.1 (the `oct.nii` header). Until then it cannot be settled, and it must be disclosed in any comparison against the baseline |
| **C5.2** | **Does re-running DANDI I58 on `flip-1` (30°) fix it?** | A free experiment. The file is on disk (A3.2), 2 890 933 645 B, never tried. I58 is the one diagnosed failure with a diagnosed fix | `prep_subject.py --mri …flip-1_VFA.nii.gz --work work/I58_flip1`, then `register.py`. ~30 min of GPU |
| **C5.3** | **Is "the 0.12 mm subjects failed" confounded with "the flip-3/flip-4 subjects failed"?** | Nobody has recorded this. The nine runs do **not** use the same MRI contrast: six use `flip-2`, I58 and I62 use `flip-3`, I57 and I61 use `flip-4`. **Of the four non-`flip-2` runs, three are wrong and the fourth (I62) is "correct (visual only)"** | Falls out of C5.2 and of a `flip-2`-equivalent re-run for I57/I61 if one exists. Currently a naming-level observation, not a diagnosis |
| **C5.4** | **Which of the three readings of the depth anisotropy is right?** | (A) I46-only sidecar bug — **fails**, because I55 returns **0.8570 = 6/7** and I38 is clamped trying to get there (A2.7, A8.4). (B) the 7/6 sidecars are the erroneous ones and I46's isotropic sidecar is the correct one — **partly fits** (I55 hits 6/7 dead on, I56 0.936 and I62 0.980 are partway) **but cannot explain why I46's vascular stage goes to 1.214**. (C) ±15 % anisotropy is registration error absorbed by the least-constrained direction — **fits the sign scatter** (0.837 → 1.214) **but not the 6/7 and 7/6 coincidences**. None of the three is clean; the project's prose presents (A) as settled, and it is not | Re-prep **I46 at `--oct-spacing-um 14,12,12`** and **I55 at `12,12,12`**, and compare. One heavy GPU job each; the exact commands are in chapter 4, The data (§4.5). Prediction if (A) is right: I46's `stretch_ijk[0]` drops from 1.219 to ≈1.04 and its vascular corner motion drops from 1.52 mm toward I55's 0.33 mm. **This decides whether the project's most-cited external-agreement result survives.** Q8(d) — the anisotropic-pooling question — would settle it from the other end |
| **C5.5** | **What is the `ves_seg` z-offset for I46?** | `ves_seg.tif` has **561** z-slices against the OCT's **627** — a 0.79 mm depth-alignment ambiguity the data cannot settle by itself. `zoff0` wins (167 µm vs 302 µm) but only relatively, and **only after** the vascular stage: before it the structural rows invert the answer (276 vs 245 µm). `prep_subject.py` assumes a provided `--oct-vesseg` is z-aligned at slice 0 ("as verified on sub-I46"); the older `prep_vessels.py` computed both offsets precisely because this was once unknown | C3.1. Note the circularity risk: the offset is currently decided by the metric the vascular stage optimises |
| **C5.6** | **What is the section period of the Xiangrui brainstem OCT?** | `slab_window = 60` at 20 µm has **never been measured**. It is the only dataset where the window may be badly mis-sized, and A3.3 shows a non-integer window leaves a residual sawtooth | Apply the A3.3 method (FFT + autocorrelation of the per-slice in-tissue median) to `data/xiangrui/OCT_to_MRI/I58_Brainstem_mus_Slice_full_20um_corr.nii.gz`. Needs a nibabel reader rather than tifffile. ~10 min CPU, read-only. Also **Q9** |
| **C5.7** | **Does the section period reconcile across the whole dataset?** | Measured on exactly two subjects, giving 0.396 mm (I46) and 0.420 mm (I56). If `period × declared_spacing` is ≈0.40–0.42 mm for *all* nine, the vibratome cut is ~0.4 mm rather than the nominal 500 µm, and B2.1 is settled from the data alone — which is also the reading that forced the withdrawal in A8.3 | Measure it on the remaining seven DANDI subjects, by the A3.3 method. ~10 min CPU each, read-only. **This is the cheapest way to settle B2.1 without an email** |
| **C5.8** | **Does the singular-value spectrum of every subject's final affine show a clearing signature?** | If several subjects show σ₁ ≈ σ₂ ≈ σ₃ that **would** be an isotropic-shrinkage signature; if all show one-axis structure, the effect is metadata or registration everywhere. Run so far on I46 only (1.21149 / 1.03593 / 0.98222 — one-axis) | 5 min, read-only, on data already in `result.json` |
| **C5.9** | **Is the 167 µm vessel floor a registration limit or an annotation limit?** | B1.5. `label_offset.py` would answer it and its output was not persisted | Re-run the script |
| **C5.10** | **Does mutual information work on this problem?** | **Never implemented, never measured on this data.** The argument against it — not FFT-able, poor at ~1 % overlap, no spatial structure — is sound and is sourced to the lab's own review, but it is an argument, not a result. "Did you try MI?" is the first question at any registration venue | A masked-MI multi-start affine is baseline **B1** in `/Users/yyttim/workspace/lsfm-project/literature_review/working/classical_partial_methods.md:441`, which already carries the configuration |
| **C5.11** | **What do the never-swept hyperparameters cost?** | `n_rot = 8000` never swept (I48's search score plateaued at 4 000/16 000 and did not change at 16 000; the Xiangrui run converged by 4 000 — both suggest 8 000 is generous). `topk = 24`, `min_sep_mm = 3.0`, `min_sep_deg = 10.0` never swept. `reg = 2.0` / `ls_clamp = 0.15`: the *direction* is verified but the values were not swept. `window_mm = 1.35`, `deep = 0.5`, `prom = 0.05` not swept. Two that **were** swept came out as ties or near-ties — the `--vascular-w` and dark-vs-Frangi channel sweeps, whose full tables are in chapter 6, What we found, and what it means (§6.10) — and in the second of them the Frangi variant is *closer to the oracle* while `register.py` hard-codes `dark` | Sweeps, if a reviewer demands them. The honest framing today is "defensible but not optimal", not "tuned" |
| **C5.12** | **A true random-pose-in-hemisphere control** | The shipped `random_shift_control` is a ±3 mm translation of the accepted pose with rotation, scale and mirror preserved — the weakest link in the evidence. The honest chance level that **does** exist is a point thrown uniformly inside the block: **530.2 µm median, f150 0.117**, against the registered 167 µm / 0.473 | ~1 h: reuse the existing 16 000-orientation grid and score `vessel_distance_stats` at N random accepted-overlap poses |
| **C5.13** | **Do neighbouring blocks from one specimen abut after independent registration?** | Untried, and it is the cheapest unexplored **label-free** evaluation idea in the project: two adjacent blocks registered independently should produce placements that abut, and the residual gap/overlap is a scalar error in millimetres requiring no annotation. The public data cannot supply it — one `S01` block per subject — but the lab's own 20+ specimen dataset presumably can | Depends on **Q4**, which is why that question now asks explicitly for *adjacent* blocks and not just more blocks |

#### C.6 Disagreements that are settled on the record, and what remains open behind them

| # | The disagreement | How it is settled | What is actually still open |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C6.1** | Whether "500 µm / 33 slices = 15.15 µm" is an independent line of evidence for the I46 sidecar bug. It was written up as a third line, then promoted to a fourth | **Settled: the line is WITHDRAWN** (A8.3). It fails outright on I56, where the same arithmetic implies ~42 µm against a doubly corroborated 35 µm sidecar, and read consistently it implies a correction of only **1.06**, not 1.167. Any document that counts it as a fourth or fifth line must recount without it — there are **three** | Not the withdrawal, which is decided, but the physical question underneath it: **what is the real cut thickness?** The 500 µm premise is `[UNVERIFIED]` (B2.1). Settle by C5.7 (measure the period on all nine subjects) or C3.3 / Q8(c) (ask the authors). Note the I46 sidecar bug itself does not depend on this line and stands without it |
| **C6.2** | "The tightest-converging runs are the wrong ones" | Narrowed to **I58 and I61** once I57 was corrected from 12/12 to 10/12 (A2.2) | **I38 is also 12/12** and carries a "correct (visual only)" verdict, which no audit pass mentions. Whether the inverse-correlation argument survives with I38 included is open. The mean statistic (11.3 wrong vs 10.2 correct) is unaffected |
| **C6.3** | "5 of 9 DANDI subjects correct" vs "2 confirmed, 3 unresolved, 1 undecidable, 3 failed" | The honest count is the second (A4.9) | Which one is *true* depends on B4.2 / B1.8 — fixing `map_labels_to_grid` and re-evaluating. **~1 h of work, no re-registration needed.** Until then the project cannot state its own success rate |
| **C6.4** | Three different counts of what exists only on the server — 7, 20, and 21 | All three are correct and reconcile exactly (A6.2) | Nothing. Recorded here only so nobody re-opens it |
| **C6.5** | The project's own files diagnose **I57 and I61** as tissue-mask failures | **Settled from `prep.json`, re-read 2026-08-24:** the mask story covers **I56, I58 and I61**. It holds for I61 (threshold 6.80 below median 10.42, fraction 0.742, 1 838.8 cm³, `valley_ratio: null`). **It does not cover I57**, whose threshold sits above its median, whose mask volume is an unremarkable 518 cm³, and which found a valley at 0.0631 (A4.4) | **I57 has no failure diagnosis at all** `[OPEN]` (C1.3), and **I56 — currently marked correct — has the worst mask in the dataset** (A4.5). Separately, `valley_ratio: null` is the cleanest automatic red flag the pipeline already computes, is written into every `prep.json`, and **is surfaced nowhere** — not in `result.json`, not in `results_inspection/INDEX.md`, not in any figure. It is one line to print. Do not read it as a verdict on its own, though: **I55 also has `valley_ratio: null` and is correct**; the discriminating combination is a null valley **plus** a mask volume above the ~1 210 cm³ gate of §A.4a |

#### C.7 What is open because nobody has done it yet

Not questions in the epistemic sense — these are simply undone, and each is listed with the reason it
has not been done, because a successor will otherwise assume they were tried and rejected.

| # | Undone | Why it is still open |
|---|---|---|
| **C7.1** | The baseline has never been run | `mri2oct_affine.sh` was read flag by flag, never executed. Every "we removed X from their pipeline" claim is a **reading, not a comparison** |
| **C7.2** | No reject gate exists | Two gates are fully justified by fields already written into every `result.json` / `prep.json`, and neither is implemented. **(i) Separation, not score:** reject when `top1/top2 < 1.02`. That alone catches I48 (margin 0.0013) and DANDI-I58 (0.0001). **(ii) Mask volume:** reject or flag when the MRI "tissue" volume exceeds about 1.5× the top of the measured hemisphere band — i.e. **> ~1 210 cm³** (`1.5 × 806`), derived from the 806 cm³ maximum of §A.4a. On this corpus that flags I61 (1 838.8), I56 (2 519.0) and I58 (1 453.4) and clears all six sane masks, the largest being I38 at 805.8 cm³. Surfacing `valley_ratio: null` alongside it costs one more line. **~20 lines in total.** — **What must NOT ship is any absolute-score clause.** An earlier version of gate (i) added `or top1 < 0.35`, and a "good result scores above *x*" rule on `refine.final_ncc` has been proposed more than once. Neither works: **I61 refines to 0.5020 and I57 to 0.5121 and both are wrong, while I62 refines to 0.2842 and is correct.** Any cut that passes I62 passes both wrong runs; any cut that fails them also fails I62 and I56, and the `top1 < 0.35` form would additionally reject the brainstem run. **Absolute NCC does not separate right from wrong across subjects — never state a numeric acceptance threshold on it without this counterexample attached.** The pipeline currently emits a transform regardless, and every diagnosed failure was caught by a human looking at a figure |
| **C7.3** | No target-registration-error protocol | The only proposal on record is ~20 matched points per pair, ~30 min of annotation, and it has **never been requested** |
| **C7.4** | The quantitative maps `{PD, T1, T2star}_VFA.nii.gz` were never downloaded | ~45 GB for the nine subjects. This is the **scientific payoff** of the whole registration — every registered OCT voxel gets a T1/T2*/PD value — and nothing in the project demonstrates it |
| **C7.5** | Subjects I45, I59, I60 were never added | I45 and I60 carry OCT `ves_seg.tif`. Tier-1 vessel evidence currently exists for **one** subject; these would make it three. One line each in `data/manifest_multisub.txt`, 2.53 + 2.85 GB of OCT plus MRI. Note DANDI presigned URLs expire in 6 h — the aria2 watchdog described in chapter 7, Failures, dead ends, and things that bit us (§7.2.10) is required |
| **C7.6** | The figures the PI approved have not been human-verified | All six five-panel PNGs in `octreg/figures/` were generated by Claude Code. **Disclosed in the 2026-08-23 meeting**; action item A7, still open. Until it closes, "looks pretty good" is not independent confirmation |
| **C7.7** | Laminar / cortical-layer alignment | The labels carry infragranular vs supragranular; the evaluator collapses both to GM and the OCT side has only two classes. **Layers are what the cell census is organised by**, and nothing here demonstrates layer-level accuracy. Would need a three-class OCT representation |
| **C7.8** | The PSOCT **birefringence** channel | The Costantini OCT is acquired with a polarization-sensitive rig, and we use only the scattering channel. The birefringence data is not in the files downloaded and `octreg` has no code path for it. It is the single most obvious unused signal — a fibre-orientation channel would be a natural fourth NCC channel |
| **C7.9** | Version control | `git init` on the authoritative tree, after a `.gitignore` that excludes the `.m4a` recordings, the copyrighted PDFs, `slack_archive`, `code/costantini/` and `external/`; the draft is in chapter 10, State of play: where everything is (§10.10, Risk 1). **First action on takeover**, together with rsyncing the 21 server-only files off a rented container that reassigns its address on every restart |

#### C.8 If only three of these get resolved

Ranked by how much of the rest they unblock:

1. **B4.2 / B1.8 — fix `map_labels_to_grid` and re-evaluate the six 0.12 mm subjects.** One hour, no
   re-registration, and it is the difference between "5 of 9 correct" and "2 of 9 confirmed". It also
   decides C6.3 and re-opens or closes C1.3, C5.3 and A4.3–A4.7 in one pass.
2. **C1.1 / Q6 — the scientific endpoint.** One question to one person. Until it is answered, nobody
   can decide whether C7.1 (run the baseline) is mandatory or merely expected, which is the largest
   single block of work in the roadmap.
3. **C3.1–C3.3 / Q8 — the one email to the Costantini authors.** It closes B1.6, B2.1, C5.1, C5.5 and
   C5.4 simultaneously — part (d), the anisotropic-pooling question, is the most direct test of the
   depth-scale hypothesis anyone has proposed — and it has been recommended twice without being sent.
